Just be careful not to assume those are part of the lunch specials and getting those pairings will set you back full price for each item. So the expected bill vs. the actual bill was way off! But still, at least I got to try numerous items. Would definitely come back to try more.

Came back here right before they close and I must say they deserve another star from me for how legit their esarn grilled meats are and the jiew sauce. It transported me to Thailand as I bite into the grilled pork which was the crying tiger version, came with grilled sticky rice which was a nice touch - I don't see those are menus too often. Me being an esarn food lover the sauce was really authentic they did use lime and some toasted rice in it as well. Some places just skimp out due to customers not really knowing what real jiew sauce tastes like.

For the friend chicken thigh aka piece of heaven thigh - still blew my mind. nuff said.

Got the nam tok nua which was equally amazing as the cartilage soup where my friends started licking the bowl after. They use good quality beef for the nam tok and the soup was just really flavorful even for the second time having it. 

The basil fried rice wasn't as good - too oily but the pad see ew seafood was really good I just had to order some main dishes just to see how it is and compare with Larb Ubol which may now be my second go to for Thai food now after eating here. 

Great service, accommodated our big group and right before they closed. Will definitely try to eat here every time I'm in east village. Although, I'm hoping you guys open another branch soon, maybe in Hell's Kitchen? :)

Delicious, spicy, and friendly. what else can you ask for? Awesome papaya salad options, gorgeous noodles, the place is pretty. Absolutely a must try if you love your thai food on the spicy side. Beware of the spicy scale of madness, though! From 1 to 4, 2 is pretty spicy yet delicious, if you dare, do try number 3! number 4 comes with sweat attack.
Recommendable, yes.

As someone who eats Thai food weekly, has been to Thailand and has somewhat of a healthy addiction to the tart spicy dishes in particular, I'm pretty confident in saying this is the best Thai food I've had in NYC.  Som Tum is a personal favorite dish of mine, and they exceeded my expectations.  In this version the unripe papaya had purposely been pounded more than usual in the mortar and pestle, allowing the bright, sweet dressing to permeate.  To some, this is almost blasphemous; papaya should retain its off white color and crispness.  However both my wife and I found this version to be even more enjoyable.  The papaya because a true conduit to the lime, not just a vessel to deliver crunch.  There is also a healthy layer of sauce on the dish, far more than alot of well regarded Thai places, just beckoning for an order of Sticky Rice.  Or perhaps the delicious Grilled Sticky Rice (on a stick!) reminiscent of the Southeast Asian favorite grilled in bamboo that we loved on the side of the road in Cambodia and in Bangkok's Chinatown.  The vegetarian version of Som Tum is as amazing as any version with fish sauce I've had, although we did miss the dried shrimp.

One of the more delicious and adventurous dishes on the menu is the Coong Chae Nam Pla (Thai Prawn Sashimi with Green Curry Sauce.  Excellent raw shrimp, finished with a bright curry dressing, sprinkled with garlic and chillies.  Just enough heat and flavor to complement the subtle sweetness and slight sticky tackiness of raw shellfish and not overpower it.  The texture was delicious and reminded me of raw lobster. 

The highlight of the night was the Tum Pla Too + Kao Mun (Thai Mackerel in Papaya Salad with Coconut Rice).  Even more bruised and pounded than the regular Som Tum; the tomatoes released nearly all their juice, the papaya was broken and absorbed all the liquid, the Mackerel mashed and incorporated throughout the salad.  This was incredible.  It was as bright as usual but sweeter and richer, perhaps the best Somtum i've ever had (that and a Strawberry version last year in Queens...).  The coconut rice was steaming hot, rich with coconut flavor and super fluffy, perfect match to the cool, crisp salad.  I could eat this everyday.

Even their version of  Larp Pla Dook Yang (Spicy Minced Grilled Catfish Salad) was a standout.  Unlike the description, or the usual ground version, the Catfish was cut in to small cubes, big enough that I could tell I was eating catfish, but small enough to fit on my spoon with all the accoutrements.  Loved this version.  I often find this dish a bit to heavy with (raw) red onions and just a little to herbaceous for me, but this version had perfect balance.

The chef here clearly knows the traditions of Thai Isan cooking, but also adds his own touch which is much appreciate.  The flavors are perfect, and the staff is as friendly as we encountered in Thailand.  Excellent vibe, however it can be very loud since there is nothing soft in the restaurant to absorb the sound, they may want to add some padding here or there.  Prices also are excellent, around what I would pay in Queens for a similar meal.  Even the drink prices are inexpensive.  I had a huge cocktail with Thai liquor for about $7, a steal.

My only regret is that it took me so long to eat here, especially after so many evenings at DROM next door.  Do try this place, and be adventurous! I'm sure the Pad Thai is delicious, but if you're going to order that, do yourself a favor and start your meal with a Thai salad.  Aroi Mak!

Fun and lively joint serving authentic Thai dishes. Somtum Der was recommended by my Thai friend, so it's legit. 

Cons:
* Perfect for big groups! You can fit a group for up to 25 people. 
* Fast, friendly and attentive staff. Especially with a big group they made sure to keep asking us what we wanted to drink and eat. They were happy to do separate checks- AMAZING!
* My friends and I loved the slightly grilled coconut rice sticks, very spicy beef salad, and chicken satay. Honestly everything was pretty delicious! 
* Huge array of beers and cocktails!

3.5 stars - Thai ranks second to Chinese as cuisines my fiancé and I don't care much about. But after attempting to walk in without reservation to 4 different restaurants in the area and knowing it's far more familiar to my grandma than any "white" food, my fiancé and I decided to give Somtum a try. 

We all had Northern Thai cuisine once at Zabb Elee just a few blocks away and weren't too impressed. This time, armed with our yelp app, my fiancé and I read up on all the recommendations and ultimately decided on duck spicy salad, beef skewers, catfish soup, and house special seafood suki. 

The first dishes - duck, beef, catfish all arrived fairly quickly. Not quite sure what was the hold up with our suki, we were literally done with the first three plates and ready for our bill when we finally asked our server to check the order. Nevertheless it was worth the wait because it was one of the better dishes of our meal. 

Spicy duck salad - way too salty, sour and fatty. It had a strange funny after taste where I couldn't stomach a second bite. 

Catfish soup - the fish was way overcooked and really dry even after being dunked into a bowl of soup. I did enjoyed the enoki mushroom. 

Beef skewers - I wished we just ordered more of these because they were one of the best skewers I've had in life. So well marinated, so juicy! Loaded with flavors and went so well with the spicy dip. Came in 3 per order - perfect sharing for us! 

Seafood suki - the suki noodle was way overcooked to a point they were indistinguishable in our plate. It was however pretty tasty in the sweet tomato sauce along with the fish cakes, shrimp, and calamari.  

We ended our meal with their jelly shaved ice - which was frozen herbal jelly in milk tea. It was quite refreshing and would had been perfect summer treat! 

Overall - Perhaps Northern Thai is more of an acquired taste for us, again we weren't overly impressed. Service was warm, food was well priced. Probably won't return any time soon but if we do, skewers for appetizer, entree, and dessert please!

Being that I'm from Thailand I can honestly say that this is the most authentic Thai "is an" style food in the entire city and I've eaten at plenty of Thai establishments here in the city. I would have loved to give this place 5 stars based on their food alone, but when it comes to service, this place still needs work: The male servers are always very attentive, bubbly, and have a smile on their faces the entire time. I cannot say the same about the women servers. They always seem as if they are irritated about something and look like they just left a funeral. I made a simple mistake once when placing an order, I changed my mind about an item and female server says to me " you want to change your order?! Uh! " I understand changes can make for some headache in the kitchen but she did not even place my order in the system yet because I was watching her the entire time. That was un called for, and she has been nasty on other occasions as well in which I will not state. I am going to either stick to take out or ask for a male waiter. Fix yo face hoe!

Went again last week and had a feast with three friends. 

Tum Thai Kai Kem (spicy papaya salad with salted egg): delicate and refreshing. 

Tum Suo Der (papaya salad with sweet chili sauce): too fishy for me. 

Larb Pla Dook Yang (spicy minced grilled catfish salad): loved it; those pieces of catfish were delicious. 

Larb Hed Kao Kuo (minced mushroom salad with peppermint, lime and roasted rice): flavorless; the mushroom had no taste whatsoever. 

Chef's signature wok-fried seafood suki: tasty; interesting combination of flavors. 

Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay (noodles with shrimp & calamari): truly mouthwatering; I couldn't get enough of it. 

Totally recommended. :)

For the price, this is thai food that is significantly better than the likes of Spice or your ordinary take-out spot. 

Me and my brother had the vegetarian papaya salad, sticky rice, spicy pork and basil noodles, and coconut milk marinated grilled beef.

Papaya salad was killer. So flavorful and spicy. I recommend you get the vegetarian one if you are having other meaty foods because it isn't oil and is sort of like a palette cleanser for the rest of the food. 

Sticky rice: honestly, maybe I'm just not a fan of sticky rice. It felt hard and dry. I used the leftover salad dressing to soften/flavor it up. Next time, I would just get steamed rice or coconut rice as this was bland. 

Noodles: These were very tasty but too oily. Spicy with real slices of chile and hunks of ground pork. The basil leaves were fried and crispy (I would have preferred them just fresh). Could have used something to cut through all the fat like lime juice.

The grilled beef skewers were very tasty but the cut of meat itself was obviously a cheaper one as I could barely chew it. I ate two skewers and thoroughly enjoyed the flavor but wish it was a little easier to process. Not really recommended for a date if you're trying to be classy, haha.

Can't speak to the drinks as I didn't have any but the bottles of wine seemed affordable ($29-$$30)

I would come back again. Total bill came to $48 including tip

very spacious, very friendly, but everything was just okay if not below average because you couldn't taste anything else but fish sauce. 

We had the papaya salad with pork neck, alot of strong flavors and fish sauce that overwhelms your mouth. We also had the grilled coconut rice which was decent, but my sister said she could only have a few bites. We also had the fried chicken thighs, which were okay, parts of it were too fried. We tried the larb with vegetables, but you couldn't really enjoy it because all you can taste was the damn fish sauce from the papaya salad.

Really awesome and authentic Thai food. Recommended by friends and have been there twice since! 

The recent visit I finally got to try their grilled sticky rice. They were out the first time I was there. And they were so good! Definitely a must order item! They do fill you up though. 

I love spicy and they were SPICY, especially the thai prawn sashimi that we ordered! So for those who can't have it too spicy, you can tell them to cut it down a notch (which will still be spicy just not as fiery hot.)

I will definitely go back and keep trying all their other dishes.
My body is traumatized. I will not be coming back. Everything is spicy here. Bathroom all night long. Stomach hurt the entire next day, and my ass is swollen.

I have been wanting to try this place and I haven't had Thai in awhile.

I ended up ordering the Original papaya salad - nice and spicy and good.

I got the Pad Ki Mao Pork and Basil -Spicy flat rice noodles, wok-fried with ground pork and crispy basil leaves. I am not sure where the crispy basil leaves were, but none were found in my dish. I didn't like this dish, because it was too much salt and too much sugar. I had to add vinegar to cut out the salt and sugar flavour.

I would try other things, since the food wasn't too bad for me not to give this place another try.

I absolutely love this place for the authentic and quality ingredients. So much so that I tolerate the service. It's slow but not in a neglectful way. More in a way that seems confused. As if they aren't quite sure who all these people are and what to do first. Like the first time you decided to throw a dinner party and everyone showed up on time.

I am Thai and I can guarantee you that the food here is really good.  My friend and I went together last night and we ordered fried chicken, grilled sticky rice, grilled pork, Som Tum Plata (papaya salad), and Panna Cotta Thai tea. Everything was good! My favourite was probably the fried chicken.  Totally recommend this place! :)

somtum der is a delicious.  the flavors are wonderful and across the board.  they also have thai style fried chicken, which was the best thing i ate in bangkok.  i haven't seen it on the menu at any thai restaurant in the states, so when my friend recommended this place AND they had this chicken, i knew i must go.  the chicken was delicious.

Came for dinner with G, who recently visited Thailand, and he attested to the authenticity of his dish (larb ped = spicy minced duck salad with green vegetables and chilis) and the spices used in our dishes. We started with an order of Moo Rong Hai Der and Khao Ji (= grilled marinated pork) which came with 2 sticks of sticky rice. The sticky rice is amazing - easily my favorite part of the meal and must order side (both bc its delicious and you likely will need it bc the dishes here are so spicy!). I wasn't feeling as adventurous and ordered the Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay (broad flat noodles with shrimp & calamari) - a little too oily for me, will probably order one of their spicy salads next time. Everything was delicious but very spicy, so if you're more of a "medium spice" person like me, definitely ask them to tone down the dishes for you (pretty sure we ordered the larb ped medium spicy and I still needed a ton of sticky rice/water). The portions are a bit small but filling. Cute decor, could probably seat two big groups comfortably in the center of the restaurant, with smaller tables meant for parties of 2 or 4 along the perimeter.

I searched for a lot of times for Thai restaurants that serve street food in bangkok, which is my fav. After I tried many many time, this is the one fully satisfied me!! Just like what I had in many food shelter in Bangkok, only cleaner, nicer and closer!!

It's great, but amongst the din of competent Thai restaurants sprouting up all over NYC, a bit hyped up due to its plum Alphabet City location. Still, very good and quite affordable. There is a lot of stuff on the menu to explore and order. I had a cold chrysanthemum tea to drink which was really refreshing with the hot and spicey salads and dishes. I'd come back again but would not go out of my way for it as I am usually nearer to hell's kitchen or in queens where it all began.

Holy Jesus.
Somtum Der and Pok Pok are the only Northern Thai restaurants I've been to, and holy crap, it is good. Somtum Der is like a cheaper, chiller experience than Pok Pok, but just as good. NO wait (usually), no bullshit, just incredible freakin' food. I would get into a bathtub filled with their coconut rice. The pro play is the papaya salad with the salted egg, duck larb, coconut rice, and pad ki mao. Do this and be happy. I would eat this all day, every day. Be warned though, if you ask for stuff spicy, it gets SERIOUSLY spicy. Be prepared to sweat.

The atmosphere is chill too, and all the waitstaff wear these funny straw fedoras, in addition to being super nice. So extra points there.

With this and Larb Ubol opening, Manhattan actually has some real Thai food.  I've eaten at the one in Bangkok and this place comes close to replicating what they have over there.  I went here with a group of 7 people and we shared about 8 to 9 plates I forgot exactly how many. I can say that if you're with a group of 7 hungry people I would probably order 10 dishes just to be safe . The food is meant to be shared like how traditional Thai food usually is served. I would also be careful of the spice level since this food is made Thai style could be too spicy for some people even if indicating a medium level.

I think the food pacing was horrible given that food and accompaniments were served at different times. Asian dining experiences usually suck in when it comes to food pacing, especially in this instance when something like Larb should be accompanied with sticky rice and they don't even come out at the same time. 

The largest group I can picture being waited on is 10, given the size of the tables and overall lack of the wait staff to service the amount of requests.  The service was so slow but friendly. If they don't get their service together in the next few visits then I would just stay home and make this stuff myself.
Highly recommend to the person who love Authentic Northeastern Thai food. High quality of food and the taste is very good.

This place is exciting. Everything is a flavor explosion - a mix of tart lime, spicy thai chiles, salty fish sauce and fresh ingredients. And then there's the cooling side of coconut rice/sticky rice. And the setting's pretty cute on top of that. 

Little bit obsessed.

The noodles are all alright, not too much to go crazy about.  If you want pad thai and pad see ew just go to another restaurant and get it for a little cheaper.  The meats though, are all really tender and very flavorful.  One dish quantity-wise is enough for a person, except for the one glaring downside of having no vegetables on it.  So it's probably best to get two meat dishes and then one of their papaya salad things to share as an appetizer.  I haven't had one of their papaya salad dishes despite it supposedly being their main thing simply because i've had the dish elsewhere and wasn't a fan.  Decor is upper casual, so maybe good for a casual date, no bueno for a romantic date.  The wait staff is nice enough too.

This is one of those reviews where I should probably just leave the rating and not comment, because I'll likely echo the other reviews and it's also hard to articulate why I loved this food so much. But alas, here goes. 

Don't come here looking for pad thai and drunken noodle and green curries filled with little dry peices of pork. I say come with a few friends who enjoy and appreciate food, get a variety of the papaya salads and cold meat. The heat and sweetness is addictive. Also get a serving or two of the fried chicken thigh. Holy moley. I actually prefered it sans dipping sauce. The sticky rice sticks aren't the greatest, but they're fun. If you're expecting the traditional chinese zongzi style (wrapped in a leaf w/ savory things like mushrooms and pork inside) you will be dissapointed, bc this is sweet and flavored with coconut. Many of the flavor profiles reminded me more of the food my Vietnamese and Cambodian relatives make. 

Bottom line, this place will redefine what you consider Thai food, as it should, and it'll leave a feeling of firey fullness in your stomach. Afterward, when someone asks, "Hey, wanna get Thai?", you can smugly say "Depends on which region you mean".

Excellent Isaan food in NYC, friendly service and beer Lao! The prices were much more reasonable than the run of the mill Thai spots in the area. We had excellent mushroom laab, namtok and grilled pork-all at a spice I grew accustomed to in Thailand and all of which tasted fresh and traditional

The restaurant was very accommodating to a large group of us and the service was very on point. Staff was friendly, informative and very generous, especially to some of our party who have never had Isaan food before.  Go there!

May have found my favorite Thai spot in the city!!! Hands down the best Larb Moo!!!

I came here with my wife for a Sat lunch.  I love spicy food and my wife not so much but I convinced her to come and I am glad we did!!

First, like my wife pointed out,they are so smart to have their entire menu loaded with pictures!! And the food that comes out actually resembles the pics, so def happy about that.

Now for the food, we ordered the somtum with salted eggs, the larb moo was to die for!!  We also had the grilled pork skewers and they were delicious!  

My wife actually enjoyed the level of spice and topped the meal off with the Thai iced tea panna cotta!!! A must try!! Gotta come back soon for their fried chicken!

Was it worth it to trek over to the LES from Jersey City for Thai food?  Ah - hellz ya!  Somtum Der has a good thing going here.  Great service (with a smile), cool vibe, coupled with some bangin' spicy-ass, tapas-like dishes; sort of like a Thai Izakaya joint.

Going back to the food, we had ordered the following:

- Spicy prawn sashimi salad (most excellent)

- Crab meat Pad Thai (arguably, one of the best Pad Thais I've ever had)

- Fried Chicken Thighs (excellent; it's ginger hint reminded me of tatsuta age)

- Grilled coconut rice (very good; can't recall if it came with one of the other dishes or not)

- House special grilled marinated beef (excellent)

All washed down with some Singha beers and a bottle of prosecco.  Very highly recommended!

The larb and papaya salads were some of the best ones I've had.  Each was nicely balanced with acidity and the level 2 spicy was just right - though I would consider going to 3.

Pad kee mao had good flavor, but portion was a bit small, and I prefer the pork in slices versus ground.

Been a fan of this place since it opened but my last experience has me a bit concerned. I've always been impressed by the flavoring of the chicken soup with mixed herbs--kind of chili dill--and have enjoyed the unusual vegetables that come with it, but the last time it wasn't quite up to the standard of the past. Which isn't to say it wasn't good.  
I also ordered the flat noodles with seafood--which I hadn't had before. Tasty enough but the seafood consisted of 2 smallish shrimps and a few barely discernible bits of squid.
This restaurant is listed in the frequent flier plan of an airline, which usually indicates that its having financial problems. The plans typically offer the business a loan which then is paid off from a percentage of the bill. I'm guessing that this restaurant is trying to save money by skimping on the ingredients.
This place is legit.  Some of the very best Thai I've had anywhere including in the Kingdom itself.  Serious flavor and genuinely good service.  $10 corkage.  I'll be back, soon.

LOVE!!!!!!


I thought Zab Elle was the best Thai in the city, but this place totally beats it.


They're authentic and their spice level goes by Thai standards, not American. So be careful. Which means .... They're "1" for Spicy is equivalent to a hot hot 4 already.


Get the crispy chicken, original papaya salad and their crispy pork. 


I'm addicted, I come at least once a week !

As I'm recovering from some tummy turmoil it's hard to add more stars but I'll try to be fair. 
First, we ordered several dishes: orginal papaya salad, chicken thighs, Larb Moo (pork) and Duck Larb with sticky rice. The first round was delicious. Everything. the Larbs were very spicy. Yummy and flavorful but after a while the huge glasses of water were VERY necessary. 

The plates are small for sharing (think tapas) so we were still hungry and wanted to order more. This is where things went downhill. Our server turned into bartender and we didn't see her ever again. Had to wave down some other guy to bring us another menu and take the order. We decided on a different papaya salad, the ginger garlic beef, and the larb springrolls. Unimpressed on all fronts. DO NOT ORDER the rock crab papaya salad. I expect seafood dishes to taste seafood-y when fresh but this tasted like straight sea bottom. we couldn't get past one bite! The beef was kind of tough and just not very good. The springrolls were ok but very lemongrass-y to almost overpowering.

Although I saw this on the NYMag Cheap Eats list, it wasn't very cheap after you ordered what you needed to feel satisfied. Maybe they meant cheap in comparison to similar ihsan restaurants in Manhattan?

I don't think I'll return but I can agree with other Yelpers that they have some good dishes and if you're into spicy you'll like it.

Okay, apparently I review only Thai places. 

Here goes:
Basically my last experience at Somtum Der was about as good as it gets. We ordered   spicy catfish soup (Tom Klong Pla Dook Yang), pork larb (Nam Tok Moo), papaya salad with crab (Tum Poo Plara), and fried Isan sausage.

I think the port larb was my personal favorite, spicy, with a perfect texture. The soup was pretty amazing too: the broth was sour and delicious with tons of aromatics, and the catfish was miraculously crispy despite being submerged in liquid. I literally drank the broth after the soup was gone. Papaya salad was another gem. Sometimes crab can be really messy and tricky to eat in this context, but the crab they used had a soft shell where you could gnaw on the shell and let the raw crab kind of squeeze out. Sounds gross, but was actually super satisfying! The sausage, one of my all-time favorite Thai dishes wasn't as good here as I've had it elsewhere, and it was still solid, and given the rest of the food, I'm quite pleased. 

The service was impeccable too. It was the kind of thing that isn't overstated, but each time you reach for your water glass (which I did, necessarily but happily), it's full or when you hand them your credit card, it comes back before you start to twiddle your thumbs. Everyone was perfectly nice too and asked us how we were, etc., but for me the efficiency was key!

All in all, it's been a while since I've walked out of a restaurant feeling so satisfied, and although my stomach kind of hurt from all the chilis the next day, it was worth it.

This place was recommended in Nymag's cheap eats section so I was excited to try it. I ordered the Der styled papaya salad but it was inedibly salty. I can't recall the last time I felt I physically couldn't eat something I've ordered in a restaurant. Boo. I ordered mild and it was crazy spicy, too.

The fried chicken was good, the place is cute and the service was very nice, though.

Food is delicious ! One of d best Thai in d area .. Service varied on 2 occasions..one day was so nice and courteous but another day a different lady was so rude ..no greeting .. Didn't even  ask how I was doing and no water refills ..

Update November 2015 : came her after long . Food still rocks ,service still sucks ! This time I had a fly for company that I just couldn't drive away ..

I ordered Tum Suo (Thai noodle and papaya salad), BBQ pork Skewer, BBQ pork tender, chicken soup, catfish salad, sliced marbled beef shark salad.
I gave 5 stat for BBQ pork tender, BBQ pork skewer, and Chicken soup.
4 star only Tum Suo.
3 star catfish salad.
1-2 star for sliced beef salad (do not recommend).

Overall the style and food were delicious.
Server is good.
The location is a little far by walking from subway (2ave, F train) bet 5-6st A ave.

Love love love this place.

It is so delicious and so affordable - it's like Narnia in Manhattan.  

The best things I've had there are the papaya salad with pork neck, the raw prawn with chilis, and the grilled meats.

I haven't been a fan of the papaya salad with field crab (way way way too fishy for me) and the duck larb.  The service is great though, and when the waitress saw I didn't eat the field crab papaya salad, she took it off my bill even though I said it was fine.

Note - it is SPICY.  The one chile pepper heat (on a scale of three) is hot so if you're not used to real Thai heat, I would stick with the one.

Redeemed a GrubHub credit here for the "chef's signature seafood suki lunch special", forgoing the papaya salad and mushroom larb mentioned around the web. Staff was friendly upon pickup and the dish was tasty upon consumption. (I requested that they simply remove the chicken in the soup so they could use it elsewhere or simply not include it, but they didn't)

Chef's Signature Wok-Fried Seafood Suki Lunch Special
[Super Peek Kai]
$ 10.00
Subtotal $ 10.00
Tax $ 0.89
Tip $ 0.00
Free Grub $ -5.00
TOTAL $ 5.89

Michelin Bib Gourmand 2015

Village Voice = "You won't find curry on the menu at Somtum Der, nor will you find many of the other specialties that fill the lists of more Americanized versions of Thai restaurants. This offshoot of a Bangkok eatery specializes in fare from the northeastern Isaan region of the country, and it's unyielding in representing that cuisine authentically. Somtum der refers to the green papaya salad, and so that dish is front and center here -- there are several different variations to choose from. After you've selected yours, you should move through pork rolls and sundried beef, a platter of chopped meat larb, and soup, skewers, or one of the versions of fried rice. And chile fans should note that heat can be dialed up intensely here -- so if you're sensitive to spice, you might want an order of sticky rice to temper your meal."
Awesome Thai food, just the right amount of food. Definitely recommend getting a lunch special. And be warned, the hot soup is SPICY!!!!!

Love this neat Isan Thai joint tucked away in East Village. The service is friendly, the food is reasonably priced, and the ambience is hip. The signature Somtum salad possesses such a wide array of flavors that meet in the most delightful way. If you love tender fried chicken, you will not be disappointed in the fried chicken here. The spice level in some of the dishes can be quite high, which for me is a good thing :). Plan on making this a regular stop on my trips into Manhattan!

Very chic and great decor. I love Northeastern Thai food  if you sick with green curry , red curry or Tom Yom. This is the Thai restaurant that I highly recommended you to come. I went to Som Tum der's at BKK Thailand once. The menus is exactly the same . By the way I have been to this place many time and I never disappointed.
The food very yummy.  I like papaya salad with crab , BBQ pork, Laab duck and super chicken wings soup.
Service was great.

I was addicted after the first bite! Everything we ordered was just the right amount of spicy, it was the good kind of spicy not overwhelmingly so that it loses its flavor. We got seated right away, and took a long time deciding on what to order, but as soon as we figured out what we wanted our server was prepared to take our order. Drank a lot of water, and my cup was always full, so the service was great as well as the food. I'll definitely be back!

Attending for an evening meal with friends after a show. The decor is spectacular, very fresh, comfortable, and clean. The staff are friendly and attentive. We arrived with about 20 minutes before the kitchen closed and staff told us right away to get our entire order in soon. This was helpful.

They are willing to make your meals with less or more spice. Try the Mangosteen beverage, it is NOT mango, it is a mangosteen fruit that is sweet and has a bit of a spicy flavor in the beverage. It will not disappoint if you dig sweet alcoholic drinks.

This location is NOT wheelchair accessible. There are 3 small steps to walk up and a heavy glass door to pull open, which pulls out towards you. You'll need help opening this door and entering. If you use a walker you'll need help getting in and out, if you use a cane you may be able to walk up the steps, but if you are in a wheelchair you will not be able to enter unless you are comfortable with folks in your party lifting you.

Once inside the entire location is one floor and leveled. The bathroom is wide and the door opens inward and is very chic and clean. 

Some tables have a booth with chairs accompanying them with backs. Other seats are like picnic tables but the benches move outward. If you need back support keep this in mind.

Yum Goong Yang was ATOMIC hot. Like licking a volcano. Service was crazy slow and we got someone else's food a few times but it was a Saturday night. I had the Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay and it was phenom. Fiancé had the Pad Thai Mun Poo. Best Pad Thai we've tried. Oh and the Thai tea with milk was delish. Would go again on a slower night.

This is probably my favorite Thai in all of NYC along with Uncle Boons (which is fairly overpriced) and Pok Pok (which is in a really remote part of Brooklyn). I stepped in here with my brother about a month ago and again today and both times had an utterly amazing meal. 

The menu may look confusing but make sure to try the Tum Kor Moo Yang (spicy papaya salad with pork neck), the Nam Tok Moo Larb (spicy pork and toasted rice salad), the Moo Rong Hai Der (marinated and grilled pork), and the grilled sticky rice (which is almost like a dessert)

I also really dig the coconut rice here as a side. Anyway the food here is indeed spicy but you can get it from level 1 to level 4 spicy. I always get level 3.

The interior is nice, the people who work here are awesome and, aside from all that, this is some of the best priced and most authentic thai in the city. Definitely my favorite place to get some papaya salad or larb in Manhattan.

Quite possibly the most legitimate thai I've had in NYC. The venue is casual yet clean, great for group or a date. Usually very busy so I'd advise you to make a reservation in advance. Somtum is a must order with seven or so different kinds but I recommend the one with salty egg(first thing on the menu). I've been with a large group and have never not liked anything on the menu.

A little out of the way in Alphabet City but worth it for sure!  Menu is different than the normal Thai restaurant but in a good way.  Highly suggest the papaya salads, larb salad, fried chicken, and pad thai.  Other dishes I had were also good.  Service can be slow but not that bad.

Just named one of Michelin's Best Places to Eat in NYC on a Budget, Somtum Der lives up the hype. In a city full of excellent Thai, it's rare to find a place that offers friendly service, amazing food and a beautiful trendy atmosphere at a reasonable price. I loved the spicy papaya salad, and the grilled beef was flavorful. Queens and 9th Avenue have some great choices when it comes to Thai, but Somtum is among the best in Manhattan for sure. 

And if it's your birthday, they have a really funky and fun ritual :)

With so many Thai restaurants sprouting all over NYC like mushrooms, it is always amazing to stumble upon the ones that stand out.

Somtum Der offers a fantastic Thai Isan cuisine (northern part-spicy). The long communal tables and the Sai (fish traps) hanging on the ceiling speak truly of a Thai ambiance.

Since it's family style dining, we started with Pad Thai Mun Poo; it's a special Pad Thai made with crab meat and crab paste with home style sauce. its so delicious and it disappeared on our table with a blink of an eye. Next was the Papaya Salad (Tum Poo-Plara) it is Isan salad with fermented fish sauce and field crabs. Unfortunately, the taste was too pungent for our Americanized palate. The waiter incidentally over heard us and was kind enough to offer to replace with another salad called Tum Thai Kai Kem (spicy salad with salted egg). +1 star for that!

The fried Isan sausages (Sai Krok Isan) were simply epicurean. the grilled coconut marinated beef skewer (Moo Ping Kati Sod) with sticky rice on the side made our dinner sumptuous.

With top notch customer service and its inexpensiveness the competitors near by should really be worried.

Probably the best i-san (Northeastern Thai) food in the whole East Coast. I like almost everything we ordered.

The second time I was there I spot owners were discussing something. Later I learned that some of them came from the original location in Bangkok to QC the dishes. They come probably twice a year. Pretty neat!

I love this place! It's a little out of the way for me but worth the trip for authentic Somtum (green papaya salad). They make the somtum fresh to order, as spicy as you like (zero to four peppers). Somtum is supposed to be spicy - many mediocre Thai restaurants serve it mild (maybe because they are afraid Americans won't like it spicy) and it's pre-made, but not here. The version with field crabs was a little too intense for me, I prefer "Thai style" version with dried baby shrimps. I order my somtum with two peppers, one time I was a little bold and asked for 3 peppers and it was a little too hot. If you love spicy food, go for it! The Laab Moo (ground pork salad) is also delicious, as well as the fried chicken thigh. Atmosphere can be a little loud on weekend nights, but not too bad. This place ranks up there with Sripriphai and Zabb Elee for quality Thai food, although the menu is more specialized. If the only Thai food you've ever had is sweet noodle dishes (Pad Thai) and curries, this place will be an eye opener. Go with a few friends, order a variety of dishes and share everything family style (that's how it's done in Thailand).

There is something there to Somtum Der which opened a short time back to critical acclaim focusing on Isan / Issan cuisine of Northeast Thailand. Since I travel once or twice a year to Thailand I had to taste what the fuss was about.

Being in the East Village, the restaurant competes against a slew of Thai and Asian restaurants. Somtum Der has a cool trendy vibe, with a casual, almost communal atmosphere. 

The menu is huge and pictorial, so we let the waiter recommend items and we ate family-style, sharing dishes.

Isan food is typically very spicy with lots of chili heat. The three of us asked for medium spicy and it was plenty hot. The Pad Thai mun poo had crab meat and crab paste which was different from other Thai restaurants in NYC. The taste and texture of the noodle dish was excellent and probably my favorite of the evening. I was surprised since I rarely order Pad Thai.

The Isan pork sausages, sai krok, were delicious! These are staples on every table in Isan. The beef skewers marinated in coconut milk, Ngau ping kati sod, were tasty too.

The truly exotic dish we tried but couldn't eat was the fermented fish/field crab papaya salad, Tum poo plara (which the waiter did not pick). It was way too fishy and I haven't "acquired" a taste for it. The waiter was nice to switch it for a spicy papaya salad with salty egg, Tum Thai kai kem. That we finished!

Service was great and our waiter was always checking up on how we enjoyed the selections. He made us feel special even with a full house and a wait line. Wines and beers are reasonably priced although surprisingly they were out of Lao Beer.

We are coming back soon. There is so much more to taste! Its authenticity and complex flavors are worthy of the Michelin and Yelp acclaim.

My bf and I went to this restaurant last night and we were thoroughly pleased with the food and service. The pork skewers with noodles which was spicy and delicious and the shrimp and calamari with flat noodles was diving. The papaya salad was also great. I highly recommend this place!

This was a great experience.It helped to go with friends so we could try multiple small plates out. The flavors were so bright n fresh and we really enjoyed some very different thai food. The laarb took the cake as did the papaya salads and the soups. While i wasnt a fan of chicken on the bone in a soup.. The greens and flavors were just divine.
Best Thai restaurant in the US. I am from Thailand and after I have traveled to many cities in US and tried a lot of Thai restaurants. This one is the most delicious and authentic one.

I was drawn to this place by the flashy ambiance and colorful menu. Upon first glance, everything looked amazing, but I soon discovered that this is not the kind of thai food I am used to living in New York. Apparently, it's the cuisine of a particular region in Thailand, so don't expect the typical pad see ew or pad thai. I really didn't know what to order, and our server was pretty much non-existent, so I more or less arbitrarily ordered a Tum Thai Kai Kem, which was some sort of spicy papaya salad, along with some spring rolls and Nue Dad Dieo (deep-fried sun-dried beef). While there were some unique flavors, I would classify the food as decent at best. I'll take a decent pad thai over this any day.

We ordered a selection of the Asian 'sausages'. The cooked one was definitely the best. They did lack having a sauce for dip. The shrimp salad was good but wasn't much 'salad to it. The flat noodles with minced pork was excellent & best choice. 
The glass noodles with seafood was too spicy. We had asked for all dishes to be only '2 chilli' hot but this was too much in this dish. The papaya salad with picked crab was ok. It is a dish for those who have had it before as the flavour is very strong. 
The pork neck came with a very spicy sauce that overpowered the taste. 
The staff seemed a bit unclear when serving on how spicy our dishes were and we think they didn't follow our requests.

I guess eating 2 dinners is a typical thing in New York??? (ah, that's how they drink all night long).

After a couple of cocktails, at some hour where I usually head to bed (10? 1030?), my friend's bro and his friend took us here for a "second dinner".  Fine with me since my friend L and I ate a light dinner 2 hours prior.  Also, I was wearing stretchy pants (thank you lululemon) so why not.  I guess in your 30s, the wild thing to do is to eat dinner at 10pm! Woo!

They ordered this spicy shrimp dish and I took one bite and my mouth was on fire. Also the shrimps were raw.  Shudders.

Thankfully their delicious papaya salad and out of this world fried chicken more than made up for the awful shrimps.  The fried chicken is some of the best I've had, right up there with the kind from Addendum in Yountville.  The skin was crunchy without being oily and the meat was succulent, tender, juicy.  I think my waistline thanks me that I don't do this late night indulgent dining too often.

Bit pricey for sure ($70 for 2 fried chicken dishes, 1 papaya salad, 1 ground pork appetizer I didn't try, 1 eeky shrimp dish and 3 thai ice teas), but then again, you are in NYC where everything has some mystery 30% add on cost.

It's been a while since my last visit to EV. Yet again, another Thai dinner with friends. This time we were in a mood for something savory and spicy. Of course, the E-saan food came to mind. 

10-minute walk from 2av station on the F line, we arrived at Somtum Der. This place offers a wider range of Thai food, but mostly sticks to the dishes from the northeastern part of Thailand AKA E-saan. 

We started off with a very spicy Papaya Salad with Pickled Crabs and Fermented Fish Sauce. You need to order sticky rice to go with this, just to soak up all the juice. 

We were aware that we asked for 7 chilis, but, OMFG, our mouths were on fire. Yup, they delivered it, and it was friggin amazing! I swear it was hot to the point my head started to sweat. 5 stars!

Then came the next dish, Deep-Fried Chicken Thighs. This one was also perfect with the spicy dipping sauce -- a must-try.

I was a little disappointed with the Spicy Bamboo Shoot Salad as the bamboo shoots were supposed to be shredded into a long rope but were chopped in pieces instead; however, the taste was there. 

I also found that the beef in Grilled Marinated Beef with Grilled Rice Ball on Skewers was a little tough. Maybe we ordered that after we were almost stuffed. 

One more thing, they coulda offered more beer selection here, not just Singha and Beer Lao. 

I was happy with the meal after all. I definitely have to come back to try more stuff especially the spicy soups.

Tasty meals, affordable price, but small portions.

For my party of four, we ordered four items: Tum Thai Kai Kem (spicy papaya salad),  Beef Ping Kati Sod (skewers), Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (deep fried chick thigh), and Chef's Signature Wok-Fried Seafood Suki along with one order of sticky rice and one order of coconut rice. Don't get me wrong, each item was very, very tasty! However, to be complete full, we could have ordered a couple more items. I usually stick to my main dishes (Pad Thai, Pad Sew Ew and Panang Curry). I'm glad I got to try other Thai dishes here. The place is delicious! Just make sure to order two items per person to be full.

I haven't had authentic-tasting Thai food outside of eating over my Thai friend's house.  Dishes are a flavored with the perfect amount of herbs and spices - not over done.  Somtum Der is worth the trip to the E-Vill. The dishes are quite spicy and if you are sensitive like I am ask for 'very mild' as regular mild may still be too spicy.  Larb Moo is my favorite!

Everything here is pretty much solid. I love their black tea, their crab pad Thai (spicy!), I always get the sticky rice on sticks and the isan fried noodles with the grilled pork skewers. It's so flavorful and delicious! Their raw shrimp salad is insanely spicy- but amazing nonetheless if you can handle the fire. Generally, a lot of their dishes are a tad spicier than the typical westernized Thai spot so watch out! Somtum Der will always be a go-to for me. 

Delivery is also fast and packed nicely.

I'm so glad Somtum Der opened so close to me. The food here is divine. 
I've pretty much ordered everything here and they can do no wrong. I'm cambodian so their food is very comforting to me. It's Issan style thai, which is more similar to Cambodian food than traditional Thai. Their namesake, Somtum (aka green Papaya salad) is amazing. And very authentic. 
I highly recommend their Somtum (all are delicious!), grilled pork skewers, Larb (again, all are yummy), even the pad se ew is delicious. Try it!

Don't mean to come across as pretentious or anything, but as a one-time visitor of Thailand, I can 100% vouch for the authenticity of Somtum Der's food (I can just sense everyone's collective eye-roll from my comment).

My extremely worthy credentials aside, one glance at Somtum Der's menu will tell you everything you need to know about them.

Besides the classic staples, Som Tum (green papaya salad), Pad Thai, Pad See Ew (anything but ew), etc... the menu also carries a variety of other traditional dishes, ranging from larb (Laotian minced meat salad) to variations of khao (rice, mostly fried).  

Somtum Der does a masterful job of combining a variety of flavors and sauces, giving each dish a uniquely distinct taste and style. Due to this, and the fact that most of their entrees are either spicy or sour (with the exception of dessert of course), a lot of the food can be either hit or miss for people. If you're not particularly adventurous, I'd actually suggest sticking with what you know. 

Some things to note: Their fermented dishes use fish sauce, which gives it a slightly fishy (duh!) taste. I know that can be a turn off for some people, so consider yourself warned. 

Also, when they say something is spicy, they really mean it. Their dishes definitely pack a kick. 

The prices here are extremely fair, if not slightly cheap than other comparable Thai restaurants. 

If you're looking for an authentic meal with authentic tastes, then I highly recommend Somtum Der. If you're just looking for Pad Thai, then the flavors here might be a bit too much to handle here.

It's awesome! 
tips:
if u like spicy, order a medium spicy papaya salad! It would be spicy enough!
sausage is really nice, noodles with minced pork and seafood noodles are really nice! 
ice cream is kind of snow, not my favorite...
I would definitely come back! :)

For delicious authentic Thai food, Somtum Der is the place to go. They have a location in Bangkok that I've also had the opportunity to visit. There are a few differences in the menu, but for the most part it's the same, as is the food quality. You'll find a lot of spicy salads and meat dishes that you won't find in a typical Thai restaurant in the city. The perfect place to go if you're into spicy food (but in case you're not, they ask if spicy is ok when you order). A nice cozy, casual feel that pairs well with the food, and a mix of communal and private tables. I'd even venture to say this might be one of my favorite restaurants in the city. Especially recommend the spicy duck salad!

I cannot say enough good things about Somtum Der. 

Today, despite the weather outside being misty and disgusting, I went BY MYSELF so I could have the Tum Pla Too & Kao Mun for lunch. It's one of my favorite meals in NYC. The mackarel is crispy and delicious and the juice of the papaya salad and the fish combine to coat the rice, which is fragrant from the coconut milk. 

In the past, I have completely gorged myself on multiple orders of the fried chicken, the many larbs, and the milk soaked grilled pork skewers. Everything has been excellent, spicy and transcendental when washed down with Singha.

Also, today, they gave me a free Thai iced tea because they were sorry that my order was taking so long as they were changing out the oil to deep fry my mackerel. This was particularly nice given that I hadn't even noticed the wait time; I was busy being the weirdo lady eating by herself in a corner, engrossed in her book.

Dinner at Somtum Der while visiting NY this week. I really didn't know what to expect as the dishes are completely different than the average Thai restaurant. 

You will want to order family style - about 2 dishes per person depending on how hungry you are. But definitely get your own sticky rice!

We were a big group so I was lucky to try a lot of items. Here's what we ordered in order from favorite to least favorite:
- Papaya salad with salted egg - this was my favorite thing we ordered and I would 100% go back just for that dish. We ordered ours medium which was spicy but not mouth on fire spicy. (That came later)
- Grilled marinated beef - this was a close second for favorite of the night. Really tender and flavorful. Try it without the sauce before you add any spice. You might find it doesn't need it.
- Mushrooms and bell peppers - because we needed some vegetables to round out the meal and because it was the only thing we ordered that did have the word spicy in it.
- Deep fried chicken thigh - personal bias: I am not a huge fan of chicken skin but the inside was juicy. It had the same hot sauce as the beef and really added to the flavor. It's spicy, add it anyway.
- Prawn sashimi - SO spicy. My mouth was actually burning and I couldn't get the taste out no matter how much beer and sticky rice I consumed. 
- Catfish larb - despite the spiciness of the sashimi, this dish was my least favorite. The catfish had a ton of bones and there was just overall a weird texture to it.

By the end of the meal my mouth was on fire and my nose was running like Niagara Falls. Bring tissues. Wear waterproof mascara. Do not bring your date, boss, or anyone else you are trying to impress.

Service was very attentive.

Dinner at Somtum Der on December 25th was my version of 'Jews Eating Chinese Food on Christmas.' The reservation was relatively easy to get [7PM] though the restaurant filled up quickly as our meal progressed...or didn't [more on that later]. 

We started off with drinks, all of which are in the $8 to $9 price range. Honestly, I find this pretty incredible given the location and how big the cocktails actually are.

I don't remember the exact name of the drink I had. In fact, it was unmemorable. There were toasted rice seeds in it. They didn't add anything to the actual drink which was on the sweeter side. Once you finished, you were left with a whole bunch of seeds at the bottom of the glass. 

Tum Thai Kai Kem [$11]: This is the spicy papaya salad with salted egg. As others noted, everything at Somtum Der is s.p.i.c.y. The salad started off mild and refreshing and then the heat progressively built up. I didn't find much egg and what I did see of it, disintegrated into the dressing.  

Sa Poak Kai Tod Der [$8]: I was really excited to try the deep fried chicken. The pictures on the website look amazing but the dish was underwhelming in comparison. It came out lukewarm and not nearly as crispy as it should have. The sweet thai sauce on the side was tasty though.

Tom Saab Kradook On [$12]: At first I was skeptical about eating pork cartilage soup. Needless to say, this isn't the great description for a dish. In actuality, it was quite tasty minus how spicy it was. There were long pieces of pepper in it, bite into one and GAME OVER. I couldn't feel the tip of my tongue and my lips were on fire.

We passed on dessert. 

The service at Somtum Der is pretty horrendous. Maybe this was because it was a holiday, not sure. The spacing between courses was uneven. 

For example: we asked for change of a $20 bill. The server left to get said change, had said change in his hand, passed said change off to someone else who stood at the register for awhile. My friend was so fed up that she [who paid with credit card] took the bill to the server and had it taken care of this way. 

I spent about $35 for my portion of the meal, which isn't terrible. The portions are of decent size, and whatever you don't finish, you can wrap up to bring home.

If you want it Thai spicy - they'll make it for you. Just emphasize that you can handle it (and won't send food back for actually making it super spicy). This is my fave Manhattan Thai joint now!

Crispy leaf fish rice and grilled pork rice salad, grilled sticky rice are some of my favorites. Fri nights after 7 are crowded so I tend to prefer off hours.

We came for an early Sunday lunch. I think this food works for brunch, but the place was fairly empty. This is a good time to come.

A beeraquilla cocktail provided  some sweetness to offset the spice, my companions went for white wine and hot tea (a pot for an extra charge).

The papaya salad with salted egg started things off. I thought the spice level was perfect - we asked for medium.

Coconut rice took some of the edge off the spice effect of the salad.

Duck larb was a nice portion, milder than the salad I thought. A catfish soup tasted primarily of lemon grass and fish sauce, but contained a fibrous leaf as well- not sure if it was a kaffir lime leaf -this had a stem.

Fried chicken thighs were crisp and savory, did not even need the sauce.

The fried sausages were relatively mild, and not unlike kielbasa.

An order of beef skewers did not arrive at first, requiring a second request. They were delicious,  accompanied by little nests of rice noodle, but with the same standard dipping sauce as the thighs. However, the beef was a bit on the chewy side, and a small portion for the price.

Thai tea panna cotta was a winner as was taro in condensed coconut milk, a good choice for the dairy free diner.

It was very yummy, I got the papaya salad and the some grilled pork ( marinades in coconut milk ) 

I must confess thai food is not usually my thing but I was in the mood and this place is michelin recommended so have it a try.

It was very busy but then again it was Saturday 8 pm ! I liked the service also.

I def recommend it.

Issan thai food, friendly service, and cheap booze make this a very solid dinner out with friends! everything is pretty reasonably priced but somewhat small portions so you'll need to get several things to fill up. the grilled rice and side order of noodles can definitely help with that. 
we like the larbs a lot - my fav is the catfish. you cant go wrong with papaya salad. and the grilled skewers are a good bet too. i have tried a few entree noodle dishes and have never been very pleased with those orders so i would stick with the rice salads and meats.

Muy caliente. Wrong description of what is known to me as hot hot Thai food. Somtum Der is known for its thai chili dishes and they definitely are generous with large helpings of it. Be forewarn, the dishes are explosively spicy and although I can handle a decent amount, it still left me hurting the day after.

The highly recommended prawn and fried chicken thigh dishes are a must here. Both were satisfying to our tummies and the heat kept us wanting more. As a reminder, this is not your traditional Thai place to order Americanize pad thai and your level 1 spice curry. For once, try something authentic because Somtum Der is exactly that.
Really great Larb! I don't think you can go wrong with this menu :)

The best dish here is the fried chicken. The fried chicken alone gets this place 4 stars BUT the other dishes are not very good so I had to take it down to a 3. The fried chicken is ($8)- tender, juicy, delicious- potentially better than bonchon (korean fried chicken). I also got the pad thai (SUPER SPICY) and really dry ($15).


Lesson Learned:  get the fried chicken

Service is a little slow.

FOOOD AMAZING minus 2 stars for being over charged and having to explain myself, "uhh lai wah???"(WTF in Thai)  just becareful and look over your bill they over charged me then adjusted after explaining twice why is shouldnt be 330$ when all we had extra after the gilt city coupon was 4 drinks, 2 sides and 1 entree.  Took a lil bit of explaining.  Had to explain in Thai to the Thai guy. when the waiter was trying to explain to me how it was 330$.  Apology accepted looks like a honest mistake.
Legit authentic Thai dishes which are rare in Manhattan. Prices are decent considering the location. Definitely will be back to visit this place when we have a craving for great Thai food.

Sorry to be the hater here, but this was one of the worst meals I have had in New York. 

I ordered the soft broiled prawn with herbs and veggies and it was so spicy, I took one bite and couldn't even eat the rest because my mouth and throat felt like I had just consumed lava. I am not shy about spicy food either; I use red pepper flakes in just about all of the dishes I cook, but this dish looked and tasted like it had been cooked in an entire container of red pepper flakes. Sorry, but I like to taste my food when I eat and that was not possible with this dish.

On the bright side, I got the food to go, went to a bodega and got a can of coconut milk, which I prompted recooked the food in, then poured it over quinoa. So. Much. Better. Still spicy AF, but at least edible. 

Would never go back to this restaurant unless I had sprayed my mouth with liquid nitrogen in preparation.

I thought I was a champ when it came to spicy foods, but Somtom Der definitely won this round. However, it's the kind of spicy where the food is so delicious that you keep eating anyway, despite your burning palate and the sweat on your brow.  I loved the larb and the fried chicken.

I didn't feel so hot the following day, but I'll chalk that up to my own overzealous appetite. Next time I'll dial it back a bit and order more sticky rice.
Definitely get the duck larb, fried chicken, coconut rice and grilled pork.

Good, spicy Thai for when you're tired of your corner take-away spot.

Somtum Der has a pretty simple menu, lots of spicy larb/salads, some soups, some fried rice, a few variations on your corner take-away staples and a few specialties.  Most folks dining when I did seemed to get a Fred rice and noodle dish like they would those corner Thai shops in every neighborhood of New York.  Those are good at Somtum Der, but the wrong things to order by themselves. There are probably seven different spicy papaya salads, and another page of pork, fish and beef salads.  Get one of those.  The papaya salad with field crab is very spicy, seemed fermented like a kimchi, and was delicious.  The catfish soup is also great, a spicy fish stock with leafy vegetables, lots of straw mushrooms, some inedible ginger bits and extra crispy pieces of catfish.  The pad Thai with crab is about what it sounds like, but spicier, and might renew your appreciation for pan fried noodles.  Just be sure to try something else while you're at it.

That was one satisfying lunch this afternoon.  My buddy and I came armed with a Gilt City deal: $19 for one salad/larb and two entrees - saved us almost 50%.  The first thing I noticed was the superb decor and atmosphere of the place - high ceilings, clean, modern lines and the air won't leave you smelling like food for the rest of the day.  Plenty of tables and space - however, I would still make a reservation via OpenTable just to be safe.

Our waitress was very nice and helpful with our understanding of what we could order and what the spice levels were of each.

For our appetizer, we both shared the spicy duck larb - this was amazing.  It was very similar, if not better, than the Isan larb I had at one of the famous Isan restaurants in Bangkok.  The tangy, perfectly spicy marinade was spot on and the cilantro, scallions, and red onions totally gave me the "umami" moment.  Love this dish - will come back a million times for this.  Novices be warned, the pieces of duck meat in this aren't necessarily the fleshy part you're familiar with - there's liver and all sorts of goodies that authentic Thai cuisine would have in it.

For our entrees, we both got the pad thai.  Now, I NEVER EVER order pad thai at any Thai restaurant - EVER.  It's boring and tasteless, in my opinion.  However, the special crab pad thai here really captivated my attention what with all it's crabby goodness.  When I asked the waitress if I could get spicy sauce on the side, she told me that it was already pretty spicy (which I didn't believe, since these Thai restaurants like to downplay 'spicy' sometimes).  It came, and I was beyond impressed.  Best pad thai I've ever had.  The crab pieces were plump (though not much in quantity) and the sauce was ACTUALLY pretty spicy - the perfect burn, actually, and had tons of little crab tidbits in it.  This was enjoyable for the both of us and we agreed that it's definitely not your average pad thai.

Give Somtum Der a try if you're looking for some legitimate, non-boring Isan Thai cuisine.

Somtum Der has some truly authentic tasting Thai food, but a word to the wise: THE SPICE WILL BLOW YOU MOUTH UP!  I'm not kidding.  My girlfriend and I loved our meal, but we had to take several breaks to regain our composure.  So if you can brave the spicy adventure that lay ahead, then definitely give this place a try!

We ordered the papaya salad, fried chicken thighs, pad see yew with pork and basil, and the minced pork salad.  All of these dishes were delicious, but the pad see yew took the cake.  They also whipped up a delicious lychee martini that I shamelessly downed in three gulps.  I will be returning soon, once my mouth has fully recovered.

I was craving a taste of home...and in my quest to find this in New York thus far...have yet to find it. I really should just learn to make some of these things, but too much work and New York is supposed to have everything after all. This was on the list for best Thai food, I just haven't been so I finally made my way...at the start of a winter storm...a little bit of snow never hurt anyone.

The decor is nice...it's clean looking, wooden tables...and nice som tum station where the bar is (which is kind of cool). It's open, but small, but not crowded (room to walk between tables), which is nice.

Really, let's just get down to the food (because that's why I'm really here):
Tum Poo-Plara (Isan payaya salad with field crab) - it was good, a little on the fishier side (but it's supposed to be). Great level of spice with a slow to build burn. I would probably try their other somtums next time. It was good, great event, but didn't quite hit the spot.

Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (fried chicken thigh) - made multiple fried chicken list, but honestly, I wasn't impressed and probably wouldn't order it again. It was good, but not really anything special for me. Wasn't exactly what I was expecting. Chicken was very moist and not insanely heavy, but was a bit greasy...

Larb Ped (duck salad) - this hit the spice level I was looking for (we got for chilies = nose running)...my friend, on the other hand, was dying a bit. It was good. All the right flavors...a lot of onion...almost a bit too much, but oh so good. I'd definitely get this again.

Sticky Rice - sticky rice is sticky rice...and it's $3 for a personal serving. I call it a personal serving because if you grew up eating it...1 order is the amount (or a little short of) for one person to eat with the food you order.

TLDR: definitely check this place out. Great food, pretty decent prices. Portion sizes look small, but are actually pretty good especially if you order "recommended combinations" for two people...for one person it might be a bit more food than you want.
Wow never had such authentic thai food before! Amazeballs.

HALLELUJAH!! First off let me start off by saying I am from California and I am Lao,( that should explain about from there) hahaha. I always enjoy me some authentic Thai food since it's very similar to Lao cuisine. This is my go to spot every time I crave for something SPICY/SOUR. The papaya salad w/ fermented crab is hands down the best papaya salad I've ever had in NYC! Believe me, growing up in a Lao family and having a little taste of home is simply amazing! 

My friend and I ordered: 
*Somtum Der platter: papaya salad, vermicelli noodles, pork grinds, butterfly shrimp, pork loaf, etc. all that goodness in one plate. BEST CONCOCTION EVER!!! (Can always modify how spicy you want the papaya salad I like mine with 7 peppers) 

*Chicken soup: Basic sour chicken soup, but still very yummy. 

*Grilled beef: This was my least favorite, beef was a tad bit dry, but not bad. Beef came with a spicy dipping sauce and grilled sticky rice.

Service is great, cute and cozy place, cannot wait to go back!!

This is my Thai girlfriend's favorite Thai restaurant in the city and we finally made it out to sample all the food. This place is NYC trendy inside, with beautifully presented food, with 100% authentic thai taste. A word of caution: with all that flavor comes some serious spice! She ordered the table a plethora of dishes. There wasn't one dish that wasn't amazing, but I'm only going to list my absolute favorites here:

- Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (Der-Style Deep-Fried Chicken Thigh). Crispy, juicy magic.
- Moo Rong Hai Der & Khao Ji (House Special Grilled Marinated Pork)
- Pad Ki Mao Pork & Basil (Spicy flat rice noodles wok-fried with ground pork and crispy basil leaves)

I want to go back and try everything on the menu! Great for dates or for large groups! They take large group reservations and have terrific service.
Papaya salad (somtum) is so magical, you find yourself eating more despite the tears from they spiciness.

Seriously authentic thai food! In love. Was recommended by friends who are also from Thailand. Had pad kra pao and somtam. Wish they didn't fry the pad kra pao contents together with the rice though. Would be more authentic looking and definitely not hot enough though most wouldn't be able to handle that level of hotness. Nevertheless, it's real thai food.

Very mediocre. Ordered the basil fried rice with beef and chicken soup. The rice seemed like it was days old and the soup had more bones in it than chicken. Overall, very disappointed with the meal. I would consider going elsewhere.

Authentic Thai northeastern food, my friends & l went there to celebrate my birthday. We had a great time; the food was amazing & the service was great. It's not easy to find good authentic Thai food in the city, highly recommended..

Holy.cow. This place is amazing. After seeing the name of the restaurant I was already excited, papaya salad might be one of my favorite dishes ever. I bookmarked it like I did every other restaurant that I found but after stumbling across a deal via Gilt City I had no excuse to stay away. For $19 we purchased the lunch special that included an appetizer and two entrees. 

Do yourself a favor a look through the menu - I mean really read through it they do a great job of telling the Somtum Der story. Their cuisine draws its inspiration from from the Isan region, stemming from Northeastern Thailand nestled between Laos and Cambodia. They boast of a simple presentation with healthy ingredients on the spicy side. Following with Isan culture, the dishes are meant to be placed in the middle of the table to be shared throughout the meal.  

With that being said, Somtum Der is not your typical Thai place with the normal options of curry and tom yum soup. They have a wide array of unique dishes: many Somtum (papaya salad) selections served in many styles such as different meats and seafood options, a deep fried selection of different meats and rolls, grilled meats, hearty soups, Larbs (spicy salads) and a selection of rice and noodle dishes. It took me a while to narrow down on what I wanted - honestly I spent more time trying to determine what Somtum I wanted. We couldn't decide so we chose the Tum Thai Kai Kem (Spicy Papaya Salad with Salted Egg) and the Tum Poo - Plara (Papaya Salad with Fish Sauce and Fermented Crab). They were both extremely different and delicious in every way.

The Salted Egg Papaya Salad was topped with crunchy green beans, salted duck eggs, tomatoes and chopped peanuts. It had a mild flavor, with saltiness from the eggs and sweetened lime base. My only critique is that there was more of the egg white then the yolk of the egg (for the record - the BEST part of the egg). The Fermented Crab Salad was my absolute favorite dish. The sauce had a fish sauce base and fermented crab base creating a pungent flavor mixed with the slight flavor of the Thai eggplant. The crunchy texture of the papaya pieces were offset by the soft tomatoes and eggplant pieces. Fore warning - when they say their food is spicy they mean it! We requested no chilis in our salad and yet our noses were runny from the heat. Sorry to be graphic but I'm trying to paint a picture here. 

For the two entrees, we played it safe and ordered our usual Pad Thai dish and the Pad See Eiw, only these dishes were all different. The Pad Thai Muin Poo had a crab paste base and crab meat infused throughout the dish. I only got a few bites but I found it a bit drier than other Pad Thai dishes I've had. The Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Taiay was amazing. The rice noodles were tossed in a delicious light gravy alongside a generous proportion of calamari and plump shrimp. The soy sauce flavor wasn't overwhelming and had a subtly sweet aftertaste and a slight pepper undertone. Also, there was an occasional fermented soy bean mixed allowing for a slight salty piece here and there. 

As I was leaving I noticed some glass jars filled with palm sugars, sesame seeds and other ingredients for Thai dishes. Made my heart happy that I wasn't eating food out of a jar.

Authentic and delicious!  I am not Thai but was there for a month and fell in love with the food (the real Thai food, not typical American Thai).  I feel lucky to have this place in the neighborhood - if you have any sense of adventure (and can handle spicy food), give this place a try.

Loved it - great food, great atmosphere! felt like I was in Bangkok once again! I will definitely go back.  
I had a Gilt voucher for 4 and was able to eat there with just another friend.  we took the other 2 dishes home.  They didn't fuss, never complained and I was very grateful that it went so smoothly.  The house white wine was good and paired nicely with the spicy food we had.  I highly  recommend the sticky rice on a stick (lol)! it was delicious, slightly sweet and chewy and paired up really nicely with the spicy food.
Sitting can get a little tricky because it all feels like a huge communal table but again, I enjoy this time of place.
Might not be the location for a romantic first date, but definitely worth it for a casual evening out.
Go, eat, have fun....remember it's spicy.
Oh and try the fried chicken....amazeballs!!

Disclaimer: I'm not a fan of spicy foods. I can't handle the heat and my nose starts running like Usain Bolt.

This food is SPICY! I think they go on a scale of one chili to four. I could not handle even zero chili peppers.

The menu notes the spicy foods, which is handy. The pad thai had no chili peppers on the menu, but I couldn't even really handle that without drinking lots of water. I told our server this and he laughed cause he didn't believe it was spicy. Very endearing.

If the food isn't spicy, then it's probably sweet. The grilled sticky rice is very sweet.

My favorite dish was probably the side order of noodles. It wasn't spicy and it wasn't sweet. It was seasoned well and the noodles had a nice chew to them.

The fried chicken thigh was very ordinary. The fried appetizers were also average.

Overall, it's a nice space with friendly servers. Just make sure you know what you're ordering and know what level of spice you can handle.

The prawn sashimi is the best, super spicy too! Thai Iced Tea isn't too sweet and I went through mine pretty quickly. 

Other mentionables are the spicy pork eggrolls (very spicy) and papaya salad (not spicy). The Tom Yum soup as a bit too sour for me.

I was excited to come here on a Friday night because I love Zabb Elee, and this place looked a bit cooler. Overall, the food was good, while the service and drinks were lacking. 

We ordered our drinks before looking at the food menu. I got the citrus cocktail because it had lime in it, which I love, and they use so much lime in the dishes, so I thought it would match nicely.

It took us a while to flag down the waitress again, but for food we ordered the larb ped, the original styled papaya salad and the pork spring rolls. The larb was at the upper level of my tolerance for spice, but still delicious. The spring rolls were filled with minced pork and I really enjoyed them too. The papaya salad was not as tasty as I have had before, and I would skip next time. It is possible that by the time I reached them I had burned off my taste buds.

Unfortunately, I received my drink after we got two of our dishes. I watched it sit at the bar while drinks made after mine were served to other tables. When I finally got the drink it tasted very chemically, like that fake lime juice. This was really disappointing because as I have already mentioned, they use lime in so many of their dishes! Why not spare a lime for a drink!

It definitely seemed to service a student crowd, because it was very cheap and the ambiance was pretty hectic and loud. If I were a student, I would probably have loved this place, but unfortunately I am now old and boring, so I will probably not return.

I went to this place because it is listed as one of the top ten Thai restaurants in NYC. But beware for all those pad thai and crab rangoon lovers, this is a THAI restaurant, this is not Thai American. I like spicy and this place is spicy, really really spicy. Also,everything is really big, we could not eat an appetizer and entree per person, that was too much. The fried chicken was forgettable, the papaya salad was spicy and really yummy. We got a fried rice that had ground beef and did not like that at all. It was the spiciest of all. I got seafood noodles which were really yummy. The desserts are also more authentic Thai. The coconut milk dessert is warm, so beware if you want something cold. The dessert that is black ( dont remember name) is good and not too sweet. This place was completely empty at 5:00 pm on a Thursday. Not sure about other days. I probably wont come back because there are more Thai options that are better.

Food was very tasty and authentic.

However, the service was rather slow on a lazy Sunday evening.

Will definitely return to re-taste the marinated pork skewers.

Overall, a good experience, and I'll happily come here again. That said, I was somewhat disappointed by their signature green papya salad dish. The version we ordered (Der style) had rice noodles in it. Not sure if that is typical of all their papya salads or of Isaan cuisine, but I felt that they added nothing to the dish and I would have rather had more papaya. 

Other dishes were much more impressive. The dried beef was tasty, and I really liked the fried kaffir lime leaves they used as garnish. The grilled sticky rice was the perfect foil for the spiciness of the other dishes. The pad kee mao seemed a bit bland after the more assertive dishes but the texture of the noodles and of the pork was perfect.

The standout dish, however, was the mushroom larb. It had a healthy kick of chili balanced by the crunch of the roasted rice and freshness of the herbs. Great dish, especially considering the relative paucity of veggies on the menu.

When I think of thai food, I think of pad thai, drunken noodles, the sweet curries, and the stir fried meats with various vegetables. This is what you usually get when you go to a thai restaurant.

Yet somtum der offers something different. Their menu has different things. It's a specific style of thai food, from some northern region. 

I tried their papaya salad with salted egg and a fried rice dish with some kind of fish. The food was delicious, beyond anything that I've ever had at other thai restaurants. In fact, I usually don't like thai food or thai restaurants, but this place... I like a lot. I'm actually going to come back here, again and again.

Good job somtum der.

Average thai food. Lots of space.
I'm not that much into spicy food and all their dishes are spicy, albeit they say they can tone it down.
STD is so wonderful.  Some of the best Thai I've had.  The fried chicken was juicy and the noodle dishes were all top notch.

Located in the East Village, this Thai restaurant comes highly recommended. 

It's decor is warm with lots of wood and great lighting. Seating is ample with bar, family-style seating in the middle of the restaurant. 

Food was flavorful and the service was great. When I expressed an allergy, our server made sure it wasn't in any of our dishes. We went a few rounds of selecting, checking, and informing to make sure that there wasn't any allergic reaction served with dinner. 

Medium spicy level is quite spicy so beware. However, if you like a good spice and some Thai food, come here. You won't be let down. As a note, the coconut rice is amazing and really helped cool my mouth down after a spicy bite.
We tried it based on the positive reviews but we were incredibly disappointed by the food and the service.

Great place! A change from the usual Thai menus, this place makes dishes specifically from the Isan region and the menu has pictures for each dish which was definitely helpful!
