I had the Crab pad thai which was great, more spicy than I expected though so maybe ask before ordering if you're sensitive. I would definitely go back.

My Thai food bar is so high it actually handicaps me with any new Thai restaurant I try. 
My North Hollywood neighborhood Thai gem is so good its impossible to for me to give a place like Somtum Der in New Yorks east village the five stars it probably deserves. 
That is a problem but what can I do?
The food here is excellently executed and the service is fantastic. They have a full bar and mix a mean martini.
The menu has the Thai standard along with some very cool specials. 

My wife and I really enjoyed our dinner, but the comparisons to our go to place in North Hollywood hung over our table like a cloud. But four stars is still a very good rating even though it probably deserved five?

I'm very happy I found this great Thai spot hidden in the LES. Amazing food, decent portions and chill ambiance. I had the Tum Thai and Larb Moo, which I asked to make very spicy because that's the way I like it, and they both came out deliciously hot! Will definitely go back to try other menu items!

I asked a Thai waiter in a high end restaurant in New York City for recommendation to a REAL THAI restaurant. She suggested SOMTUM DER. I live in Toronto, Canada and have been craving for REAL THAI food for a long time. SOMTUM DER fulfilled my cravings today with glorious marks. This East Village eatery makes you feel at home no sooner you arrive. They welcome you with folded hands and seat you with all courtesies. Genuinely Thai. The cuisine is North Eastern Thai, means no curries. 
We ordered Papaya Salad as an appetizer. It was heavenly with the freshest raw Papaya taste with a sweet and sour dressing. The fish sauce perfectly balanced the dressing. 

Now on to the main course. We ordered seafood Suki, a stir fried preparation of the freshest seafood and straw mushrooms topped with rice vermicelli. The mushrooms stole the show both in terms of taste and the visual. The sticky rice presented in the shape of ice lolly with the paddle is unique. The presentation caught my attention but the taste left a pleasant memory. 

We enjoyed our meal with a Laotian beer branded BEER LAO. It brought back memories of our visit to Luang Prabang in Laos. 

We will return to SOMTUM DER soon.

Suresh Chawla
Toronto, Canada

Pretty authentic and reasonably priced food. One sign of good service is the refill of water, they were on top of it. 

One watch out is if you don't eat spicy and if you have a kid maybe not the best place but if those aren't conditions this is a good place for a reasonably priced meal.
I though is real deal, there are much better and authentic  Thai Restaurant  out there

Simply some of the best Thai food I've ever had. The duck larb woosen (with glass noodles) was outstanding - deeply flavorful, complex, delicious textures, searingly spicy... It was addictive and memorable and phenomenal. The best larb I've ever had.

The green papaya salad with mackerel was also incredible - the mackerel was salty, flavorful, and a great texture. It went really well with the salad, too, which was spicy, sweet, and refreshing.

To finish, the Thai iced tea panna cotta was superb and unique, but delicate.

My meal at Somtum Der left me giddy, and I can't wait to come back.

Authentic Thai food!! Only down side is that the dishes are tapas size and they can get pricy. But we ordered an order of everything practically and it was filling for four people. Good was tasty and spicy and flavorful. You can ask to lower the spice level, if you'd like.

Went here with my bf last saturday night. The wait for a table was ~20mins so we just sat at the bar. 5 mins later, a table opened up so they moved us over. sweet! +1 star

I wanted this meal to be so much better than it was. The menu looked FANTASTIC! I was so excited! They went into detail about their authentic cuisine and explained every item beautifully +1star

I started out my meal with the thai iced tea. Milky and delicious. A little on the sweet side, but I enjoyed it!

Then the entire meal went downhill. As an app, we had the papaya salad (note: I LOVE PAPAYA SALAD). I wanted it medium spicy, but my boyfriend was afraid of the spice so we got it with just 1 chili pepper. Thank god we did this, because it was SO SPICY it burned off my entire palate! I am Indian so I am very used to spicy food, so this was just so surprising! I think they may have gotten our order wrong! 

The rest of the meal was just meh, especially because I couldn't taste anything after. We got:
1) pad thai (with 2 chili peppers - wasn't as spicy as the papaya salad - maybe because the peppers were cooked?) - this was actually a relief after the spice of the papaya salad
2) Pork skewers with coconut milk - again just meh - we originally wanted the beef skewers, but they ran out of beef
3) Beef basil fried rice - this was good, but was really greasy, and there was barely any beef in it.

I might try this place again only because I really really really wanted to love it, but I definitely wouldn't go out of my way to go there again.

Nice decor when we walked in. No greeting for awhile and it was only 3 tables. Now for the food. If you have been to Eastern Thailand, the food are close (slightly sweet). Appetizers are awesome. A big note for first timer, please be careful when you are ordering spicy. Thais don't play around when it comes to spicy.

Also, check out the back of their menu, they have some  combination for you to try first.
Waited over half an hour for a flavorless plate of rice that ran 15 and lacked any moisture whatsoever. It was like eating sand.

Ordered the Thai fried rice with crispy leaf fish for lunch. When they say its spicy, beware because it is spicy!!! The fried rice was too dried, the fish was extra crispy, together the dish was just too dry. Although the dish did have flavor and the heat gives it a nice kick. It also came with the coconut sticky rice which in my opinion tasted good. I'll have to try their other items to see.

Get their pad Thai if you like chewing on crab shells, and if you like a 2:1 sauce to noodle ratio. Their coconut rice has the faintest (almost nonexistent) hint of coconut in it, I don't see the point of calling it coconut rice. I also do not see how they've "mastered gastronomy" as their menu says. Most of their menu comprises of fusion foods and to top it off their staff seems to give off a condescending attitude when you point out there's bugs in the restaurant. Don't be fooled by their nice decor and the long essays on their menu, it's just a mediocre restaurant for what it's worth.
Had the Khao Moo Tod Kratiam Prik Thai. Service was fast. Food was great- mildly spicy. They constantly had my glass of water filled up, which is nice on this hot New York Day. In and out in 30 min.

One of my friends only comes here for Thai food in the city, and no where else. While I'm not as selective as him, I will say that this is my favorite Thai restaurant in the city. I haven't had a bad dish here, though some are better than others (the shrimp sashimi is delish).

If you have to wait for a table, go enjoy a libation at Amor y Amargo around the corner. Don't worry about getting too drunk - the spice will sober you up very quickly :)

I've probably been here at least once a month over the last 3-4 months and it just doesn't get any better than Somtum Der. Food is consistently delicious, and they miraculously ALWAYS have space for groups (10+) for walk-ins. Service is fast (don't want to be hangry!) and when you order family style, it's surprisingly cheap (budget-friendly!).

It's a decent place. It's nice you can sit near the window and watch people go by. The view isn't very nice. The food is pretty good. I always get Thai Iced Tea and it frustrated me that the glass was 90% full of ice. I mean this is already one of the most profitable items on a Thai restaurants menu and they can barely give me three sips of Thai Iced Tea. Frustrating.

Damn, this was good. Tried several dishes and everything was awesome. Fantastic flavors.

Service could have been better - took a while for someone to approach. It was also really hot in here. 

Beer - they had Singha & Beerlao.

Watch out for spice - they don't mess around.

This place is AMAZING. Authentic Thai food! My Thai friend took me here and even she was amazed how good the food is. I don't remember the names of the dishes, there is a fried rice with crispy fish, my favorite! And the shaved ice is great. Just order anything, everything here is delicious.
Amazing. Got the fish and papaya salad. Been dreaming of coming back.

I give two star because of foods, especially papaya salad. I like salad and some Foods actually good but it's not enough for some dish 11$. Nice decoration but I don't feel like  the restroom, there!!!! it like be high your table. Which when you open the door we can see you walk out the restroom from our table and I feel bad to say some of stuff who act nice but some bad service for me.

This was my second time dining at Somtum Der. After having been to Thailand recently and eating authentic Thai food, most american Thai places seem dull in comparison but Somtum Der is as close to authentic Thai as it gets. 

My favorites are the pork skewers, fried chicken and papaya salad. Must try!

Never knew what isan Thai food was until a friend explained that its the polar opposite of " regular " Thai food and when they say spicy, they really mean it.

Been here twice now and the dishes we got have all been incredible and diverse:
1. Fried chicken: like everyone says this is wonderfully crispy on the outside and tender and juicy on the inside. Like me.
2. Mackerel papaya salad was really good. It's such a different type of cuisine: papaya salad, greens and hunks of marinated mackerel and super fresh herbs. Delicious but be prepared to have your breath smell like fish all day.
3. Catfish salad. This is my favorite dish so far. Crispy pieces of catfish doused in flavor popping cilantro with rice and fresh greens. I love Louisiana style catfish and this dish took that to a whole other level, highly recommend this
4. Grilled sticky rice was nice, it helps offset the spicyness of the food if it's a little too hot to handle 

There's a whole other section of the menu with noodles and grilled meats, but I'm just too curious about trying all these awesome northern thai dishes that I'm not sure I can bring myself to get the pad Thai  or any other of the noodle dishes which I hear is awesome.

The service here is also fantastic, it's crazy how happy, nice and attentive service really makes a difference in your experience. The decor here is really cool as well, bamboo everywhere and nice lighting tho from the outside this place looks like nothing special.

All in all, highly recommend this place for everything: food, service, ambiance and price.

Late at night on a Friday goes hand in hand with wild cravings. Thankfully Somtum Der was nearby with it's large selection of food that isn't quite the traditional Thai items you'd expect. 

Ordered the Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (fried chicken thigh, $8) and a can of Thai beer ($6). Nicely breaded chicken that was juicy on the inside. Very well prepared and perfect meal after several drinks. Friends got the drunken noodle and a beef dish respectively that was also solid. Best part of all, between the 3 of us the meal came out to be around $40. Very inexpensive for such a meal.

Place seems to be pretty popular at night (service is fast though), so want to try out during the day.

The restaurant was authentic, delicious and really well priced! The staff are really nice and helpful in letting us understand the menu and helping us with decisions. Highly suggest getting the grilled stickey rice and the marinated grilled pork. 

Its a great restaurant to take friends too and share a big "family style" meal. I cant wait to go back!

excellent. from the outside, doesn't look like much. once inside though, it is an airy, professionally designed spot with light wood abound, splashes of red, and oversized supply jars- which both look cool and are actually used to make the delicious papaya salads. one half of the dining room has a long bar, part of it dedicated to a very creative cocktail list, and the other part to making their many variations on the signature thai papaya salad (including the classic). 

recommended order: 
classic papaya salad- 2 peppers on their spice scale is sufficient for some zing but no numbness
duck salad (larb ped)
fried chicken thighs
pad ki mao pork basil (amazing wide noodles)

this will be another regular spot for me. 

also, do not miss the happy hour until 7pm weekdays- good glasses of wine are $3!!!!!

I have a long standing love affair with garlic. Any cuisine from any part of the world that celebrates its use, I am down to try. I've always loved the way Thai cooking makes use of this magical bulb. When a good friend mentioned Somtum Der as being neck in neck with Pok Pok in authenticity, I knew I had to go. 

We ordered pork skewers oozing garlic, chillies and delectable fat. They were tempered by tiny puffs of coconut infused vermicelli. It was such a brilliant combination of flavors and despite the tender, richness of the meat, surprisingly light. The garlic fried beef and pork slices were a little tougher and not quite as garlic-y as I was expecting, but very satisfying. Rounding out the meal was a flat noodle dish with seafood and pork that was super sour and savory. What I found utterly amazing was that neither of us felt heavy even after eating a ton of animal protein fried in copious garlic. I didn't even have garlic breath afterward. What is this alchemy???

Once the humidity dies down, I plan to brave my other love - spice. I've been warned about the heat level of the Larb dishes...my tummy says, "Bring it!!"

This place is absolutely amazing, I was in yelp looking up different places to eat in NewYork and found the gem. Me being from Laos definitely wanted to taste something from home away from home.  Service was great, quick and attentive. Also them serving "beerlao" was definitely a plus. Place decor was beautiful real modern and creative.

It was a Friday night and I picked the venue for a double date. 

Stakes were high, so I went with Thai. Somtum Der boasted an authentic variety of dishes, and I needed to show off my good taste (aka satisfy my own cravings for delicious Asian food). The ambience was just right with a full house and perfect mood lighting. I was already dreaming of larb and fried chicken, but I asked the server for recommendations just in case. He pointed to pretty much every dish on the menu... And holy schmokes he was probably right.

The duck larb salad was so flavorful with the perfect spicy kick.

Fried chicken thighs are a MUST with the chili fish sauce for dipping. I swear I could swim in that stuff. Crispy on the outside, and juicy tenderness on the inside.

My bottomless pit of a stomach still had room to sample some of my friend's pad thai as well. It was a spicier take on your typical pad thai, but I would rather have the opportunity to sample all of the other dishes on the menu that you wouldn't find at other Thai food joints.

Another one for my mental list of "Best East Village Eats."

Unfortunately the delivery service leaves a lot to be desired. Two hour wait for a meal that was supposed to be 30min wait. Disappointing as the food is solid. But the delivery time is too variable. Not again.

I came to this restaurant for my friends farewell party. They got mixed up with the orders and they were blaming on me for not being clear, but I repeat my order in the end and he reviewed as well. They never gave a folk and spoon when I asked, and when I asked for water they ignored. I wasn't rushing but after missed order they stared to ignore our table. Food was way too salty, there is many better Thai restaurants. I only wish staffs were nicer. I would give 0 star if i can.

I was looking forward to authentic thai, what I got instead was a severe bought of gastrointestinal distress. My friend and I ordered the papaya salad with crab, the fried chicken, and the pad kee mao. The fried chicken was a standout, and the noodles were well done. But... the crab was obviously not fresh, and it was unlike the version I had in Queens which came with large portions of crab. The crab here was spindly with no crab meat. Both my friend and I got sick immediately afterwards. I wouldn't hazard coming back here again.

Easily my favorite Thai restaurant in East Village.  Focusing on the regional cuisine of Northeastern Thailand, Somtum Der doesn't have the ubiquitous pad thais and the like, but instead offers an interesting menu of a wide variety of dishes.  Some of the stand-out dishes are the papaya salad (in various different versions), the minced duck salad, fried rice with pork/basil, and last but not least the spring rolls - some of the best I've ever head.  Most of these dishes are super spicy, and absolutely delicious.  Most days you can wash them down with Beer Lao (IMHO, a better choice than any of the Thai beers).  So, why not five stars?  Service and delivery, while generally good, slips up every once in a while.

A thai friend brought me to this restaurant and claimed that it was one of the most authentic thai food he found in NYC. We ordered more than the normal Pad Thai and Green Curry and all the dish were really delicious. This was a good dinner to taste the southern thai cuisine.
Delicious and fresh. Not the usual thie I'm used to. Different recipes. Definitely a place to come back!
The Crab Pad Thai is the best Pad Thai I've had in New York and I've had lots. Favorite was Soho Thai (Thai Angel) until now.

This is my new favorite thai place. I just got back from thailand and my thai friend had recommended this place. This is the most authentic thai food I've had in NY. 

The place was very modern and open. I sat at a bench like table which was not ideal because there is no back support. The menu is kinda confusing because they have combos but those are just suggestions of what to eat what with, not a price discount. What is nice is that there are pictures with all the menu items. 

I ended up getting the beef with coconut rice, spring rolls, and spicy pork salad. DELICIOUS. Highly reccomend the coconut rice. It was so different coming on a stick and thick. The beef was so so good as well. Very well seasoned, cooked perfectly and came with a yummy sauce. The spicy pork salad had a kick and the ingredients were fresh and refreshing. 

The only reason I can't give it 5 stars is because of the service. It felt like there were no waiters and when I'd ask a question they didnt really understand my questions. Friendly none the less but it took forever to order and get the check. 

But I can't wait to go back for the food!

Somtum Der was so damn good, I went there for lunch two days in a row the last time I hit the city. I'm a huge fan of Isan style Thai cuisine, and they did not disappoint.  

The Good:
Food was excellent.  Well prepared, well presented, and simply delicious.  For me, the standout was the Pad Kee Mao with ground pork.  It's one of the best I've had.  We also ordered Larb Tod (really delicious fried balls of spicy pork mince), Coconut milk marinated pork skewers (so tasty and tender with deep flavor), Grilled marinated beef with a chili sauce, and grilled sticky rice (so good, and infused with coconut flavor).  Service was outstanding -- very friendly and willing to discuss how things were prepared.  

The Bad:
It's not cheap.  Really, it is kind of expensive.  This is very simple fare and the costs were pretty high all things considered.  

The Ugly:
I spilled my water.  They have these tall, narrow glasses and my arm kept knocking into 'em.  Those glasses gotta go!

I strongly considered giving this place five stars.  And I hope to give them the chance next time I stop in.

BEST somtum I've ever had in a restaurant! I come from a strong traditional Laotian background and whenever I go to a Thai restaurant to order somtum (I call it thum muk hoong and in English they call it spicy papaya salad) I ask to make it extra spicy and Laos style. When I showed up here earlier for lunch this afternoon there was no need to mention Laos style. 

I ordered the somtum with marinated sliced pork and I was in love! they made it the perfect amount of spicy and the server was so sweet! 

It has always been my favorite dish growing up and I make it at home from time to time, but this one tasted just like my fathers recipe. I look forward to coming back as this is a restaurant like no other.  Very authentic and classy yet affordable. 

I could go on all day, but I shouldn't. 
Please enjoy!

Hands down, Somtum Der has the best North Eastern Thai Food (Isan) in New York. Perhaps, it is even better than the food in some restaurants in Bangkok's hotels and malls. 

All dishes were authentic and fantastic. Fried chicken, papaya salad, Larb Pla Dook Yang (spicy grilled catfish salad), and Khao Klook Kapi were amazing. The Thai milk tea was very good, but perhaps too thick and sweet for some people. The Isan Martini was not worth the money. Lemongrass infused vodka sounded enticing, but the taste did not live up to it. You could barely smell the roasted rice. Their Bua Loy dessert (taro rice balls in coconut milk) is a MUST. No matter how full you are you must get it.

Although the waiters and waitresses were all nice, there were not many of them. Orders were forgotten. On a Friday night, it was a 45 minutes wait. Also, it's almost impossible to have a conversation in this restaurant without having to shout. It was incredibly loud.

I'm not usually a fan of Thai food, but this place have really good flavors. You can adjust the spiciness to your preferred taste.

Papaya Salad - light and fresh, don't remember which one but probably the original 
Spring Roll - average
Fried Chicken Thigh - delicious
Iced Thai Tea with Milk - delicious
Pad Thai - really good, but don't recall the exact name

I don't usually review really popular places, but would be seriously remiss if I didn't review my favorite Thai place in Manhattan. I am also terrible with spicy food, but for these dishes, I will absolutely endure it for the amazing food. 

Ask for everything mild! I've taken seasoned spicy eaters (those Koreans who foolishly laughed when I asked them if they were sure they could handle this much spice) and they have all failed and bowed their heads in defeat before Somtum Der). 

Recommended dishes: Tum Thai Kai Kem (papaya salad with salted egg), Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (very heavy and a little dry, but still pretty good), Larb Moo (one of my favorite dishes!). Get it all with the coconut rice. For those considering the grilled sticky rice - honestly, I don't think it makes that much of a difference in taste.

Overall, an excellent deal for the ambiance (not a hole in the wall despite the great food), taste, and prices.

I've heard about this place for a while...so when I have a chance I come to check this out... And everything is delicious like traditional Thai street food... Lao style papaya salad , Duck larb salad, Roasted pork Thai style, Tom Zab etc that I try ... It's remind me to Thailand... I will come back again

Ok food. Casual service. I'm not familiar with this style of cuisine, so I found the menu to be very confusing. The categories didn't make sense, but I settled on a spicy rice dish after talking to my server. I was disappointed when it arrived with a tiny piece of chewy dried fish on top, not the fish filet I was expecting. The server was nice enough to change it for a different fish dish which she said would be grilled. It was the same dried fish, bigger piece. So I'm not really a fan of this place - the food is exotic and new, rather than actually good.

Alright, Somtum Der won me over.  Lunch is the way to go here.  It's less loud, less hot, and there is less crowding by your table.  This is probably my new favorite lunch spot in NYC. It satisfies my craving for legit Thai food.

They do have some cheaper lunch deals/combos, but since I only get to go to NYC every few months, I wanted to order what I was craving.  First up was that delicious, highly addictive crispy catfish laab.  It did not disappoint!  I also ordered the grilled coconut sticky rice again.  It's great at mitigating the head of those spicy salads.  Of course I had to get the som tum (papaya salad) with the rice paddy crab again because I love that heat and that funk.  

The two new things I tried were the mushroom laab and the bamboo salad.  The mushroom laab was not very spicy and I didn't really care for the texture of it.  It was a little gritty.  Also, it was the most boring thing I've had here in terms of flavor.  That being said, my husband enjoyed it.  The bamboo salad was delicious.  It's listed like a soup, but it's a room temperature salad.  If you like bamboo, heat from peppers, and fresh herbs, and fish sauce, this is the salad for you. I also tried the rosella juice.  It's basically hibiscus juice and tastes like a sweet hibiscus tea.  It's was refreshing, but a little to sweet for my taste.

We made a reservation for lunch, but I don't think it's totally necessary like it was for dinner last time.  There were people there, but plenty of empty tables the whole time.I left stuffed and happy.  We passed on dessert this time, but I'm still curious about a few of the offerings.  I'll definitely be back.

Yummy!! My favorite dish is the dessert 'Taro in the condensed milk', the taro is chewy and coconut milk is always great! The jasmine rice marinated in shrimp taste is surprisingly good, it's not a popular dish but I strongly recommend it! All other popular dishes were great as well!

Pad kee Mao is amazing!!  A little spicy ,though. Strong recommend!
Thai milk tea is also my favorite...
But you may wait for 30min for the food...

This is one of the few restaurants that has a fairly large menu but where basically everything is very good. If you had to try just one dish, I might recommend the fried chicken. I am also a fan of the papaya salad, and various fried rice dishes. Somtum der is definitely one of the best kept secrets in NYC.
Great depth a flavor with everything I've had there on multiple occasions. Must try.

OK ish Thai place. Didn't find the vegetarian dishes good except the vegetarian papaya salad. We asked for mild spicy but it was pretty spicy as well sour for one of the dish (larb hed kao kya). Even the non vegetarian dish (larb duck) was very sour n spicy n the meat wasn't good either.

I really, really liked Somtum Der. The vibe, the ambience, the location. The portion size was also perfect. My friend and I shared the Thai Fried Chicken and it was just the right amount of crispy...and wasn't too overcooked or dry at all. We also shared the sticky rice on a stick, and I thought it was the cutest thing ever. It actually tasted better after it got a little hard. Yeah I said it.

I had a rice dish, but can't for the life of me remember the name of it. It was like five words and after I pronounced the whole thing when ordering, our waiter excitedly clapped for me. lol I remember it having pork, a fried egg and was spicy af.

I'd love to come back and try more stuff.

After having gotten really sick of Thai food in the city, this place shows up. It's amazing and totally different. Get the papaya salads or the larbs, they're awesome. You can also get a pad Thai if you must, but that's really not the main event here.
The laab Pork was so good and we ordered the cat fish soup which was tasty as well but wish we had more people to try more dishes...will just have to go back!

Food are authentic and really looks as good as the pictures on the menu.
If you're a fan of duck you have to try their duck salad . The sampler plate was a lol much and for the most part we didn't know what we were eating. Still pretty tasty. 
Their infamous pork cartilage soup missing some spices action. Need to be a lil more bold. It's a cross between a tom yum soup and northern Thai turmeric chicken soup.

Pad kee mao was good although they can use a lil less oil. But hey those noodles came in a package contain with oils to keep them moist so it's not their fault.

Overall this place is a hit for me and I will be back!

Where do I begin? Everything we tried was delicious and legitimately spicy. "Mild" still means a little spicy, so it may not be the place for everyone. If you can take a little heat, you would appreciate the fresh, bold flavors of lemongrass, cilantro, tamarind, lime and fish paste--a specialty of the region. The duck larb was perfectly mop-able with sticky rice without a greasy residue. Unlike typical Thai joints, they only offer one type of pad thai (crab, yummy), but many varieties of papaya salad prepared at the counter. They also specialize in a variety of regional dried and cured meats. Try the fried, dried beef or the fried pork meatballs with beer after a work day, when the crowds are thinner. 

Our server made great recommendations and explained the menu, but was a little slow handling the check.

Delicious, well priced, good service. I especially liked the larb. We ordered two kinds of papaya salad, but both were too spicy to eat, even though we ordered moderate, could have been a fluke, I'd try again ordering mildest.
As a Thai, I can can say this place is one of the best Isaan places in NYC. I either bring friends there or order in at least twice a week. Portion is a little small but totally worth the price.
Nice decor. Authentic and creative Northeastern Thai/Lao dishes. Rather quiet at lunch time but can be pretty packed for dinner.

Went with a friend and a stomach in some distress, so I wasn't able to order as much, or as spicy as I would have liked to.  

We shared the fried chicken, the catfish salad, the grilled sticky rice, and the thai iced tea panna cotta  All were excellent.  The catfish wasn't as nuanced as I would have expected, but very good, and the fried chicken, of which I had one piece, was nicely seasoned and a perfect texture.  

With regards to authenticity, it's definitely a step above Zabb Elee.  The food is closer to the stuff I had in LA and Thailand. And there was an honest to goodness Thai couple next to us!  Not all farang at this place! .  

Can't wait to return to try the other stuff on the menu, in particular, the som tum.

Really authentic and delicious Thai food! Met up with a friend around 7:30 on a Wednesday night. It was crowded but luckily they still had a few spots open. We ordered the papaya salad, pork skewers, chicken soup, Pad See Eiw, and grilled sticky rice. The portions are decent sized so it was lot of food for two people and yet we still finished it all! Most of the items on the menu are spicy so this is definitely a place for diners who can handle the heat!

When a friend asked how does it compare to Kin Kao, it's because Kin Kao is also Michelin Recommended, got written up in New York Times, and is located just off Union Square in San Francisco. It's more inventive Thai than the normal stuff. Somtum Der has the same flair of inventiveness, but this being Manhattan, it's less expensive than San Francisco (yes it's true, I've seen it over and over again), and the food is prepared better (more competitive) and the setting slightly more creative (and more spread out, for that matter, because San Francisco real estate is even more insane at the moment).

So yes it's better here. I think.

Papaya salad with salted egg reminds me a bit of Chinese southern food, where salted egg is more than just a condiment, it became essential in flavor enhancing creative cuisines, the other protein in the otherwise vegetarian dish.

Grilled Beef is nice and tender, came with rice balls on sticks. Very creative. Get that.

Best of all is the chicken soup. It was recommended by the server. I did not believe her at first, but I was glad that she insisted on me getting it, she's Asian, I'm too, I figure she's not pushing it onto me because I was white and therefore cannot withstand the exotica. The chicken soup is distinctive different, the use of dill reminded me of Laotian food. Which btw is my most favorite South East Asian Cuisine de jour (since circa 2013) and there are only three legit ones in the entire bay area, all in Oakland. I was puzzled but I had a slight suspicion that it is somewhat similar to Laotian food. And I would be right.

Here is the gist. Somtum Der originates from Bankok. It specializes in Isan (Northern Thai) cuisine. Which surprise, surprise, is a bit like Laotian. The main language is Isan, which is a dialect of the Lao language. 

This is a Thai version of Laotian food. No wonder I'm stoked.

Had to catch Frank Stella at the Whitney, told the servers, and they served food quickly which meant, the service is excellent. 

Not your typical thai, close to Laotian food, is the outpost for Bangkok's most celebrated Isan (Northeastern Thai) restaurant, service is great. Restaurant is very pretty. Wifi available on premise. Ice coffee is strong.

Take F train and get off on 2nd Ave, walk pass the long line on Katz's deli, and you are not that far away from it. Do it. Do it.

They sat a party of six at the last minute which was amazing!  But they do not have enough waiters - it was one of those looking around, are they seriously not going to come to table moments - we waited for easily 15 minutes before a waiter showed up - they didn't come back until they brought the check.   Food was good not great - I think I ordered wrong but it's easy to end up with Thai food that tastes good but just like the normal thai food you would order for delivery in your hood.  Not Queens thai amazing.

Terrible service. Cannot even comment on the food because the food literally did not arrive before the check!!!!! 

We ordered four dishes and within the first 20 minutes two of them arrived and after waiting for another 40 minutes, the food was still not there. Worst of all was when we checked in on the food and asked for the check, they did not even acknowledge that they did not put in the order and just kept us waiting. 

Definitely not worth it.

Expect to not feel your mouth for about a day after this meal.  If you don't like spicy food, this is NOT the place for you.  If you like spicy food, this is the only place you want to go.  Stop searching New York...I legit don't even KNOW how they make things so perfect and so hot and so addicting, but they do.  

Every dish here is delicious.  They are complex and have layers and layers of flavor.  I personally am a huge fan of their signature somtum's and their crab phadthai.  

My favorite somtum is the one with the salted duck egg.  I highly suggest it because the flavors just explode in your mouth.  The thin slices of young papaya, with their beautiful blend of spices, peanuts, basil, lime and lemongrass, and salty duck egg to even out the sweet and spice.  It's perfect.  When eating the somtum, my mouth is on fire and my brain and stomach are begging for more.  They don't want me to stop.  Ever.  

The crab phadthai is my favorite main there.  I know.  Typical to order the Phad Thai at a Thai place, but this dish is nothing typical.  The flavors are nicely complex and they put a lot of crab meat in that dish.  It makes you think of what fishermen would eat after a long work day.  Hearty, fresh, quickly made.  It is comfort food at its finest.  Of course, with a kick. 

The prices are legit and the staff are patient and explain their dishes well.  My fiance and I have made this one of our go to places when we want some real thai food.

I have been to place a lot of times and have brought in more than 30 different people to it over the past two years. The reason is simple, the place makes me cry with it's reckless use of thai red chillies which sometimes are so hot that if you use your hands to pick up a dish, you shouldn't touch your eyes for the next 5 hours even if you washed your hands.

My assh*le really really rebukes me the next day for the atrocities it has to go through, but on that day, when you're crying sweet tears of hot joy, future doesn't matter. This place is like  Scarlett Johansson with Chlamydia, sure you're going to regret it some parts of it the next day, but if you get a chance to spend a night with it, you will rarely refuse.

The service is poor, the waiters slightly creepy, but the food makes you blind, literally, to everything else.

Let me get this straight right off the back, dear readers-- Somtum Der is not the unseemly slime of a restaurant these three stars might have you believe! I am just a picky licky, who has eaten three lifetime's worth of incredible Thai food. I am also a bit wine tipsy upon writing this.

Somtum Der is A-OK in my book. They have a nice selection of dishes. However, since good Thai food in the area is hard to come by, I believe this place gets a little bit more credit than it deserves. The meat in particular leaves a lot to be desired-- tough and generally flavorless, unless you use some of their complimentary dipping sauce to add to the depth. I've been here around four or five times since it's right across the street, and every time I order a meat dish I end up slightly disappointed. The rice and noodle dishes are a bit more satisfying. Their sticky rice skewers are always a welcome addition to my meal.

As for the interior, it's quite nice, if not a bit too darkly lit. I feel slightly weirded out coming to a Thai street food restaurant and having a romantic atmosphere, as if Thai street food is suddenly haute cuisine-- which it may be becoming. Well, despite what I think of Somtum Der, this angle is obviously working in their favor!

Give it a try. You'll either love it or feel 3/5 yelp stars about it. If you hate it, maybe avoid Thai food in general.

loved the authentic dishes that were prepared to perfection here. a really interesting, diverse menu and a great list of starters. the overall meal experience tends to get a bit heavy with all the meat, oil and carbs, but still the best thai place in the city that i have visited so far.
Great thai food. Reasonable price. Might be little too spicy even though you order mild spicy. But I like it.

The Pad Thai was good, just know it only comes with crab meat (in case that's not something you like).  The house roasted pork was pretty fatty, and beware, it was so spicy we could not enjoy the rest of the meal.  I am usually someone who enjoys spicy but this was intense.  We also got some mushroom fried rice, which we were surprised to see all the mushrooms came on the side of the rice, rather than mixed in.

I highly recommend:
Green papaya salad with salted egg ($11)
Crab pad thai ($15)
Marinated grilled beef

Definitely expensive for Thai food, but very authentic flavors. Expect a wait unless you have a reservation. Better than your ordinary thai place, but i thought it was pricey for 1) where they're located (i.e not close to a subway and hard to get to); 2) the small portions you're getting. But service is fast and friendly and the restaurant is beautiful.

Nice spot. No wait ~9pm on a Saturday night. If you don't have reservations at nearby bars (and encounter 2hr+ waits everywhere you try), this is a good option for some tasty cocktails (not quite artisanal but creative & sweet). There's food as a bonus. Friendly service.

* Mangosteen - 4 stars
Very tasty, refreshing, and not too sweet! This does *not* actually taste like mango. There is a fruit called mangosteen that actually tastes more like a lychee.

* Lemongrass Martini - 3.5 stars
Light and refreshing. Not quite what my boyfriend was looking forward to, as he wanted something stronger. It was a bit weak even for me.

* Cocktail with Honey (forgot actual name!) - 4 stars
More boozy than all the other drinks, still tasty and pretty well balanced considering. You have to stir it to keep the honey from settling at the bottom!

* Per Pia Larb Moo (deep fried spicy pork spring roll $7) - 3 stars
Good crunch, a nice light appetizer, but this was pretty spicy! The filling was quite gooey, you can't exactly taste chunks of meat, and flavor-wise the spice kind of took over.

* Chef's Signature Wok-fried Seafood Suki (wok-fried rice vermicelli w/ seafood, vegetables, & signature suki sauce $12) - 3 stars
Decent. I liked the vermicelli, but it clumped together quite a bit. Not too flavorful, seafood a tad overcooked. 

* Pad Thai Mun Poo (special pad thai made w/ crabmeat and crab pasted w/ home-styled sauce. $15) - 3.5 stars
This was good, and the crab meat was unique. Quite strong on the tangy flavors.

Food was good but way too spicy for me. Be careful when you order if you cannot handle spices well!
Service was ok, a bit too slow and they forgot one of our cocktails and we had to remind them.
Great authentic Thai food. Loved the price. Favorite thing on the menu was pad see ewe, the noodles taste so fresh and home made. Great for a low key dinner in an awesome neighborhood.

(STAFF GET 0 STARS) Ill start off with the bad so I can end on a good note (Because the FOOD GETS FIVE STARS)
You walk in to a nice dining room without a host or any one to greet you. Accompanying you are other confused guests wondering what they should do. Once in a while, one of the waiters will come over and seat people, but there is no one who's sole job is to seat guests or anything. RIDICULOUS! 
When we ordered I gave special instructions because I have a few allergies. 10 minutes after that, another waiter comes over and tells me the last guy didn't understand what I was saying and he didn't order any of our food. The new waiter told me I couldn't eat half of the food we ordered...when the food came i was suspicious (the things I'm allergic to aren't usually in thai cooking) so I took a few careful bites only to discover I wasn't allergic...to anything.

Flagging down the servers is a nightmare. If that wasn't bad enough, they bring everything out at once and don't clear anything...ever! Between my dad and I, we had to put 4 beer bottles on the floor just to make room...pretty sad considering how good the food is.

Papaya salad - my favorite dish. A perfect combination of chilis, palm sugar, lime, and fish sauce. Thai fried chicken was lightly breaded, crispy, and very enjoyable with chili dipping sauce. Duck Laab had a generous portion of lean meat complimented with toasted peanuts.  

Dining experience was pretty infuriating considering all of the issues we had to deal with. In a restaurant filled with over 100 people you need someone who's job it is to host. They have an abundance of staff running around but it seems like they aren't ever doing anything. Regardless of the service I would definetly go back. Its that good.

Really nice ambiance and solid food selection. A lot more than the typical pad Thai and Pad See Euw you would see in the Americanized restaurants. Be careful if you can't handle spicy, this place's spice is no joke. Although I love it, it can be a bit much if you aren't prepared.

WAYY TOO SALTY!! 

I was recommended by a friend and was really excited to try it but not only was the mild so HOT, the rice dish was so salty it was like they dumped the whole box. 

Not a great experience unfortunately.

This was my first time dining at a Thai restaurant that specializes in food from the Isan region. According to what I learned from the menu, Isan is an area in the northern region of Thailand with specialty dishes including sticky rice, hot soups and charred meat. The food skews on the spicier side as well.

It is small inside so reservations are recommended, especially for the weekend. It was hopping on Saturday night. We started with the spicy pork spring rolls - when they say spicy, they mean it! I enjoyed the crispy coating and mayo-based sauce to help balance the spiciness of the meat. I ordered the garlic pork for my main and enjoyed it very much. This dish was not spicy. The meat was very tender and the garlic flavor was just right.

A real nice place for great Thai food. The papaya salad is great. It's tough to evaluate Thai restaurants since most of the time the food is amazing. This place is no exception, but don't expect pad Thai. Instead they have chicken soup which was nice but I think I will try something else next time. The one piece fried chicken was also good (8$) but amazing... I'm not sure. Overall I would recommend this place but Michelin star? I'm not sure. Certainly over four stars but definitely not five.

Sadly sitting in front of my inedible takeout that I waited an hour for (my bad for trying doordash when the place is 500 ft away, but I had a coupon). I always get the crab pad thai, and it's a nice twist on typical pad thai. However, this time as takeout, the dish is completely different. Super spicy (not sweet at all, which is what usually highlights the crab), really dry, tons of huge red pepper flakes or something, and every bite is full of these hard inedible seeds. I can't chew a bite without hitting one or five - it's infuriating enough to write my first yelp review. I've gotten other takeout before and the dishes are definitely lacking in comparison to dine ib, esp. In portion size, but this is ridiculous. Money down the drain. Will not go back.

The food in this place was and is great but they weren't  as friendly  to me my waiter was very rude non of the food came out at the same time it just wasn't  a great dining  experience  I hope they can do better
lets just say i finished less than half of what i ordered i think i need to give dine-in a chance but i got the wrong dish

Came in with my family around 8:30pm with a party. Only to be ignored the entire time we sat there. Everything on the menu is super spicy. Everyone's food came out at different times. I will never come back here again.
I LOVE their papaya salad and their noodle dishes. they have amazing skewers too.  Top 3 Thai place i've been to in Manhattan!

I ordered the chicken soup (Gaeng Om Kai) here for dinner and was satisfied with the fresh ingredients and the unique herb flavour. Staff were friendly but super inattentive, every request was met with ~15 min delay and cards got mixed up. I typically am pretty relax when it comes to service, but this just really annoyed my friend and me.
One of the best Thai restaurants in the city IMO. Very authentic Isan cuisine (I was born and raised in Bangkok). Definitely my go-to Thai spot in the city.
This place, honestly, has good food but the service was whack. It wasn't even busy, rather really slow and the service was pretty bad.

Absolutely incredible culinary experience. Let's start:
Atmosphere: Spacious, clean, well-lit, high ceilings, really interesting light fixtures, big tables (you'll need a lot of room). You can see the drinks being made.
Staff: Very friendly and quick.
Food: Hallelujah for this authentic Isan food. These creations were incredible. Each one bursts with really unique flavor. I really enjoyed the pad thai (I know, typical), steak, papaya/pork neck salad, and prawn. And for dessert the thai tea panna cotta was surprisingly very "Thai-tea-y." Exceptional menu items. Portions are not skimpy.
5 Stars all around!

If I lived closer, I would definitely come here more often/get delivery! This is quite possibly one of the more yummy and authentic thai places in NYC :). Although I wasn't completely wowed by the dishes (aka it wasn't that unique or anything), I still thought everything was cooked well! This place also came highly recommended by my sister, so I had to come by to try some of the food.

The food came out pretty quick for us, and the first thing served was the thai prawn sashimi. Loved the presentation! I was the first one to try it, so I ate it as is...man, was this dish spicy! If you don't want your tongue to be numb throughout the meal, I'd suggest scraping off at least some of the chilis and chili seeds off first! But still, I thought dish was sooo good!

Everyone raves about the deep fried chicken thigh, so I got two orders for the 4 of us. This was, in my opinion, super delicious, but my friends thought it was good but nothing special. Totally reminded me of the huge deep fried chicken steaks (炸雞排) from taiwan nightmarkets, or the popcorn chicken (鹽酥雞) - similar flavors. Came out super fresh with crispy skin and moist chicken thigh meat (the two things I absolutely appreciate with my food...that it comes out hot, and that there's a crispy element somewhere haha).

We also got an order of the Tom Saab Kradook On, which is described as a spicy Isan pork cartilage soup. I actually didn't know this would be a lemongrass soup, but I didn't mind it! It was definitely more sour than most lemongrass soups I've had, but I loved the bits of cartilage in there.

From past yelp pictures, I noticed grilled Sticky Rice everywhere, so we got that too - nothing special...just sticky rice balls on a skewer. After the spicy prawn sashimi, I honestly couldn't taste much of the coconut sweet flavors at first, but after a while, I liked the subtle sweetness.

For the main entree rice/noodle dishes, we ordered two things:

Khao Moo Tod Kratiam Prik Thai (Fried garlic pork with jasmine rice) - again, nothing special...tasted kind of like korean kalbi. Came with a fried egg on top.

Pad Ki Mao Pork and Basil (Spicy flat rice noodles, wok-fried with ground pork and crispy basil leaves) - Loved this! The flat rice noodles were made sooooooooooooo well. It's kind of like how you want pasta to be al dente. This is how I imagine rice noodles should always taste. It had a good chewy consistency (in a good way); I feel like most of the rice noodles I get in the city are slightly mushier than they should be (In Taiwan, we refer to this texture as "QQ" haha).

For dessert, I had to get the Black Jelly with Fresh Milk that my sister has been raving about. Did not disappoint! If shaved ice and grass jelly had a baby, this would be it haha. They probably crushed up the ice first, mixed it grass jelly (and red beans I think), and refroze it again. Then, probably a drizzle of condensed milk / sweetened milk. YUMMMMM.

Prices are super affordable; Next time, I need to try their Tum Thai Kai Kem - Thai spicy papaya salad with salted egg!!!

Extremely cute restaurant with great ambience. Staff were polite and attentive. The food was great and not your typical run of the mill Thai restaurant. The tum Thai Kai in is definitely a must try! Prices are also very affordable with each dish being less than $15. Definitely recommend. Will be coming back again!

The noodles, seafood, vegetables and sauce of the Seafood Suki are delicious. I recommend it! Also, the fried rice with crab meat was very good. The traditional Dong Der Lao big platter looked great but, besides the Somtum and Pad Thai, it wasn't that tasty. The Martini Der is good and that was the first time I've seen Singha Light. I'd definitely return.

I would give the food 5 stars for flavor. 
4 stars for service.
No stars for the drinks. The martinis are the biggest ripoff I have ever experienced. When thinking martini, I think of a strong beverage. There was no booze in my $9 martini!!? WTF? 
In general we think was that the delicious food was lacking in portion. The crab salad has very little crab in it which was very difficult to retrieve from the tiny shells. It seems like the crab is more of a garnish than anything. 
The shredded pork was very tasty, but I could have easily eaten another entire order to be satisfied.
They also charge $3 for rice.
Just seems like they are being cheap.
The staff was very friendly except for the bartender.
He was useless. Terrible personality and terrible drinks.

My friend and I love Thai food and so we decided to come here for lunch. I guess I have never been to an authentic Thai restaurant because I didn't even recognize most of the items on the menu... So we probably were a little more cautious with what we ordered..

I ordered their mushroom/lemongrass soup which was very delicious. It was not supposed to be spicy but was. The little spices in the broth unfortunately had me coughing for a short while. 

I ordered the chef's special fried seafood suki which was absolutely amazing!! The sauce was slightly creamy and there was plenty of seafood. There could have been a bit more vermicelli, but it was definitely not overdone with noodles.  My friend ordered the pad see eiw which was also absolutely amazing.

Prior to ordering a soup and an entree, I did ask the waiter if those two portions were doable for one person to which he said "oh yes, no problem." But it was definitely the size of two entrees... As the pricing suggested.

Definitely delicious food.. Would like to try a variety of their dishes next time I am in town.

Trendy/casual restaurant, pretty roomy (for a Thai restaurant), and really tasty stuff. The food was delicious - every dish we ordered was a flavor bomb (in the best way possible). I've often heard that Thai food is difficult to make because it takes just the right balance of salty/sweet/sour/spice, and when it's done right it is addictive. 

The papaya salad with salted egg was really good, not overly salty and refreshing. The veggie dish makes me feel better about the meat and carbs to come. We also had grilled marinated pork with a side of coconut rice, which was shaped onto a skewer and also grilled... amazing. The pad thai mun poo (crab) was kind of underwhelming, the crab doesn't have a strong presence. Sadly I dined with only one friend and could only finish this amount of food - I recommend coming with a group of 4+ and order family style.

Nice restaurant for some small plate action to share with friends. It would be tough to fill up on just one plate here, but if you bring a friend and share, I think it's definitely worth it. If you like spicy I would consider this place a must try as they don't try to just make food spicy, it's also TASTY. I actually enjoyed the sweat dripping down my forehead because it tasted amazing.

The restaurant itself is pretty clean and modern looking, but the lights were a little wonky the last time I went. Nothing that wouldn't make this a fun place to go on a date though. The beer selection was average and the prices of the multiple dishes really adds up quickly. That said, I'd definitely come back and try it with someone who enjoys spicy food.

Nice little spot for dinner! The food has a great combination of spices that make for tasty plates! As several has mentioned, as with most Thai food, you may be craving more after you finish! Prices are reasonable and portions are fairly generous. The pad thai with crab meat definitley seemed to stand out as having an exceptional balance of flavors.

I must say I think this is the best Thai restaurant in NYC. The food is very nice and very spicy. Although it's americanized a little bit, I think its taste is closest to real Thai food compare to other restaurants in NYC. 
 The most impressive dish for me is the shrimp sashimi (a must try). Even though it was very spicy, its taste was so nice. A little bit sour from the source, sweet from the shrimps and very very spicy from the chilli ( we ordered medium spicy and I thought I had a burn in my mouth. But believe me, it was totally worth it!!!). I suggest you order lemon grass drink. It tastes nice and different and might help you with the spicy from the food.
I also love the panna cotta thai tea. I am a big fan of Thai tea, and this dessert melted my heart. Although I think it might be a little bit creamy for some people, the feel of the panna cotta melting in my mouth made me feel like I'm one of the happiest person in the world . 
 The decoration of the restaurant is very modern and cozy. The bathroom is clean and organized. The waiters were caring and helpful. I suggest you should make a reservation because it's full very soon. The food camr quickly after 15 minutes of the order.
 I would have given this restaurant 4.5 stars if Yelp has 0.5 point. The only reason it couldn't be 5 stars was because the waiter messed up our order a little bit and we had to waited for the last dish around 15 minutes. 
 I love this restaurant and I will definitely come back to try other dishes.

SD is one of the few CHEAP Michelin restaurants in NYC. I have had so many bad experiences with unauthentic Asian food in Manhattan before, but I once again lift up my expectation because of one Michelin star. After one dinner at the small restaurant in East Village, I have to raise my glass to their beautiful performance.

I love how Somtum Der moves its exact food quality from Bangkok to Manhattan. Most ISAN Thai flavors (from Northeastern Thailand) come out as too strong for Americans, so many restaurants decide to remove their signature fieriness. I'm glad that SD values culinary culture more than commodities. 

If you think you know Thai food, I challenge you to go to Somtum Der. Isan food is incredibly SALTY, SOUR, AND HOT. You may shed your tears and burn your throat (seriously tho'). You may feel extremely unpleasant, but enjoy that, that is the GENUINE quality that no other restaurant dares to do. Grilled Sticky Rice is not salty, not sour, and not at all hot, so it is the most popular dish on Yelp because of course, it is the most comfortable to eat. 

You may dislike fish sauce, dislike Thai food, and dislike Somtum Der. But you cannot deny its authenticity. 

And if you LOVE real food, you better reserve. SD is sold out every night. 

Appetizers+Entrees: 5/5 (heck yeah) ; Desserts: 4/5 (too sweet and too big) ; Service: 4/5 (they forgot my order twice)

This may be the best drunken noodle I've had, even better than pure Thai cookhouse!!
Hope to try out the other dishes on the menu.

The food was spectacular but the service well below par, especially for a newly Michelin starred restaurant.

I don't usually complain about service but it took half an hour for me to get the drink I'd ordered - the Siam Sunbeam. My friends Lemongrass Juice took another half an hour too. But they're inconsistent with their timing. Other drinks at the table came in under two minutes. They seemed tremendously understaffed and had a difficult time following what we ordered. Earlier when I'd called to update our reservation, the person on the line said he'd updated it but hadn't actually. When arranging the table for our party of 7, it took the waiter 5 minutes just to understand instructions. Our food an inordinately long time to get to the table too.

The food, however, was spectacular. Papaya salad, seafood suki, the pork fried rice and the panna cotta were all amazing (and affordable)!

I don't think this is anywhere near Michelin quality. I'm not sure how Thai places like Zabb Elee and this restaurant get starred despite having alrightish (and very affordable) food. I'd probably not be dying to go again. Nothing spectacular.

This place is FIRE! lol at least that is how your mouth will feel if you order anything more than "mild". Thai's must have a different concept of spiciness because even the "mild" will be considered "Spicy" by most standards.This coming from someone who likes spicy food. Get the Green Papaya salad. I usually get the vegetarian version but they have some other varieties, including one with a salted egg...  get the lemon grass drink... very refreshing.

This was my first time eating Thai food outside of Pad Thai - i have a sensitive stomach and pallet so i eased my way into eating the sticky coconut rice and larb ped. Both were delicious, but i didn't know if this was for me. The back and forth from spicy to sweet was difficult for me to eat. The food was well presented and in great proportions - the drink selection was also amazing. I would recommend this place to anyone who is a Thai fan - the ambiance was very welcoming and comfortable. The staff were very helpful and informative of items and ingredients in each meal.

NYC is never short of decent restaurants; yet there are not too many of them fortunate enough to be part of Michelin family - Somtum Der was one of those lucky ones that just got upgraded to the list. In my opinion, it well deserved the star!

They had a huge menu to choose from - I'm so glad that I consulted my friend so I knew exactly what to order. Marinated beef with Der style sticky rice - my favorite of the day. How can they mix the flavor of sweetness (rice) and spiciness (beef) so well that neither side overwhelmed?? Papaya salad was another signature. Peanut and papaya made the best combo - just make sure to order mild spicy...Cannot skip dessert! My friend and I shared the black jelly ice and the coconut milk mochi, both were fantastic and had a strong Thai tilt!

Reservation was a must! By the time we started to eat, the place was already completely packed! There was no miss, from flavor to ambience.

Awesome food, very different from any meal I've had related to Thai, with some excellent flavors. Order what looks good, dive in, and enjoy. 

Had the Larb Moo and the Seafood with Suki sauce, both of which were awesome. Very well priced for shareable plates, and drinks were in line with East Village pricing as well. Definitely bringing others back for.

I've spent four months in northern Thailand where the food there is "Isaan style". Ever since coming back, I've been on a search for authentic Isaan style Thai food in nyc. Finally. Finally I have found a place. 

The main dish is "somtam/somtum" or papaya salad. I love how this place has so many different varieties. My favorite ones are the regular Thai papaya salad and the Isaan one with crab and fish paste. They also have big platters with the papaya salad in the middle, surrounded by different toppings. I've ordered it once but I didn't like the toppings as much as just the papaya. It's also quite pricey. The food here is VERY SPICY so be careful. 

Another Thai staple dish is sticky rice. I ordered the grilled coconut sticky rice and oh my gosh, it was amazing. I also ordered grilled pork sticks (muu ping) which came with thin noodles. Also amazing! The soups here are all very good, my favorite being the pork cartilage soup. I also loved the spicy pork salad and fried chicken. Every bite was bringing back memories of my trip in Thailand. 

I didn't order any Pad Thai because let's be real, all these other dishes are so much better. If you want real, delicious, Isaan style Thai food, definitely come here.

The BEST THAI food in New York City..hands down! Authentic and traditional..like no other Thai place in the city- I've tried Thai food in Thailand and all over and this place ranks as one of the best!

Great Thai experience in the Lower East Side of NYC.  I enjoyed everything from my lemongrass martini to my fried chicken thighs.  I was here on a date and that was perfect because the plates are shareable. The ambience is cute and it's perfect for a quick grab and a sit and chat.

Found this place randomly. Had no idea it was so popular. We walked in just in time before the restaurant became packed! I recommend reservations. Based on the reviews, I tried the fried catfish salad and the deep fried chicken thighs. Both excellent choices. Portion size was small for the salad, so I am glad that I ordered the chicken as well. Service was not particularly friendly, but was efficient. They are used to dealing with a very busy service. Cocktails were not worth ordering. I am not usually in the area, but I would love to return to try more of the menu.

I should remove a star for the burn your eyebrows off spiciness of the papaya salad, but honestly, everything was so good, I can't bring myself to do it.  This place well earned its michelin star with delicious and flavorful Isaan style dishes. The mushroom larb stole the night simply because we weren't expecting mushrooms to be THAT good.  I'm not a big dessert person, but highly recommend the Thai panna cotta.  The fried chicken is pretty amazing as is the coconut fried rice on a stick.  Reminds me of the awesome street food I've had traveling thru Thailand.

I ordered a Pad Ki Mao & Basil (with beef for extra dollar). The small portioned flat noodles were all broken up into tiny pieces, and the meat was small bits of ground beef. The dish tasted pre-made. Like it was heated up in a microwave, stuffed in a bowl and turned over on a plate. Seafood pad see eiw that others ordered smelled fishy and tasted funky. 
    One of the dishes came out way too late. The green tea tasted weird. The seats are uncomfortable. There are food stains on the wood panels on the wall. When complained that food was bad, the waiter acted like he didn't care. 
    This is the worst Thai food I ever had. It was also very expensive for no reason. Places like Pongsri would be a better choice. I'm thinking that because this is a more of a college drinking spot, that they just don't care about their food?

Not sure why it has a Michelin star, but Somtum Der is certainly a very good Thai place that is unique from all the other millions of cheap Thai spots in the city. It's nice to see places that don't just Xerox copy each others' menus, you know? Of course they have your usual Pad Thai too, but the menu is much much more extensive with many more "exotic options". Plus menu comes with pictures for all us confused non-Thai folk. Spicy dishes can get really spicy though, so be warned. I had a couple appetizers as well as a rice entree and was super pleased. There's lots of seating and they can accomodate large parties but I did come during an off-peak hour so I don't know how busy it gets. Only complaint would be that the food takes a while to come out.

I was planning to come here with a group of friends. But when I wanted to make reservations on a Friday night, they informed me that the whole place has already been booked for the whole night. I thought I wouldn't be able to try this place any time soon, but we were able to make a reservation the following month on a Saturday night.

We were a party of three, but one friend was not there at the restaurant. Although the waitress stated that she's unable to seat us until the whole party was there, she guided us to our table. The atmosphere was really nice. The lights were dimmed, and the noise level was loud enough that people wouldn't be able to hear each other's conversations, but low enough that I didn't have to scream in order to communicate. 

We ordered our entrees. Not the biggest fan of the alcohol drinks, but the food was definitely really good. Salad was fresh, and the meats had a lot of flavor. I think it was some special day, because the waiters would put on a happy birthday song when people ordered desserts. But the funny thing was is that during our meal time, it happened three times. My birthday was around the corner, so I knew what my friends wanted to do. Eventually they ordered desserts and the loud birthday song was played. As embarrassed as I was, this was definitely a nice experience.

Food was great. Ambiance was great, and service was awesome! Will definitely come back!

Everything we tried here was fantastic.  The papaya salad with salted egg.  The shrimps. The noodles.  After trying each dish we looked at each other slightly wide eyed, this is really fucking good.  Definitely northern thai style, not the place to go for a chicken green curry!

A Thai restaurant with great dishes in general, with likely the best fried chicken. It was/is super crispy and comes with a good sauce too. Definitely the place to go for spicy Thai food and things that are delicious and not heavy. The black coffee and thai iced tea is good too. All in all, a great place and another tried/true restaurant.
Excellent, super authentic Thai food. Lots of interesting options you will have a hard time finding anywhere else. One complaint is that the food can be a bit overly spicy..

Great one-micheline starred thai restaurant. No item costs more than 15 dollars and the quality is great. If you wanna have a good start of the meal order one of the papaya salads (super spicy) or a duck salad. As main course chicken or noodles (pad-thai) are a must. Service is kind and quick. Would go back again with no doubt.

The food for most people is an acquired taste.  This is not the usual thai food - red curry, massaman curry, pad thai, etc.  The flavors are stronger (especially the fish sauce) and the food spicier.  I wouldn't say that makes it better - it may be more authentic but not everyone will love it.  The Tum Thai (papaya salad) is interesting - tasty, spicy, tangy, pungent - but there's a limit given its strong flavor.  I enjoyed it, but it's not something I will likely crave.  The fried chicken thighs were awesome.  They felt like home to me.  Amazing lemongrass, just the right amount of salt, and since it's fried dark meat, it's soft and juicy.  The sauce is nice, but even by itself the chicken was great.  I did take out and they were pleasant and quick with my order, but can't say much else about the restaurant.  It's good and interesting and different, I will go back to try more, but it's probably not going to be a regular for me.

I'm surprised by how well reviewed this place is, whether they filter or not. Perhaps I'm a growing boy but the portions here are on the smaller side and they're not by any means cheap. I've been here several times but never felt a single popular dish I ordered was particularly flavorful.

Went here on a date last night who had been before after coming across Somtum Der on a list of best picks for spicy food in NYC. 

Please pass on the crappy Chardonnay. DO order everything containing pork.

The deep fried minced pork -- oh-my-lawd-in-heaven....This dish knocked me right back to my favorite Thai restaurant I frequented while living in Sydney. I haven't tasted those flavors in years. 

We also had the bbq pork skewers, a soup (I was clearly affected by it), and coconut rice. Coconut rice is so so if you're into that -- order ANYTHING pork here. 

Come early because you will be up to your ears in neighboring tables any time after 8.

Deeee-licious. This restaurant was recommended to us by a Thai friend who defined it as "one of the two places to get real Thai food in NYC". Trust me, it was not a disappointment. The fried pork in all its glorious variations is a must-have. Throw in some classic papaya salad for some greenery. Wash it down with some Beer Lao. Boom. Oh, and make reservations!

I was never really a fan of Thai food before Somtum Der. All I had ever really had was pad Thai or some variation with a peanut base. But this restaurant offered a variety in the menu and dishes that are so rich in flavor in spice that I now love the cuisine. 

If you like spicy foods this place is definitely for you. The spiciness of the food is unlike that of any other food you have had. It is not overpowering, but compliments the natural flavors of the fresh ingredients offered here. One of the best things I have had is the soup with chicken wings-- so warm and tasty, my mouth is actually watering as I type this review. Another dish that is to die for is their pork skewers with coconut -- the pork is so tender and delicious and the coconut noodles that accompany it are so light and juxtapose the spicy sauce it's served with perfectly. You should also get one of their juices to calm the hotness of the food, so sweet and delicious.

We walked in on a Saturday night and while did not have a reservation, they were able to seat us within 10 minutes.  The dish flavors and combinations here are just a surprise party in your mouth.  The duck salad (Larb Ped) was spicy, flavorful and unlike anything I've had at typical thai restaurants.  Pad thai tends to be my benchmark for thai restaurants, and the crab pad thai here did not disappoint.  Both dishes were ordered with "medium" spice, but beware because it sneaks up on you.  Be sure to order plenty of grilled sticky rice to soak up the tears (and because it's just so freakin' delicious!)

My FAVORITE THAI place in NYC so far :) 

The aroma when you come in smells like Thai heaven. The service is excellent and the food is even better. The spice is up there in levels so you definitely need to be able to handle the heat! If not, tell them no spice whatsoever because even mild was pretty spicy for my mom. The flavors were excellent! I couldn't stop thinking about this place. 

Do try everything :)
the fried rice was especially delicious.  the portions aren't very big, though, so I recommend going with a small group and ordering a number of things to share.

Oh. My. God.

Very delicious Thai food. I had food orgasm from the very first bite. Seriously. I wanted to hug the cook (and perhaps get the recipes). 

My favorite is the Kuey Tiew Pad See Eiw Talay which is Thai styled fried flat noodles with shrimp and calamari. The aroma is just mouth watering. You'll notice distinct smokey flavor that right away. Delicious! The Rice with fried beef and basil is another hit. It has enough fat to hold the structure and flavor together without being too oily. It comes with side fish sauce and slices of thai red chilli if you like your dish spicy. I had that and it was like fireworks in my mouth with every bite. I was a happy camper.  

And you gotta try the name sake, Somtum, which is Thai young papaya salad. Have it as an appetizer, although in Thai people eat this with rice at the street side. It comes with slices of salted egg that complements the vegetables well. Very tasty dish.

The interior is clean and have Thai traditional touch to it. The service is friendly, lots of smile which is no surprise as Thailand is a land of smile. 

The pricing is fair. Note that if you order something that needs to be prepared at the bar, like the drinks or even Somtum that they prepare fresh there, there's a 10 dollars bar surcharge. I don't really understand this.

This is a place that provide me enough joy from the food I feel content and even grateful to be alive. Heck it makes me even wanting to forgive my enemies. 

Totally recommended.

I do not know how this restaurant has a michelin star because it was the dirtiest thai restaurant I have ever been to in my life. The food was decent but we told the waiter we wanted it to be mildly spicy and everything came out to be extremely spicy.

4 stars for food, 2 stars for service. 

With the Michelin star and everything, I wish I could say that I loved this place. The service was below-par: no water for a good 20 minutes, slow to take orders, forgot part of my order when the food came out, didn't give utensils until asked, and was just overall really inefficient. The two neighboring tables also frequently asked the service staff to get things, and the servers never checked in with my table.

That said, the food was on the whole, really good. I thought that the selection was super varied and I wanted to try everything. Alas, my stomach is not big enough, so I settled on sharing the H'orderves Der, larb ped (minced duck salad), and fried rice with crab/egg, with a side of the grilled sticky rice. The sauces on the duck salad was top-notch -- sweet and spicy at all the right levels. The fried rice was pretty plain, but adding some of the fish chili sauce that came with the dish really helped. 

Definitely get the grilled sticky rice -- it's crunchy and soft at the same time, and is just cooked really well. 

I'd definitely recommend if you're willing to take a gamble on the hit and miss service!
The review is solely on service only. The food here is amazing! I hate to put bad reviews, but when your order is messed up not once, not twice but three times then something is wrong here.

Absolutely delicious - but wow, make sure to prepare yourself for a spicy meal. The best way to go is to order a bunch of small place and share with the table. The fried chicken is incredible. The raw shrimp is worth a try - because how often do you eat raw shrimp? The papaya salad is deceivingly spicy. I'm sure everything is delicious. I can't wait to come back and try more!
Awesome lunch special. Papaya salad and coconut rice were awesome. Fries chicken was really fried. Nothing great.  12 dollar lunch special. I would comeback for the rice and salad.

Second time here (went a month before the Michelin star). Had party of 2 reservations at 630pm on a Friday. Promptly seated upon arriving at 640pm. About 6 waitstaff/runners attending to all the tables. Kindly reminded it was hour pricing for drinks at (655pm) - this waiters one job was to take all happy hour drink orders - and even came back at 715 (after happy hour) to offer a last round of happy hour drinks!! Ordered the Fried Chicken, spicy prawn salad, coconut marinated pork skewers, grilled sticky rice, and a tum thai somtum. Split everything between the wife and I,except we each had our own fried chicken - it's too good to share, seriously! Note: 3 grilled sticky rice skewers per order (1.5 each) and the same for the pork skewers - 3 total so 1.5 each.

"Catching Fire" - think Katniss Everdeen Hunger Games - Girl on Fire - the moment she tries on the new dress... We call it "catching fire" when you are about 3 spoon/fork servings into your Somtum and it's beautifully painful to continue because the heat of the dish has caught up to you and you have to find the courage to continue on...you must continue on!

Make sure you save the Somtum (unripe marinated shaved papaya) dish for as late in the game as possible so that you can enjoy the flavors of your other dishes before the all out heat assault on your mouth begins.

Attentive waitstaff in rotation run out the food and check on you, but leave you alone which is a delicate balance they maintain very well.

All food was excellent - left perfectly satiated all in 40 minutes!!

The cucumber in the prawn salad is refreshing if you have some left by the time you are eating your somtum!

The grilled sticky rice is unreal and you will want to order 1,000,000 of them - order 1 and come
Back 1,000,000 times!

The marinated pork skewers are exquisite!

Total bill was only $70 with tax...I was prepared to pay more then $100. Remember, it's definitely important to split the dishes (except the fried chicken)...

There is no formal order as to what will come
Out first last or second - or so it seems, but definitely ask for the Somtum to come out towards the end!

Do yourself a favor and come with an open mind, appetite, and a flame retardant napkin - because here's to "catching fire"!!

I finally got to try it on my birthday. The Michelin 1 star is no joke.
We had reservation, but took a while for everyone to be there. (Everyone has to be there to be seated.)
Service was extremely nice. Surprised by the birthday music they played (in a joyful Thai accent) with a panna cotta in Thai ice tea flavor.
We all praised the quality of the dishes from appetizers to entrees.

One thing we played it wrong while ordering. Looking at Somtum's prices, we thought the portion would be small but it was not the case. We ended up ordering too much and were almost fulled when entree showed up.

Everything here was fine, the food, the atmosphere, the staff, but it just didn't "wow" me. I got the rice and pork dish and my friend got drunken noodles. The prices are totally reasonable and we went around 7pm on a Monday, so it wasn't hard to get a table. Might go back if in the area, but wouldn't go out of my way.
