The setting of the restaurant is very simple and clean. I love their fried chicken, their other items on the menus are very good too. It's a little different from Thai food but it's from the near country. I had been coming back over and over again for more chicken :)

I came from bkk, Thailand and food here tasted 100% authentic thai food from Northeastern part of Thailand. I went here at least twice a month when I craved for real thai foods. Highly recommended Moo Rong Hai with coconut sticky rice.

Excellent Food, excellent atmosphere, excellent service, but way way way overpriced for Thai food. 

Food quality was great, but very small portions. The flavor was a little sweet, typical Thai-American restaurant adaptation to suit western tastes. 

Atmosphere was nice, but tends to get a little overcrowded and the tables are stacked very very close to one another. 

Overall OK place.

The food was ok. My favorite was the taro coconut milk with mochi dessert. 

Food:
Classic papaya salad with salted egg - ok
Shrimp sashimi - quite fishy 
Fried chicken - mediocre 
Taro coconut milk mochi - delicious 
Thai tea panna cotta - good

this is easily the best thai food in nyc.

order: several beer breezers with extra tabasco, fried chicken, sardines, larb of any kind, pad ki mao(this is definitely NOT the basic shit you were raised on)

I was so excited to try out this place with my girlfriends because a) it's Michelin rated, 2) the price tag on each dish is pretty darn cheap, 3) Thai food is always so great, and 4) I've never had the chance to experience authentic Thai cuisine. We opted for 
1) SomTum (the first option on the page): a papaya salad (tastes nothing like what I imagined it would. The taste mostly resembled a combination of fish and vinegar).
2) Grilled marinated beef (medium spicy): Holy cow. The spiciness/ spice that encrusts the beef is not the usual spice I'm used to tasting. It was way more savory (and spicy) than I expected. This was the dish that made me realize that authentic Thai food is made of flavors that I've never experienced elsewhere. 
3) Pad Kee Mao (AKA drunken noodles) was my favorite dish by far. We got medium spicy (I accidentally bit into one the little chilies shortly before so my mouth was pretty numb and almost invincible by the time this dish came). I watched my friends sweating and gritting their teeth while chomping this dish down but I loved it. Every single bite. The basil taste was very fresh and prominent and I would not have changed anything about that dish. 
4) H'Ordervores Der: a sampler of sausages & such. Meh. Skip out on this. You could definitely choose a way better dish for $12. 
Conclusion: I wasn't used to the flavors and it didn't sit with palate too well. If I do come back, I will order completely different items (and ask for mild). Heh.

I have a short list of restaurants that I will forgive for just about anything.  Sripraphai in Queens is one of those places.  I have suffered through a few downright bad meals with even worse service while dining there over the years, but when they are on, they are so on, and even when they are semi-on, the food is still better than at most NYC Thai restaurants.  Besides, they remember my kid and that goes a long way for us Mamas.  So yeah, they get a pass from me.  Som Tom Der.... Not so much.  

I've eaten here several times now, and the food is very inconsistent.  For my most recent visit, a friend and I caught the tail end of happy hour, which if memory serves, runs 4-7pm M-F, with half off on drinks and $3 off their famed Fried Chicken.  Anyway, friend and I both got Lemongrass Martinis and an order of Fried Chicken.  

Martini wasn't very strong and did not even hint of lemongrass, but it was refreshing, and for $4.50 in a town where $15.00 cocktails are the norm, I wasn't complaining.  Fried Chicken came VERY fast, as if was pre-made to feed the Happy Hour masses.  This became painfully clear after the first lukewarm, dry, chewy bite.  A real shame because I've had this same dish here done right and it would put Popeye's to shame (and I love Popeye's).  

Another misstep came in the form of Papaya Salad with Salted Egg.  It was DROWNING in fish sauce.  Friend agreed and we sent it back, but not before we caught the staff person we mentioned it to rolling her eyes.  Nice.  Another shame because I've had this very same salad made deliciously here before. Anyway, we got the Vegetarian Papaya Salad instead and it was MUCH better.  *Almost* always a sure thing, Grilled Coconut Milk-Marinated Pork was good, as was the Coconut Rice (though Sripraphai does it better).  Also liked the Grilled Minced Catfish Salad, though portion was tiny for $13.00.  

We ended on a high note, with Thai Tea Panna Cotta, which had a really nice pop of tea flavor.  Not high enough, though, to save this once 4-star place from losing a star.

Took my family here for lunch all 8 of us. The staff was nice enough to honor our reservation on a Saturday at noon with fifteen minutes notice. The fried chicken thighs had the lightest batter and was crunchy goodness. We ordered four of theses appetizers, couldn't get enough of it. The green papaya salad was a combination of different spices and sweet & sour. Spring rolls were thinly rolled and spicy as was the pad Thai. The noodles and ground pork was a real winner, mild and super delicious. Will be back!!

Tasty spicy Thai food. Lots of pork and catfish options. Service was incredibly slow to order when I was there. Overall ok though. Nice spot in the East Village of you are looking for a low key Thai meal.

I LOVE SOMTUM DER. My boyfriend and I have become frequent patrons of Somtum Der... and when more than a couple of weeks go by, I find a little tug stronger and stronger to go back.  The spicy, sweet, tangy combination is INCREDIBLY ADDICTIVE.

Here's my favorites:
- Suki Seafood stir-fried vermicelli noodles: The sauce is amazing. I don't know what exactly goes in it but there's definitely a distinct saltiness from fish sauce, heat from thai chilies, sweetness from palm sugar, and creamy texture from the sesame seeds. It comes piled with shrimp, calamari, enoki mushrooms, and fried tofu. This is my absolute favorite dish at Somtum Der.
- Grilled beef w/ coconut sticky rice: Like the grilled pork, the beef is bursting with flavor. The coconut sticky rice also helps to tame the heat. 
- Spicy shrimp salad with roasted minced rice: This is similar to the larb and if you like shrimp, choose this one over the other larbs. I counted eight shrimps, which is quite generous. Sometimes I take a spoon to get all the marinade and unlike the larb, this one comes with roasted minced rice that adds a nice textural crunch.

Take a 5 star review from me to heart. I don't throw them around. And I used to cook for a living. I've been here a few times and have tried the coconut marinated beef skewers, sticky rice, grilled sticky rice, fried chicken thighs, (warm) mushroom salad, and the seafood pad thai and other pad se ew dish. AmAZing. This chef really gives a shi*^. Also, I love a good non-alcoholic beverage and everything I've tried has been so good: the red drink (can't remember the name), lemongrass drink and the longon drink. The service is really great as well. This place is worth every penny.

Okay, this is another must go to Thai restaurant if you want the authenticity of Isan (Northeastern Thai) taste. Let me enlighten you about the Isan flavors since reading some of the reviews on here make me realize that people are not sure what it is and how it should taste. The Isan food is generally eaten by the working class heroes of the Northeastern region of Thailand. The Isan flavor profile is very complex, comprising of the usual Central Thai flavors:  sweet, salty, sour, and spicy, plus the sharpness and pungent smell of the other ingredients such as mud fish, dry shrimp, pickled crab and so on. Such weird food stuff adds tremendous delight to the dish and transform the so-called "normal" Thai flavor to the wonderful flavor of the Isan region. People who are not familiar with such sharp contrast to the Thai food they are used to may find Isan flavor to be strange, unusual, or even offensive. If you suspect that you are a picky eater, have food sensitivities/allergies, or just simply not really open minded to trying something new and different, you may not really enjoy the food here. You've been warned. 

The food here is exceptional, definitely worthy of the awarded Michelin star. I personally enjoyed everything I had at the restaurant, so it's definitely a yes for me. A question, you may ask, what is so special about the Michelin star? Well, for starters, only a dozen or so restaurants in NY received such an honorary award. Second, the Michelin recommended restaurants are generally very very good. Somtum der received not just a recommendation, but  a solid one star and that is a big deal since it's the ultimate recognition of culinary prowess coveted by all the top notch chefs everywhere. 

I heard someone ranting about the prices here and I would say that it's comparable to most other not so good, made for farang (westerners) Thai restaurants. Remember good things don't come cheap because if it is you know something has got to be compromised i.e. your ingredients.

This is a cute spot to catch up with a friend on a weekday night (which is what I did). We started with lemongrass martinis, which are a good option if you're looking for a not-so-sweet cocktail. As an appetizer, we had a papaya salad which, despite asking for "no spice," was still quite spicy! But it was still delicious, so I just lived with the tingle ;). 

For my entree, I had the Thai-style fried flat noodles with shrimp and calamari. It was pretty solid -- nothing to write home about IMO, but pretty solid.

The service was great. Both of the people who were helping us were very friendly and accommodating.

Overall, it was pretty good, but I wasn't completely blown away. I'd like to go back and try other dishes to see if I overlooked some superstars.

There is something there at Somtum Der, and it's delicious food.  I was blown away by their Pad Kee Mao.  It was flavorful with just the right amount of spice. The service was excellent, fast and attentive. I will definitely be stopping by again.

One of the best Thai food places I've had in NYC. Their prices are super affordable and their smaller dishes allow for you to try a larger variety of foods. My favorites are the papaya salad with salted egg, basil fried rice, and the pad see yew. definitely worth your time to come because the food is completely amazing. We came late on a Saturday night and only waited 40 minutes.

Really good and flavorful Thai restaurant! 

1. Sa paok kai tod der (der styled deep fried chicken thigh) - literally amazing fried juicy chicken thigh. Comes with this amazing tangy hot sauce 

2. Khao pad kraprao moo / nue (fried pork with Thai basil, mixed with rice) - good solid fried rice mixed with ground pork / beef with fried egg. Yolk is runny and decent flavorful fried rice. Even better when asked for the tangy hot sauce 

3. Pad ki mao pork and basil (spicy flat rice noodles, wok-fried with ground pork and crispy basil leaves) - okay. Not as flavorful as other items. Fried rice is better in my opinion but I also like more salt / flavor. My boyfriend loved it though (he eats less spicy than me)

3. Tom saab kradook on (spicy isaan pork cartilage soup) - this was when I was sick so take it with a grain of salt, but this soup was a little too spicy and vinegar-y for me (and I love spice and vinegar flavors). Probably wouldn't order again

Overall really solid place and even the "3." dishes were decently solid / still constitute a good meal
Delicious Thai food. I had the garlic beef and several pork appetizers. Nice, spicy, delightful.

One of the best thai restaurants that I've tried in the city.  

I've spent a month in Thailand with my friend and stayed with her family - this place comes pretty close to some of the food that we had there in terms of deliciousness and authenticity.

Loved the sticky rice (MUST ORDER STICKY RICE) with fried chicken & the grilled marinated pork.  And ZOMG, the papaya salad was to die for.  

Ambiance was pretty casual - could be big enough for a big group.

All in all, you gotta trust me - this place will not disappoint.

This is the best Thai restaurant in Manhattan, and up there with the best in Queens. They specialize in the cold salad dishes, which are really out of this world. I haven't tried them all yet but I will eventually. The meat and noodle dishes are great too--do not feel ashamed to order the crab pad thai here because it is incredible and like no other pad thai you've had. Also the atmosphere is great and the service is fast. And the best part is I only live a few blocks away!

Had a high expectation before coming!
heard a lot of good things about this place.
Made reservations so the wait was not bad!

ALERT: to people who can't take spicy food - DON'T COME!
I cannot take spicy food, and when you look at the menu, almost all of them had the little red spice icon on the top

Both my friend and I do not eat spicy food so we picked the dishes without the icon:
1) Pork Skewers with vermicelli ($10)- the Pork was very very good, on the sweet side, and they also had a spicy sauce that came with the vermicelli, we asked for fish sauce tho and it was good. vermicelli though, tastes entirely of coconut oil

2) Chef's signature wok-fried seafood suki ($12)- very very good noodles, the seafood was amazing, the octopus is a must try, The dish in general is on the salty side

3) Sticky rice on the side - we did not like it at all. it tastes completely like coconut oil, same as the vermicelli

I would not come back because I feel like i've tried pretty much all the non-spicy options that they have, and all the rice and vermicelli taste like coconut oil
Excellent Thai food. Feels like more authentic Thai food. Coconut pork skewers amazing. Will be back

Great place for yummy thai food! The crab meat fried rice and grilled pork dish were amazing! Definitely recommend. The duck larb and papaya salad with crab were good too, but a little too spicy. I should have asked for the spice to be dialed down more but the dishes definitely seemed very authentic. I loved the beachy and laid-back space.

I enjoyed the place. However the food was all very esoteric so unless you really know Thai food from their specific region (I forget where) you'll be a bit lost on the menu. It was helpful that they had pictures of each dish though! More restaurants need to do that!

That being said it was tasty for what it was, aside from one sauce I got which tasted like vomit. Like actual vomit, like bile. Portions were a little small for the price, but well done plates for the most part. 

Word of caution: it should go without saying but the food is spicy. Personally, I love spicy food and I had no problem eating any of it, but some members of my party were having trouble with it. 

Service was attentive and friendly. No complaints there. 

Overall I enjoyed it and would go back.

I love love issan Thai!  Glad I don't have to go to Elmhurst Queens to get the real deal- though I do prefer the places out there. Somtum Der's been on my list and is very good. The deocr is really cute, very Thai like with warm wood colors.  Definitely a good place for groups but make a res - it's not very big. 

Came here with a 7pm ressie with my fiance and my parents.  We did not have to wait long to be seated maybe 10 minutes, but we were able to order while waiting.  Love that the menus have photos and detailed descriptions of the food... everything here is shared small plates.  I enjoyed a Thai iced tea. We had the:

- grilled marinated beef with sticky coconut rice- awesome, with good dippping sauces
- Ko Moing (or something like that) - grilled shrimp salad with the usual spicy Thai fixings (you know, shallots, lime juice, fish sauce, chilis), my favorite, delicious
- Somtum der (the traditional Spicy papaya salad) - deliciously citrus
-Larb moo - spicy minced pork salad - delicious but could have used more crunch, not the best larb I've had (Larb Ubol, that'd be or Ayada Thai in Queens)
-Pee Kee Mao with minced pork - Kind of wish I went with the pad thai that had crab, vs. the Drunken noodle but still really good with lots of Thai basil
-We shared a side of steaming hot black sesame sticky rice, yummy
-Dessert: black rice in milk

We asked for everything mildly spiced; which was really good - tolerable and not overly spicy. They gave a free beer for Dad on Dad's Day! 

$80 for everything, def will be back
Food is very spicy, just full of flavor and very authentic tasting Thai restaurant. I would come all the time if the wait was not that long.

Food: 10/10
 I've been here on more than one occasion and everytime I come here the food is freaking amazing. I had the Papaya Salad as an appetizer which is hot as hell, even if ou ask for mild, but it burns SO GOOD. DEFINITELY NEED THEIR AMAZING THAI ICED TEAS to calm the burn. For my entrée, I've had the Pad Thai before and it's different than what you'd expect at a "thai restaurant". So I'm guessing this Pad Thai is more "legit" than the other Thai places or that's just what Isan cuisine is like. I've also had one of their grilled meat and rice dishes (I had the pork). The meat with its sauce had a little tang to it which really balanced out well with the spice from before and the buttery smoothness of the coconut rice balls they give you. We also ordered a side of the regular coconut rice and that was great as well (make sure you ask them to bring it out with your entree if you intend to have it that way! We forgot and it got a little cold). The coconut rice was great too and the texture was that of basmati like but still good. Balances out the intense flavors from the meat! Everything I've ordered I HIGHLY RECOMMEND.
Service: 6/10
 Their service is good but they don't really have a lot of staff so when it gets busy (which it does most week and weekend nights), their staff can be a bit hard to flag down. But all in all though, they're amazing. I've seen them deal with some unruly drunk customers (on a thursday night specifically) and they have a ton of patience.
Overall: 8/10
Additional Notes: This place is what hey call Isan cuisine which is more northern Thai (or something, you can read their menu). But the food and the experience is different than your standard Thai restaurant and I highly recommend. Not to mention, this is the cheapest Michelin Star restaurant in NYC.... c'mon, gotta come here.
incredibly (almost impossibly) spicy isaan thai food - good prices, friendly staff.

This was the best Thai food I have had in NYC! Great flavors, service and atmosphere! Also had $3 Singha beer during happy hour from 4-7pm. Didn't wait to get in and sit at the bar at about 6pm on a Friday also, but I would suggest making a reservation.

Seriously just wish this place closer.  But then... I probably won't be able to stop myself from coming here every meal.

Everything, every single dish I've tried here is rich with flavor and complexity - the textures, aromas, and spices are simply delightful.

My favorites so far as I work through the menu:

- mackerel with som tum and rice is incredible - one taste, and it's hands down work the trek all the way here from the west side.

- sausage platter is delightful and tasty

- fried garlic beef with rice is very good with the sauce and egg

Service is fantastic and the place is adorable.

Look forward to coming back already...  Wonder if they have a table for two tomorrow...!
Very fast delivery! I've only ordered the Crab Pad Thai but it's consistently delicious!

They have the traditional thai menu items but a lot of options that US thai restaurants don't serve. Grilled sticky rice is really good. I got the grilled marinated beef which I liked but coconut marinated skewers are the move. Highly recommend those

I was excited to come here, as I've been on a short trek to 'affordable' restaurants which are Michelin-starred. [Short because there are very few... :'(.] We entered this restaurant, which is just a few blocks down from St. Mark's. The decor is cute, very Thai (?) with red and gold colored walls and gold lighting to offset the mood. The staff was friendly, and welcomed us immediately.

We ordered the Papaya Salad with Salted Egg, Duck Larb, Pad Kee Mao, Coconut Beef Skewers. Overall, everything was pretty good and spicy in just the right ways. The coconut beef skewers was probably the best dish, as the beef was juicy, though I wish there were more pungent coconut flavors. 

The reason behind the 'just okay' rating is that nothing absolutely blew my socks off. Everything was good, but I feel like I've had better Thai at a certain place in Elmhurst with bigger portions and a cheaper price. There was no dish that clicked the Michelin lightbulb inside my head & had me saying "Ah. this is why!" Instead, I was a bit disappointed as the dishes definitely delivered spicy heat levels, but not flavorful levels. The coconut rice here is also not as good as a certain place, since the flavors were subtle and the grain was a bit dry. 

The prices are a bit on the pricier end for the smaller portions as well. I probably wouldn't come back here...

The food here is different from the usual Americanized Thai food. We got a spicy duck larb salad, and it as definitely very spicy. The acidity of the salad and fried duck went along really well with the spice. 

We ate the duck with a vegetable fried rice to ease the spiciness. The mushrooms the fried rice came with were surprisingly fragrant and we didn't really need to use the spicy soy sauce that came with it.

Lastly, we also got fried minced pork balls. They were piping hot when they came, and the meat had a similar sour kick as the duck. 

The bill came out to be about 35 dollars (including a Thai iced tea) for two people, which wasn't bad considering the quality of the food and the nice atmosphere of the restaurant.

Visited here because of the Michelin star rating.  Well worth the star. The tables seem to be a little too squeezed in together. The food was flavorful and different that Hells Kitchen Thai places. Can't wait to go back.

Somtum Der
NY Manhattan LES
8pm Sunday 17th July 2016
Four Stars

Somtum Der has a current Michelin Star which is just as impressive as their food. This restaurant pops up as one of the best thai restaurants in the city. So Tiffany, her Brother, and I decided to try it out. The red walls, basket lanterns, black pleather booths, and glass jars filled with ingredients complete the look of this place. We started with the "Tum Thai" which is the classic Papaya Salad. They have several options but the pork neck one sounded delicious to me (Next time).  We asked for 1 chili and it was still spicy (which I thoroughly enjoyed). The papaya was fresh, the dressing was spicy, sour, and salty, the peanuts and green beans added crunch.  It was simple and delicious. The "Koi Goong" was a prawn salad with thinly sliced red onions, herbs, lots of spice, and roasted minced rice. It packed a lot of flavor into such a small dish.  The "Moo Ping Kati Sod" or Pork Skewers were marinated in coconut milk and grilled to perfection. It was served with rice noodles and salty, citrusy dipping sauce. The Beef Skewers were similarly good. The toasted sticky rice skewers complimented the meat superbly.  We finished the meal with "Pad Ki Mao" with pork. It is similar to drunken noodles with fried basil and a touch of heat. I am sure it could have been spicier but my dinner companions needed two diet cokes and two thai ice teas to cool their tongues.  The final bill was $87 which was not so bad. The service was a bit slow and I ate off a chipped plate which high irregular for such a high rated place.

Came here on a date. Nice cozy place and food was good for sharing.  Both of us lived spicy food and came here look for something really spicy. The food was not that spicy for us but it was more spicy than normal Thai places.

Appetizer platter: fish cake, sausage, pork. All tastes great. I just dipped everything in the spicy sauce that came with the platter. Didn't know what to do with the peanuts and some raw chili peppers.

Spicy crab pad Thai: normal pad Thai but more spicy. A bit of crab meat on top. It's pad Thai; so Generally good!

Marinated beef with Der sticky rice: nice nice nice! My date liked it a lot. Probably because it is that rare Asian dish with all protein/meat and no carbs. The beef was marinated but I didn't think it was spicy. It is more like sweet, soy sauce flavor. 
I loved the fried coconut sticky rice. Can really taste the coconut.

Sontum Der really brings a slice of Thailand into NYC. The food here is pretty spicy but you can ask for it to be toned down for you. They have the typical goto dishes (pad kee mao, etc), but the highlights are the isan food, the glutinous rice  with fried chicken/pork/beef, and the coconut rice was great.

I am a Thai American so I am more critical of Thai food than your average New Yorker. I visit Thailand twice a year so I have a very good understanding of what to expect from different regions of Thai cusine. Somtum Der is an Isan Thai restaurant, which is North Eastern Thailand, their cuisine is influenced by Cambodia and the region is known for their papaya salads, grilled meats, citrus meat salads and sticky rice. Isan has always been my favorite kind of Thai food, so it kinda pains me that this dinner was a miss. Overall, the meal was just OK to me, it was very very very clear to me that they adjusted the flavors to fit the local clientele. The flavors were Americanized, the spice level was toned down, the portions were small, and the biggest kicker for me was everything was too sweet. Also, it was dark as fuck inside so forget pictures. lol Also, turns out they have locations in Thailand, Vietnam, China and Tokyo.

The food:

Sa Poak Kai Tod Der- Der styled deep fried chicken thigh. This is one of their popular dishes and I thought it was good, the chicken had good flavor and was nicely fried without being greasy. This was my fav dish of the night.

Goong Chae Nam Pla- Thai prawn sashimi with house special green chili sauce. I was pretty surprised how much I enjoyed this dish. I normally get this as an app in most Thai restaurants since when done right, it is an explosion of flavors, this place did it right. The raw shrimp had really good flavor and it was a very good spice level but it would be too spicy for many, I did feel the dish should have had more sauce. Overall, a dish to get. And if you want it less spicy, then push some of the chilies off to the side.

Nue Rong Hai Der + Khao Ji- House special grilled marinated beef. This was the dish I was most eager to dry and it was kinda a fail. The beef was just OK, the beef fell flat. I felt the beef needed to be marinated more and the meat should have been more tender. This dish makes me sad =(

Tum Thai Kai Kem- Thai spicy papaya salad with salted egg. The salted egg is not something I normally order since the egg is pretty aggressive but this dish wasn't half bad, the flavor was good but the egg yolk made the sauce pretty chalky which was kinda off putting. I ordered this dish medium spicy and it had a quick burn but it disappeared quickly.

H'orderves Der- Samplers of Nam Sod, Moo Yor, Moo Dad Dieo, and Fried Isan Sausages. I didn't really care for this, the platter was lacking and nothing really stood out. I would skip this.

Tum Kor Moo Yang- Spicy papaya salad mixed with grilled pork neck. I normally love pork neck but the pork neck here was way too sweet. The flavor of the salad was good and the papaya salad was nice and crunchy but the sweetness of the pork neck really messed up the dish. I ordered this medium spicy as well, but this one came off more sweet than anything else.

Grilled Sticky Rice- Der's Style. Personally, I thought it was kinda silly to serve this on skewers, the flavor was OK but I thought it was too sweet and the sticky rice came out too mushy. The rice should have had a drier, more firm texture.

I went late at night (around 9PM) with 2 of my friends and we were VERY hungry. We were lucky that we didn't have to wait long to be seated. 
Service was good- the water were served right away. Because we were so hungry, all of us ordered whatever we wanted to eat and once the food came out, it filled up the table. The food came out quick and every dish was delicious. But it wasn't worth the price because the portion was small. My favorite dish is moo ping (grilled pork)! We cleared every plate. We mistakenly ordered dried suki- I've eaten better dried suki at other places.

What I would recommend for those who are going to this restaurant is the Isan food such as som tum (papaya salad), larb, and nyuen nam tok. The spicy food here are very delicious! For the dessert, I'd recommend buao loy.

I would come back to this place again.

This East Village restaurant has a funky, modern, somewhat hipster look. It looks exactly like a Thai restaurant I'd picture being in Manhattan. It's clean and thankfully doesn't reek of grease or anything. We came here looking for Isaan cuisine that we fell in love with at Zabb Elee, and lucky for us this non-conventional (for USA anyway) cuisine is catching on in NYC. All the food we ordered is the really large photos in the menu:
Tum thai kai kem (papaya salad with salted egg): This has got to have been the best papaya salad I've had in my life! It's chock full of sweet and sour flavor mixing together, with great texture too. 
Sa poak kai tod der (deep fried chicken thigh): Also, quite possibly some of the best fried chicken I've had in my life. I thought BonChon Korean fried chicken was as close as can be to heaven but I was wrong. This has a softer texture while still being crispy, with a winning mouth-watering flavor. We actually had to order a second portion after finishing one plate because we couldn't get enough of it the first time! 
Moo Ping Kati Sod (grilled pork skewers): Another amazing dish, beautifully-marinated, but not overly sweet like typical Americanized Thai food.
There are so many exciting dishes on the menu and the beautiful photos definitely help entice the viewer, but make it impossible to choose one delicacy versus another. Just come to Somtum Der for yourself and experience the mind-f*ck that this exotic menu has to offer!

I went on a Friday night with my boyfriend.  The place was casual yet hip.

The food was flavorful and spicy.  We ordered the Tum Thai, Larb Moo, Pad Ki Mao Pork & Basil, Nue Rong Hai Der - Khao Ji.
 
The Tum Thai is an original style Thai spicy papaya salad.  It had more rice powder than what I'm used to having at other Thai restaurants, which added an extra crunch to it.  

The Larb Moo is a spicy minced pork salad with vegetables and chili.  Beware, my boyfriend asked for it to be mildly spicy, but it wasn't mild at all - it was HOT!  But, I love spicy food, so it didn't bother me and it wasn't where it's too spicy that you can't taste the food.  

The Pad Ki Mao Pork & Basil is a spicy flat rice noodle that's wok fried with ground pork and basil leaves.  It also had a sweet taste to it, which was nice.

The Nue Rong Hai Der - Khao Ji is a grilled marinated beef that came with grilled sticky rice.  The beef was mildly sweet and you can taste the coconut flavoring in the sticky rice.  It was delicious.
nice service i ordered fried rice with shrimp but rice was dry

Came here for a very early dinner on Friday night. I would definitely recommend making a reservation for weekends. Not sure about the weekdays, but since this is probably the cheapest Michelin star rated restaurant in NYC, it would make sense.

The atmosphere is nice. Spacious restaurant, nicely decorated. Staff is very friendly.

I ordered their Pad Thai, which is made with crab (not chicken which is what I'm usually used to seeing). It was good, but not exceptional. Only complaint would be that the serving size is pretty small...one of the smaller servings of Pad Thai I've ever gotten.

It's been very hard for me to find a good Thai spot and this is one of the better ones I've tried so far.

Somtum Der is a mid-sized trendy Thai place where you can go for a modern/hip spin on Thai. I went with a few friends and the service was quick and friendly and wait time to get in relatively short. The food itself was delicious. I ordered the spicy basil beef which was essentially Thai basil, ground beef, and rice which made for a pleasant meal - albeit portion sizes being a bit small. I went with a few friends, one of whom was vegetarian, and we were pleasantly surprised with the vegetarian options and tastiness of the meal. Overall great place to go if you're looking for Thai with a casually upscale vibe.

Went back last night and it was just as good, AND SPICY, as the first time.  We ended up getting a lot of the same things I had the first time but we also added in some soups.  We got the chicken soup and the spicy pork cartilage soup and both were amazing.  The chicken soup was reminiscent of Tom Yum and had about 7 or 8 chicken wings in it.  So good.  The pork cartilage soup was awesome too but I preferred the chicken.  

The som tum's were delicious as expected as were the coconut pork skewers and the prawn sashimi.  Such great flavors from this place.  My old man and brother were both extremely impressed.  This place is a gem.

Still not sure if this place is michelin star worthy but food here is pretty decent! Especially the northeastern thai food! 

Get somtum and all the laab, namtok my friends! I dont thunk their pad thai or pad see ew are any better than those you can find in nyc. The point is this place is northeastern thai restaurant so order their signature dishes, which i shall warn you-- they are spicy.

Order the coconut rice on the stick! They are sooooo good and will help you when your tongue is burning from the chillis in somtum :)


The dessert was very interesting! The shaved ice was delicious and so is the grass jelly in milk!

PRAISE and RESPECT.This is THE BEST thai food I have had outside of Thailand.....period.
This place is the real deal.
Great service,food arrives fast,water glass is refilled quickly and you will need it if you order spicy!
Somtum der is Reasonably priced and authentic,which is a rarity in a sea of mediocre thai food in NYC.
They prepare the papaya salads out front in a big wooden pestle and mortar.These salads kick serious ass and are so fresh and healthy.
I have one small complaint- I wish it was a little bit brighter and well lit at as I like to look at my food when I eat it.
I can't wait to go back!

I've lots of different thai place all over and have to say this place is just plain spicy. I don't eat much spicy but my friends who are thai and eats spicy agrees.  we order a variety of salad, entrees, and dishes to share.  the salads were either too salty or too spicy, except the mushroom one as we asked to make it not spicy. sashimi shrimp was just shrimp except for the chill peppers on top so not exactly like a ceviche.  fried rice was okay. fried chicken was ok. crab meat pad thai tastes like tomato sauce with rice noodles.  The sticky rice was great the grill beef was good just a bit salty as well.  overall it was either burn your tongue or dehydrate your body from the salt. if you just want spicy food go here otherwise stay away.

My friends wanted to visit this fine establishment for a farewell party. The staff was incredibly hospitable and patient with my large crowd. #ServicePoints

Everything looked good in their photo menu and I couldn't decide on what to get. Like many of us in the yelp foodie world, I follow Mike C. religiously and saw he wrote a review.

I got the fried chicken with a side of coconut rice. That fried chicken and all of its glory incapacitated me. The whole time I thought "WHY IS THIS SO FUCKING GOOD?!" Am I allowed to cuss on yelp? But seriously the perfect combination of crispy and juicy. The sauce added some solid flavor. Heads up, your breath gets funky.

Time for bed...

Everything is good

Up until the delivery guy handed me a paper that says "TIP: CASH ONLY" so i was caught in a moment where i had to tip the guy

But actually, when ordered through yelp, tip is Always included. 

AND ALSO IT SAYS FREE DELIVERY

Came here last week with high expectations because 1) I am a hugeee Thai food lover, and 2) that Michelin Star though. Somtum Der did not disappoint, although I was not as mind-blown as I was hoping to be. 

My friend and I ordered and shared their special pad thai (Pad Thai Mun Poo), prawn sashimi with green chili sauce (Goong Chae Nam Pla), and spicy papaya salad with salted egg (Tum Thai Kai Kem). The pad thai was really delicious and fresh but not super different from other pad thai's I've had before. The prawn sashimi, on the other hand, was very different from anything I'd had before. I've never had raw shrimp, so the texture was very interesting (squishy but chewy), and the green chili sauce was SPICYYYY. My spice tolerance is on the low-medium side, and I was legitimately in pain while eating the sashimi. I could only handle a few pieces before giving up completely. However, I did enjoy the papaya salad a lot -- the spicy and tangy flavors reminded me of ceviche. Although over-hyped, it was a tasty and affordable meal, especially for a Michelin Star restaurant.

Loved Somtum Der, the best Isan Thai food I've had outside of Thailand. It is faithful to the cuisine to a T, even down to the portion sizes. I'd eat here on a regular basis if I lived in the area, the food is so delicious and affordable. I've had only so-so experiences with one star Michelin restaurants, but this pick is a winner. Can't wait to return!

My first Thai food experience it was. Busy place, we waited about 10 minutes to get a table. If your party is not complete, you won't be seated. 

They've placed many tables to meet the demand so if you do not like crowded, packed places, beware. And there is only 1 bathroom next to kitchen's entrance which makes lining up hard.

For the food, we ordered some salad, grilled meat, sticky rice, pork stuffed rolls(so spicy!). I guess due to coconut oil, everything tastes so sweet, sugary. I am Turkish so more of a kebab person :) My palate was not trained for Thai food but it is always nice to try.

Service was fast considering the crowd and reasonably priced place.

Ridiculously delicious. I visited Thailand a couple times and ate good Thai food. This place was BETTER. 

We had a large group of 8. It's awesome to come with a big group so you can try a lot of things. Things we ordered: pad see ew, papaya salad, fried chicken, pad thai, fried rice with prawns, fried sausages. 

Literally everything was heaven in each bite. It can be a bit on the spicy side so beware of tiny chilis.

Ahh, northern Thai at such an affordable price in NYV!? Triple yes!

Came here on a whim with 4 other people (2 were familiar with the place, 3 of us were not). We got promptly seated even for a relatively large group. We came just in time as the restaurant immediately filled up.

We had a plethora of food: salted crab papaya salad, egg papaya salad, fried duck salad, larb, pad Thai, pad kee Mao, and longan juices all around.

I was beyond thrilled to have the salted crab papaya salad. Having tried the street food version in Pai in Thailand, I didn't think I could find another one again! It was super flavorful (as was all the other dishes). 

My favorite had to have been the Pad kee Mao. I know, I know it's very basic but it hits the spot every time. I use it as my baseline wherever I go. Boy, it was hot, flavorful, and hearty.

Also where ever can you get longan juice!? Sweet and tasty! 

Highly recommend. Also, I didn't know this at the time but I can definitely understand why, this restaurant has 1 Michelin star. Keep kicking butt SomTomDer !

This place gets BUSY, but I thought it was worth the wait (45 mins at an "off dining" time around 8:30 on a Sunday).

Everything we ordered was so flavorful and delicious: pad thai, coconut beef skewers, papaya salad and deep fried chicken thighs. Everything was also VERY spicy though (even though we asked for medium spice), but the coconut rice toned down the spice a bit.

They had a fun twist on panna cotta - thai tea with condensed milk. Not too sweet and just the right portion size to complete our meal.

Decently priced for amazing food and prompt service, no complaints here!

We arrived for dinner at 10pm since we wanted to beat the queue. Sadly the grilled marinated beef we ordered had been reheated and served to us - it tasted chewy, stale and cold. We knew we would have a bad stomach if we ate anymore since it just tasted wrong. The papaya salad was not bad though. Quite shameful to award a restaurant that does this with a michelin star. Avoid this place like the plague.

After moving to NYC, I have been looking for a good Thai restaurant beyond the usual pad thais and pad see ews. My friend introduced me to this place and I am hooked! I have now been here twice and I will definitely be coming back. My repertoire here would be the salted egg papaya salad, deep fried chicken thighs and the kuay tieo pad see ew. I've tried the beef skewers and their various soups but they tasted pretty average. If we could give half points, I would've knocked off 1/2 a star because it gets pretty loud and the wait could get pretty long. Bottom line: Solid place with good vibes.

Probably some of the best Thai food I have had. I ordered a noodle dish, cannot recall the name, but the waitress was more than happy to substitute the meat/seafood for vegetables & tofu. There are many dishes that can be made vegetarian friendly!My dish wasn't spicy but they brought sauce on the side for me to add in. 

Would highly recommend! The staff was friendly & the food was good. Had to wait ~30 minutes for a table but that's expected on a Friday night.

Liked it, didn't love it. We were lucky to come at an off hour (1:30 PM on a Saturday) and were seated right away, although the restaurant was packed by the time we finished our late lunch and walked out. We had their fried chicken, beef skewers, and pad thai with beef (originally comes with crabmeat). I thought their chicken and skewers were well seasoned. Their food/sauce is definitely on the spicier side. Although I usually handle spicy pretty well, my tummy is still simmering from the heat about two hours after our meal ended. 

I would say their pad thai was their weakest dish by far. I appreciated that it wasn't as oily as some restaurants make it, but it was quite bland. I'm not sure if our beef substitution had anything to do with it. 

We had also ordered the tum thai kai kem, their papapa salad with egg, but our waitress must've missed it :(... I was really looking forward to trying that particular dish. We were so full that we didn't ask for it again. 

I would come here again if I'm in the area, but wouldn't go out of my way for it.

Came here around 7 on a thursday night with a friend and the place was packed! Make sure you make a reservation or come early to put your name down otherwise you will be looking at an around an hour wait. We decided to settle for two seats at the bar, which was fine with me because it had better lighting for my pictures anyways. 

It would've taken us forever to decide what to get if we didn't already look at the menu outside because everything on the menu sounded so good. Once we sat down we ordered the spicy papaya salad with salted egg, deep fried chicken thigh, pad ki mao, grilled sticky rice, and thai iced teas. Everything was delicious! The spicy papaya salad was very refreshing and addicting. Wish there was a little more though because we ate it pretty fast. I was afraid of the chicken being too fried, but it was just the perfect amount. Crispy on the outside, tender on the inside. The pad ki mao was very flavorful without being overly salty. Would highly recommend it! I loved the texture of the sticky rice. It didn't have much taste to it so I ate it with the fried chicken. The thai iced tea was a perfect touch to balance out the spiciness of the food.

Can't wait to come back and try the other items on the menu.

We LOVED this restaurant! Having spent years in Southeast Asia I'm often disappointed in "americanized" Thai restaurants.  Somtum Der did not disappoint.  The small plates are plenty to share and we ordered two per person and couldn't finish all the food. The papaya salads are phenomenal and very spicy. The grilled marinated beef - delicious, fried spring rolls also delicious but heavy on the coriander for those of you who aren't fans,  you might not want to share the fried chicken it's so good. The chicken soup with herbs is difficult to share altho they helpfully provide small bowls - but is so good you won't want to share anyway. Pad Thai is as good as you will have anywhere and the fried rice with crabmeat was very tasty.  Go in a group so you can order alot of different dishes.  So incredibly worth it and very reasonably priced.
This place was amazing. I went here on a Saturday night and loved the design and the food was amazing! Highly recommended.

A section of the menu entitled Central Thai includes familiar Pad Thai dishes, which can steer the uninitiated off the beaten path. After all, the point of eating at Somtum Der is to order the restaurant's specialties.

I can spy the kitchen huddled around our first dish, the Gaeng Om Kai, a large bowl of spicy chicken soup with herbs, from my seat across the dining room. A server gives me a better look when she presses through the kitchen doors to get the plate and deliver it to our table. She places two ramekin-sized serving bowls for me and a friend to share, and we ladle an aromatic spoonful for each other. I happen to like the kick, and beyond the spiciness are hints of dill, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves, tenderly cooked. The chicken is easily stripped from the bone with a fork and added to the steaming mixture.

In no time, the waitress returned with a series of small plates: Moo Ping Kati Sod, a sweet coconut-marinated pork skewer that comes with three small nests of thin rice noodles; Larb Ped, a spicy salad of minced duck, green vegetables, and red chilies; and Tum Thai, a signature papaya salad with green beans, shrimp, and crunchy peanuts. Each is a stand-alone, but what I return to is the side of grilled sticky rice on bamboo skewers to ease my palate. They are sweet enough for me to eat endlessly as dessert if I tried.

Sa Poak Kai Tod Der, a der-style deep-fried chicken thigh, is juicy and tender at its core, and encased in a layer of perfectly crisp skin. It comes with a side of the restaurant's house chili sauce, but the meat is delicious enough on its own to pick at and eat without condiments. By far, it is one of the city's best fried chicken dishes.

I dare to try the Thai delicacy "mum," added to the menu and highly displayed to celebrate the restaurant's second-year anniversary, after finding out that the dish can only be found in two locations in Thailand, in Ban Pai and Muang Phol districts in Khon Kaen and in the Sriboonruang district in Nong Bua Lamphu. These sausage lookalikes are stuffed with minced pork or beef, liver, garlic, and animal entrails, and hung by street vendors for sale along the famed Friendship Highway. Provided cabbage, parsley, and garlic, I crumble up a few pieces together and delicately assemble my first bite. It is garlicky, but has darker undertones of aged meat, and I suspect it is an acquired taste.

When dessert comes don't be intimidated by the pink snow ice with syrup, which at the table may reach eye level. It floats like a cloud on white bread, easily defeated with friends. A scoop of my spoon glides through it like hot butter, and it tastes vaguely of bubblegum. I try not to cause an avalanche.

Also try the Thai tea panna cotta with condensed milk. The table beside us purred after inhaling the tiny dessert.

Ordered take out from here because the last time I tried to come on a Saturday night, the line was out the door. Couldn't wait, but really wanted to try their food. I've passed by this place so many times and can't believe I've never tried their food. I ordered the pad see ew, which is my Thai favorite. This is the dish I always use to compare Thai restaurant. Also ordered a pad kee Mao and the taro in condensed milk dessert with 2 Thai iced teas. The pad see ew was sooooooo good. It was full of flavor and it was so on point! This place made it with shrimp and squid which was interesting. Since I like seafood in general, I didn't mind it one bit. The pad Kee Mao was also really good. This place made it with ground beef which I'm not sure we liked, but besides that, the dish was still good. I thought the taro dessert was way too sweet. I definitely won't be eating that again. I also didn't taste much taro. I thought there would be taro pieces, but I ate mochi instead so I'm not sure why it was called taro dessert. I definitely will come back here some time for dinner or lunch! Great Thai place!

My two Thai roommates recommended me this thai joint in east village. They said it was the most authentic Thai they've had, and is their go to restaurant when they're craving food from home. Absolutely delicious! The ingredients in each dish is so different from the standard pad Thai or kee Mao. I always get the kuay tieo pad see eiw talay and a papaya salad to share with the table. The drinks are also very reasonably priced! A bottle of wine is only about 35 dollars. Great for dates!

Went here with my sister on a Monday afternoon and ordered the duck larb, pad see ew, and Thai iced tea.  IT WAS DELICIOUS!! The portions were small but perfect in the sense where I didn't end up overeating and having to drag myself out of there with all the extra weight. The Thai iced tea was so good, not too sweet, would definitely recommend this place !

Just had dinner here and the food was 4* for sure but the service & experience, only 2.

Be warned, if you come here before they take down the Halloween decorations - do not eat near the spiderwebs! I got so much of that cotton stringy stuff on my silverware and in my food (It stretches and becomes practically invisible and sticks to your clothes and plates!). We told management but they didn't make any moves to really fix the problem.

For the food: GRILLED STICKY RICE was amazing, and a great counterpoint to our pork larb with vegetables. (LARB IS EXTREMELY SPICY - we ordered medium spice and were blown away!)

Beef skewers and salt egg somtum also delicious.

I just wish I hadn't eaten the decor. And also that they hadn't called a few hours earlier that day to ask us to change our reservation time. But the great food pretty much made up for it.

Pricing seems a bit high for the amount of food you get. I wish they'd either lower the prices slightly or increase the portions more. The main part of the entrees don't have to be a lot more but the vermicelli or rice that they give you is very disproportionate. 

Tonight I ordered the por pia larb moo which was a little spicy even though I ordered it mild so I wish they offered sauce options instead of just the one they send. I would have preferred a sweet chili sauce to cut the spice. $8 for 4 was ok but I wish it was a little cheaper like $6 for 4 or $8 for 5 or 6. 

I also got the moo ping Kati sod which was a good but slightly overcooked. For $12 to get 3 skewers, they were very cheap with the vermicelli that came with it and I wish they would have given 3x the amount of vermicelli. I portioned it out and it left me wanting more. I could have eaten all of the vermicelli they gave me with just 1 of the skewers. 

I would order from them again but hope that they read this review and take my suggestions into consideration.
Awesome authentic Thai food. Watch out for the spice levels! Medium spiced Larb salad was actually pretty darn spicy.

Not as good as I expected for a Michelin Star.

Came here for a friend's birthday dinner.

We ordered couples dishes. 

The grilled sticky rice - must get - unique with a little sweet flavor - our favorite

Everything else just meh

The fruit flies were all over our dishes while we were eating.  restaurant grade pending when we were there - should've known better not to go in.

No I don't think I will come back

Had the marinated beef with sticky rice and I think I fell in love. The beef was perfectly cooked and marinated and came with a delicious dipping sauce that had a little spicy-citrus kick to it. Really quiet and friendly atmosphere that has a romantic aura to it because of the dimmed lights and candles. Perfect date spot.

The food is great, and the service is quick. 
It is not pricy at all, and considering the fact it's a 1 star micheline restaurant, one can say it's even cheap. 
The cons: the menu is not very big, so you can't enjoy a wide variety of Thai dishes. 
The seating is not very comfortable, you sit on wooden benches. 
And the worst thing: they INCLUDED the service in the bill (18%), which is unacceptable.
Very friendly and welcoming staff. Nice ambiance and food was very good. Was not the best thai I have had, but still very good.

In all honesty, I came upon Somtum Der as a result of Yelping for Gai Yang (Thai grilled chicken) which, hysterically, Somtum Der actually doesn't serve. But that's ok. 

I thoroughly enjoyed it and even went back a second time. In all, we had a number of dishes. The stars (tasted and presented properly) included the following:
-Lard duck
-Namtok beef (spicy beef salad)
-Isarn sausage (omg)

The honorable mentions included the moo ping (which are way larger than most photos led them to be), the krapow, and the desserts. Of course, we did have the som tum (poo paraa - not for novices) which was the least liked out of all the dishes.

Until the next.
One of my favorite thai places in New York. Delicious, authentic, and pretty cheap.

I'm a bit surprised this place had a Michelin Star. Don't get me wrong, it was good but not mind blowing. 

I appreciated that they were not your typical Thai restaurant but northern Thai and focused on that type of cuisine. In fact there was no curry on the menu. 

They have an awesome variety of somtum, or papaya salad. They even have a bar for papaya salad in which it is made to order fresh in the traditional style with a huge mortar and pestle. 

We ordered:
Tum Pla Too- papaya salad with mackerel. It was good until- damnnnnn this is spicy! We ordered three star spicy but I gulped down my Thai iced tea so fast was unable to enjoy the salad, and will admit that I do have a fair spice tolerance. It's probably the freshly ground red chiles. It came with coconut rice which was pretty good, although I wish I could've tasted it before my tongue was set on fire.

Deep fried chicken Thai (Sa Poak Kai Tod Der)- which was crispy and seasoned well. It came with a sauce that was too salty for my liking. 

Lara Hed Kao Kuo (minced mushroom salad)- this was made with rice and fresh peppermint and when eating it tasted very earthy and natural, made with all fresh ingredients. The downside however was that the spices used in this weren't so finely minced. I kept getting chile chunks stalled in my throat that I would have to wash down. 

Pad Thai Mun Poo- Pad thai with crab meat. This was pretty good, probably my favorite out of the things we ordered. It was also three star spicy but totally edible. It was sweet and tangy like pad thai is supposed to be. 

Taro in condensed coconut milk- I love taro and I love coconut milk. This was a warm dessert with, well, taro in coconut milk. It was good but I've had better. It had a sour taste which I did not like not sure if that is the way it is meant to be or what. 

All in all I enjoyed trying a different type of Thai cuisine. Prices were reasonable honestly for a Michelin rated restaurant. I will say that reservations are difficult to secure on Friday and Saturday, they are booked months (!) in advance. We had no problem securing a Sunday reservation, the place had many open tables at 6pm, all filled by 7pm though.

I wasn't even aware this was a Michelin-starred restaurant until it was mentioned to me. Now that's not a bad thing, heck I don't particularly go out of y way to find these. How did I stumble upon this gem? Solely from being asked to join some other fellow human beings for a meal. 

With that said I did do a little research on it before going. Namely just seeing what kind of food it was. That was what solidified my visit to this rather unique (in NY) establishment. They serve Isan region Thai food, interesting stuff. That's the thing though, it makes it difficult for me to review a restaurant like this because I've never had such food before.

The food, let's get on to that. I'm sure it feels better eating this kind of food in the hotter months (Thailand is a fairly hot place after all). I don't particularly enjoy lukewarm or often cold food in the cooler months, especially when I have a good amount of it.

Amount, I see a good amount of people complaining about portion size. This here is the little dilemma you run into here. Is the food good enough to warrant it's price and portion size? Debatable, the sizes aren't small 5 star restaurant, but they are on the smaller side.

I'm not going to go into what I got as I have no idea how to pronounce them but I can note a couple things throughout the food. The taste itself is rather unique, fresh and often spicy is what you are presented with. In other times you get something really salty. They really have the flavors on blast here.

With no complaints it would seem that a 5 star is deserved. However there just isn't anything particularly mind blowing here. I tend to think that when I visit Thailand food there will on average be just as good if not better. A restaurant deserving of 5 stars would just be a bit cheaper, or contain an experience that I would think is difficult to find elsewhere in the world.

WARNING: there was a used bandaid in my water...........

Gross. Health hazard. The manager offered us 50% off our meal after we told them. I was offended they didn't think this was a huge deal. They were calm and rude and did not deal with it appropriately. After arguing for 20 min, they offered us a free meal, because we were in rage. Unprofessional.

No wonder they have a pending review for sanitary and cleanliness......

Came along to this place when walking around. Terrible music, menu does not reflect the food, and the waiters were constantly hovering and quite rude. 

Food was edible but not likable.

I'm not one to write bad reviews, but please decide to go to another restaurant. I warn you.

Cozy, dimly lit dining room with really delicious food!  My tiny complaints were that they started  us with the spiciest of our dishes which took away from some of the more subtle dishes that followed, and I felt the pacing of the service (food to the table) was a bit overwhelming - we ordered 5 dishes between the two of us and we had 4 come at once.  That said, everything else was terrific - bright flavors, nice spice level (we asked for medium) and friendly service.
We had the Larb Ped/minced duck salad - this was the spiciest plate of the evening but with a nice hit of citrus and cilantro for balance.  I loved it but just wished it could have been served after some of the lighter, less aggressive dishes.  The Der Style Fried Chicken was cooked perfectly with a crispy, light batter, very moist meat, and a tangy, sweet and slightly spicy dipping sauce.   Nue Rong Hai Der + khao Ji- House special grilled marinated beef- was good and served with sticky rice skewers which proved helpful in putting out some of the fire of the larb ped.  The meat was not the most tender and cooked a little more than I would typically request.  This was maybe our least favorite (but not terrible).  Tum Thai Kai Kem - Thai spicy papaya salad with salted egg- was one of my favorite dishes of the night.  Loved the sweet/salty/citrusy combo of the papaya, peanuts and lime dressing.  Pad ki mao pork and basil- I didn't detect much spice here, but this was a very satisfying dish none the less.  The crispy basil was a nice touch for both taste and texture.  Looking forward to coming back!

Absolutely in love with this Thai place, I came here as I saw it was a Michelin one star and it wasn't difficult to make a reservation, besides the grilled sticky rice on Yelp looked irresistible!  

Came here with my friend who also love Thai food, we ordered Green Papaya Salad, Thai Prawn Sashimi, Green Curry with chicken, Tom Yum soup and Grill Sticky Rice. Everything was absolutely delicious and I was particularly in love with the Thai Prawn Sashimi, it's not easy to find in the city. 

The service here is very friendly, fast and attentive as well, we want to come back here again to try other things!!!!

Hello my deliciousness!  This place is a must if you're around the area, heck, if you're not in the area, make your way there!  A friend of mine had been raving about this place as not being your basic Thai place- it's Isaan Thai- the northeastern part of Thailand.  

The plates are smaller albeit packed with a lot of flavor.  I typically eat very spicy but on this occasion I went with friends which can't tolerate the heat like I do so sadly, I had to eat medium spice.  Medium spice to me had no heat but again, my tolerance level is out of this world (per my friends).  One of my friends said that the medium spice level was perfect and one more level up and he would not have enjoyed it.  

Food comes out quick! 

I ate here before knowing it was a one star Michelin rated restaurant.  I walked in during Xmas week and there was no wait but I can't speak about the wait when the city is back in full swing.  

Definitely will be back to try out other dishes.
Felt like I was back in Asia. Food is freaking good. An explosion of flavors in your mouth. What's not to like. And it's "cheap" for what you get.

Horrible food. Horrible service. Waiters were too busy to care and food came out at all different times. Took over an hour for dishes to come out separately. Food was salty and all seasoned with the same spice. Better go else where for your Thai fix.

My previous experience here awhile back wasn't so good, I recall getting a catfish soup and it was just beyond spicy for me to handle.

Now a couple of years later, I come back to give it another go. And this time, the experience was much better, however, it wasn't the best Thai I have had in NYC.

On the 2nd day of the New Year 2017, and after being filled with too much mofongo, we wanted something on a lighter side, with kick and flavor, so naturally Thai made sense. 

Just a note that during the holidays in NYC, places which you would never be able to get a table within reasonable hours are all now available because everyone has gone elsewhere. We were seated immediately, so that was awesome. 

For appetizers, we ordered the bamboo shoot salad. This dish was excellent and highly recommend it. Make sure to ask for a side of rice as this dish is spicy and salty. I ordered the flat noodle with shrimp and calamari and my date ordered the grilled beef strips. My date states the beef strips were just ok, nothing memorable. I would also say that the flat noodle I ordered was decent, but nothing that would make me come back.

Overall, the best dish would be the bamboo shoot salad, however, the main dishes are a reasonable portion, so you will have another meal of mediocre food. 

The atmosphere is chill and wait staff were prompt and courteous and this place can seat a party of 4 comfortably. 

I could see myself coming back, but it wouldn't be a destination dining, just a good place to meet up with friends and have a solid meal.

Michelin Star-rated Thai restaurant that came highly recommended from a friend. And at about the same price as many other thai spots, it seemed like a no-brainer to go here and get a Michelin star under the belt as well. Somtum Der is best enjoyed family style, and instead of focusing on the more common thai dishes(noodle-based dishes, curries, etc.), you really want to diversify and get their northern thai specialties. We split the Larb pla Dook yang, Larb tod, and wok-fried seafood suki. The dishes were on the smaller side, but the flavors were all incredible, with a great balance between spice and fresh herbs and traditional thai tastes. Would be ready to come back and try out some more dishes, as it seems we missed some of the more popular ones including any of the namesake papaya salads, the fried chicken, the marinated beef and pork skewers, and grilled sticky rice.

Super delicious especially if you love spicy food as much as me. Service always friendly. Get the fried chicken thighs! And I like the grilled coconut sticky rice! Pair with a spicy, tangy larb and YUM

nice ambiance. great and friendly service. food is served up fast. wide variety of choices on the menu and dishes you're not likely to find at most American Thai restaurants. their specialities are well cooked and presented. reasonably priced.
I call to order food for delivered.the food is very delicious But the amount of papaya salad is very small compared to the price.

Didn't love this place despite the Michelin star. Crowded had to wait  15-20 min despite our reservation. The papaya salads was good but the service was terrible. They forgot to bring out half our meal and when our food came out it wasn't even warm. We had the crab pad Thai which was standard. Don't think I would go back

So spicy and so good.  There was plenty of space for a late afternoon lunch and food came out quickly.  The Thai lemon iced tea had great flavor and thankfully, a good degree of sweetness which I was later very thankful for.  We ordered the Tum Thai with salted egg salad (spicy papaya salad), Nam Tok Mue (spicy grilled beef with toasted rice), and Pad Ki Mao with pork and basil.  

We ordered everything "medium" spicy.  For most without Thai palates, I think medium = wicked spicy.  I had a hard time with the grilled beef as my mouth was on fire after a few bites.  Before this happened, I could appreciate the citrus and fish sauce flavors.  After?  I drank every bit of sweet tea on the table and was beet red and sweaty.  My husband pretty much licked the plate clean.  My favorite was the Pad Ki Mao - I love big noodles - the fatter the phatter.  The ground pork was tasty and seasoned and the noodles just sucked up the flavor.  I was also a big fan of the salad.  The sweetness and citrus helped mediate the fire from the beef - but don't get me wrong, it had its own heat as well.  The salted egg had a creamy, custardy yet funky taste that paired well with the crunch of the papaya and peanuts.  

All three dishes were standouts - as others have said, if you are looking for Pad Thai and satay, this is not your place.  If you're looking for Thai adventure, highly recommended.
Spectacular. Spicy, flavorful, and delicious. Maybe one of the best Thai places in the city.

We ordered: Larb Pla Dook Yang {spicy minced grilled catfish salad}, Larb Hed Kao Kuo {minced mushroom salad with peppermint, lime and freshly roasted rice}, Goong Chae Nam Pla {Thai prawn sashimi with house special green chili sauce}, Pad Thai Mun Poo {special pad Thai made with crabmeat and crab paste with our home-styled sauce}, Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay {Thai styled fried flat noodles with shrimp and calamari}, and Sa Poak Kai Tod Der {deep-fried chicken thigh}.  

* * *

6 selections was the right amount of food for the 3 of us.  All were tasty and at varying degrees of spiciness.  The raw prawn dish was so perfectly flavored, and the chicken thigh was juicy and well-seasoned.  I preferred the catfish salad over the mushroom salad.  The catfish salad had a more interesting texture and complex flavor profile; the mushroom salad was a little too spicy although we ordered it 'mild'.  Our 2 noodle choices were solid and were pretty big portions.  We finished with the shaved iced dessert but it was nothing special.

Service was a little spotty and it was hard to get a server's attention, but everyone was polite throughout.  I also wish our waters were refilled more regularly, particularly as everything was so spicy!  The few mixed drinks we had were good, too.

* * *

RECOMMENDED.

This was honestly the spiciest food I've ever had before in my entire life. I'm not even positive it was good because it was so spicy. It was hotter than the 7th circle of hell. I ordered off Seamless and got: Tum Thai (spicy papaya salad), Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (deep fried chicken thigh), Khao Pad Kraprao Moo (fried pork with Thai basil and rice), Pad Thai Mun Poo (pad thai with crabmeat), and the Grilled Sticky Rice. The total came to slightly over $60 with tax and tip which I thought was totally reasonable for the quantity and quality of food. 

I'm not quite sure what exactly was the culprit in terms of spiciness - the Tum Thai and the Khao Pad Kraprao Moo were definitely the hottest but I'm not sure what did me in. I can't stress enough - I never thought I had particular sensitive taste buds but I have truly never felt more American than when I was eating this meal. Both were delicious, but holy shit I should have asked for them super mild. The Sa Poak Kai Tod Der was amazing and was a nice way of cutting the spiciness. The Pad Thai Mun Poo was hot, but totally manageable by my standards, and was phenomenal. The Grilled Sticky Rice came on skewers and were a yummy sweet dessert. Portion sizes were pretty large - for two people, we ordered way too much food and had a ton of leftovers. 

Overall, I would totally order again, but HEED MY WARNING: it is veritably hot. Like if you have any doubt at all about your ability to handle extremely spicy food, ask for it mild or milder. Highly recommend the Sa Poak Kai Tod Der - the chicken was super tender and flavorful and the dipping sauce was delish. It was totally not the Thai food I'm used to, but was a welcome change and I look forward to including Somtum Der into my Seamless rotation.

Had great takeout from here - mackerel salad with coconut rice and a side of fried noodles. It was more than enough food and I had a ton of leftovers. The salad was delicious, if a little spicy for me, and the rice was just perfect. All rice should be coconut rice!!

100% recommend!! This place is pricey, but SO GOOD. Some Thai places don't use the full potential of the Thai spices, but this place has every flavor imaginable. We got the yum nue lai, and it's got the perfect amount of sour and spicy garlicness. We also got the fried chicken, which we ate in 2 seconds and debated getting another one. We also got chefs signature wok fried seafood suki, and also so delicious. We all got a bowl of the coconut jasmine rice, and it was so fresh and fragrant and soft. For sure my favorite Thai spot in the city. The only issue is that the portion sizes are a bit small, so you have to order lots of dishes to get full.

One Michelin Starred restaurant that serves authentic Northern Thai cuisine with dishes mostly under $15? What a catch! My friends and I were in cravings of some Thai food and heard this place does the wonder. We arrived around 7:30pm on a Monday evening and were able to be seated promptly at a table facing the entrance.

Restaurant itself is dimly lit with bamboo light fixtures, along with wooden walls, dining tables and benches that gives a casual, homey vibe with some cozy atmosphere. The menu features huge food pictures and detailed descriptions, makes it so much easier to decide as you will be able to see how your dishes look even before you order. We ordered several dishes to share - started off with Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (Deep fried chicken thigh), Larb Pla Dook Yang (Spicy minced grilled catfish salad), Goong Chae Nam Pla (Thai prawn sashimi with house special green chili sauce) and Larb Hed Kao Kuo (Minced mushroom salad with peppermint, lime, and freshly roasted rice) as our appetizer. As for cocktails we order the Thai cocktail, punch and lycheetini.

Chicken thigh was excellent - juicy, crispy and tender. Prawn sashimi was delicious - really fresh and tasty, with lots of herbs and spices that brings out the freshness and flavors. The two salads were unexpectedly spicy (we requested to prepare in mild when we ordered) -  it was the kind of spiciness that doesn't hit you immediately, but slowly spreads through your tongue (with a 10 second delayed reaction) and set your mouth on fire that last continuously for the next 5 minutes. I was chugging ice water and my drink to soothe the spiciness but the moment I try to lift my lips off the glass, it called for help and I basically had to rest my tongue with an ice cube to numb this fire hot burning sensation from the spice. 

For main course we got Pad Thai Mun Poo (special Pad Thai made with crab meat and crab paste) and Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay (Thai styled fried flat noodles with shrimp and calamari) to share. The pad thai was phenomenal and surprisingly amazing! I was expecting your-average-American-style pad thai but this, IS definitely something else. The crab meat and that specialty house-styled sauce (its gotta be a secret recipe!) brings out the best characteristics and flavor of the rice noodles and despite my tongue being on fire, I was still able to taste the explosive flavor of this wonderful dish! The pad see eiw was also prepared in a Northern Thai style and it is not sweet (like the Americanized flavor) but instead reminds me of the dishes that I had when I traveled to Thailand a few years back (tears of joy). We ended our dinner with dessert (the snow ice with syrup, serve with condense milk, red beans, and bread) which however wasn't anything spectacular to our taste-buds. 

This place is as authentic as it can get! Being able to eat something so authentic that brings back memories of Thailand, that is a first ever in the USA and boy I am so glad that we picked this restaurant for dinner! I highly recommend but be warned for the SPICINESS!!!! *FIRE*

Came back again to get their super steal of a lunch special!

There is only one lunch special that includes a small papaya salad and it's $12, comes with sticky rice and deep fried chicken thigh (sa poak kai tod der).

The other lunch special, for $10, you get a choice of any main with a drink of your choice.

My friend and I shared the tum Thai, original papaya salad, and we enjoyed this very much. They're famous for the version with salted egg and I tried that the last time I came, but I felt that it was too salty for me, so the original one was perfect.

For my main, I ordered the chef's signature wok fried seafood suki. Came with a heaping amount of seafood! Not like most places that give more noodles or rice than protein. SO GOOD. Totally recommend. For my drink, I got the lemongrass juice. Very good as well but too sweet for my taste so I asked them to give me half and add water to it, and then it was just right. Super refreshing and nice because my dish came out piping hot. 

My friend ordered the fried rice with prawns, meat, and eggs (khao pad goong) and it did not disappoint either. HUGE PERFECT TOWER OF FRIED RICE! Especially when you broke it apart. She had to take the rest home. It's the fried rice of any fried rice lover's dream. Fluffy rice that's got that hint of burnt taste from the wok, and the perfect mix of eggs.. mmmmmm. She got the Thai iced tea with milk and liked it so much she ordered another one to go.

Still my favorite Thai restaurant in NYC. It's honestly my goal to try everything on their menu. It will be done. My only wish is that they had more options on their lunch menu that included their papaya salad!!!
This place has legit proper Thai food. Might be too spicy for white people though.

This is the place to go for authentic northeastern Thai food!  My go to item would be the grilled marinated beef or pork.  The meat is tender, flavorful, and has a slight crunchy topping.  It comes with 2 sticky rice grilled on a stick.  I've also tried the mushroom soup and they really do not skimp on the mushroom.  The seafood suki is also another item i'd recommend.  The suki sauce is incredible.  I would order a side of coconut sticky rice to go with this.  
You can request non-spicy/mild for dishes...otherwise prepare for your mouth to be on fire. 
The portion sizes are small but each dish is packed with flavor.
Sometimes I sit at the bar and eat until my belly is on the verge of exploding, and then order some more grilled sticky rice.

Ordered the Khao Pad Kraprao Nue i.e. fried beef with basil and fried rice. Guess I was expecting something different, like beef strips rather than ground beef. Also not the thai fried rice I'm normally used to, pretty salty, didn't pack that much flavor in my opinion.
The egg that topped it however was well cooked.
Surprised this is Michelin starred place, maybe it was just this dish, I guess I'll come back to try another dish cos of the Michelin star...
Portion of this dish was kinda on the small side too...
Great happy hour specials on snacks and drinks so try and get the before 7! The service is a 3 but the fried rice, larb tod, grilled pork, and sticky rice are a 5!

So so good. this place is a great change of pace from your typical pad thai noodles and chicken satay.

come if you love spicy food. 
everything is amazingly flavorful. (you'll be mad thirsty after from the sodium content but so so worth it)

Recommend:
thai prawn sashimi 
coconut milk marinated pork skewers
pork neck papaya salad
It's pretty pricey and the portion was small. But the foods were really tasty and delicious!!! Highly recommended!

Excellent food! Been looking for an authentic Thai restaurant and I've been to Thailand countless times, able to differentiate amateur/ fusion to authentic. I can't be happier when I found Somtum Der.  The papaya salad is to die for! The grilled pork, sticky rice ...just all that's on the menu. Love it!!!

Yum! Super tasty, a Thai friend took me so its pretty authentic and there is one in Silom Bangkok too-- it's fast paced, dishes come out quickly-- it is very flavorful-- you can get dishes in fireball spicy if you want! Phew~ she loves her food that way but for me a weak Korean medium spice was pretty intense too. They have wine and beer~ A must try in the east village!

Yummy Thai food!  Several "pre-fixe" type options make it easy to try a few different types of food from the menu.  Very casual atmosphere, and friendly staff.  Overall, the food is more unique than other Thai spots in the EV.

It is impossible to leave Somtum Der without feeling ripped off.  Although the tastes are authentic Northeastern Thai, the portions are pathetically small. So don't be lulled by the $10 to $13 price range. You'll be receiving tapas-sized bites. The only large dish --chicken thigh--turned out to be a labor-intensive chore. It arrived hacked into small strips, with all small bones intact. Not fun trying to find them before they get stuck in your throat. Somtum Der is also not a space designed for leisurely dining. The tables against the wall are less than a foot apart and the center area consists of long high-school cafeteria shared --and backless-- stool seating.
