The message in the seating is "Eat quickly and get out or your butt and legs will go numb from the horrid seating. The busboys were super alert in clearing tables and refilling ice water. But the wait staff were frosty and perfunctory in explaining dishes both, during ordering and when the plates arrived --all at once.
Michelin star restaurant! Very reasonable price and very authentic. The highlight menu is the "Papaya Salad" with sticky rice.
Amazing food and staff. Definitely can't get better Thai in the city. I visit every time I'm near LES
Came in and ordered the duck larb, coconut rice, pad see eiw, and tum Thai. Everything was spicy and delicious. Be warned that anything you wear here will smell of Thai for months to come.
The food here is so scrumptious lol. The meals are fresh and the variety of the dishes are superb. Visited last summer  and will definitely go again soon

I could have Thai food every. single. day. If I could eat at Somtum Der every day, I'd be a happy chick.

I came here last night after taking a Flywheel class with a friend, which gave me all the excuses to eat noodles. Although this was just a friend date, I could tell upon walking in that this would be a good place to go for date with a significant other as well. 

We shared a total of four dishes together: the salty egg papaya salad, glass noodle seafood "salad," the grilled marinated pork, and pad thai munpoo. This was the perfect amount of food, where we each ended up only paying ~$34 with tip (no drinks though)

My favorite was the pad thai, which unlike your typical pad thai that can taste sweet (overly so), this was savory and had a good meat to noodle ratio. The papaya salad and marinated pork flavored with nice spices and Thai sauces were also good. The pork came with a side of sticky coconut rice, which was a nice treat to have.

One disappointment was the glass noodle dish. Onions and scallions make me sick, so I made sure to ask for them to leave those ingredients out multiple times, but they forgot to do that for the glass noodle dish. I had enough other food to enjoy, so it wasn't as big of a deal.

I'm seeing a lot of rave reviews about the lunch special, so I'll have to come back for that.

The restaurant is not located close to any subway station. However you won't be disappointed to have food in this Thai restaurant.  They have happy hours with half price for every type of drinks.  It's a big plus. The food is very delicious.   The fried chicken I had was my best choice. I love the way how the rice is placed in a bamboo container.
The restaurant on my top list. The pork face  meat and coconut sticky rice are heavenly great. Can not ask for more.

Very authentic! I am from Thailand also from the same culture of isaan food. I found this place so real -- they have right ingredients and make it out so well. My favorite is bamboo salad, and Tum mursur not recommend for everyone. But try duck salad and those protein salad. I am isaan girl and I am  isaan chef, I found this kitchen is comfort isaan food!
The people who served us we're very kind. They have incredible rices. I ordered the sticky rice and it was incredibly good incredibly sticky and not overly sweet.
Absolutely amazing food but this one waiter kept taking people's dishes/drinks away before they were finished. Rude!

When you first walk in you catch a whiff of the fish sauce and you rethink the decision. But when you sit down you don't regret it. We started with the spicy duck salad and usually I can take a lot of spicy food but this is tearing mouth watering spicy. We then ordered the fried chicken which was amazing but not one of a kind. 

The grilled pork however was freaking delicious! It was tender, flavorful and amazing. Had a light coconut taste to it as well. We also order the sticky coconut rice which was crack! All in all such a good experience highly recommended.

It's easy to find food in NYC but finding really really good food can be harder. Somtum Der - you nailed it! 

I came with a 4 friends and we ordered around 6 dishes. A good amount I'd say. Everything was packed with flavor and if you like spicy food then you're going to like this!

My favorites from the meal: 
1) Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (fried chicken thigh) - not much more I can say besides it was fried chicken, obviously going to be delicious 
2) Larb Tod - (deep fried mince pork) - My favorite from the meal. These had such a punchy lemongrass flavor and they are served with a dipping sauce which really combines the flavors together
3) Pad Ki Mao Pork and Basil - I pretty much like all noodles but I love spicy flat rice noodles so these were right up my street!

I was mostly looking forward to trying the Pad Thai Mun Poo before i came here. Its was a take on a pad thai i hadn't seen before as it is served with crab meat. I did really enjoy this, but not as much as the other dishes. Never the less, would probably still order it if i came again!

All 6 dishes with a beer each came in at $30 which is not bad! I cannot recommend this place enough if you like spicy food. Will deffo be coming back.

This was in my list of Thai places to try; was happy to be in the neighborhood. We had to order 7 dishes for 3 adults to be barely full. The dishes were ok, but nothing special (except very spicy). I had much better food (and less expensive) at Thai Market (my usual spot).

This place was recommended from a bartender at Dream Baby, she was soo right. NOODLE DISHES = YUM!!

This place was really tasty.  They were on a wait, but we only had to wait about 10 minutes.  I saw that they also deliver.  

The spicy noodles w/ pork and crispy Basil leaves was Delish, and had the perfect about of spice.  The other noodle dish we ordered was good but would have been better if it hadn't had calamari as the calamari was very fishy. It also had shrimp but had no spicy taste so I asked for chili paste to spice it up a little for me.  We also had the pork spring rolls and I wasn't crazy about those.  The noodle dishes were very good though and would be back based on those alone.

If you stumble upon this place, you'll be glad you did.

Cheers & Enjoy!
Food was good. Service was attentive. My only complaint would be that the papaya salad was too little for the price they're charging.

This place is not consistent. I've been here 7 or 8 times. Last time, I brought two friends after I raved to them about how spicy and delicious the food is. They ordered extra rice to accommodate for the spiciness. We ordered dishes that I've tried many times before. However, this time there was no spice at all. Very disappointing. Flavor was still good, but just not as amazing. Really noticeable absence of spice. We had even informed the waitress that we could handle spice when she questioned us. Maybe because my friends look a certain way? 

Anyway, this is a good place to eat raw prawns if you're into that. Prawns come very large, juicy and sweet. Spicy limey dipping sauce is great too.

Pad Khee Mao is also extra excellent here. Very appetizing 'fresh off the wok' aroma.

This time we tried Goong Chae Nam Pla - hard to find prawn sashimi in NYC and it was worth a 5 star! Pad Thai Mun Poo was sweet and sour - the house-styled sauce was amazing. Beef skewer was marinated just the right way. Tom Saab Kradook On was a Tom-Yum taste and the pork was very flavorful. Tum Thai Kai Kem - Salted egg on the top was a best match. Too full for the dessert menu LOL.

Maybe I had too much expectations after much reading about this place, maybe the fact i just came back from Thailand, Somtum Der is just alright! papaya salad, fried rice and drunken noodles alright, not anything better than what I had in Thailand or at Ayada; fried chicken thigh is crispy, juicy and tender. Friend ordered a raw shrimp dish (forgot what it's called), i was initially hesitate to try but was convinced, seasoning is rich and refeshing, glad i tried it. most of their dishes are abit on the saltier end, and portion is kind of small; service is quick, appeared like they just want us to eat fast and leave so they can turn over the table, we had to ask for our waters to be filled due to the spiciness of the dishes, but the check was delivered without asking, as soon as our dishes were clear.

If 1/2 stars were possible it would be 4.5/5 but rounded up. :) 

Atmosphere: Casual setting and nice simply decor

Staff: Very nice and considerate. When my friend and I were trying to share each other's dish, the waiter took note and decided to bring extra plates for us. And as I was about to leave, I accidentally knocked over a water glass and it shattered all over on the floor. I felt terrible so I was trying to help clean up but they immediately said no no and asked if I was okay. They also told me to watch my foot since there was a piece of glass in my shoes. 

Food: The food came pretty quickly when my friend and I ordered. The portions are pretty good as well and we got full pretty quickly. Being that it is a Northern Thai Cusine, it is going to be heavier on spices and hot flavors. 

Koi Gong: This dish is made up of soft broil prawns, beef and rice. This is another flavorful dish and also got pretty spicy at one point. 

Khao Pad Kraprao Moo: This dish consists of fried pork and thai basil mixed with rice topped with a fried egg. It can get pretty spicy but overall, the flavor is good. However, it can get a little too salty after a while too. I still enjoyed this dish nonetheless. 

Prices
Koi Gong: $11.00
Khao Pad Kraprao Moo: $12.00

Likes: Good run for your money, big and comfy restaurant, friendly staff, authentic thai food

This is a great Thai restaurant if you're looking for Isan food. Every dish has really tasty flavors and they have Beer Lao. I'm Lao, so that's pretty cool to see!

Fried chicken is delicious.
Beef skewers are good too.
Pork Nam Tok was good, but not a favorite.

The papaya salad though is where it's at. Last time, got the Tum Suo Der maximum spicy and YO! it was a bit of a struggle but it's life giving. I drank like two pitchers of water and the server was like "Is it too spicy for you" and I'm thinking "I mean a little but if it's not out of control spicy what's the point??" .....You might not share that view and I should probably be ordering medium.

Definitely give this place a try if you haven't! They have recommended pairings for dishes but you're fine ordering anything off the menu. If you like to plan ahead, make a reservation they even have OpenTable. The staff all wear cool hats too. 

Oh! The tables are very close to each other so be prepared to end up on @overheardnewyork.

I haven't enjoyed much Thai food in New York since I went to Thailand because it never seems to live up to the complex spicy flavors. This place is an exception and worth trying. We ordered an excellent papaya salad - medium spicy was hot enough for us and we like spicy! It was so tangy and the texture was great. Like another reviewer commented, it was salty, sour, sweet and spicy all at once. Not to be missed.

We ordered the Koi Goong, the Soft boiled prawns that were spicy and tasty with rice. We also shared three noodle dishes. I recommend the Chefs Signature Wok Fried Seafood Suki. The rice vermicelli noodles were tangy and the seafood was covered in the same spicy red sauce. The flat noodles with pork and crispy basil was another favorite. Great combination of flavors that to me was better then the pad see eiw with calamari. That's my usual go to at other Thai restaurants but here white it was also good, it was just not as exciting as the other spicier dishes. Service was friendly, prices were very reasonable and the place was not too crowded. Go!

This was perfect. Really great food, casual atmosphere, super nice attentive staff, and reasonably priced, especially for NYC!
I like hot spicy food and this delivers. Don't be ashamed to ask for medium or mild; they're not kidding when they say it's hot. I warned you!
I would definitely go back if I were on the lower east side again.
Second time in this place. the food is good and not expensive.

This place is great. But, the server gave me terrible experience. l was always waiting for the waiter. Their thai food is the worst l have had in the city. And the food was not worth $60. Please do not go.

This place is so awesome! Great Thai food in NY at an affordable price! Somtum Der was recommended to me by a close Thai friend, Supachaya. The fried chicken here was the best. I've been to Thailand a few times, and this was on point. I love spicy food and the soup was perfectly spicy and flavorful.

I went to Somtum der for Monday lunch at 1pm. The place was half filled with people. 

I ordered the $10 lunch special - seafood suki and ice Thai tea. My food came out quickly and it was really hot. There were flavors of sweet and sour though I didn't find it spicy at all. The amount of seafood was generous, too. I'll probably crave these kind of dishes on a day when I don't have much of an appetite - it brought all my taste buds to life!

My servers let me eat in peace and they were courteous and brief. 

I was glad to be in and out with a belly full of lovely flavors with no hassle.

Too hit and miss. The pad kee mao, coconut beef skewer and pork/beef fried rice were solid but the spicy duck salad and marinated grilled beef were disappointing. The pad Thai was flavorless and inedible tbh.   IG @_dasharenee
The food is very authentic and very tasty. Although it is very spicy in some sense, it has its unique style.

Love it here!! Authentic North East thai food...normally I come here for dinner but today I came here for lunch and I like it! Not to crowded and food always great here. If you love spicy food, this place is a must.

This is my second time at Somtum Der and it's still my favorite Thai restaurant. Why? Well for starter the food is amazing! I've tried a few dishes and I haven't had one bad dish. I even tried raw shrimp for the first time and it was soo good. 
I came here both times during a late lunch on a weekend. There wasn't a wait either time. We were seated quickly by the staff. They were very helpful in helping us choose what to order. The decor is really cute. 
I highly recommend the flat noodles worth the ground beef. It's so flavorful. The raw shrimp like I said was good. It's very very spicy and citrus-y- just like I like it. The coconut stick rice was delicious. My friend had pad Thai with crab meat and that was to die for. 
I highly recommend this place.

This place was highly recommended by one of my good friends who lives in the area. She told me it was her favorite Thai place and she has good taste. As if she needed to upsell me further, she told me that this place used to have a Michelin star rating. Absolutely sold to try this place.

There was a wait but not too long. For us, a party of 2, we waited maybe 10-15 minutes? Their menu has pictures with helpful descriptions of what each dish is. It was so hard to choose one dish! I got the beef with rice (forgot the actual name of the dish) plate and my friend got the papaya salad. I got a thai iced tea and my friend got the lemon tea. The lemon tea was very good, very deep flavor.

Wait staff is very friendly and helpful! The interior is dim lighting. It looks small on the outside, but it's bigger than expected when you walk in. Apparently they take reservations too! So I'm definitely doing that next time. They also do carry out which sounds like a dream if you live locally. We got our food pretty quickly and the food was A+.

I would definitely come back to try their other dishes and their dessert. Well done!

Somtum Der had been on my list of bookmarks for a while, so when my friends and I were looking for a Thai place, I suggested this restaurant. The four of us came in on a Friday night with an OpenTable reservation for 6:15. 

Happy hour is from 4-7. I can't remember the pricing but the drinks were only okay. We tried a few of their different martinis, which were pretty basic. My friend had one that straight up looked like mouthwash. I tried some lemongrass rice martini, which I didn't like at all. Stick to the basic martinis - think lychee, or mangosteen)

To start, we all shared the papaya salad, and the grilled marinated beef. Both were great. The salad was nice and light - a perfect balance to the beef. The beef came with this special spicy dipping sauce, which went well with the rest of the flavors of the marinade.

For the main, I had the pad kee mao (drunken noodles). The texture of the noodles were perfect, and overall, I enjoyed it. However, when I ordered it with pork, I was expecting either sliced or shredded pork, but it was ground pork. Not a huge deal, but just a bit strange since I've never had this variation before. But the ground pork wasn't very good.

Also, not sure what was going on - maybe someone had a few too many martinis, but the entire place smelled like vomit and cleaning fluid. It was very unappetizing. Maybe it was a one-off situation but I think next time I come back, I'll order my food to go.

Second time coming here, and again it's a good, solid, cheap eat in the east village. The waiting staff are all extremely friend and wear natty little Jason Mraz hats. What's not to love?

Onto the food.

Larb Tod - this is basically Thai seasoned little pork meatballs (but shaped as a doughnut). Served with a chilli vinegar dipping sauce. Crispy on the outside, soft inside and delicious all over

Khao klook kha pi - a mound of fried and seasoned jasmine rice, with all the extra trimmings served around it for a mix-it-yourself treat. The trimmings include BBQ pork, scallions, crispy onions, dried shrimp, and crispy chillis. Delicious, but the meat portion is tiny. For meat lovers, is suggest getting a meaty side to go with.

Menu wise, I find all the dishes to be a little samey. They're all typically a meat with a dipping sauce, or a dry fried rice/noodle dish. There lacks anything really saucey on the menu. In my ignorance however, maybe that's what northern Thai food is?

Either way, great eatery you should definitely check out once in your life!!

This place used to be good! Now everything is overly salty. This is my fourth time going to this place ever since it had a Michelin recommendation. I can't recommend this place anymore till they fix their use of salt. 

The fried chicken appetizer is still pretty good! I just personally can't recommend this as the spot to goto base on price and salty taste.

I have been to this cute Thai restaurant twice already and both times the food certainly did not disappoint! This time my inner fatty ended up ordering pork skewers with vermicelli, fried chicken thigh, and grilled sticky rice. The fried chicken thigh was crispy and juicy but portion wise is more like an appetizer.  The BBQ pork skewers was a decent portion size and grilled perfectly, sweet with a little char. The grilled sticky rice was a little underwhelming. For those that don't like sweet drinks, you might want to pass on the Thai iced tea and coffee for they come premixed and taste like diabetes in a cup. Though if they just tone down the sugar a little bit the drinks would have been awesome. 

Service wise have been top notch both times. This place definitely hired some good staff. Everyone was pleasant and gave good recommendations when asked. One even pointed out that it was happy hour and my group would have saved more money on the fried chicken thigh. Our water glasses were never empty and plates were promptly cleared. 

All in all, this a great Thai restaurant with friendly staff. I would highly recommend checking this place out!!!

Always one of my favorite places to get some papaya salad because of the fact that they have different varieties of papaya salad which allows you to try different version of Isan food. They also allow you to choose spice levels so that if you're not a fan of spiciness you don't have to worry too much. I usually go with the salted egg papaya salad because it give a nice saltiness to the tartness of the papaya salad. I need to try the crab one next time.

During my visit I also had the raw shrimp since this is a preparation I don't often see at other restaurants and I'm a big fan of raw food. It had a nice hit of spice with each bite with it's special sauce. Always a fan of coming back here and getting more food.

My boyfriend and I loveeeee Thai food, especially since it's spicy. We made a reservation and missed it because of traffic #NYCproblems. The restaurant was semi packed when we arrived at 7:30 on Friday. We were able to snag a seat by the bar in the front. Shortly after we got seated, the waitlist started to grow. 

We stared off with a Thai iced tea and Singha, the tea was way too sweet for my liking. The menu is broken into several sections, making t straight forward. We decided to skip the noodles/rice because everything else at the beginning of menu looked more appealing.

We ordered 4 dishes + a side of grilled sticky rice. We had the Larb Ped (minced duck), Pork Neck Papaya Salad, Shrimp sashimi and lastly the Grilled Pork Skewers. FYI all of this is spicy, topped with chilis. I think the spiciest was the Larb Ped, which was bursting with flavor! It honestly didn't taste like duck because it was covered by the onions, herbs and spices. The sashimi was very fresh, not fishy at all. There was a crunch/snap when you chewed. The grilled pork is self explanatory, loved the vermicelli side and unique dipping sauce. The papaya salad may not seem spicy at first, but it'll hit you in the end. The grilled sticky rice was a good snack in between dishes but don't eat too much as you'll be too full to eat anything else! 

Overall, service was great even though it was a packed house. The food was beyond my expectations. I will definitely be back for more! Oh yeah, we didn't finish it all, has some of each dish left.
Excellent service, delicious food and perfect lychee martinis. Glad I got to try this place and will be back soon.

The food is Absolutely delicious and just hits the spot when you are craving some Thai food. The food is northern Thai and for those who can't handle spice, just ask for non spicy! All the beef appetizers are mouth watering delicious. Recommend the beef skewers or even spicy shredded beef salad. The Thai basil fried rice and Pad kee maw are a must. Get the papaya salad but once again stick to non spicy if you can't handle spice (or even if you can think about it twice). 

7/22/17 Update - Bumping this place from 4 to 5 stars for consistently delivering exceptional food!

Hands down best Thai food ever. I'm half Laotian amongst other nationalities but this place hits close to home. Beside Khe-Yo in TriBeca, this place is my go to and my favorite. I've never been disappointment. Because they're Isan, it hits close to home and the flavors are authentic. 

I love the spiciness and the food is just so mouth water and smells delicious! I have yet to be disappointed. It's so funny because the delivery guys know me so well, they chuckle every time they see me, I order at least 1-2 times a day and more than 4x a week. It's quite addicting when you crave homemade food and this is near to it. 

NOW THIS PLACE IS AUTHENTIC THAI!

I came here to Somtum Der Thai Restaurant last week with three friends. Everyone enjoyed their meal a great deal. I had a green curry with beef and it was delicious. I started with the spicy papaya salad. Just great. Fresh and just enough spicyness without loosing the flavor of the papaya. The decor is warm and friendly yet still casual but nice. Clean restaurant. Recommended if you're in the east village or near avenue A downtown.
Sad service for a Michelin star and is definitely not on a budget. Spicy was too spicy and I was offered jasmine rice when they saw me shedding tears, which they charged me for later.

Come In with a friend for a lunch. I never try this spot before. Give them a shot.
We order 4 dishes for 2 people.
1 spring roll. ( pork meat, inside have a spicy favor with basil leaf, very crispy )
2 pork liver sAlad (my favorite, a lot of favor and i love the spicyness in my touge)
3 grilled pork with thin noodle( with a lot of coconut favor, a little sweet) 
4 pork noodle ( small size , and too salty, try to avoid this one)

As I sit here sipping my Thai beer, I only have three words to describe my dinner - "oh hell no." We got the fried chicken thigh and the shrimp fried rice and wow, was surprised at how bad it was. The restaurant itself is decorated like a high-class place but right when you anticipate a roaring rush of goodness as you eat is when you realize the food is glazed with a thick, hefty layer of mediocrity. The price is just not worth it for this place. Being from California where it's Asian food galore, regular Asian food can't even compare to this place. No no no. Avoid. Run. Do not recommend. 

The beer was ok though.

Overall, the food tastes authentically Thai but lacks a few things here and there.. At this price point, I think Somtum Der is a great way to take friends from the "Thai place on the corner pad thai" to authentic Thai flavors. 

I had dinner here on a Tuesday at 7pm with coworkers - the place was fairly packed. The room is well decorated but fairly dark and can get quite loud. Here's the food:

Lemongrass Juice (drink): my coworker had this and said it was quite refreshing and he ended up having a second.

Rosella Juice (drink): Rosella is hibiscus - it has a deep red-purple color and the sweetness is balanced with a tiny bit of astringency that reminds me of the skin of a black plum. It's quite concentrated at first but I think it's perfect once some ice melts. This leans on the sweet side, but does have some acid for balance.

Tum Poo-Plara (somtum): This had fermented field crabs! I actually never got to try this while I was in Thailand. Surprisingly, the crabs are more savory and seafood-sweet than I expected however they did confer a moderate-mild amount of fishiness to the somtum. I don't think the papaya was pounded very much, if at all and I think that the savoriness & fishiness could have been better balanced with sweet and sour - was a bit overwhelming. I would go with the basic somtum next time.

Sai Krok Isan (fried): Not fermented enough; there's a depth of flavor from fermentation but there's no real tartness or pungency. Also because it's fried, it's not very juicy. The flavor is good overall, but lacks authentic juiciness and sourness. Beware the chopped birds eye chilis.

Larb Ped (larb): This was the duck version: overall, I think this lacked punch. I could smell the roasted glutinous rice, there was a decent amount of greenery in this but the flavor isn't as dense as the ones I had in Chiang Mai. There wasn't that much acidity, and the greenery didn't taste as herbacious and fresh as I was hoping. I did appreciate the kaffir lime leaves that I got a bite of though. The duck has a tiny twinge of that liveriness to let you know it's duck. I probably wouldn't get this again though, try the larb moo or nam toks next time.

Khao Pad Krapow Nue (Rice): This was the surprise hit of the night. It's just fried rice but excellently executed. Each grain of rice is distinct and tastes like it's been hit with some real wok heat. The little bits of beef have also been fried and mixed in nicely. The dish is seasoned with sweetness and a depth of savoriness. To be honest, I'm not even sure how this flavor happened, maybe some fish sauce, palm sugar, possibly some tamarind paste. The thai fried egg was also perfectly creamy inside, crisp edges.

Goong Chae Nam Pla (salad): Marinated raw shrimp was surprisingly mild. Not very spicy, and the texture of the shrimp was similar to that of lean tuna in sashimi. It was seasoned to be somewhat sweet. No fishiness at all, I trust that the shrimp must have been very fresh. Clean seafood flavor with a bit of depth probably from some fish sauce.

Wish i could give half stars because I would have probably given it 4.5/5 for price, service, and great food

Ive been meaning to come here bc ive heard nothing but great things and it definitely lived up to the hype. I luckily came at 6:53 and the waiters still let me and my friends take some time to think about happy hour drinks which I really appreciated. I think our general consensus was that the drinks were great prices since they were half off but not the best drinks we have had (we tried the thai tea-tini and the lychee pineapple lemon cocktail)

The food was really great for the prices too but I think I expected more for a once michelin starred restaurant. The pad kee mao was delicious and authentic but nothing too different or much better than any other good hole in the wall in chinatown.

So great. $11 dishes of delicious Thai food. Even medium level is spicy so you might want to do 2 out of 5 not 3 out of 5 spice level. I had green papaya salad and minced spicy pork "salad". Both were awesome!

Somtum Der is officially my new go-to spot to grab Thai food.  The restaurant offers unique eats in a casual and laid back atmosphere.  

Service was pretty average, however.  The pacing of the meal just wasn't right and there was a "hitch" with one of our main dishes (three got served, but FOUR were seated).  The "hitch" was rectified a few minutes later.  We also brought two bottles of wine with us after a BYOB night gone wrong due to the closure of a nearby restaurant.  They charged two $10 corkage fees (which is kind of annoying) and were hoping they might let it slide.

Anyway, on to the meal.

We started off the night with Sai Krok Isan (fried isan sausages) and Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (der style deep fried chicken thighs) for the table.  The chicken was very tender and juicy... but for some reason everyone seemed to prefer the sausages.

For entrees, the table ordered a mix of rice and noodle based dishes:
- Khao Pad Goong (fried rice) with crab meat... we're talking real crab meat here people, not imitation!  Yum.
- Khao Pad Kraprao Moo (fried pork with Thai basil mixed with rice).
- and two orders of the Pad Ki Mao Pork & Basil.  Holy moly the dish packs a lot heat.  Thai chili peppers... oh so good.

I docked one star for the mediocre service - the food is five stars in my book.  It's a welcome respite from the boring/tired "pre-pack" Thai places all over the city :-)

The food portion and price was pretty good and the drinks were great. I like the location and the outlay of the restaurant. The mirror in the back gives the illusion that the restaurant is bigger than it is. The service was pretty good. The waiters didn't hover but they came at the perfect times. I ordered the Khao Klook Ka Pi which is the fried jasmine rice with egg, onion, meats, and mango on the side. You have to mix it all up. I also ordered the Mekhong Punch which was pretty good. My friend was satisfied with her food too.
According to my Thai friends this is the most authentic Issan food in New York City. It is very tasty but very hot

This restaurant has been sitting amongst my bookmarks for a while. I was recommended Somtum Der in the past when talking to my friends about Thai food, and in particular they highly recommended the crab pad thai.

I ordered via Yelp, and you have the option to choose spiciness levels. I went with mild because I figured that it shouldn't be too spicy. Wrong! There was an INSANE amount of red pepper flakes in my pad thai. The spiciness also left my stomach burning all night after I ate. I appreciate that their crab meat is actually that: crab meat that was carefully extracted from a real crab and none of that imitation stuff. For a good portion of my meal I thought I was eating pieces of crab shell (although it had the texture of shrimp shell) until I spit a piece out and realized it was the pepper flakes!! Again, too many pepper flakes.

Other than the crab, nothing makes their pad thai particularly unique. However, because of the crab, they can and do charge way more for their pad thai than most Thai places in the city ($16 for a smallish serving). I probably won't be back for take-out, mostly because there are plenty of Thai places a little further from where I live where I can get a good sized chicken pad thai for much cheaper. However, I recognize that this may be a good place for happy hour specials with a group of friends. 

I recommended this restaurant to someone else who went and had their pad see ew the same night, and I think he was as disappointed as I was with what he got for the price.

Really nice space and great service but again a few meals it's pretty clear that if you don't order everything super spicy, it's going to be pretty bland. I know Thai food is supposed to be spicy but even the things that I have tried that weren't Thai spicy were a bit lackluster. It's let to a few really amazing but insanely hot larbs and tum salads as well as some boring fried dishes and noodles. 

Overall very good but I definitely prefer Chao Thai and even Zabb Elee

Good food but nothing too special or unique. Obviously not super authentic but do taste good and pretty decent quality for both food and drinks. They have happy Hours except for wines. Most staffs are friendly and helpful. Price is pretty reasonable and the atmosphere is quite good. Smaller place but a mirror that gives it more space and dim lighting and interior design have a romantic feel. Nice for catching up, a date, or farewell or congratulation dinner. Good for small or big groups, family, or if you're alone. Kids are okay but not the best.

I've had the entire spectrum of Thai food in the city: the bad, the mediocre, and good. I first went to Somtum Der last fall when my boyfriend, who was living in the E. Village at the time, ordered it for us one night. Oh em gee. I was actually mad at myself that I hadn't been to this spot before. Since then, I haven't been able to eat at any other Thai place (only when desperate and don't feel like heading to E. Village). 

The space isn't that big and apparently they get booked. I've only dined in twice and I've never had to wait. However, I tried to make reservations for 2 last Friday before I headed over just to make sure, and they were fully booked on OpenTable. I called and they said walk-ins were fine, and I went on the early side (6pm) so was in the clear. 

They have your usual Thai dishes (pad thai, drunken noodles), but they also offer Thai dishes I've never seen before in the States. The restaurant is known to offer dishes from the Isan region of Thailand.

Here are my go-to MUST orders: SPICY PAPAYA SALAD with salted egg (sounds weird, but so good), DER STYLED DEEP-FRIED CHICKEN THIGH (3 pieces), GRILLED COCONUT MILK MARINATED BEEF OR PORK SKEWERS (3 pieces with 3 blobs of noodles), SPICY MINCED PORK SALAD WITH GREEN VEGGIES & CHILIS (my fave). 

The only qualm I have is that they charge you $3 for a small blob of rice. What a rip off. The other dishes are priced reasonably okay -- a little on the pricier side I think for Thai food. BUT this is hands-down the best Thai place I've been to in the city. At least try it once!

Some buddies and I were going to grab dinner at another spot which ended up having a really long wait and decided to eat here instead. Turns out this might have been the better spot all along. The menu can seem a little intimidating at first if you aren't used to Thai food, but the food is amazing and the portions are just right. Nice atmosphere and everything is pretty reasonably priced. Would definitely come here again.

I love love love this restaurant. Somtumder received 1 Michelin star last year but unfortunately lost it this year. I had to try it either way and was hooked ever since. Since moving from Boston I was struggling to fine the perfect thai place to satisfy my thai food cravings (let me state this again for the 100th time that I am thai) and this place just hits the right spot! Highly recommend it!

This place serves what is called the esarn food, which is the north eastern food in thailand. It has a very flavorful taste, and you usually eat the meat and papaya salad with sticky rice. There are a few bangkok food available like pad thai and fried rice - but I highly recommend you try the esarn food they serve here.

The restaurant is decorated nicely, super clean with a generous amount of seats. There is a bar available near the entrance and the decor just screams "THIS IS THAILAND" lol. You will constantly hear chatters in thai because I swear, lots of thai people keep coming back for more food here. 

As for the food here we go: 

Yum crispy leaf fish - urgh the best, imagine papaya salad but with crispy leaf fish. There's a chunk of salty fish that is super flavorful, you can taste the spice, the lemon, and it compliments really well with the purple onions and lemon grass. Yum! This dish is so hard to find in America. 

Khao pad pu - this crab fried rice is amazing, rice cooked perfectly and it has that "burnt" smell from the wock. Tastes delicious and pretty authentic. On the side of the dish are a few chunks of crab and eggs. It goes well with the "prik nam pla" sauce that came with it (9/10)

Goong chae num pla- raw shrimp in salty and sour and spicy sauce. This is super authentic and it probably takes lots of guts to try, but this tastes amazing, not too spicy and is just.. amazing. So hard to find in america! (9/10) 

Moo Rong hai der -very tender grilled pork served with this special sweet and spicy sauce. Goes really well with sticky rice (you would have to order this side) I would recommend the black one (10/10)

Moo ping kati sod - super tender pork on a stick. It tastes of coconut and has this amazing sweet glazing on top and serves with the fried sticky rice and a spicy sauce. Totally worth it, must try (10/10)

Moo daed diaw (deep fried sun dried pork) - my least favorite dish because the pork is a bit too dried and chewy. The taste does taste somewhat authentic (5/10)

Dessert

Taro in condensed coconut milk - must try! Super authentic and not too sweet. The taro has real chunks of taro in it. Don't be thrown off by how hot it is, it's supposed to be that way (10/10) 

Drinks:

Lemon grass juice - soooo good, not too sweet and tastes like lemon grass. I can't find something like this else where (10/10)

Singha beer/Chang beer - these two beers are thai beers. I usually drink singha but some may find it too bitter.

Outstanding take on Thai food. It's not your typical delivery Thai take-out. Although the coconut rice wasn't as strong as I thought it would be ... depending on how much you like coconut, this could be a good or bad thing.
Great meal after a long day. We got the mackerel and papaya salad for appetizer. It was very spicy but we loved it, especially after ordering some cucumber slices. We will visit again.

On a whim my boyfriend and I decided to go out to dinner here because it was nearby and date night! Why not? Yeah!

It was a Sunday night and it was decently busy, so we sat up at a bar. All the while, people kept steadily coming in and there was a wait. This added to the expectation that it should be awesome, based in part on online reviews. I guess we just both built it up too much in our heads...

Well, he got a Dr. Pepper combo beer drink, and a triple combination meal suggested on the last page. I just got one dish and a side of coconut rice because I wasn't TOO hungry, but the cuisine is one of those that you share entirely. On the upside, all the dishes were pretty big and filling. Moreover, they came out relatively quickly proportionate to the crowd size, so the wait wasn't bad.

I got a spicy mixed duck dish with the coconut rice. It had a LOT of basil. The flavor was there, but entirely overpowering and not too spectacular. His combo included some sort of deep-fried (pork?) rolls, which were just kind of plain, served with a sauce remnant of mayonnaise. Also, he got marinated beef strips (THE BEST part of the meal) that came with a dipping sauce (not good) and grilled sticky rice sticks (decently good! But he didn't like). Also, he got a mackerel plate with papaya somtum salad and rice. It was good, nothing special. 

Overall it wasn't bad just wasn't anything special, subpar even. I'd say traditional flavors but I won't be going back really. I enjoyed myself ok but wasn't blown away.
addicted to their fried chicken at the moment. it is a bit pricey for southeast asian cuisine. cocktails are nice but light on the mix.

Authentic Thai cuisine served in a non-ostentatious setting. All of the food and drink items we ordered were delicious, including the Thai iced tea, vegetable fried rice, and chefs signature seafood and vermicelli. The service was prompt and friendly. I will definitely be returning.

I loved our dinner at Somtum Der. We've been meaning to go there for so long, and finally made it on a night when we were in the mood for salads, vegetables, and lots of flavor. They definitely delivered on all three.

We started out with the Tum Thai, the original style of the papaya salad, and it was so fresh and delicious. They have so many varieties of papaya salad, and we can't wait to try more of them. Definitely among the best papaya salad we've had.

We also got the Larb Ped (duck). This was good, although when it comes to duck larb, I think I still prefer the version from the (sadly gone) Kin Shop. They do have some varieties of larb that aren't common elsewhere, like mushroom which hopefully we can try next time.

While both the papaya salad and larb were very good, the best thing we ate at dinner was the Khao Klook Ka Pi, which was rice seasoned with fermented shrimp paste and a bunch of accompaniments, including green mango, sliced egg, pork, green onions, string beans, and cucumbers. Mixed together, everything on the plate just worked so well together, and I loved the strong flavor of the shrimp paste in the rice (been craving that type of flavor for a long time).

There is so much more on the (very large) menu that we want to try, and we can't wait to go back for more.

3.5 rounded up to 4. Came here for take out on the way home and we were pleasantly surprised. Standouts include the Yum Tra Krai Sardine (but order a side of sticky or coconut rice to go with it) and the Gaeng Om Kai soup. I actually can't get the soup out of my head. Chicken, herbs, and fresh eggplant floating in a delicious, spicy, tangy broth with ample amounts of dill. Crab fried rice had ample amounts of crab, was well seasoned, but needed more vegetables. The crab pad thai was just OK (a bit dry). Will definitely return.

Larb moo, beef skewers and papaya salad were the best we had in NYC by far.  Stay away from the special menu.  Would have given the final star if they are not so heavy handed on the salt.  Aside from the skewers, everything else are pretty salty.

Solid Thai restaurant in the East Village. We forgot to make reservations, so I came earlier to put my name down, and was informed there would be a 45 minute wait. Since it was a Friday night, we were expecting a wait time anyways. 

They have a really extensive menu, so much of our time was spent deciding on what to order. I opted for the fried garlic beef with jasmine rice + fried egg ($14). Food came out a lot quicker than expected, which was a pleasant surprise. I really enjoyed my dish! The beef was perfectly marinated, but a little on the chewier side. The dish itself isn't spicy, but came with a side of spicy sauce, so you can adjust to your liking. 

The atmosphere was very lively and loud so several times we had to shout to be heard across the table. The staff was really efficient and friendly, which made it a pleasant evening overall.

Dropped by on a Sunday at 8:30. No wait. Communal table available. Friendly staff. Entrees came quickly but maybe a bit too quickly because our papaya salads came after them. Food was very good. If you ask for spicy, be prepared for some heat. A few vegetarian and pescatarian options.
I have been in this place last night. They have little bit different menu than other Thai places. The food was tasty, and decoration was authentic.

Yum! My boyfriend and I decided to come here for a date night on Friday, the restaurant was packed when we arrived but thankfully no wait time for a table for two. The ambiance is intimate and casual, very cute decorations. Service was a little delayed, took me a while to flag down a waiter to take our order. We ordered the shrimp and calamari pad see ew and spicy beef fried rice for our entrees. I enjoyed the spicy beef fried rice more than the pad see ew, I thought there wasn't anything special about the pad see ew. The beef fried rice was delicious, definitely had a spicy kick. Overall, I enjoyed my meal here and I would come back to try their spicy papaya salad and other traditional Thai dishes.

this place offers the most authentic thai food in NYC! everything was good, my favorite was por pia larb moo and larb duck. Drinks were also delicious. I didn't adjust the spiciness and I found it super spicy, but overall the food were very flavorful.

Authentic thai food served here made me feel like i am home. I love som tam and thai-style fried chicken. They have nice iced tea and herbal drinks that you should try as well! Desserts are okay. The place is normally packed during peak hours. It might be better to be there off-peak hours so you would not waste time in waiting. However, if you have to wait like 20 minutes, it is still worthwhile!!!

Your place for comfort Thai food.

I'm a huge fan of Thai food -- I can't get enough of it. There's nothing outstanding about Somtum Der, but it's a causal restaurant that satisfies my Thai cravings. Will come back here for a casual meal.

Having had tons of great Thai food in Elmhurst recently, I went looking for a good place in Manhattan. Somtum Der was one of the first places to catch my eye. I made reservations via OpenTable and when I had to push it 30 minutes back they happily accommodated the last minute change. 

The interior is bigger than I originally thought and it seems to be able to fit a few larger parties. Its dimly lit and has a cozy, intimate vibe. It seems like the perfect place for a date or catching up with friends. After looking at the menu and the dishes on the other tables, it seems like most of their dishes are better for sharing. They have a lot of options, but most dishes are just meat dish or a salad, with the option to order rice on the side. They do have a few set entrees like noodles or meat and rice. My friends and I decided to share the following: 

-Der styled deep fried chicken thigh
-Grilled coconut milk marinated pork skewers
-Crispy leaf fish
-Fried garlic beef with jasmine rice
-Steamed sticky rice

Everything was really tasty with my favorite dish being the grilled coconut milk marinated pork skewers. I loved the richness from the coconut milk. That and the sticky rice were the perfect combination. 

Overall, we had a nice dinner at Somtum Der. The dishes are on the smaller side so I would definitely order a few and share. I can't wait to come back to try more of their dishes (their menu is huge!).

For a restaurant that had received 1 Michelin Star in the past, is currently on the Bibs Gourmand list, and has been praised by a number of my friends, I was underwhelmed. 

I went with some friends and we split two papaya salads, the fried chicken, grilled sticky rice, then got our own entrees. The toppings to the papaya salads were interesting - salted egg on one and grilled pork neck meat on the other, and both had a good level of spice (we got medium spicy). Apart from that, the two dishes tasted exactly as expected and isn't particularly memorable considering papaya salads are the partial namesake of the restaurant.

The der style deep fried chicken thighs (Sa Poak Kai Tod Der) were easily the highlight of my meal - I don't believe they used breading at all and it was perfectly crispy with juicy insides.  However, the grilled sticky rice der's style fell a little short; tasty, but could have done with another ~30 seconds on each side on the grill to achieve a crispier outside. Among the six of us, we split two orders of each but could have done with more of the fried chicken. 

For my main, I got the fried garlic pork with jasmine rice, which was overly salty and must be offset with the jasmine rice; I didn't even bother finishing this and the leftovers are still sitting in my fridge 3 days later. My boyfriend ordered the fried pork with thai basil, mixed with rice and he enjoyed it well enough - the flavor profile on this dish was a little more interesting because of the herbs and spices. My friend's chicken soup with local herbs had too much dill in it. 

Overall, it's a decent spot - I would revisit for the fried chicken and perhaps try out more of the grill items, but not for the papaya salads or the rice dishes.

Very busy place for a Monday night. Great place to have a casual dinner with friends. We ordered several dishes and they were all hits except for the fried enoki mushroom which was a tad to sweet for all of us. Everything else was good and reasonably priced.

Being from L.A., two types of food I miss that I wasn't getting here in NYC: authentic, excellent Thai food and Mexican food.  Tex-Mex don't count.  (For Mexican food found the hole in the wall Great Burrito on 23rd; see my review for that.)  But finally, finally FINALLY, found the great, authentic Thai restaurant...this place.  It's Isan food, which is from the northern Thailand (Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, etc).  You know its good when the local Thai folks go there in droves.  Deep Fried Thai chicken and their noodles and soups are great, but what makes it authentic is it's spicy, spicy, SPICY, not watered down to Western tastes.  Plus, great atmosphere and a beautifully decorated, roomy restaurant (not like those hole in the wall pseudo-wannabe-Thai places in the Upper West Side or even in Chinatown).  Worth traveling the Really Lowest East Side so highly recommend if u want the real deal.

Having been highly recommend by a few friends, I knew I had to check out Somtum Der. I can say I was not disappointed by this formally 1 Star Michelin rated Thai restaurant, which serves up some authentic dishes! 

I tried to come here previously and there was over an hour wait on a Friday night, but I made a reservation online in advance this time and it was easy peasy! Didn't have any issues or have to wait once we got there. 

Having seen other reviews, I wanted to try one of the papaya salads. They offer a few options, but we decided to go with the Tum Kor Moo Yang which had pork. They can adjust the spice, but even if you go with the mild, it still has a bit of a kick. Just a forewarning to non-spice lovers! 

Looking to try something new, other than pad Thai, I went for the Khao Klook Ka Pi. This is a rice based dish served mixed with pork, fish paste and a few other side items to add a unique flavor. As a fan of fish paste, I loved the flavor of the dish and how everything worked well together when combined. My husband thought it was too fishy for him, his looks. 

Only complaint I have is that we felt a bit rushed during our time there when it came down to ordering food and drinks. We were in and out in about 35 min which is surprisingly fast for a place where we ordered a round of drinks, an appetizer, and an entree at a sit down restaurant.

The food was amazing and the vibe was great but I didn't like the fact that they were kicking me out the minute I paid. SMH didn't have the time to digest my food plus I'm an out of towner I wish I could of Been able to enjoy the atmosphere
Amazing authentic Thai. I went there and saw some dishes that is not found elsewhere. Amazing food. Reasonable price. Would definitely recommend.  Coming from someone who have a Thai best friend.

Rude staff, long wait but good food! My husband was not too impressed with his food, but I was. I got the pork salad and sticky rice. I'll get the coconut rice next time if I can convince my husband to go back. Sticky fried rice on a stick was the highlight of the meal!
Excellent decor and service.  Food was perfect.  Nice lunch menu.  Had some sliced pork and rice.  Will be back.

For a restaurant in Manhattan, portions were OK for their price. I didn't sit in, only got take out. I went about 20 minutes after we ordered food and our order was ready.

Their papaya salad was super spicy but delicious nonetheless. If you like spicy foods, definitely get this.

I also got their Pad Thai with crab meat because of the reviews I saw on yelp. It was a twist on a regular Pad Thai which I liked. This is a dish to try but I think I will stick with regular in the future.

We came here for dinner as a large group of 8 without reservations around 9:30pm on a Saturday. We were seated almost immediately. There was a lot of food that was ordered between us - I particularly enjoyed the sea food papaya salad and the pad Thai noodles. I would definitely go back again!

Wanted to try a Michelin star restaurant some time in my life without brekaing the budget, so I decided to stop here with my girlfriend during a day trip to NYC. As expected, it's pretty popular so expect to make a reservation or wait, but the staff is friendly and fast so turnover is pretty quick. We wanted to go all out, so we got a ton of stuff.
 
Tum Poo Plara: Isan style papaya salad with fermented fish sauce and field crab. Super spicy with a surprisingly balanced taste from the freshness of the seafood and papaya, but some of the crab chunks were quite hard to eat.

Sa Poak Kai Tod Der: deep fried chicken thigh. Super crispy but juicy all throughout, served with a nice citrusy chile sauce. Would definitely recommend

H'orderves Der: a meat sampler appetizer with a bit of Laotian sausage, vinegary raw pork sausage, fried pork roll, and beef jerky, all served with a sweet chile sauce. Everything was pretty tasty, especially the sausage

Soup Nor Mai: shredded bamboo shoot and Isan herb salad. The bamboo was quite tender and the sauce was surprisingly balanced. After the chicken, it might've been my favorite dish there

Der style grilled sticky rice: three sticks of their sticky coconut rice, grilled until the outside has a nice crispy brown. Pretty good, eat it with their other savory dishes.

Somtum Der is not your typical Thai. Yes, you can find pad thai on the menu, but it'll come with both crab meat and crab paste. Treat this place as more of an adventure than your usual green curry comfort meal.

We came by on a Wednesday night around 7. It was a bit of a wait to get a server to get seated, but there were empty tables so no actual wait. The ambiance is nice and looks warm and inviting. Menu is long and a little bit overwhelming; the pictures are helpful.

We had the spicy mushroom salad (seasonal special) and H'orderves Der, their sampler platter. The first proved way too spicy for me, and my boyfriend who has a much better spice tolerance was also challenged. The second was a winner-- I hadn't tried Thai sausages before and I loved them. The fried tofu is also great. Definitely recommend; it's a great snack to start the meal.

Next, we had Super Peek Kai, or super spicy chicken wing soup, which was... not actually super spicy. It was just really great chicken soup, with a nice note of heat. A bright sweet-and-sour broth with liberal lime juice. Love it.

Finally, we had Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay, which is pad see ew noodles with shrimp and calamari. The seafood was great. Overall, though, I would call the dish pretty standard, with those broad noodles and sweet, thick soy sauce. You can do better than this.

We spent about an hour here and left full. It ended up being $70 after tax and tip for the two of us. We should have gotten one less dish as we had leftovers. Service was a bit AWOL even though the restaurant wasn't full, though it's a large dining room by New York standards. It's a big menu so I would come back to try out new dishes.

easily some of the best thai in new yawk city! warning to the wise: spicy at this place means spicy! portions are generous but not overwhelming, definitely a great idea to share. service was awesome and i loved the overall vibe. definitely swing by next time youre in da east village.
This is some of the best, and most flavorful Thai food that I have had, including those 2? 3? weeks I've spent in various parts of Thailand.

We went here on a Saturday night without a reservation. 3 ppl and only had to wait about 10min. So not so bad at all! Service was good and friendly. We ordered the papaya salad and it was delicious. The noodle dishes were warm, and pad kee mao was delicious and flavorful. Many of the dishes had a veggie option which was a nice touch! 
The ambiance is nice but can be loud at times but nothing too bad. Would recommend this place, and would also recommend making reservations if large party and having dinner a bit later.

Excellent choice in a city full of excellent Thai restaurants. We visited this place during off hours- a little hesitant based on the sketchier street where they're located. But boy they made up for it when we were inside.

What stood out for us was the amazing noodle with beef (I won't even try to remember the actual name of the dish), the fried chicken app that everyone orders (and loves), the papaya salad with pork, and lastly (but not leastly) the grilled pork.

One of the best finds in Manhattan of any food genre this year... served with a side of Thai hospitality.

You know I had waited quite a long time to get to Somtum Der. My husband and I initially planned a date night when we lived in the city but for some reason did not make it. We then, subsequently moved to Denver, CO and I thought visiting was a far off idea, I was wrong. While in town for the annual company Christmas party we got the chance. It was a Wednesday night after a great happy hour that we decided - tonight was the night. A group of 5 of us arrived without reservation and were seated immediately at around 10:00 PM.
 
Our waitress was kind and efficient but pretty quiet. The space itself fairly small and very, very dark. I will say I had built up in my mind that it would look different. Our table decided to split two appetizers: one of which I can't remember for the life of me but it was small kind of bites of pork and to be honest the texture was just off and it was not great. The second was the Tum Suo Der a decent papaya salad in a chili sauce. Nothing to write home about with either of them. For the entrée's my husband and I as usual split two different dishes: Tum Kor Moo Yang which was better than average and pretty spicy and again another dish I just can't remember.
 
Now, listen this is a poor review in the sense that I don't remember half of what I ate but I feel like that says something - it's just not that good! I mean it's average at best to me and I just don't like to pay for and experience average food. I would not go back to Somtum Der but would recommend that other people try it because it does get good reviews it just may not have been for me.

My Thai friend and trusted culinary tour guide brought me here to introduce me to Isan cuisine. It was awesome! People say to order as many dishes as your table can hold and to share family style. We ordered 10+ dishes for just two of us so needed a second table just to handle all our dishes. The flavors were complex. The food was amazing. Also enjoyed the drinks that included a longan juice and lemongrass juice. I'll be digesting for a while but will definitely be returning soon.
Service was good, but food so so, not many vegetarian options either.  Portions a bit small for the price.  Small place, feels like sitting too close to next table.

This is not your typical Thai place...maybe that's why I was taken back at the menu options. 

Food-2/5. Based on other reviews, people must like something about this cuisine but I just don't. Don't get me wrong, I love exotic and Thai food but I got to try several different dishes (party of 7) and it just wasn't for me. 

The beef salad had an interesting very slight grainy taste and I couldn't figure out if it was nuts finely crushed or if the spices weren't properly diffused into the beef. If you are feeling adventurous, try the papaya salad with mackerel! I loved it, although my stepdad thought it was too salty. Coconut rice was delicious. Pad see ew was flavorful and noodles were tender. My mom is picky and she said it was one of the better ones she's had (you can trust her because she rarely like anything lol). My sister thought pad Thai but nothing special.

Service-4/5. Food comes out extremely fast. They were not rude. Very attentive when it comes to filling up your water (food was spicy! Lol). Not sure if there was a language barrier because the waiters were all fairly young and understood what we said...but maybe it was a cultural barrier because it was hard to get information out of them. For a first timer eating Isaan cuisine, I felt like I had to pry recommendations out of them.

Been wanting to try this place and it really did not disappoint. This place is the talk-of-the-town among us Thai people in New York that are desperately missing the taste of home. I haven't talked to a single Thai person I know that dislike this place.

If you are down for some spicy food, come here, as that's what 90% of the dishes in the menu consist of. You can ask for different spice level as well (at least for sure on the somtum) -- I usually go for the Tum Poo Plara with 4 chilis, but I will have to warn you that most people from Bangkok don't eat this dish because of the unique ingredient smell, and 4 chilis is the burn. If you're a newbie, maybe go for the Tum Thai and 2 chilis, or just ask for recommendation I'm sure they have lots to say!

Having all Thai people as the staff is definitely a huge plus in my opinion, maybe because I'm Thai and just want that little extra touch of home.

Satisfied to the core. Will definitely keep coming back and try more dishes.

Came to try out "authentic Thai food" and maybe it's just not my cup of tea.

My friends and I ordered some dishes to share and we liked the beef skewers a lot -- they come with vermicelli clusters and were very well seasoned and flavorful. Their crispy fried pork spring rolls are on the spicy side, but are also delicious. I wasn't a big fan of the duck salad, which came in a small portion size and was difficult to share. The grilled coconut sticky rice looked like a plaintain on a skewer (personally didn't love it but it was ok). My friend orderered the Isan fried rice noodles as a side dish and they tasted pretty good, both as a stand-alone and as a complementary carb (need those carbs doe)

Overall, glad I experienced this cuisine. Might be back to try some other dishes that might be more to my liking (the menu is huge)
My go-to authentic Thai food. I like every dish here. I usually order the salted egg papaya salad. It's very good!

My favorite Thai place in all of NYC.  Supposedly is the most authentic Thai and my oh my is it good!  I always get the salted egg papaya salad (least spicy- which is 1 chili pepper) and either the pad thai or or pad see ew.  You seriously cant get pad thai or pad see ew that tastes like this.  It will blow your mind!! The pad thai comes with crab meat and let me tell you, they do not skimp.  Be warned, it can get quite busy.  Came once on a random Monday night and the wait was an hr and half.
the food here is really good. I really liked the papaya salad and the beef skewers. the papaya salad had a kick to it so if you can't handle spicy--I wouldn't recommend getting the salad.

So good. It reminded me of Lotus of Siam in Vegas if that means anything to you casual thai food lover of the USA.

 We over ordered and I won't keep harping on the numerous amounts of praise already heaped on this place. But I will say if you like the type of thai food thats beyond coconut milk curries and pad thai you are going to dig this place. GET THE LARB MOO spicy and some sticky rice legendary... Also get some skewers, spring rolls, pork roll and the chicken thighs / everything else... So much delight, so much flavor. We came w/ 4 
 on a saturday night and got in after about an hour wait. They take your phone number so you can go wander to a nearby bar during the wait.. But its totally worth it.


 I'll be back with more friends so we can order more...

Dear lord the food is spicy. That said, it's good and definitely geared towards serious Thai food fanatics. The menu is large, and you can pick non spicy items as well. Many of the items can not be found at typical Thai restaurants, so it's a nice break form your average Thai cuisine choices in New York. The pork skewers are the best.

Came with twice and no one dish on the menu disappointed me!  Love it and had the best pork fried rice in 2017!
 Planning to go back there with friends very soon.
I love their spicy dishes, the right amount of kick in the mouth.  And the services are friendly and attentive.

Really solid Thai food in a nondescript little spot in East Village! It's very bustling inside and quite crowded, though my friend/I were able to get a spot at the bar in ~15 minutes. 

We got the Chef's Signature Wok Fried Seafood Suki. It was a very interesting dish -- not sure if I've had something quite like it before, but very tasty!

Warning: the papaya salad is super spicy. We got medium spice and couldn't finish because it was burning our tongues.

This is by far my favorite Thai restaurant! I came here with my friend from Thailand and he absolutely loved the food. We ordered the papaya salad, coconut rice, and deep fried chicken thigh. 

Everything was delicious and had a bit of spice to it! If you're looking for some authentic Thai food, I'd highly recommend giving this place a try!

Went here when it dint have the michelin star. Absolutely loved all the food we ate. Service can be a hit or miss when they are busy. Get the shrimp salad, so spicy and delicious leaves you wanting more. The grilled coconut rice sticks cool things off. They have a limited bar menu but it works.

First time here and I love the restaurant and can't wait to come back to try more dishes.  2 of us came and we ordered the original papaya salad (because my date was not adventurous enough to try the one with crab), the pork larb, fish larb with sticky rice and coconut rice.  Everything was delicious. We got the medium spicy level, it was ok for me but my date had to down about 4 glasses of water.  We had a tiny bit left over and because I loved it so much I insisted on a doggy bag. There was a bamboo shoots dish that looked so good.  Haven't gotten so excited about a restaurant in a while.  Have to come back with a larger more adventurous group to try everything. Love Laotian food!

In a city inundated with mediocre Thai restaurants... cough cough Hell's Kitchen cough cough... Somtum Der stands out. The ambience is casual enough to go with a group of friends, family, but classy enough to be a great spot for a date. The service is quick but not rush and the quality of food and flavours is top notch. 

A group of four, we went on a Friday night for dinner and waited only five minutes to be seated. We ordered a number of dishes including the Crab Pad Thai, Spicy Duck Larb, Fried Mushroom special, Beef Pad See Ew, and Fried Chicken dish. While all the dishes were delicious and we cleared every plate, the standouts for me were the Fried Chicken, Beef Pad See Ew, and Fried Mushroom Special.
The fried chicken was juicy and had a nice golden crispy outer layer. The dipping sauce paired well with the chicken adding a spicy sweetness.
The Pad See Ew was sweet and savoury at the same time thanks to the sauces and seasoning that the noodles and beef were prepared in.
The Spicy Duck Larb was also really good. As you continue to eat it, the peppers intensify the spiciness. It has a real kick while also having a freshness to it thanks to the veggies.

The staff were efficient, attentive, and friendly. The restaurant also did not feel cramped despite having a row of tables and benches that patrons sat at. We sat right in the middle of the communal table and we had plenty of space.

If you want excellent, authentic Thai food and flavours that are not the typical and ubiquitous Pad Thai or Drunken Noodles, I highly recommend Somtum Der.

I'd go back, and most likely, I'd get the grilled pork skewers again - out of this world tender, flavor and char.  No wonder this Thai restaurant got Michelin recognition.  Expect no compromise for American tastebuds in terms of spice level, or content of the dishes at this Avenue A find. No problem getting a seat and taking time to relax and enjoy a weekday lunch. It's a cool space that feels airy with a high ceiling and a combination of modern and Southeast Asian flair.

This place is amazing. It focuses on Isan cuisine, so it's not your usual Thai food, so don't expect to see pad thai or curries on the menu. The only thing most people will recognize is the papaya salad. But it is going to be the best papaya salad you'll find by a huge margin. The main courses are all amazing too. This place is great for so many reasons, excellent service, great food, and it's something that is very difficult to find elsewhere. Would give it six stars if I could.

Came here for a quick bite. 

Larb moo: 4.5/5 PERFECTION. nice balance between minced pork and toasted rice. Very spicy and nice palate of saltiness and vinegary mixed in this dish. I was literally indulging this dish! 

Grilled coconut milk marinated beef skewer: 4.5/5 W O W . The beef was full of flavor and juicy. The sauce was mind-blowing - the sweetness, salty, vinegary, and spiciness. The rice noodle on the side was a nice cleanser to end this dish imo. 

Coconut rice: 4/5 can def taste the coconut. 

Cool place to hangout with a group of friends or with family since they have communal table. 

Keep in mind that their dishes are on the spicier side so if you can't handle spicy, ask for mild spicy and/or no spice. 

This place is definitely one of my favorite Thai restaurant! Can't wait to come back and try more of their delicious food!

First time trying a Thai spot in the Alphabet City/East Village and I must say, I wasn't disappointed at all!
As soon as you walk in, you're greeted by waiters wearing t-shirts and straw hats. The counter is surrounded by large, glass jars filled with herbs and etc. You can spot a man behind the counter using a mortar and pestle to crush something (couldn't see what it was). 
As soon as I was seated, I knew I had to start off with their famous papaya salad (classic with an egg) and boy oh boy, was it mouth-watering and the best I've had so far! 
I then had the Goong Chae Nam Pla (aka prawn sashimi). Although the dish is raw, it didn't taste like it at all; I suppose the extreme spicy chili did the trick and loved  every bit of it! I even took a bite of the chili which I absolutely regretted afterwards. Lastly, I had the Yum Goong Yang (the least spicy dish) which completed my appetite. It definitely wasn't spicy as the other two dishes I ordered but worth a try if you're looking for something mild. I finished the night with a Thai iced tea (of course) with extra milk which was made exactly the way I wanted :)
Overall, their dishes are affordable (almost everything under $15), atmosphere is simple yet stylish, waiters are attentive, and food is served very quickly. If you like hot and spicy, this is the spot to hit up.

I'm slowly getting over my aversion to Thai food. I came here with a large group of 12 with a Tuesday 7:30pm reservation. I'm surprised we were able to get a reservation so easily while only calling about two days before. They automatically added a 20% gratuity for my table of 12.  The food here is not limited to your typical pad thai, pad see ew, pad kee mao, and curry dishes, which is great because those dishes are precisely why I dislike Thai food.

Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (Deep Fried Chicken Thigh) - This looked like their most popular appetizer and with good reason. The chicken was really tender and well fried. It wasn't greasy at all. The sauce was great with it, but it didn't even need it considering how juicy and flavorful the meat was. This is a must get appetizer.

Goong Chae Nam Pla (Thai Prawn Sashimi) - I really enjoyed this dish, but I was probably the only one at my table who did. It's not spicy and the raw shrimp was really tasty. It's not as shrimpy as Japanese ebi, but the spicy marinade didn't overpower the shrimp flavor at all. Also a great appetizer to get. 

Tum Thai Kai Kem (Papaya salad with salted duck egg) - We ordered the medium spicy and it was quite spicy for me. The flavors were great though. I think they could have used more salted duck egg. It looked like they just put a few pieces on top. I would have liked if they mixed it throughout the salad. 

Khao Pad Goong (Fried rice with crab and egg, $15 for the crab, $13 for the prawn) - This wasn't the best crab fried rice I ever had. The crab is a little mound on top and mixed in with the egg on the side instead of mixed into the rice. I forgot to ask for it to be spicy so it was on the bland side for me. I've had better crab fried rice, but it was still decent. 

Khao Klook Ka Pi (Jasmine Rice with shrimp paste) - My boyfriend later got this as takeout for me at a later date. This is my favorite dish here so far. Absolutely delicious fried rice. I loved mixing the green mango into it. The best part is that it has such a strong taste of shrimp paste.

Out of all the Thai restaurants I've been to in Manhattan, which I admit isn't many, Somtum Der is my favorite so far. This is one of the few times that I actually want to go back to a Thai restaurant.

I went here on January 20th, 2018 with friends. I'm only sad I was too drunk and too hungry to take pics of the food before we all messily inhaled it. Somtum Der is delicious. 

We ordered fried chicken, several kinds of fried rice, and pad see ew. Everything was outstanding.

Wow, I love this place! Excellent quality fresh ingredients prepared to perfection.  They are authentic Northern Thai. I dream  skewers of marinated beef ! The marinate with coconut-milk is awesome.  The noodle dishes are all great with a very soft and homemade like texture.

Just had lunch at Somtum Der and I am so happy I chose this place! Everything was on point. The staff was very attentive and friendly, the restaurant was cute, and menu was different from what you usually see in typical Thai restaurants. 
My friend and I were baffled at all the choices available. I've never eaten Issan Thai food before! After asking the employee, we went with the papaya salad + salted egg, grilled marinated beef (which comes with 2 grilled sticky rice), a side of fried noodle and chicken thigh. The papaya salad was the best I've had in New York, it wasn't overly sweetened and was authentically spicy! The salted egg was good too although i wished they put more eggs in the salad. My grilled beef was a bit salty too my taste, but I kept dipping it to the fish sauce cuz geez, I miss Vietnamese meals that I eat w fish sauce :P Kind of reminiscing when eating that sauce. And the grilled sticky rice stole the show! It's the best thing I ate today!! The rice had a strong coconut smell and tasted heavenly! It's crispy outside but somehow managed to be soft inside!! I could eat more skewers of sticky rice by its own. But dipping it in the special fish sauce is the best. 

I'd recommend Somtum to anyone who wants to try more exotic Thai food. The quality here is so good! I'll come back really soon!!!

Somtum Der is a unique Thai restaurant, less of a comfort pad Thai place and more of an adventure into exoticism, both in dishes and ambiance. 

No wait on a Saturday night for seats by the window, but every table was booked. This is a popular place. 

Tum Thai Tom Krem (papaya salad with salted egg) - 3/5. A light start for the night with this salad, not overwhelming with the papaya taste, but not much taste otherwise either. 

Nue Rong Hai Der (house special grilled marinated beef) - 5/5. Couldn't stop eating this beef. The only thing wrong was that it ended. The grilled sticky rice (in a corn dog-fashion) stole the show. 

Pad Kee Mao (spicy flat rice noodles with beef and basil) - 4/5. I rarely indulge in noodles, but I'm glad I did this time. This dish was delightful. Noodles cooked perfectly, just thick enough, and complemented by the well-seasoned beef and basil. 

The NYC Thai scene needed a unique restaurant like Somtum Der, and with these prices, there's no reason not to try it at least once.

The Thai food is very authentic.   It is just little spicy.   The prawn sashimi, pork skewer and fried chicken .  The rice with shrimp paste and seafood suki is good too.  I would come back to try other dishes.
Cheap and delicious Michelin starred restaurant! Most dishes are smaller and meant to be served family style, so remember to order your own side of starch (rice).

What you need to know: 
- Went on a Monday night and it was PACKED! 
- Isan Thai cuisine: originated from the northeast region of Thailand. Sticky rice, larb and salads, grilled meats are common, curries are not. 
- Accepts credit cards 
- The waitress asked us if we wanted the food spicy, the way it comes, but I didn't think it was that spicy at all. 

What we ordered: 
- Deep Fried Chicken Thigh, price $10 - they make a mean fried chicken! This chicken was really and truly killer! The crust was crunchy and tasted substantial and the chicken meat was dark, hot and juicy! It came with a spicy dipping sauce, which made it even better! 
- Pad Kee Mao (with pork)$13 - I tend to get Pad Kee Mao everywhere I go and this ranked quite high. I liked how the noodles didn't stick together and it wasn't covered with gooey sauce. It was topped with crispy fried basil leaves. It could have been spicier, in my opinion. 
- Mixed mushroom in lemongrass soup $12 - the soup featured generous portions of three types of mushrooms: oyster, enoki and white beech. I was expecting a light lemongrass soup but the flavors punched me in the face! It was earthy, had a complex spiciness, and a slight sourness from the lemongrass. While the flavors were very good, this soup was WAY TOO SALTY! I had to take it home and dilute it with great quantities of water.

Was pleasantly surprised by the unique and authentic dishes on the menu! Overall, staff was friendly and attentive, food came out quickly and was super fresh (you can actually see them preparing spices etc in a mortar and pestle from the dining area). 

Larb moo: so tasty and spicy!! 

Spicy Beef salad: tasty, similar flavor to the larb

Sausage sampler: def my favorite. The Thai sausage was amazing, and everything tasted great when eaten with the lime, peanuts and chili's they were served with.

Pork spring rolls: AMAZING. Was pleasantly surprised when I bit in and was met with tasty kaffir lime leaves!!

Isan Sour (cocktail): unique and refreshing - highly recommend trying a cocktail made with Mehkong liquor!!

**Do not come here if you only like Pad Thai. :)
Food was amazing! We had an appetizer that was a bit on the spicy side but so worth it. Thai iced tea and desert are also must haves.

Awesome Thai food. Not my #1 Thai spot, but they're super speedy and the food is cheap. Got the papaya salad (you have to), duck (I'd skip this one), and the seafood with glass noodles (I was surprised I liked this as much as I did). Oh annnnd the coconut rice. Don't forget to get that. We ordered everything spicy and it wasn't over the top. I could hang.
