I just had my 28th year old birthday dinner there! It can be a busy place, so I appreciate that you can make reservations for groups! I've eaten here before, and i love the atmosphere & food!

It's food from Northeastern Thailand, Isan style. They can make things very spicy, if you ask  my favorite so far is the Ping Kati Sod (grilled meat that has been marinated in coconut milk). The fried meats are worth trying, too. Fried Isan sausage? Yes plz. They are known for their papaya salads and larb. I have many more dishes I'm curious about. I never claimed to be Thai, so I personally can't speak to its authenticity. My friend who was in school in Thailand & lived in the surrounding countries her whole life seemed to be impressed, though, if thats any indication!

Drink menu has a good variety. Some taste watered-down, or did not pick a good alcohol ratio for the drink. Save your money if you're looking to get drunk. Because when you're here, it's all about the FOOD!

Taro in condensed coconut milk is warm, sweet, and perfect. i try to leave room in my stomach for it. Other desserts look promising. I will be back trying more soon enough!

Lovely place to go and share small plates! I went with my friend from Thailand, and he said this is his absolute favorite place because the flavors are all authentic. We had the kee mao noodles, which was made with ground pork and topped with crispy basil -- my absolute favorite part of the dish! It was definitely one of the top kee mao dishes I've had in the city. But the prices were just a little too steep for me. Still, try the grilled sticky rice and the fried chicken! So delicious! They also have great vegetarian options. The Thai iced tea was *good* but not GREAT, but the longon tea was ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS.

Delicious authentic Thai food as close as you can get to what you'd find in Thailand. Only this place and Uncle Boons can really achieve that level of authenticity for me (in Manhattan).

The communal tables and benches make it very community feeling - prob not the best place for an intimate date but great for a group of friends. The drinks are great and service is fast. Everything tastes more spicy than you'd expect but is awesome!

Arrived there one evening at approx. 5:30. We were told that they were on a break and told to come back later. The waitress was sort of lying on one of the benches. This is how you welcome customers that are prepared to spend money!

Since he really wanted Thai food for dinner, this was one of the only places that my friend recommended to me that didn't have too long of a wait around 9 PM on Saturday. We didn't have to wait very long for a table which was nice because we woke up from our nap starving!

Between the two of us, we shared some tum, crab fried rice, and a pork dish with sticky rice. 

I was not too big of a fan of the pork - I wanted to order kor moo yang but they didn't have it and recommended this one instead. I think it was a bit too spicy for my taste and not the most tender.

However the som tum thai and crab fried rice were delicious! I just ordered the plain one because I wasn't sure if he would like the egg or the crabs. After all of the indulging we had been doing, this was so refreshing to have.

The crab fried rice was so flavorful and had a lot of crab! I really enjoyed it and the nam plaa prik on the side. 

Definitely coming back for the crab fried rice and som tum. :)

Wow, amazing Thai food! I use to work as a waiter in college at a Thai restaurant, and when the wait staff have an accent because English is there second language, you know they're legit. 

We got:
- Papaya Salad: mild is spicy for the American palate 
- Fried Chicken Thighs 
- Basil Fried Rice
- Pad See Eew w/ beef 
- Pork egg rolls 

I highly recommend this place and make a reservation as it gets busy.
Ive been here twice and ready to come back. The food is real Thai food you usually do not find unless you venture into Queens. Fresh, bold flavors. Highly recommended

Sumtom Der is a must go place for spicy lover. The restaurant specialized in E-San food.  Very authentic. The food is excellent I would give them 100 out of 100 point. Somtum was the famous dish from this place along with many E-San dishes. The restaurant decoration was nice and decent which is reflected Thai's people life. The servers were very friendly and attentive. I'm extremely recommend this restaurant for people who love Thai food and spicy.
A solid and authentic Thai food place. Recommend their papaya salad with salted egg and their coconut rice. The fried rice was decent.

This is the best, most authentic Thai food in Manhattan! My dear friends from Thailand will only come to this restaurant to eat Thai food. The food is absolutely delicious and reminds me of what we eat during our time in Thailand. The service is okay and the ambiance is okay but you are going for incredible food. Be open minded - there offering is so much more than just pad Thai. Enjoy the unique flavors!

I wish my Sunday lunch experience was better, like most of you. 

I came in late and my group had already ordered for the table, nice -- one of us was from the north of Thailand and very familiar with this region of foods and ordered for us -- so I don't remember exactly what we had.

Papaya salad - we had two kind, one with raw crab. The crab had sweetness in meat, if you can get the meat out. I love its sweet, sour, and spicy mixture in the sauce with fresh garlic flavor in the dressing, but this dressing was different, just very salty. Contrary to most reviewers, even our classic papaya salad was disappointment, just salty. I think we got the ones with fermented fish sauce, muddy color. I like fermented fish but did not translate well in this salad for me. 

Isan style mushroom soup - it was another just salty soup -- I found out it also has fermented fish (not fish sauce) -- grilled sticky rice with a stick was different and interesting.

Pad Ki Mao - drunken noodles is another favorite of mine, Somtum Der version of this dish was different, no complex flavor and just one note, saltiness. The flat wide noodles was chewy and we enjoyed it.Thai tea was good as any other Thai place in the city. 

I'll give another try if I'm in the area, because of such a good reviewers from many of you and also highly recommend by my other Thai friends.

I came here hearing that this place had a Michelin star before. Was pretty  excited to come here and made a reservation. 

Got the fried chicken, crab fried rice, grilled pork skewers. 

The fried chicken had some peanuts on it I think. It was supposed to be spicy and the sauce didn't really complement it well. I thought it was sour and the chicken was spicy. I chicken was soft and tender, but just didn't think it was that great.

The pork skewer was probably one of my favorite. It was pretty juicy and the sauce complimented the pork a bit better.

The crab fried rice was another highly recommended dish. Was the rice fried that well? Honestly I've had much better. It wasn't really crispy, and it looks like there's a lot of crab, but in reality it's just next to a lot of egg.

Another thing...the service...it was bad in one aspect...they keptttt asking us if we were done with our items even when there was still clearly food on the table. That really annoys me. How this place ever got a star amazes me. The food isn't that great, the service was awful. Overall not a great experience.

I had a few things here:

The papaya salad
Moo Ping
The ice with syrup
Thai ice tea

Everything here was awesome. The papaya salad had the right amount of heat and a touch of sweetness. The vegetables were fresh and the sauce was light but flavorful and tasty. The moo ping was out of this world, the meat was tender and i LOVED the touch of coconut flavor they had on it. The ice with syrup was cool, it was HUGE. It tasted like blended ice was a strawberry or bubble gum syrup inside maybe with some sort of milk type thing as well. The thai ice tea was also very good. I'll definitely come here again.

Excellent excellent !  Although you have to love genuine Thai food instead of the westernize Thai that typically served on most NYC restaurants, else you might think differently of the food here.

Haven't had too many traditional Thai food.  And this along with a couple of them in Restaurant Row on 9th Avenue, plus several in Queens are the only few authentic tasting Thai restaurants.

Their servers are sweet, the Thai ice tea is awesome.  The coconut rice is one of the best I've had in NYC.  Tried several dishes and some were better than others in my opinion, although they were all good. 

My least favorite was the Wok-fried rice vermicelli with seafood, vegetables and our signature suki sauce. 

Sampled the appetizer sampler and liked the fried beef.  Although the sausages were quite interesting. But that's about the extent of liking it. 

My favorite that I've tried so far is the Grilled coconut milk marinated pork skewer!!! Absolutely divine.  Eat that with coconut rice and it will bring you to Thailand without the 16 hour flight. 

Can't wait to come back and try more entrees such as the fried chicken etc. and other noodle dishes. 

They have me hooked. They earned 1 Star Michelin for the foodies that knows authentic Thai.  Just saying.
Love the variety of papaya salad. Food is great and service is very pleasant. Would visit often.

Service was good. Food was amazing. I haven't been to Thailand so can't say how authentic it was but it tasted pretty non-Americanized (they are not afraid to use the fish sauce). Make sure to come early. Even on a weekday night, there's a long wait time. I personally really liked the fried chicken.

There's nothing you can really negative you can set about this kind of place. They are fully representing Thai cuisine with the up most respect. A lot more than most of these suburbs Thai restaurants.
The food and drinks were authentic and delicious. The service was casual but attentive. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a delicious authentic Thai meal.
Papaya Salad with Salted egg! Interesting menu for the adventurous foodie. Small portions so order a nice variety and eat family style.

Finally checked this place out and it was actually fairly empty on a Sunday night. This place falls solidly in the category of places where I enjoyed my meal and had no complaints but nothing stood out so I'm not exactly inclined to go back. It's sad because I was really hoping to like this spot, as a new goto for Thai in Manhattan. 

We tried:

Grilled beef skewers - Tender savory and flavorful, 3 skewers, comes with the spicy sauce that was a tad bit too salty. 

Crab pad Thai - This comes with a bit of spice, which is probably the authentic way, but honestly I like my pad Thai less spicy. The crab was yummy.

Salted egg pad Thai - The salted egg wasn't bad although even at medium this dish was a tad spicy for me.

Here come another authentic Thai restaurant in NYC. I had fried chicken,papaya salad with fermented fish,grilled sticky rice with grilled pork. Those were delicious like you are eating in Thailand.No doubt why this place always jam packed with people.
This restaurant is mind-blowing, I wish I could give it 10 stars. I do believe this is the best Thai food in NYC.

The papaya salad (somtum) was indeed very good, and goes well with their sticky rice. I chose the medium spicy vegetarian version. Beware, medium is spicier than most people are used to. The longan tea also helped cool things down, but it tasted more like the sugar (brown sugar?) they put in it, rather than longan, which might not be a bad thing if you're not used to the taste of longan.

Great Thai food. We got a table of 3 late Saturday night. They said it was a 30 minute wait but it actually turned out to be less. The host gave us the option to leave our phone number so she could call us when the table was ready. 

We went to mother of pearl on the next block over for a quick drink while we waited. 

I got the pad kee mao, which was decently spicy and flavorful. We also got egg rolls for the table - recommend. 

Overall, this was a nice sit-down thai food place. Clean, friendly, cute decor.

This is the best Thai restaurant I've ever been to. I am Thai and know how exactly authentic Thai food should be. Service is a little slow because they were really busy. The guy who cooked papaya salad  was really clean as well.

Food is very spicy so watch out what you order.  I personally like it spicy.  But not all do.

I personally recommend the pork bbq sticks.  That is the best!

Price is right.  Who needs to cook at home and buy all those ingredients.  So worth eating there anytime.  A little far for me though.

It's definitely authentic Thai food.

Tip:  If you find the dish too spicy, they can make another less spicy but you cannot change the item you ordered.   It will have to be the same even though they are making something less spicy for you.  My friend tried to change her dish completely since they gave her a spicy version when she wanted just low in heat.  But they would not change her order.

I went to Somtum Der for dinner on a rainy Sunday, ready to have some amazingly delicious Thai food like on my previous visit... But I was sorely disappointed.

We ordered the salted egg somtum, the duck laab salad, stir-fried mushrooms, and the chef's special seafood vermicelli dish. The somtum had a lot of papaya and tomatoes, some egg, but very few string beans. It was also surprisingly bland. The duck laab salad tasted better, which was a combination of sour, salty, and spicy with onion and other herbs, but it was overly salty. The mushrooms and seafood vermicelli were much too sweet, and lacked depth to the flavor. 

The service was good - our glasses were always refilled quickly, and the waiter was easy to find. The decor is a bit minimalist but it works. The value for this meal wasn't quite there for me - the quality and quantity of food didn't really hit my target.

Overall, I'm giving this a 3 because I'm hoping this was an isolated experience, and I had such a good meal last time... But I was disappointed this time.

Authentic, tasty Bangkok street food in a comfortable eatery. Unusual cocktails as well. The chicken, beef, pork, and vegetarian dishes goes with the hot sauce and sticky rice. Also try the pork spring rolls - excellent appetizer.
I ordered Som Tum salad and it was so bland and no flavor at all! I'm Thai and this dish is more like Americanized. Very disappointing.

Love this place! 90% of the menu is spicy, but it is bearable. Very good authentic Thai food! Although the prices for the seafood noodles are high, you get lots of seafood, so it's definitely worth the higher price. They also serve Leo beer. Try to make a reservation if you can. This place get packed very quickly, especially on Friday nights.

Fantastic food and a beautiful space. The noodles left me craving them for weeks, and the salads were interesting and fresh. One star off for the staff watching me suffer from accidentally eating a pepper or some other spice particle and apparently enjoying it, but even that could not spoil the food experience

Arrived here at 4:40pm. Followed a couple in. Both of our parties were turned away because they have a paper sign on their door stating they are closed from 4pm-6pm.

Both of our parties came from across town. Different parts of town, but nonetheless. Yelp hours are posted as open until 10:30pm. Please update your hours. I wasted an hour of my time walking and catching the bus here. Traveling from out of state.

Your server told me the Manager was not present. And that the kitchen was on break already so he couldn't seat us. Ridiculous.

Terrible customer service. It wasn't even 4pm yet. Post your last seating time so we don't waste our time or money trying to come to you.

always enjoy meals here, but wish servers would communicate when auto gratuity has been applied. after a fantastic birthday dinner, my friend was left with a bad taste in her mouth when she found out later her brother had accidentally tipped over 40%.
Came in for lunch. Prompt service. Food was great. Knocked off one star for only including two pieces of shrimp in my order.

Somtum has been on my radar for awhile, their menu differs from some other Thai restaurants in the city so I've been kind of keeping them on the back burner for when I wanted to try something out of my comfort zone, but they still had the items I was most familiar with (albeit at a higher price) so I decided to try them for delivery. 

I would not recommend ordering your standards here. My boyfriend ordered their crab pad thai ($16), and while the crab was fresh the noodles were dry and almost completely tasteless. Same for the pad kee mao with ground pork: dry and bland. We were putting all kinds of condiments we had at home to make the stuff edible, I'm not sure who this was supposed to be geared towards in terms of flavor, it was an absence of taste. 

Still three stars though. I will say, in terms of deep fried nonsense, their pork spring rolls are delicious. They come with a creamy white sauce but what can I say, I prefer the sweet chili I keep in the fridge. They're super long, like cigars, so you get a nice bang for your buck there, and the pork is more pronounced than in other spring rolls. 

And their raw shrimp kills it. I've only had this once before (thanks to Ben. L!), so while I don't have much to compare it to I thought it was delicious. The dish is extremely spicy, but like Ben says, just push some of those peppercorns off to the side and you'll be fine. Or do what I do, pile on as many as you can and have a religious experience. Either way, this is worth getting and isn't easy to find. 

Finally, I had their Thai Iced Tea Panna Cotta. Damn that was a good dessert. It comes with what I think is a little container of condensed milk to pour on top. The flavors and textures were perfect, and it's a dessert that's not too sweet, and a great choice to cool your mouth off after those spicy shrimp. 

Overall it was hit or miss; but I would come back to try other things that aren't so familiar to me.

Came here early on a Sunday night without a reservation and we were seated immediately. This restaurant can get pretty busy on weekend nights, so it's recommended to come early if you don't have a reservation. 
The wait staff were friendly and served us efficiently, bringing us water and menus. Shortly after, we placed our orders for dinner, and decided to share three dishes: two salads (one was duck larb, and one was sliced pork) and papaya salad. Our food was served very quickly after we ordered. 
The duck salad wasn't as spicy as I initially thought it'd be, but was still good to eat. The papaya salad was fresh and made well, and contained a higher spice level that I enjoyed. 
The pork salad was also delicious. 
After our savory courses, we split the Thai tea pannacotta, which was silky and smooth, with a strong Thai tea flavor.
Ambience is simple and kind of trendy. Good for a casual and quick dinner.

We had Tum Thai Kai Kem (green papaya salad), Moo Rong Hai Der(grilled marinated pork chop) + khao Ji(sticky rice on stick) and Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay (flat noodle with shrimp and calamari). They are all very decent and unique taste and amazed me a lot
I honestly can't get enough of this place. So freaking delicious. Do yourself a favor and get the larb tod meatballs as a starter. Omnomnomnom
Not nearly as good tasting as it looks. They do good business and a lot of Thai folk frequent the place. Worth a shot...but don't have your expectations too high.
Favorite Thai restaurant in NYC. Their food is flavored well and from the northeast region of Thailand which is known for the best dishes. Place is small but the service is good.

Food was really delicious, good vibes, great service, place is nice and clean. 
Unfortunately , in order to enter, you have to go through a gauntlet of Homeless people that built a camp right out side the restaurant. They smell really nasty, they use the downstairs area right under the entrance to do all kinds of things....Use your imagination,   I think I picked up some flees, on my way in/or out the door. I had weird itchy bites on my ankles. 
To bad they are not doing anything about it. Will not go there again.

Visited this place for a casual dinner and man, was I blown away! We shared a bunch of things between four people, which was awesome. That way, we were able to try a bit of everything on the menu.

SPICE ALERT. I've had food in Thailand, and the spice level on the food here definitely isn't for the faint of heart. Definitely comparable in flavors AND in spice. haha

Papaya Salad: fresh but it DESTROYED our mouths with the spice haha
Fried Rice: forgot which one we got, but pick a protein of your choice. It was super tasty and had a yummy vinegar-like sauce with it.
Sausage Plate: lots of options that were great to share!
Eggrolls: always a good idea.
Beef dish: I'm so sorry I can't remember which one I got, but it was amazing.

Honestly, I'll def be back next time I'm in NYC. Want to try other things, and I'm sure I won't be disappointed.

After seeing great reviews and recommendations for this Michelin recommended restaurant, I decided to check out this restaurant yesterday with 4 of my friends. Upfront I must say that we were disappointed with the overall service. We ordered drinks first like always but we got the drinks only after we had finished all the appetizers. This happened again when we ordered entree and another round of drinks, when the drinks came when we were close to finishing our meal. The appetizers were good but not crazily amazing because I have had better food in restaurants which have much less rating and are much cheaper. I do not recommend the Khao klook ka pi. It was very bitter and we felt the pork was very old. Other entrees were comparatively ok. Overall, I felt the restaurant was under staffed and food is not worth the price or atleast we did not have a great experience

A different type of Thai experience than I am used to, but definitely one i can get accustomed to! Echoing other reviews- the spice level at Somtum Der is no joke (the papaya salad is AMAZING!) so if you are not one that is too fond of spice, be sure to ask the waiters/waitresses (who are very nice and accommodating) what is best suitable for your taste. 

Other thing we got- the larb, Thai teas all around, basil fried rice, and pad khee mao. All so so good. Came on a Thursday night at 7pm and it was filled up, but not too crowded! Would definitely be back :)

I called in about the extra gratuity issue and they refunded the extra amount. Hopefully they update their system. 
Food was great and I'll definitely be back. Their spice level is 'authentic' so order things mild if you want a medium/hot spice level!
Definitely an authentic Thai restaurant! Had the real spice and taste that I am used to in Thailand!

Cute restaurant 
Many families had lunch there
Good food
Seems specialized for their spice and sourness? 
I probably did not chose the right dishes for me

Recommendation:
1: Beef Ping Kati Sod(Grilled Coconut Milk Marinated Beef Skewer)
2: Grilled Sticky Rice (Coconut Milk Marinated)
3:Thai Tea Panna Cotta
We ordered two sets of Beef Ping Kati Sod and Grilled Sticky Rice since sooo delicious!

Authentic, delicious southeast Asian food! What a find! Located in the lower east side, Somtum Der offers a wide variety of dishes at affordable costs. When I visited, I ordered the papaya salad, chicken skewers with coconut milk, and the pad Thai. Beware: the papaya salad is VERY spicy!

The only downfall about this place is the restroom situation. With only one unisex bathroom in the whole entire restaurant, there's often a line outside - unfortunate for the people sitting by the bathroom  trying to eat their meal without feeling like anyone is hovering over them.

IG: @twomorebites

Our dinner was one of the more unique and memorable experiences in my culinary journeys. It always feels good when everyone in your dinner party is commending you for the "great restaurant choice." 
We couldn't get reservations for a party of 5 for a Friday night so some of us arrived 15 mins before the restaurant opened at 6pm to ensure a short wait time. We were the first to enter the restaurant when the doors opened and were seated right away. 
We were happy to hear that HH was 5-7pm with half off all drinks and fried chicken thighs were only $6 (we ordered 3 rounds of the chicken wings!). In addition, we also ordered the salted egg papaya salad, duck larb, Pad thai mun poo, and Vermicelli mackerel (dish of month), and also the coconut rice. We ordered medium spice for everything except for the vermicelli dish which we ordered mild spice. Nothing was held back- the taste, the authenticity and the spice! We loved each and every last dish. Every bite packed a kick and a bag of chips. (We did notice that after HH, the chicken wings dish portion size was a lot bigger than the HH dish size though.)
For dessert, we each had something different so we were able to taste everything on the menu. The snow ice was definitely big enough for 3 maybe even 4 people to share!! It started tasting like bepto bismal after a while, but still really fun to eat. My favorite was the penna cotta. Everyone seemed to like their own dessert the best so it's hard to say which one reign supreme. My advice is go with a huge group so you can try as much on the menu as you can. Can't seem to find a bad item on the dish. Fyi.. There's an automatic tip applied for large groups. Not sure what the group cut off is, but my group of 5 received the charge.

The Moo Ping Kati Sod (coconut milk pork skewers) was really tasty!! This was by far my favorite dish. SO TENDER. 

The Tum Thai Kai Kem (papaya salad with salted egg) was also very good, even though I don't usually like papaya salad.

The Pad Thai Mun Poo (crab) and Seafood Suki were also good, but not as memorable as the first two dishes. 

Service was great. Even though the front entrance isn't very nice, the restaurant is clean, well-lit, and spacious. The menu has plenty of pictures and their "medium" spicy was plenty spicy for me.

It tastes like the Somtum Der in Siam Square. A must try if you are looking for north eastern thai food. They also have a lot of Thai staple food. I must admit I probably go here at least 5 times a year!

I have a soft spot for Thai food as it reminds me of my travel days back in Bangkok/Phuket. There was a Somtum Der also in Bangkok and the food here tastes just like what you will have in Thailand! Somtum Der has your mainstream Thai food but also Northern Thai food which is absolutely delicious. A must try if you are a fan of Thai food!

I would've loved to have given this 4 or 5 stars, as the Pad Ki Mao Nue was incredibly tasty, but I'm so disappointed to have paid almost $16.50 for a container of noodles that was literally less than half full. It was genuinely so light that I thought it might have been the wrong order and that I'd just find an appetizer in the bag.

This place is so delicious!
My bf and I found this place when we went to the thai festival this past summer. We got their menu and decided to try it. 2 of our friends came along.

This spot is authentic thai! Their papaya salad is so yummy. I was never into that but this was so good! The sauce was amazing and goes well.

We ordered a bunch food and appetizers to share. We also got the pork soup. That was super spicy. I started sweating cause it was that spicy. Good for the cold weather I guess.

Nice, casual thai restaurant in the East Village, close to many bars and restaurants. Ordered the fried chicken, pad thai and the coconut skewers. Chicken and pad thai were good, the coconut skewers were outstanding and are a must order at Somtum Der.

One of the better Thai restaurants that I've tried in the city! I came here with a group of friends and ordered 5 dishes to share. Everything seemed delicious, but we ended up ordering the duck larb, papaya salad with pork neck, fried chicken thigh, mushroom and pumpkin soup, and pad kee mao. 

Duck Larb: very flavorful with a ton of spice and red onions. 

Papaya Salad with Pork Neck: the pork neck had a slight char outside and it was juicy inside. It had a similar texture to a soft jerky. The papaya salad was spicy and slightly sour from the lime. It was a mixture of great flavors. 

Fried Chicken Thigh: very crispy on the outside, but the chicken was still very juicy. The dipping sauce adds a little bit of spice and acidity.

Mushroom and Pumpkin Soup: I didn't really care for it. Not a fan of mushrooms, so it was just ok.

Pad Kee Mao: slightly spicy, but so good. I would definitely order this if you're looking for a noodle dish.

Overall, if you're craving some flavorful, spicy Thai food, then you have to try this spot! It's an ideal place for a small group so you can order various items and try many dishes. I'd recommend ordering 5-6 dishes for a group of 4 people, or 3-4 dishes for 2 people. I wish the servings were slightly larger, but the quality of the food is great! I'll definitely be back again.

I went here with a friend and split a few dishes. They have a rather large menu, so it was difficult to settle in on a few choices.

The food here is very good, but I thought that it was a bit pedestrian compared to some of the other Thai spots I have tried around the city.

That being said, the staff was super friendly and accommodating and we were able to be seated right away on a busy weeknight.

Decent number of tables and the service is great! They're strong on the mood lighting, so make sure your eyes function when you come here. 

Original papaya salad: delicious! It's got a great spice kick. 

Pad Thai: yummy as well! 

Coconut rice side: the coconut flavor is good and well balanced. 

Grilled beef: I wish the beef was grilled more, but it was good anyway. A bit salty. 

Overall, I'd definitely come back. The prices are a bit higher than other places, but the food is so good here!

Food was delicious. Their food is authentic and they are some common items for someone like us to have. Price is reasonable and service is great. They always smile and wouldn't mind when we asked for taste adjustment. Their location is a little off as it is very far from any subway and what we did was we took uber from subway. Every time I go to NYC, I never skipped this place. I love their authentic papaya salad and grilled pork with white noodles or they are even great with sticky rice!! 

I gave them 4 stars only because it is always that we have to stand at the door waiting to be seated while they actually saw us and there were tables. Staff was plenty so if one was immediately greeting us and seating us (doesn't have to be right away), they would take my 5 stars! :)

Somtum Der is awesome! This was in my bucket list for a long time, since it's in the Michelin bib gourmand list, and comes recommended by a coworker of mine who is well-known in the NYC food scene. The girlfriend and I finally came here last weekend to meet a friend.

We were a group of 4, and even though the place was very crowded we were seated right away. The service is very fast, but food quality is also real good. What differentiates this place with other Thai places is the quality of ingredients. We got entrees for ourselves, 2 apps and 2 desserts.

Among the apps, the Thai mackerel papaya salad had balanced flavors, and the sausage plate had a great variation of sausages, and red sauce it came with was awesome! I got the one of specials for my main- a traditional cold rice noodle dish (khanom jeen) that was fresh, crunchy, and had lots of umami from fish sauce. Among the dishes the others took, my girlfriend's leaf-fish fried rice was awesome. The little crispy pieces of fish and smoky flavor of the rice worked so well together! In dessert we got a Thai tea panna cotta and a huge bowl of shaved ice. Everyone loved the panna cotta because of the measured sweetness. The shaved ice was kind of ok, with an artificial strawberry flavor sauce. The breads surrounding the ice and red bean paste on top were a nice touch, though.

Overall, this place is great for coming back with friends and get a quick tasty meal. The flavors are intense and the chillies are fiery, but are balanced by plenty of freshness and variation of texture to not burden you taste buds too much.

If anyone wants to try authentic Thai food other than Pad Thai, this is the place! 

Be careful though, if you think you can handle spicy, know the difference between American level of spiciness and Thai's. A level two spicy papaya salad with pork neck sent me to Phuket, recalling that evening when I was drenched in sweat eating a spicy salad. The pork neck is tender and chewy, with every molecule filled with sweet tang and mouth numbing spice that would kill any flu virus. 

Their menu is full of the dishes you would get at a night market. Fried chicken, grilled rice ball, and spicy beef, soon would fill your belly with no room for dessert. I've learned my lesson and will save room for dessert next time.

Went in without any expectation. I ordered four dishes and all of them turned out to be very delicious! Fried chicken, grilled pork skewer with coconut, pad Thai noodle  with crab and mushroom soup was out of this world. Also don't miss Thai tea panna cotta was amazing.

BIG fan of Somtum Der. Love the many options they serve up and their Isan Thai creations. This isn't your standard pad thai/pad see ew Thai restaurant. It's authentically delicious. Some of these dishes you won't ever see at other Thai places, so feel free to ask your server for recommendations. Share with your table, so you'll be able to try more items.

Still amazing! Just wanted to add some photos of the amazing food. The somtum is the best in Manhattan for sure and their tomsabb soup is super spicy and authentic!! Order the basil fried rice and you won't regret it!

My favorite Thai restaurant in the city. Always hits the spot when I'm craving Thai. My absolute favorites are green papaya salad and mushroom soup. Thai iced tea is also always great. Even though I like spicy food, I always opt out for mild option, which is still quite hot but I'm able to enjoy without pain
The food here is amazing. Try the spicy dish with sardines: it's to die for. Portion sizes are small so you need to order more than you think you need. You won't regret it though--it's sooo good!

I love everything about this place from the food, the decor, the staff, and them taking reservations!!

I've been to many Thai places, but this is my go-to if I have visitors in NYC. I hardly order Pad Thai, but this restaurant makes a killer one. They also make delicious grilled meats, salads, and soups. 

Also, I love that the dishes here are actually spicy when they're meant to.

My kind of place. From the creative cocktails, fairly reasonable pricing, and wooden, Asian paneling decor - huge fan of it all. 

The restaurant is Isan Thai, which hails from the northern region. The plates are smaller, shareable plates, and this is exactly how a meal here should be tackled.

Warning: the food is spicy. Really. I know everyone thinks they can handle spice, but just be a little cautious.

Tum Thai: thai spicy salad. Refreshing, cold dish that really helped even things out.

Nun Dad Dieo: sun-dried, fried beef. Fun to pick at, especially with the red dipping sauce.

Moo Ping Kati Sad: pork skewers. Soft, tender. Definitely worth it.

Nue Rong Hai Der + Khao Ji: delicious, marinated slivers of beef. More flavorful that the fried beef mentioned earlier.

Larb Peb: spicy, minced duck salad. Love duck. And getting a few more veggies in you never hurts.

Pad Thai Mun Poo: can't go wrong with a little pad thai. The sweetness helped balance some of the other flavors out.

And they take reservations. Bravo.

Somtum Der is an authentic Thai experience in NYC. From the outside you might not give much credit, but once you get in the door the place has a very nice setting and you start to feel transported to Thailand.

The servers were very nice and they had great recommendations for the food. We had the papaya salad and the beef skewers for appetizers. The beef was especially good. For main we had a beef with rice which and noodles with shrimp and calamari, which were both great.

In sum, a nice dinner experience with an authentic Thai feel.
Great food, reasonable prices and fun environment. Highly recommend the papaya salads.
Beautifully prepared fast service excellent True Issan food Black sticky rice sweet Tum THAI Duck Ped Chai yen tea deliciously sweet many Thais here today interesting decor fresh an alive

Nothing not to like here. Great food, friendly service, fair prices, healthy portions. A nice authentic experience with no pretension. I had the papaya salad, beef skewers, coconut rice and the pan a cotta desert. I look forward to exploring more of the menu.

My No.1 Thai food in NYC area!
Everything tasted RIGHT, not too sweet(you know what I'm talking about.)
BBK pork belly, fried rice, pad see ew, papaya salad... the portion is great for sharing, at least for 3-4 girls I meant.


Don't forget to make a reservation before your visit! Long line girls!

Friend recommended this place since it has authentic Northeastern Thai food and the food is quite spicy. We made dinner reservations ahead of time and were seated once we had half the group. 

Thai shrimp salad was the spiciest dish we had, so spicy it made me light headed. Lots of herbs and spices.  
Papaya salad - pretty standard. Can't go wrong with this dish. 
Marinated beef skewer - these were delicious. These are apparently similar to what breakfast in Thailand is like.
Grilled marinated pork - fried with bone in. Quite good, just be careful of the bones. 
Spicy pork cartilage soup - this soup was quite spicy and had a sour spicy taste
Larb - excellent dish that I would recommend. Flavorful with all the spices and herbs. 
Thai prawn shrimp - spicy raw shrimp. Another unique dish that reminds me of the Korean raw blue crab. It's a softer chewier texture compared to when it's cooked. 
Thai iced tea was perfect. Not overly sweet and not artificial tasting at all. Also a fantastic thirst quencher from all the spicy food. 

Most of the dishes we had were spicy to some degree so make sure you can handle your spices. Good service, lots of unique northern Thai dishes that you can't get elsewhere.

I cam here with a group of 6 people. My Thai friend picked it out and from the moment he started ordering in Thai and the waiters responded back also in Thai, I knew we were in for a treat. I don't remember the names of anything we at unfortunately but I will say that everything we had was good. The food is from the northeastern region of Thailand which is my friend's favorite type of Thai food even though he is from the central region (Bangkok). The most memorable dish we had was the spicy raw shrimp which was so unexpected but completely delicious. You really can't go wrong here!
I tried two meat dishes. The meat was dry, salty, and super garlicy! I question the authenticity of the number of reviews for this place.

i knew that somtum der would be a good choice from the moment i entered the restaurant. it felt welcoming and homey. it also smelled so good. i glanced over plates on other people's tables and i instantly started to salivate. first i ordered from a large selection of martinis. i went for martini der (lemongrass vodka, lemongrass juice, roasted rice). i was truly overwhelmed by the menu because i could not decide what to order so i asked the waitress for some suggestions. she pointed out 3 entrees on the menu and i ended up orderting pad ki mao moo (flat riced noodles with ground pork and basil). i could not order better. it was pretty spicy and super complex in flavor. the noodles were soaked with flavor. if i could, i would lick the plate. i appreciated that the portion was just right. this was truly an authentic experience. i am definitely coming back.
Portion quite small for the price! Test pretty ok but a lot of msg! Very thirsty after ward 1star because I have no choice

Somtum Der is a great place for friends. They have bench seating inside and outside, so great for all weather. Also, not related to the restaurant, but the area it's located in itself is pretty rad, so there's lots of things to do before/after dinner. 

I used to live in Northeastern Thailand, and this food is the most authentic I have been able to find in NY since my return. They have such an amazing menu, much more vast than your typical pad thai or drunken noodles. Issan/northeastern thai food tends to be very different than Americanized-thai, and is flavorful and spicy.

If you like spicy, I recommend ordering somtum (papaya salad) with sticky rice. We also ordered and truly enjoyed the following:

-moo ping kati sod
-larb moo
-khao pad gai
-pad see ew

Enjoy the "aroi mak mak" (very delicious!) food

Came here with high expectations. The food wasn't bad and in fact a lot of the meat dishes were marinated really well and very savory. However a good amount of their dishes are spicy - even their crab meat padthai and there was no option to opt out for non spicy. I ordered it anyways for it's unqiueness of having crabmeat but it was just ok. It's not the usual padthai you get at a Thai restaurant, instead of the sweet and savory I only tasted the spiciness of it. The Thai ice tea also tasted a bit diluted... But yeah if you're a fan of spice, definitely recommend this place!

I was in a mood for real Thai spicy food. I came to this restaurant before with another group of friends and was impressed by the taste. It's not all Thai restaurant in Manhattan can make real thai taste. 

The location is a bit far from subway and I walk about 8 minutes from F train 2Av stop. 

Food is always delicious, we had:
- Goong chae nam pla: raw shrimp top with chili  garlic, lime juice. 10/10

- Sa poak gai tod der: deep fried chicken thighs, crispy outside and soft inside. 10/10

- Tum mao: papaya salad, crispy pork skin with local Thai vegetables and Angle hair noodles. 8/10

- Tom saab kradook on: Thai spicy pork soup with bone. 7/10

Minus one star for only have one restroom compare to the table and space. The restaurant is a medium size but it should have at least two restrooms, sometime it was a long line.

Service was good and food came fast.

I was delighted with my experience at Somtum Der. I went with two friends for Saturday lunch. The restaurant was fairly empty but it's a spacious restaurant - I would think it's a great place to bring groups. We sat down and started off with some tea. 

The menu is a little overwhelming. First, there's a lot to parse through. Then you'll notice there's a lot more than your traditional pad Thai. This place is known for their northern Thai food so we ordered a lot of different kids of food, about 9 items. Get ready for highlights below. 

Papaya salad with egg - medium spice but it's very spicy. Delicious, salty. 

Satays - I think we ordered beef. My least favorite but mostly because I don't prefer meat. The sticky rice it comes with was delicious. 

Chicken soup with local herbs - Thai soups are really strong in flavor. It was spicy, heavy ginger. We couldn't eat much of it but delicious for a few spoonfuls. 

Fried rice with pork - so good. Comes with an egg on top, perfectly seasoned. Ate it in a minute 

Pad see ew with beef - delicious. We had multiple orders of this. Noodles were wide and thin, perfectly seasoned 

Eggplant side - I'm a sucker for eggplant. Soft, delicious 

Mushroom side - a little salty but various mushrooms included

Honestly you can't go wrong here. Don't underestimate the spice and try a bunch of things.

One of the best Thai places in NYC! Super low key and casual, also relatively easy to get a reservation. 

My only complaint is that it smells a bit stinky in there due to the spices. But you get used to it and it's worth fighting through it for the food. 

We tried the pad kee mao and pad Thai - both of which were fantastic! The noodles are thin and perfectly chewy. The flavoring is on point (beware if you can't handle spicy though). The crab meat that comes with the pad Thai is a generous portion. 

We also got Thai iced teas. They were a bit too sweet but the flavor of the tea is strong and good. 

Will definitely be coming again to try everything else on the huge menu!

My friend took me here for my birthday last year, promising it would be spicy and authentic enough to suit my picky Thai tastes. It wasn't. But A for effort, right? At least the food was insanely delicious all around. Probably the best Thai spot in the city.

Tum Poo-Plara (max spicy) - Original Isan papaya salad in fermented fish sauce and field crabs. I asked for max spicy (4 chilis out of 4). It wasn't spicy enough. I asked for more. She said they could go up to 6 out of 4. Still not enough. So I asked for more. They went up to 8. Still not spicy enough. Sigh

Pork and Mushroom Soup (medium spicy) - Just perfect. Absolutely delicious

Soup Nor Mai (medium spicy) - Boiled bamboo shoots cooked with traditional Isan herbs. Another home run

Goong Chae Nam Pla (max spicy) - Thai prawn sashimi with house special green chili sauce. I legit fantasize about this dish. Like, long, dirty, screaming, orgasmic, food porn fantasies about this dish. If I had it my way, I'd put this in my mouth every night...

Both of my visits here, at least 2 years apart, were memorable. Aside from the delicious food, there's an authentic vibe to the restaurant. We ordered different items to share. The Fried Chicken was great and not dry at all. The Pad Kee Mao was just the right amount of spiciness and very tasty. I like that they used ground beef instead of slices of beef which made the dish not too heavy. The papaya salad was refreshing. 

Happy hour for drinks ends at 7:00, we were seated at 6:59 and the waitress was kind enough to ask us to order before it ended. 

It got pretty busy for a weekday night, so make a reservation!

BEST THAI IN NYC! .... or maybe anywhere besides actual Thailand.. which they have their original location in - they are the real deal. The quality of food and dishes is just so superior to the rest of the Thai in nyc it's ridiculous! If you want to try what real isan Thai food tastes like then you have to come here and skip the bland Americanized pad Thai you've been eating. You might get spiced out so if your sensitive to spicy just request mild. I can never go back to any other Thai food. Only other spots that compare are in Thailand and Laos and this is just as good!

Get ready for groundbreaking, beat all review folks... after 600+ reviews with an average 4 stars I'm coming in at, uh... 4 stars for Somtum Der.

We had a relatively early dinner after a fairly long travel day, some tromping around the city, getting to our hotel, etc. You know the drill, so specifically scouting out some spicy Thai--was on the hunt for larb that would warm our souls--we settled here. What we wanted: good heat, a couple of good drinks and zero pretense, silliness or attitude.

The casual nature of the restaurant, cute decor and the matching wait staff outfits with hats and t-shirts make for an enjoyable visit without stooping to the stupidity some chains (regarding the outfits), which this is not. At first mostly empty (we WERE early), it was packed by the time we finished. Perfect.

Larb Moo, pork with lots of heat and funk was on our minds and this plate delivered nicely. We added to that the coconut marinated beef skewers. Spectacular! A glass of wine and a beer. Portion sizes aren't large and I'm actually OK with that. Thanks, if I need enough for a family of 6 I'll head to Cheesecake Factory or a Cracker Barrel. Something tells me I can find both in the city. NOTE: quickly Googles... no Cracker Barrel in NYC, you lucky people! Multiples of CCF. Why am I not surprised?

So in all, a great little spot and I'd love to try some additional dishes and may return next time I'm in town. Still, not without odd experiences. My beer came without a glass. I look around, everyone is drinking out of the bottle. I request one and out comes a frosted mug. Well, how about offering folks one if you already have them prepared? Beer tastes better poured. And the sticky rice we specifically said we didn't want, it appeared regardless and paired quite well with the larb.

Suggests the wait staff has figured out they can get by with this and the management doesn't care enough to see the job is done right. Too bad. What could be a real rockin' place and is still pretty darn good, could be better. But I wouldn't let it prevent me from returning once. That kind of business goes on again and I'll be moving on likely. In this city, there's always a hungrier dog.

This s a true authentic taste of Thai and has a really cute setting too. If you want the good, clean raw prawns, this is a place to go! The items of the menu all looked delicious and I feel like it'll be worth it to try most of the dishes! I would go there again and I think it'll be best for a lunch meal!

Beware of posted closing times, they aren't as posted on Yelp or the website. The kitchen seems to close in an arbitrary manner. Call first if you are making a trip there to dine. If you're just passing by and they're closed, there are many other nearby, quality options.

Great Thai food that had a more diverse menu than your traditional pad see ew or pad Thai.

Would recommend coming here with a group so you can try more dishes! We got the fried chicken, beef skewers, catfish soup, papaya salad, Larb moo, and pad Thai. First thing I want to note is how spicy the larb moo is. It's very good, but beware the spice level! All the dishes have very distinct flavors and are all very different. The beef skewers had a nice sweetness to it along with the coconut noodles. The soup had a bit more of a sour taste, but was very tasty! Pad Thai, fried chicken, and papaya salad were also all solid options. 

Would definitely come back to try the variety on the menu!

The food is banging. All the dishes are very flavorful in different ways. Lots of spicy, sweet, and savory flavors. Service was pretty good. All the dishes came out quickly. They have a guy who stands at the counter and I think his only job is to mortar and pestal things. Love it. The only thing I don't like is the hats the waiters wear. They are kinda corny.
This is probably my fav Thai restaurant in the area. Hands down some of the most authentic food I've had outside of Thailand. Great staff,spicy food, and great atmosphere. Love this place.

Low quality meat cooked in low quality oil. No real taste or distinct flavour, just bland. Drinks were SUPER SWEET, the cocktail was undrinkable (we literally sent it back after a sip) Would not recommend.
My fav thai restaurant in the city!!!  The dessert is good, the main course is good, everything is good

Hands down, I never get disappointment with any of the dishes we order here... Thai food is one of my all-time favorites, and this place definitely delivers with all the flavors and portions you can be happy to spend your $ for, especially if you go with a large group and share dishes! It can accommodate a larger group so I wouldn't be afraid to go even with 7-8 people.

Not your basic Thai place, has a way more diverse menu than most and also does the staples with a step up in quality.  Would def. recommend repeat visit if just to try everything on the menu if you're in the area.  Not full blown amazing, but def. above average and very solid place for Thai!

I went here with my boyfriend and thai food is not his favorite but we both enjoyed the food here very much. The pad thai is a bit more spicy than your usual pad thai but in the best way possible. We also had the larb moo which was also really good, flavorful- I would really recommend it to those who like spicy food. Also the thai iced tea with milk is good too!

The service very prompt. Even servers hardly engage with the customers, but the service are sufficient, where they are very attentive to their patrons' need. Probably because of language barrier, but they managed to make me feel so welcome. I keep on coming back because of that and the food! Will definitely recommend and come again. Just a side note: they could do better with the single chairs. They are pretty uncomfortable.

Pad ki mao was SO delicious and flavorful! It seems to be their version of drunken noodles. I shared it with a friend today and I  have to take my husband to get more tomorrow- it was that good.

We also tried the original papaya salad, which was tasty but so incredibly hot to me it just felt like pain. I couldn't finish my portion because it hurt. We ended up ordering some rice on the side as we ate our salad just to dampen the Heat. because apparently we are both wimps. We asked for both of our dishes to be on the mild side- both items we ordered had the menu's symbol for spicy but the papaya salad was much spicier than the pad ki mao. 

So good! I can't wait to try more dishes from somtum!

Very good Thai food. Some of the best I've had in a while. Waiter was very helpful with recommendations. Food didn't take long to come here especially with the place being packed. Pretty good size restaurant without it feeling overcrowded. Noise level was average which is good so my friends and I were able to have an audible conversation during dinner. All the dishes we ordered were delicious. Service was excellent. Would love to come back soon.

My friend from Thailand took me to Somtum Der and I was hooked! 

I really enjoyed the fact that you come here for Isan-style Thai food, so no pad thai, or pineapple fried rice here... and I love it! 

The star of the show here is the Larb (spicy minced meat) and Papaya salad. The papaya salad is such a wonderful medley of sweet, sour and spicy. Paired with sticky rice, or grilled sticky rice it was such a wonderful meal! 

I brought my co-workers here the following week and they loved it as well! We did have to ask the servers to tone down the spice level for one of my co-workers but if you like heat, this place definitely delivers!
Fav thai place in town. Very tasty.  Not your kinda American Thai restaurant. Strong on flavor. Alot option for the papaya salad. Been eating there too often lately. Def will come back

We came for a Sunday lunch here where it was already crowded at that time. We are quickly sitted and started to order. 

We had pad Thai and sticky rice along with a shrimp salad. 

Sticky rice is exceptionally delicious. It's bit sweeten but not too much which is perfect to eat with their entree dishes. 

Service is nice
I just had some issues with their food portion. 
The food portion is very small whereas they charged you a very high price. 
I am little bit disappointed on that

Overall 3 stars
Excellent, tasty, authentic, reasonably priced, fast efficient friendly blah blah blah blah blah blah blah
I came here with my best friend before watching Avengers Infinity War and this is one of the best Thai food restaurants in New York City!

The food here was pretty good and tasted authentic. However, the servers try to rush you to leave, which completely ruined our dining experience. The waiters walk around and try to clear plates off your table even though you're not done eating. One waiter even dropped a dirty fork on me because he was rushing to take away my plate. 
Our table of 6 was only able to dine for less than an hour because of the rushed service. 
My friends and I were all pretty annoyed. 
STOP RUSHING PEOPLE TO LEAVE!

Overall, a pretty solid Isaan joint though I think some items on their menu stand out more than others. But first a quick word on their Thai tea panna cotta:

Get it.

With that out of the way, let's focus on what else is good here:

The papaya salads. I prefer mine with pork. The grilled pork neck has lots of delicious crunchy parts. For me, the Tum Kor Moo Yang is the way to go. 

Next tier down are the spicy salads and the larbs. I tried the duck larb here last time and while solid, I wasn't blown away by any means. I think Larb Ubol has better larbs in the city. 

As for the non-Isaan types, we tried the Pad See Eiw with shrimp and calamari which was too sweet for me. Besides, I don't love mushy, flat noodles. 

We have tried the fried chicken here as well... it's a safe call. 

I don't love any of the beef here. I think they tend to overcook beef. Also, the spice level is a bit watered down by Northern Thai standards, unless you order it spicy. Medium doesn't quite cut it if you are looking to clear up your sinuses. 

We have been here a couple of times now and I have found the dishes to be hit or miss but I think I have a general idea of what not to get here.  I know that the panna cotta will keep us coming back for more.
Excellent food! Loved the Somtum and Larb . Dishes are reasonably priced. Definitely will be coming back
edits: i found a new thai restaurant that serves food like here. it's called "hug esan" which is much better food, cheaper, and greater service !!

I decided to visit this restaurant because I love their happy hour specials. From 6pm-7pm the drinks except bottled wines were half off. Fried chicken thigh was only $6 on happy hour. The value was awesome and quality of it is usually on point.  This visit the fried chicken appeared darker in color than what I was used in the past, however the taste and flavors were still there. The mangosteen martini tasted like juiced up mangosteen in alcohol, pretty standard, cocktail did not disappoint. The po pia larb moo was something unique and it was not spicy and the cream dipping sauce complimented the pungent taste of the larb moo filling.  For dessert I had the thai tea panna cotta which capped off all the pungent garlicky  flavors I ingested with the fried chicken, larb moo and martini. 

Restaurant reopens at 6pm sharp and people were waiting outside for the doors to open. Since I was sitting alone I was given the option to sit at the stool or a table. I chose the table and I felt service was more rushed. Service was initially slow but once the restaurant got busy service felt rushed especially the waitress subtly pressuring me to order more food. The larb moo spring roll and thai tea panna cotta were recommended by the waitress.  I would return to this restaurant with more people to try more dishes.

Definitely not your average Thai restaurant - the flavours are much more authentic, and you won't find your typical oversweetened pad thai here (they do have a pad thai dish, but even that is different from the norm). Came with a friend so we got to try several dishes -

Tum Thai Kai Kem: Of course you have to get a papaya salad...the name of he restaurant literally translates to papaya salad! Neither of us had tried it before so we went with the most popular version with salted duck egg. So, so delicious - easily my favourite dish of the whole evening with the peanut, citrus, basil, and fruity and crunchy papaya. I've heard that Thai cooking tries to incorporate all/most of sweet, salty, sour, and spicy elements into each dish, and this salad totally rocks that. It's basically all the flavours you love in Thai food rolled up onto a single plate. 

Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (Fried chicken): a favourite of my friend's, though I wasn't a fan. Maybe I just only like fried chicken a certain way - shatteringly crisp skin, juicy and tender meat - but this was tougher, harder to chew, and I didn't get much flavour or heat past the texture.

Larb Ped (Minced duck salad with chiles): Good, though not a standout. Decent duck flavour, though I didn't notice any heat.

Pad Ki Mao Beef and Basil: Great dish. They were very generous with the beef and the flat noodles were perfectly chewy. Votes are in for second favourite!

Grilled Sticky Rice: What an interesting option. The rice comes shaped on a short skewer, like a kebab, and is best eaten hot. It's very dense but also quite delicious - tends to make the meal heavier though. I don't know why I was so fascinated by these when it's just sticky rice on a stick, but I'd order again for the curiosity.

Service was friendly and our waiter took the time to explain multiple dishes to us when we said it was our first time here. Ambience is on the dimly-lit side of things - would be great for a date as well.

Somtum Der is definitely not your typical Thai American restaurant! If you're looking for the usual pad Thai or green curry, this isn't the place you're looking for. If you want more authentic Thai food with spice, this is the place to go!! I got the Pad Ki Mao with Pork and basil, and it was really good!! A little bit of spice, but not too much. The pad Thai was also pretty good and it comes with crab meat. I tried a bit of the seafood suki, and it tasted yummy!! The Larb Ped (Duck) was just okay, but my friends said the larb with Pork is better. The papaya salad was hella good!!! I normally don't like papaya salad, but it was so yummy!! The Thai iced tea was also pretty good. The one negative about my experience is that they took away my Thai Iced Tea before I was completely done. I only had a bit left, so I understand why they could've been mistaken that I was finished, but it would've been good if they could've asked since there was still stuff left in the cup and because we weren't done with the rest of our meal. I don't think it was a huge deal, so I'll definitely come back still!

Had ant egg, it's exotic and good.

The duck salad is impressive. 

Coconut sticky rice is very good with the spicy dish.

Great flavors - what a wonderful journey.  The exterior of the building  had me hesitating about entering, but the restaurant space inside had a simple, yet elegant decor.  Tried 2 types of ... Somtum, of course. Both were great and the Tum Thai Kai Kem with egg was liked better

Wow. Came here for a late lunch on Friday. Pretty empty. Sat at one of the picnic tables in the middle of the restaurant.

Ordered the salted egg papaya salad, the duck larb, the fried chicken thigh, pork skewers, crab meat pad Thai, and the grilled coconut rice skewers. 

There wasn't a single dish I didn't like. If you like spicy but aren't the greatest with it, ask for two chili peppers (aka mildly spicy). The wait staff are very helpful, and the food was brought out so quickly! 

I honestly can't wait to go back to try their other papaya salads, skewers and noodle dishes.

Also great design for the T-shirt's they sell!

So I was in an Uber pool in Seattle and this guy gets in and starts speaking Thai to me, since he recognized my name was Thai. Long story short he said this was his favorite Thai restaurant in NYC. I hadn't had good Thai food in NYC before this but now I'm a believer!

I was scared there would be a wait but my friend and I got seated within 15 min on a Friday night around 9pm. Cute interior, a little cramped. 

We ordered the regular som tum, khao pad gra pao (basil fried rice), larb moo, and sticky rice. It was all delicious! Definitely get sticky rice to eat with the papaya salad. The fried rice actually has holy basil instead of the Thai basil, which is more authentic. It comes with fish sauce but it was already pretty salty so you probably don't need it. Beware of the spice levels!! We got mild for everything but it was actually pretty spicy, which I didn't mind. The flavors were awesome you gotta go!

This restaurant was my love at first bite. I love Thai food especially Isaan food which is their specialty. My favorite dishes are Tum Thai Kai Kem, Moo Rong Hai Der & Khao Ji, Khao Pad Kraprao Moo (and many more). Pretty much everything is authentic and some are even better than what you get in Thailand. Thai food doesnt have to be burning hot but a perfect blend of the flavors and heat. I live from there now and can't go back often enough.

i went to here a long time ago, shortly after it opened.  but i still think about this place all the time! the dishes are not the usual fare, which makes it worth a trip, even if you're not in the neighborhood.  definitely a place to try for those looking for something new.

the food was absolutely delicious and reasonably priced.  there's nothing demure in the flavors so consider yourself forewarned!  i'm thinking i must come back to update this review.  it's been too long!

Super spicy!  Great authentic Thai restaurant with unique dishes tucked away in the east village.  We ordered several dishes to share including the spicy minced pork salad, flat noodles, sliced beef, and friend sticky rice.  All amazing with a different type of kick to elevate the taste.  Paired everything with some Thai iced teas and had a nice experience.  Would recommend if you want not just Thai cuisine, but super spicy Thai cuisine!

nothing great here...while this place is authentic, the food was very average...the dishes were high in heat, but kinda of flavorless...also, was kind of pricey for mediocre thai fare...there are definitely less expensive and better options in nyc for thai food...
Best authentic Thai food I've ever had!! The papaya salad was amazing along with the pad see ew. Gets very busy during dinner time so I came for lunch.

Have you ever ordered coconut rice and legitimately seen the coconut milk coating the rice? If you get the coconut rice here you will. A little bit of salt, coconut milk. This is the first time I ate a whole bowl of white rice and enjoyed it. It was delicious.

We came with friends who hadn't had Thai food in forever (visiting from Hong Kong) and I had Thai twice already that week. This place was still memorable to me. The pad see ew, which is not normally a dish I like (I'm a pad kee mao girl) was to die for. The perfect blend of sweet and savory. Did they just use normal sauces or did they use a combination of Lizzo's tears and dark magic? Who knows. It sang in my mouth, I do know that.

The papaya salad? So fresh and so spicy (maybe that's why I also ate the whole bowl of coconut rice??) 

We all walked away talking about what an amazing meal this was. Can't wait to come back!

One of my fav restaurants. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu. All the variants of Somtum I have tried have been tasty and their geng hed is spot on. I've dined at this location and their location in Bangkok both are very much worth a visit. If you like Isaan food you owe it to yourself to pay a visit.

Summary:
Delicious Thai food in the East Village area. There wasn't much of a wait surprisingly when we went, but we did sit at the counter.

Food:
We ended up getting one of the larb, the papaya salad, and one of the fried chickens. The larb was excellent, with a great mix of flavors and they didn't hold back of spice or flavor intensity. 
I could say the same about the papaya salad, which I also throughout enjoyed.
The fried chicken was decent, but not spectacular. I would actually pass on that one next time unless you really like fried chicken, but it is one of the more recommended ones.
I personally enjoyed the sticky rice more than the coconut rice, but the coconut rice did help take the edge off when the spiciness in the papaya salad or larb was too much.

Service:
Great and enjoyable service, and had an overall great time.

I came here with a few friends and ordered a bunch of dishes which included: Pad Thai Mun Poo, Larb Moo, Beef Ping Kati Sod, Tum Thai Kai Kem, Beef Pad See Ew, coconut rice and Por Pia Larb Moo. Everything was amazing. The spicy dishes are pretty spicy - just a warning for those who can only handle just a little bit of spice. I also ordered the Royal Blush drink - it was super delicious! The food overall was great. 

The only complaint was that the waiters seemed to be in a rush.  I understand it was a Friday night and there was a long line of people waiting to be seated.  However, different waiters kept stopping by to look at our table to take empty dishes off one by one.  BUT they would attempt to take dishes off that weren't completely finished.  There was a good bite or two left, and they kept trying to take dishes away without asking if we were done.  We had to keep asking them to leave the dishes on the table.  We wanted to enjoy ourselves and still had other full plates of food to finish. As soon as the last dish was taken off the table, they gave us our bill a second later. Although the food was amazing, the service could have been better.

Yes, the restaurant looks as dingy as it gets on the outside, but don't let the exterior fool you because hidden behind those doors is actually a Michelin star restaurant ... but does it deserve that star?

I came here recently as part of a group of 4, so we got a chance to try quite a bit of different dishes from their large menu. We got here exactly when they opened at 6pm on a Tuesday, although we had reservations anyway. The restaurant was empty at the time, but as soon as business began, customers started filing in consistently.

One thing to definitely keep in mind prior to your meal is that this is not your average NYC Americanized Thai restaurant where you can recognize everything on the menu. In fact, put your reading glasses on because everything is listed in Thai first, followed by a small English description below it.

As for the food, we tried to get a little bit of everything or what we thought was the best of everything that sounded good, which included:

Tum Thai Kai Kem (Thai Spicy Papaya Salad with Salted Egg)
H'orderves Der (Sampler Dish)
Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (Deep Fried Chicken Thigh)
Por Pia Larb Moo (Deep-fried Spicy Pork Spring Roll)
Nue Ping Kati Soti (Grilled Coconut Milk Marinated Beef Skewers)
Pad Thai Mun Poo (Spicy Pad Thai with crabmeat and crab paste)
Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw Talay (Thai Styled Fried Pad See Ew with Shrimp and Calamari)
Vegetarian Fried Rice (Fried rice with assortment of mushrooms and veggies)
Grilled Sticky Rice - Der's Style

I won't comment on everything, but a few of them definitely left some lasting memories - some having me daydream for days about it and some vanishing from my mind like a distant memory. First, the H'orderves Der. This was an interesting dish, but mostly because of the little slice sausages, which reminded us of Chinese sausages that you can buy at a market. As for everything else on it, it was just OK. 

Some of my favorites included the Nue Ping Kati Soti (beef skewers) and Por Pia Larb Moo (pork spring rolls). Honestly, I can't resist a good beef skewer and pork spring roll (like at dim sum) and both were really good and flavorful. The spring rolls were extra crispy and had plenty of seasoned ground pork meat inside. Also, the Vegetarian Fried Rice (with mushrooms and veggies) was tasty too as the rice was perfectly fried and a large serving of flavorful straw mushrooms sat right next to it. 

However, my favorite was surprisingly the Grilled Stick Rice - Der's Style. Who would have thought that my favorite dish out of everything was rice?! The sticky rice was mounted onto a stick and literally could be eaten like a corn dog. It had a coconut flavor to it, so that was a huge winner for me since I love me some coconut.  

As for disappointments, the Pad Thai Mun Poo (spicy pad thai) was a bit on the moist side. It was too soggy for everyone at our table. Also, the papaya salad was just ehhh. There wasn't much to it.

Everything here was solid, but nothing really surprised our entire table, in terms of how amazing it was. I will say that the dishes and flavors were much more unique and exotic than what we were used to for Thai food, which was fine as it was geared toward the region of Thailand it originated from. However, the flavors from this region of Thailand didn't wow us like we hoped it would.
Most over-rated michelin rated restaurant I have ever dined at. Really expensive for what you get and the flavors didn't really work imo.
Thumbs up! Supremely authentic and tasty. Each dish was jam packed with flavor and nuance.

I've been to this place at least four times this summer and I feel like I've tried everything on the menu. It is sooooo good and I highly recommend the prawn sashimi and the papaya salad with salted egg. Absolutely delicious. The sashimi is really spicey, so just be aware of that going into your first bite. If you flick off some of the chilli peppers (though they really make the dish), it'll make the spice more tolerable!

Some other favourites are the mushroom fried rice and the duck larb!!! So so goooddd

It can get quite busy so a reservation would be your safest bet.

Ordered the tum kor moo yang with side of sticky rice off the caviar app with free delivery. This was so good! Just the right amount of spicy kick and generous amounts of grilled pork neck. Wish the portion size overall was bigger but it doesn't really specify whether it's an app since it just said "salad". Would definitely order from again but would probably have to get a side or something extra.

We're from San Francisco and stopped by on Wednesday night. Foods here were awesome. Our fave dish was Som Tum with Salted Egg and the atmosphere was great. Only one thing that ruined our dining experience here was a waitress who took our order and has never smiled. She's not supposed to work as a waitress if she doesn't have service mind. Goodbye!! We'll never come back.
Good choices for several hard to find dishes but too much MSG and a bit pricey.

I was on vacation in New York recently and was craving good authentic Thai Food. This place was chosen by my friend and it did not disappoint at all. The dishes we ordered were spicy and tasty which was exactly what we wanted. Take heed to the spice level indicator on the side of the menu; if it says spicy it's spicy. Highly recommended!

BEST Thai restaurant in NYC. The food is delicious and the staff attentive and kind. We love it here! It's our "go to" Thai place. Definitely get the raw shrimp, papaya salad, and fried chicken - they are not to be missed!
Very very worthy of their Michelin star.  Amazingly authentic northeastern Thai food, low on the sugar, high on the chilies.  This has replaced uncle Boon's as my favorite Thai place in New York
Papaya salad is delicious!!!! U have to order it spicy. Taste just like back home. The grill pork is juicy and tender. So much flavor. 100% authentic.

Consistently has great quality. Whether it's ordering or dining in, the food has been great. I always order the spicy raw shrimp (goong che nam pla). It's also one of the few Thai restaurants that have street food!

Loved my dinner here! Came here upon recommendation from a friend who is a big foodie. I had asked for reco's for Southeast Asian food and this was one of her recommendations (along with Uncle Boons and LoveMama). I got a papaya salad with salted egg, which was a nice twist as I've not seen the salted egg offered widely in other Thai restaurants. The pad Thai comes with crab and the staff asked what level of spice we wanted. I loved the pad Thai! The fried chicken seems like a special there -- it's well marinated, and tasty. 

Happy Hour discounts apply 5-7pm on any drinks, including non-alcoholic, and the fried chicken dish is offered for $6 at the Happy Hour portion. 

Clean restroom and attentive staff. Easy to walk in on a Monday night without a reservation.

Great place to eat at, order from, pick up from, whatever floats your boat in the city. This is the place to go when you're feeling fresh Northeastern Thai food in a cozy, home kitchen-inspired setting. My favorite thing is the grilled rice sticks, they're fun to eat and I feel like I'm eating a corn dog.

I really enjoyed the food here. The food seemed sooooo authentic and just like the dishes youd find in thailand. 

There is no curry here fyi.

I am a sucker for interesting martini flavors and this spot has them - mangosteen, burnt rice, thai tea, etc. Yum

The sizes of the plates are not that big - they encourage tapas/family style vibe

I'd come here again and it's always a great sign when I want to go back

Somtum Der has some really authentic Thai food. They offer an array of Northern Thai dishes that I've never heard of- that's when you know it's authentic!! Everything is also So cheap and affordable. We tried the pork Cartledge soup, papaya salad with salted eggs, pad see sew and this Charcuterie thing.

I've heard lots of good things about som tum der so I figured I should try it out. When looking at the menu, I had no clue what to order, as the options are pretty different from what I typically see at a Thai restaurant. The food was only alright and I couldn't really get myself to eat it all, as the rice was too fishy tasting for my liking and the pad Thai was a bit spicier than I expected.

One of the best Thai food I have. It is even better than most of what you will get in Thailand. Some very interesting dishes such as raw shrimp is highly recommend. Flavor is straightforward and strong. Little bit crowded but it's worthwhile.

Food was good i came 4 people with 1 baby and they already add tip on my bill they charge 18%. Anywhere and i am form Thai that day my bill total like $200 anywhere thai people alway give tip 20%. But when i see them add tip 18% my feel so down but happy same time.

Dined here for the 2nd time last night with 5 girls so I got to over order like the greedy fatty that I am. My favorites in order of preference were the fried chicken, grilled pork (so spicy but oh so good), crab fried rice and pork skewers. I also enjoyed the papaya salad with salted egg and the bamboo salad. Skip the beef salad. The vegetarian noodles looked eh too. I've also previously had the duck larb salad which was decent but not my fav but I'd take that with a grain of salt since I'm not a larb fan. We tried the taro in coconut milk and herbal jelly with shaved ice desserts. What's up with the fake taro balls? Bring on the real taro please. I drank the warm coconut milk though. It warmed up my belly on a chilly fall night. The herbal jelly shaved ice was refreshing but probably too ethnic unless you're a Taiwanese fob like moi. My Indian gfs were expecting a brownie sundae and got an unpleasant surprise. Reasonably priced. We paid $65 each including a cocktail and too much food. Don't come for a romantic date. You can however come for your birthday if you want to experience a hysterical, loud but fun version of happy bday blasting over the intercom. A real gem!
One star knocked off. This place isn't as good as it used to be. Not sure what happened but the quality definitely fell off. Still solid, just not 5-stars solid.

Girlfriend and dined here on a Thursday evening. Everything from the decorations to the food was very good. We started out with the famous fried chicken as well as the pork spring rolls which were both amazing. As entrées we got the crab Pad Thai and the Khao Klook Ka Pi (amazing dish) highly recommend this place. Only knock is they could bump up and improve their drink menu. Overall 4/5 stars. 

Will come again.

East Village has a variety of asian food, and one day my friend and I liked to venture out this local That restaurant for something new. I loved the place! It is not necessary my top favorite Thai restaurant to go to, but at least I had a pleasant experience. I grew up in Vietnam, and I had tons of Thai food from Thailand in my childhood. The food here is very good, authentic to what I have had in Thailand. I was a little bit hesitant to order their popular dish of Pad Thai, because it is on the pricey side. It turned out to be okay.
