Its spiciness level is already made to be medium, and it can be spicy to some people. Their pad Thai was definitely not the best one I have had, but it's quite unique: they served it with crab meat, and their sauce is quite expectable with a little twist of seafood in their sauce. 

Their papaya spicy salad with salted egg was phenomenal. I'd order it again and again. I can't wait to look up the recipe and make it myself some time. 

The service was quick and attentive. I can't complain, and I would come back for different food in the menu.

Somtum Der might be the most authentic Thai place in Manhattan. This is good if you like strong spices and fish sauce, not so good if you want generic Thai food that's toned down for the masses.

Some dishes here will be violently spicy and if you ask them to make something really hot you will be in pain. That being said, every dish they make tastes authentic and they don't hold back using seasoning and ingredients which Western senses are not accustomed to. There will be dishes that smell funny and may be too hot, but they are good if you give them a chance.

Some standouts are the Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (fried chicken), Goong Chae Nam Pia (raw prawns), and the crab pad Thai.

Yummy Thai place in the city! They definitely  catered to less spicy  clients and for those who absolutely  love love and can take on the real thai heat well make sure you the staff!!! And make sure you emphasize  it. Of course spicy levels  can be adjusted!
Come here almost every week to be honest. The food was AMAZING! I would die if they close the restaurant!
The Goong Chae Nam Pla is delicious and very authentic. Highly recommend this place and will definitely come back.
If you love spicy Isaan food this is one of the best. Cute little spot, great service and great food! Yummy for reals

My friend and I chose to come her for lunch prior to our mochi making class as it was close by on a Saturday. Upon arriving, I thought the restaurant would be larger than due to a mirror placed on the other end of the wall. Regardless, the restaurant is quite spacious. There is one communal table for big groups and then smaller tables on the side of the wall. The decor inside was simple and had a cozy feel to it.

Usually I don't order a lot of food for two people as I get full easily, but there were many different dishes we want to try so we ordered 4 dishes to share. We ordered the Thai spicy papaya salad with salted egg, fried chicken, grilled coconut milk marinated beef skewers and pad see eiw talay. We asked the salad to be made more mild as Thai food can be quite spicy and wanted to be able to try the salad. My friends and I both enjoyed the salad a lot as it was refreshing and it had hints of saltiness from the salted egg and spiciness. The beef skewers were very flavorful and the meat was tender. The fried chicken was also very good, but it's probably something that I would just order once to try so I can try other dishes. And finally, the pad see eiw talay, the noodles were flavorful and not too salty as it is usually cooked with soy sauce and there was a good amount of shrimp and calamari for the two of us. 

Overall, all the dishes we ordered were really good and I would definitely come back to try their other dishes if I am in the area. The staff are also friendly and the atmosphere is really nice.

Went to Somtum Der with a few friends on a cold day.  We went early and had no wait.

The restaurant is cozy, industrially decorated, and small.  Service was good.  The menu is pretty expansive.

I tried the following dishes:

Tum thai (spicy papaya salad) (4/5): This was a really nice dish.  It was spicy, so be prepared.  The papaya was super fresh.

Pad thai mun poo (crabmeat pad thai) (4/5): This was a nice dish.  It was definitely an interesting take on pad thai.  The crabmeat was ample, and the dish was a little spicy as well.  The noodles were nice and springy.

Overall, I liked Somtum Der and would definitely return to try more of their dishes.  Next time, I would definitely try more small plates.
My Thai friend took me to this restaurant, and I had a great time trying out new Thai dishes. I love how spicy their dishes are and love the stinky fishy dishes. Very delicious.

Amazing! The decor inside is homey but feels authentic, and I left feeling completely stuffed. The wait staff was very nice and was great at filling up our waters. I ordered the marinated skewers and a side of sticky rice, and then split another entre with someone at the table which had an egg, rice, and pork. So amazing!! Would 100% make the trip again.
Some of the best and most authentic som tum recipes. Larb and dessert were great too. A must visit

I've spent a good amount of time in thailand and i would say this restaurant is pretty authentic, especially their papaya salad.  Drinks were okay-- not bad not amazing.  Service was great and decor was very modern.  Overall i would come back.

After my less than satisfying dinner at Wayla, I wanted to eat some authentic Thai food. My Thai friend had suggested Somtum Der to me a while back and I decided to visit here with my sister as it is in the neighborhood.

We ordered the som tum kor moo yang, pad kee mao and nue rong hai der. The som tum was one of the best renditions I've had stateside aside from my mom's. It was the perfect level of spiciness when we ordered it hot. It was so satisfying that both my sister were eager in anticipation of the mains after eating it.

The pad kee mao was slightly sweeter than I expected but also delicious. I enjoyed the nue rong hai der - this was my first time eating this dish as my Thai  family doesn't eat beef - but the accompanying sticky coconut rice was not my favorite but also delicious. 

All in all, very solid Thai food. I will definitely be back as it is close, authentic and affordable.

I ordered the yum poo-plara  and it was not edible. Random crab legs with basically no meat and I was constantly biting down on little shell pieces. I then had the soup Tom Klong pla dook yang. It had fried cat fish with tons of bones in it and lots of lemon grass pieces and some other leaf that was inedible. Both my dishes I couldn't finish. Also the party I was with (8ppl) had an automatic %20 tip but we didn't even have our own table. A couple and baby were sharing a table with us. Overall I would say it's not worth the money. And I question there business ethics (with the tip).

This place is perfect for any given night when you are craving authentic Thai food. Casual dine-in but the food is Michelin quality. Tried the Papaya salad, spicy noodles and fried rice. Would definitely come back for the papaya salad and noodles.
Amazing spicy Thai food. Had the pad see ew, a cold shrimp dish and the fried chicken thighs and would 100% come back again.

I ordered pad see eiw and my mother ordered catfish soup, we both were satisfied and finished our dishes. I saw more spicy options compared to other Thai restaurants out  there, we ordered non spicy options. Waitress was polite and I'll definitely go back.

Their mushrooms gave me food poisoning. Food is great, servers were very nice and respectful, cozy ambience, and the prices were great too! But won't be coming back after the terrible illness I fell upon after eating their mushrooms.

This place isn't afraid of spice (both in flavor and in heat) so if you don't like heat, you'll want to let them know as some things just come out in one level. This place was one of the places we went to that has a Michelin star in New York and this place is yummy. Came here with a friend and her family for dinner, thankfully they were able to get us in without a reservation (midweek). We got a bunch of dishes and decided to do family style. We got the fried chicken (juicy and flavorful), prawn sashimi (great but has a bit of heat so watch out), pad thai (good, not too sweet), and a bunch of other food that I can't remember. Service was good and I would totally come back.

I've been going to the Experience Thailand festival in NYC a couple of years in a row now. Last year at the festival in Union Square plates of perfectly cooked crisp chicken were floating around and soon enough we heard where it was coming from, the Somtum Der tent

Lines of people waiting stretched pretty far. The wait was worth it, it's not often friend chicken wows me. But this was one of those moments. The seasoned chicken perfectly fried and delicious sauce made it quickly one of my favorites i've ever had. I only wish we got a bigger portion. So last night for our friends going away dinner we sat at one of the big tables at the restaurant and ordered various salads, appetizers, main dishes and more. Plenty of chicken of course and getting to taste not one papaya salad but a few styles makes Somtum even more special.

That's part of their name Som Tum, they were making salads all night. Even the to go orders were made fresh.

Go to Somtum Der if you'd like to try new Thai dishes that you won't ordinarily see on other menus with surprisingly interesting flavors. They have classic dishes too.

I'm so glad I went to the experience Thailand festival and got to try your chicken. Aroy Mak!!!

From the outside, it's hard to tell this restaurant has a Michelin star however once you taste the food it becomes very clear. I've come here twice and both times the food was excellent. The ambiance is very casual and authentic. One of the best Thai restaurants I've visited in New York
There are serving you with E-San style. So tasty yummy. I like fried chicken it very crispy. And grilled beef with sticky rice is so so good. I will be back there again.

One of the few places I've been to that delivers on the Thai spice as it should be. The beef skewers were very good. Tender, sweet, salty, and a light spice. The fried chicken, while good, is probably something I wouldn't get the next go round. The spring rolls were crunchy and also packed a mild spice punch. The drunken noodles were very good. I got pork. Good flavors and textures to match. For me the highlight was the fried rice. It was spicy and jam packed with flavor in every bite. This is certainly the one dish that would be ordered again next visit. This place is around some very good bars so I am sure that I'll be back here again soon. You should definitely check them out. ENJOY!!!

A fantastic dining experience. The food came all at once, and each dish had interesting flavor after flavor. The papaya salad with salted duck egg is a must-order, as were the coconut sticky rice Moo Ping Kati Sod. The meat was tender and flavorful with a strong kick. Of the five dishes we ordered,  I'd say the catfish larb was the weakest, though still good.

The best tasting Thai food I've ever had in my life and by far the most affordable Michelen star experience!! Thank you for existing, I don't know what I would do without my weekly coconut rice and pao ki mao !

My wife and I went to this place a few time. The food was usually pretty good. But today I ordered a papaya salad to deliver to my work place and when we open the portion was so little. Roughly 1/2 of what we usually have when dine-in. We were so disappointed.

Oh my gooooodnesss! This place was superb! I have eaten Thai in a lot of places of New York, but usually they all end up being good but the same. This place is something S-P-E-C-I-A-L. The have turned up the heat and the flavor in this gem of a spot. They also sport some more interesting dishes. Never have I ever felt like I NEEDED to return to a Thai restaurant, but this place got me feeling some sort of way.

This place has the best papaya salad. It's extra spicy and the the papaya strips are fresh and crispy  I can't get enough of the papaya salad here. They also have lunch specials for $12 fried chicken sticky rice and a small papaya salad. I been here many times and they ever disappointed me. Service is good and food comes out fast.

I don't normally write reviews.   But, one time about 12 years ago, I had the unique pleasure and experience of eating at the Wat Thai Temple weekend food market in LA.   I had papaya salad with crabs and coconut rice with mango.   I have never forgotten it, and I've never experienced anything on the same level since.   Until now.  The Tom Poo Plara here is the closest I have ever come to finding the same authentic experience.   And, trust me, I've been searching for over 12 years.  If you've never had this authentic version of papaya salad, be warned that you may not enjoy it.  It's salty and it has strong flavor and it's spicy (I ordered mine "spicy" and it was just about right - a little less heat than the one I had in LA so many years ago).  But if you are looking for an authentic Thai papaya salad experience, OMG this salad is HEAVEN!  I also had goong chae nam pla.  Upon first opening it, I was a little worried because it is truly whole raw shrimp, but it is DELICIOUS!   The grilled sticky rice is also so good - I'm saving that for dessert!  Thank you Somtum Der for finally opening back up amid this Covid-19 disaster and allowing this nurse from Colorado to revel in some of the most authentic Thai food in this nation!

Super flavorful food. I think they might have gotten my order wrong because I swore there was supposed to be rice in my meal, but it ended up being fine. I was full from what I ate. Noodles were great as well. I wouldn't mind going back for some new dishes in the future!
My favorite Thai food spot in the city. If you cannot handle spice, you should take to your waiter about the level. Always a pleasant  experience!!

Stopped by for Sunday Brunch with friends! They have a cute backyard dining area with big umbrellas with plenty of shade complete with a fan. We ordered:
Pad Thai with crab- hits the spot, and would definitely order again
Salted Egg Papaya Salad - perfect for the summer heat and has a kick to it 
Beef with sticky rice - first time ordering this dish, so not sure what to expect! I thought there would be a sweet side to it, but it's mostly savory with a side of chili sauce. The sticky rice on sticks were so cute!

Portion size is on the smaller size but the quality is on point. 
Will be back to try their snow ice- it looks bomb!

I've been here several times in the past. Not once has it let me down. By far my favorite Thai place in the city.

Go nuts with the menu, you won't be disappointed.

Not for vegetarians or pescatarians who don't eat shellfish. 

I lived really close to this place for three months a couple of years ago and forgot why I never came here. Now I remember - just a few vegetarian options and every fish option besides one has shellfish. 

We ordered the vegetarian papaya salad, the fish rice dish (only one option without shellfish), and the coconut rice sticks.

The coconut rice sticks were tasteless - couple barely taste the coconut and absolutely a waste or $6. If you want to try the coconut rice, just have the side instead. 

The fish rice dish was pretty okay - I love spices but was definitely over spiced and the pieces of fish in it were super chewy. Not recommend.

The only recommended dish is the vegetarian papaya salad that was bomb. We asked for it spicy and I added additional peppers and it was perfect. I would only come back here for this.

I've never been to Somtum Der in person, but it's been one of my main go-to's for Thai food delivery during my weekly cravings, and has quickly become one of my favorite Thai spots in the city. The portion sizes are on the smaller side since most of the menu is composed of salads/small dishes, so I recommend getting 3 dishes to share for 2. You really can't go wrong with any of their papaya salads (my favorite is the one with pork neck, which they are very generous with, and it's only $1 extra versus the original papaya salad) or any of their larb dishes (my favorites are the catfish and duck). I also really enjoy their pad thai (I know, so basic) but it's sweet and light and topped with a few chunks of crab. The flavors at Somtum Der are always extremely bright from the herbs, balanced by tangy acidity from the lime and punchy goodness from the fish sauce. The food also travels very well, so highly recommend for those within the delivery zone!

I came here recently with a friend for lunch on the weekend.  I was worried that they were going to be full, but luckily there weren't too many people so we were able to get outdoor seating without a problem.  The people that worked there seemed pretty nice when I was asking questions, so I appreciated that.  

We ended up ordering two orders of beef pad see ew ($15 each) ane one order of the papaya salads (tum thai - $11).  

The papaya salad was startlingly good actually.  It was very refreshing, crunchy, and had a decent level of spiciness (we asked for mild on the spicy scale).  The pad see eew was pretty good too but didn't seem like it was any better or worse than pad see ew I've had at other places.  Portion sizes could have been a little larger in my opinion; it wasn't that much food overall.  

All in all, I had a pretty decent experience here.  I think overall the food is a little bit overpriced but it could be worse.  So I think 3 stars is pretty fair.

[pre-COVID dine-in review]

Short version: loved it, you can't go wrong, but standouts for me the seafood suki and beef skewers. 

Absolutely loved loved loved my meal here, and service was fantastic.

Wok-fried seafood suki - favorite dish. Very smokey, kind of sweet, kind of spicy. Didn't really know what we ordered so it was a pleasant surprise
Tum thai kai kem (papaya salad with salted egg) - it just tasted like a very well made papaya salad
Sa Poak Kai Tod Der (fried chicken thigh) - so light and crispy
Nue ping kati sod (beef skewers with coconut milk) - Another of my favorites of the nights. Meat was coconut milk is such a great combination, idk why more places don't do this. The coconut vermicelli on the side was interesting, I didn't think much of it
Khao ji (grilled coconut rice skewers) - well made, and who doesn't like grilled rice + sticky coconut rice
favorite. best thai spot in manhattan. i ordered pick up 4 times in 5 days!!! std is what dreams r made of

This spot has tasty small plates good for sharing. Authentic Thai flavors. Go with a party of 4 to try different dishes. We ordered the larb egg roll, traditional larb, glass noodle with seafood, a few other appetizers and entrees and drinks. I enjoyed the Thai Tini- not sweet, subtle tea flavor. Does not accept reservations, went on a Saturday in the summer around 630. Would recommend!
The Chef's signature seafood with suki sauce and the shrimp and squid pad se eiw we're both sooo good. Papaya salad was actually a lil spicy! So so good.

Yummy delicious Thai food in east village. We sat down outdoor around 6:30pm on a Friday night. You will have to scan the barcode on the table to view their menu for less contact. Waitress will come take your order but because everything is outside and staffs are inside, you will have to wait until they come out. We waited for a while to get the order placed because the waitress was too busy and there was only one. Line up formed around 7pm.

We ordered two cocktails for start. Lemongrass and Bangkok cooler. I'd recommend lemongrass because the alcohol taste was not strong but still gives you the feeling. Bangkok cooler tasted like syrup lol. Not a drink for us. 

We got fried chicken thighs, crab fried rice and basil fried rice. Chicken thighs were so good. Crispy and tender! The best part of tonight was the crab fried rice. The plate was loaded with crabs and fried rice. It was delicious. Highly recommend the dish. Basil fried rice on the other hand was too salty for us. We didn't really like it. Overall we will come back again. We really enjoyed the food here! 

Another thing for outdoor dining is that flies and mosquitos are flying everywhere and sometimes stop on the food which is unhygienic so be aware of that.

Ohmygod this place just reminded me how bad my spice tolerance is nowadays. When I ordered the Seafood Suki, I asked my waitress how spicy the dish was. She said "barely if any spice at all." Then my dumb self said, "can you make it just a little bit spicy?"

Twenty minutes later I was breathing fire. It was absolutely phenomenal, but I had to pause every few minutes to drink water and eat rice to calm down. My friend, who ordered pad thai, was also trying to not melt. 

10/10 would absolutely do it again. It's one of those foods that's so good that I would willingly handle the pain, and Somtum Der is now easily one of my favorite Thai restaurants in the city. 

Other than that, the papaya salad is their most well-known dish. It's super refreshing, especially on a hot day, but the portions are on the smaller side.

The best papaya salad I've ever had. Coconuts sticky rice is also very good! I also like their cocktails, they look pretty and taste refreshing.
The outdoor setting is also very cozy. 
Best of all It's tasty at a affordable price in east village. gotta say that restaurants at east village is a bit overpriced, which is fair given it's location.

Had a few things delivered from here this weekend, which, compares to some recent Thai takeout and delivery we've had, didnt really meet the mark. It was just fine, more so spicy than flavorful. The pad Thai mun poo was the best of the lot, while the papaya salad and the larb were fine, and the sundried beef simply didn't travel well. I've had it in person and it was much better when hot and fresh. Wouldn't recommend delivery here but maybe in person would be good.

Why did this have to happen! I ordered my favorite papaya salad, and while I was enjoying it at home found a black hair in it. Ek. Nothing crosses me out more. Walked back to the restaurant, they offered to make me a new one or refunded me. I chose the latter. I was grossed out. Probably will not come back for a while after this.

Awesome big outdoor dining space in front of the restaurant. Prompt service. Lychee martini was fantastic. We ordered the larb, papaya salad with fermented fish and grilled sliced beef. The larb and grilled beef was amazing. You also get two grilled coconut rice skewers yumm. The papaya salad was ok, the fermented fish probably wasn't my thing. Overall great meal, good value, love the uniqueness of the menu. They have Lao beer which is hard to find anywhere else.

I used to travel extensively to Thailand in the 1990's.

The food there is absolutely nothing like the Thai food I was used to eating in the USA. I realized that the gloopy, sugary "Pad Thai" that you get in typical Thai restaurants is pretty horrible compared to all the styles of delicious food you can get in Bangkok and beyond.

If you've only eaten Thai in NYC restaurants and think you know Thai food, it would be like forming an opinion about Chinese food by eating Egg Foo Young and Fried Rice in strip mall restaurants or disgusting dishes from P.F. Changs.

Having said that, I was passing by Somtum Der a few weeks ago, and noticed they had a "Field Snail" spicy salad as a special.

I sat down in the outdoor dining table, ordered it with a Beer Lao, and was transported back to Bangkok. This is the real deal, with dishes not modified for American tastes. The salad was very tasty, with lots of marinated snails and lots of flavor.

I had asked for it spicy, not watered down for "farang", and spicy was what I got. The food was bright, fresh, with a delicious burn of chili.

This is dead on genuine Thai food, as served in Thailand.  I have not been able to find food that tasted like real Thai food in any NYC restaurant until now.

Since that day I have been back, I got Duck Larb, Papaya salad with Salted Egg, and a few other things. I like the Beer Lao too. (even though it is Cambodian).

If you want "American" Thai food, this might not be the place for you. If you can eat spicy and enjoy it, and you want unique tastes and flavors, this is it.

I've had cravings for more food from Somtum Der, and will return. Excellent.

(I also want to say the the waitresses are very pleasant, and they seem to be taking careful COVID precautions. The place is very clean, they give you sanitizer on the table, and you can scan a Q code for the menu on your phone if you want)

Amazing spot for eat in, delivery, or takeout. Much higher quality and different cuisine than your typical Thai spot. Highly recommend the pad ki mao- no idea how they get the noodles to be the perfect consistency every time. Can be spicy tho so watch out for those red peppers! The staff are always friendly and professional and never takes too long to prepare.
The best Thai food in nyc! Chicken, rice, papaya salad  highly recommended to anyone.
Food & service was great! Staff followed COVID guidelines & had hand sanitizer for us at the table (we ate outside). Thai tea is a must here! Everything my table got was great. Would recommend!

Food was phenomenal and the outdoor seating was really comfortable. We went on the coldest winter day and I was in a blouse in the covered outdoor seating. 
My drunken noodles (not spicy) was amazing! 
HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Best papaya salad I have ever tasted in my whole life! It's fresh, tasty, and spicy! Also the egg is cooked to perfection. Iv tried other specialties of the menu and they have all been tasty. Prices are affordable. Every time I go to this establishment, I'm never ever disappointed! I highly recommend it!
Good pad see eiw with seafood, flavorful and loaded with calamari. Friendly and attentive staff and great outdoor setup for Covid.

Came here for dinner with my friend. We were able to reserve a table inside. The service was quick and friendly. They have an extensive menu so it took a while for us to decide on what to get. 

They also have a good selection of drinks. I got a sour and it was really good. They got one of our dishes wrong but the rest of them were good. I really enjoyed the grilled coconut sticky rice! It was able to neutralize the spicy larb we got. The papaya salad with salted duck egg was amazing! I enjoyed the raw shrimp too although it is on the spicier side. The chicken soup was also really good. 

Overall a really good restaurant, would be back!

This place is amazing! The duck salad was my favorite item by far. They have a lot of spicy dishes but they're also willing to add spice to anything if you want it to be taken to the next level! Indoor seating area is nice and very spaced out with dividers between each table. The waitstaff was very helpful and provided several great recommendations for us. Will definitely be back!
Excellent! Our only regret is not being able to eat more food. Ordered the Pad See Eiw, Pad Thai, mango salad, and Signature Fried Chicken Thigh. Outstanding!
The food are authentic. Finally found a place in NYC that serves raw shrimp salad! Crispy Thai fried chicken. Pad kee mao and fried rice is so good! Nice and clean place!

Very bad food 
Very bas service 
They treated me like Trash!!! 
Never experienced something like that in my life!

I always love to come here. The best Isan food in NYC , the service has always been excellent however, I was there yesterday and the service was terrible. My party felt very uncomfortable dining in at the restaurant. It was something that I didn't expect at all. I will still go here just maybe on a different day with different staff.

Loved their outdoor setup. 
I wouldn't return with a non-drinking friend as most dishes were flavorful, but a bit salty and tapas-like sizes. 
Nice and reasonably priced cocktails, although they could reduce the amount of ice. I can see myself returning here for drinks and snacks (main dishes are basically app sizes) 

We ordered medium spicy for duck somtum, but our mouths were on fire. And I've been going to Thailand since I was 13. If you can't handle the heat, order mild.
The food here is so goddamn tasty it could make you weep. Get the fried chicken, the salted egg Yolk salad, and any laarp. Never disappoints.
so delicious. best thai food. kee mao, grilled sticky rice skewers, and papaya salad are great. the food is actually spicy.

Came on recommendation from SO many friends. Maybe I was under impressed because I came with such high expectations?

Despite hearing the wait to get a table, we were seated right away at 7:30pm on a Saturday. Staff were very attentive and kind. 

However, the food was disappointing. I often order pad see ew at all new Thai restaurants I try. I did see many new and exciting options on the menu that I don't see often, but thought that the see ew would be a good marker of if I'd come back and try the other options. So onto my dish, it was cold. That was very disappointing. The restaurant wasn't that busy so it should not have been sitting around after being prepared. Also, the dish tasted like one note. Sweet. See ew is often sweet but more complex with beef flavors. Mine tasted as if the beef was just tossed in after cooking with no see ew flavor on the beef and vice versa. 

My friend ordered the Ki Mao and although also cold, she did love the spice level.

If you think you know what thai food is -- Think again. For most of my life I've had more "Americanized" thai food, and it wasn't until I visited Somtom Der that I realized what I was missing out on.

Sure, there's nothing wrong with americanized thai food, but the real deal is something completely different (I can say with confidence that the food is authentic, my girlfriend is thai). The food was incredible. We started the meal off with larb, papaya salad, grilled calamari, and a tom zap (sour and spicy short rib stew). The larb was savory, tangy, spicy, and overall a great choice. The papaya salad was a refreshing break from the larb (although both were spicy) and the calamari was cooked perfectly (a little hint of smokey flavor from the char).

For mains, I ordered the pad thai. Unlike anything I had had before, this pad thai had such an amazing depth of flavor and was a vibrant reddish color (from the spices). The shrimps were juicy, tender, and perfectly cooked.

If you're on the edge of coming here, let me help you make a decision: Come and you won't be disappointed. Every single one of dishes we ordered were a hit and the place takes very nice precautions for indoor covid-conscious dining. One thing to note, however, is make sure to ask for mild spice if you can't handle spicy foods (a lot of the dishes are quite spicy by default).
My favorite Thai restaurant in the city ! Food is easily 5/5 and it's even great as take out or delivery. Service is always great, but they're pretty crowded so a bit of a wait during peak times.

When my friend said this was the best Thai food in NYC, I wasn't sure if it would live up to the title. TLDR: This is the best damn Thai food in NYC! (Okay, I can't speak for the entire menu, but they have the BEST Pad Thai in NYC).

Seriously, what are they putting in their Pad Thai that makes it so delicious? The sauce is tangy, smooth, and has a perfect kick. They also have fresh crab meat as a protein option, so bonus points for that. I don't know what else to say other than that it was truly the best Pad Thai I've ever had. I grew up in an area dominated by Asian food, so I know good Thai when I see it. The friend who recommended Somtum Der is also from Thailand, so when she says it's good--it's law.

Amazing! Delicious! Check it out.

Had the khao pad kraprao nue (basil beef stir fry with egg) and it was really good. Might be a bit spicy for some but flavor was great. The pad Thai mun poo was decent but the noodles weren't as great. Would definitely reconnect the khao pad kraprao though !

Phenomenal Thai food- lives up to the hype! Very light and flavorful. Visited during the week right when it opened and got seated/served quickly. I ordered nam tok nue- beef thicker than expected with strong lime/cilantro flavor, sticky coconut rice skewers- definitely try these/a bit on the sweet side but a good balance to the other items, and tum thai- still very spicy (even we opted for a less spicy option) but really good- sweet and tangy with fish sauce and spicy with the chili. Also the prices are amazing for what you get.
The workers were so nice, the inside set up was very cute, and the food was so delicious. I went for lunch while I was shopping around for apartments nearby, definitely recommend!
Best thai restuarant in the city for sure! So amazing and the staff is super friendly. I've eaten here over 150 times no problem haha they know me.

Prob a better in dining experience. Food arrived 30 minutes after expected time. (Was supposed to be 40 minutes, but came at 90 minutes). And luke warm. In sustainable packaging, so calling it decent for that, but will not order delivery again.

I tried Somtum Der for the first time today and I had a great time. They have a lunch special for $14 which comes with a main dish and a drink. I ordered the Pas See Eiw and it was delicious. I also loved the Thai Ice Tea that I ordered with my lunch. It was delicious and not too sweet. My cousin ordered their Chef Signature Wok Fried Suki and their Ice Thai Tea  with Lemon. We recommend both (If you like seafood definitely try the wok fried suki).

They have both inside and outside seating. They now provide a QR Code menu option as per Covid-19 changes. The restaurant was spacious and comfortable. The servers were nice. I highly recommend!!!

My boyfriend was looking for a place to try Thailand's spices, and this really was the perfect place!! 

He ordered the Tum Poo - Para by recommendation of a really friendly waitress. He truly got the spice he asked for and ALL of the flavor! 

I got the Pad See Eiw since I'm a baby with any spice. The flavor profile was actually present unlike most Thai places I've tried, and I HIGHLY recommend it for anyone who is new to Thai food and needs a non-spicy option.

My friend got a Pad KI Mao that was also excellent!! 

The pictures on the menu are ACTUALLY what you get, and I love the authenticity of this place 

100000% coming back

My delivery and dine-in experience were both great. The food here is much more authentic and unique - and of course, spicier - than those mediocre, run-of-the-mill Thai places. Highly recommend the larb/spicy salad - both duck and tilapia, Larb Tod (kind of like fried meatballs), and Moo Ping Kati Sod (skewers with vermicelli). We also got the Pad See Ew but didn't expect much since it's such a common dish, but damn, it was just so much better. The flavor was more intense and complex, and even the noodle itself had better consistency.

Very reasonably priced given the quality and taste of the food! I can see why my Thai friend would not stop raving about this place. Think this has replaced Soothr as my fav Thai place in the city!
one of my favorite Thai in town. Love their noodle, the "wok work" - heat control is just right.

If you have a hankering for Thai food, I mean REAL authentic BOLD flavors, then head to Som Tum Der.  Whenever I feel like having bold flavors, amped up sour, amped up spicy that really fulfills my cravings, I head to Isaan restaurants where I usually get exactly what I need. 

Food: 5/5
All I can say is that everything we ordered was excellent.  I mean every single dish.  If you go to this restaurant, be sure to order a few items that are special to this restaurant ..  Sai Krok Isaan, Tom Saap, Khao Kruk Krapi, Goong shoop Nam Pla.  After you've tried these specialities, let me know what you think.  Your welcome!!! 

Safety: 5/5 
There's an option to dine outside or inside.  If you go inside, be prepared to show vaccination card. We ate inside. Also, menus are thru QR code. 

Service: 4/5
I felt a bit rushed but aside from that very good service. 

We will definitely be back.

We had the pork liver, canned sardines, papaya salad with salted duck egg and peanut sauce, and the mackeral papaya salad.

Starting with the positives, the mackeral papaya salad was perfect in every way.  The brightness of the lime juice, the crunch of the underripe papaya, the savory taste from the mackeral, and the aromatic flavor of the coconut rice.  The peanut sauce was nice.

Unfortunately, the duck egg and pork liver were both too salty, and the canned sardines wasn't prepared in a way that down-played the "canned" taste.  I had the lemon grass juice and that was far too sweet.  I didn't order dessert because it was so unbelievably sweet.  When there's already sugar in a lot of thai recipes, it would have been nice to have a more tangy drink.

Had very high hopes for this spot due to great reviews.

Ambiance: hall in a wall type of feel. Super casual eatery/cafeteria style long table seating. Photos made it look fancier than it really was. Very, super loud inside--cannot hear your own voice amid all the noise. 

Outdoor seating--again, looked so nice in the photos but the reality left me speechless and my guests annoyed. The ugly outdoor shack was not decorated with any greenery (as per deceiving photos). Unpleasant graffiti line the walls of neighboring establishments all around. The garbage was piled against the shack's sides. The smell of that garbage on a lovely, warm September day was permeating everywhere and not adding anything to our dinning experience. Flies were bombarding our food. The street traffic all around us was SUPER loud. We got lucky: a mentally distributed person started bothering us and a few other dinners. 

Worst service imaginable. At least for big parties. 20%gratuity is automatically included for parties of 6 or more. That tip was NOT deserved. I am all for tipping generously. But for the amount that the service deserved. My birthday party was left without attention, water, or common courtesy. Waitress had attitude the entire time. We had to wait who knows how long for her to pass by so we could call her over to ask for water. Just for awful service that we had to leave 20% tip, will not be returning. Nyc has too many better restaurants to choose from. 

The food was standard Thai, nothing to write home about. Pad Thai (shrimp, veggie, and beef) are spicier than your Americanized versions. Everyone in our group prefers mild versions, so we asked for mild spice. We were repeatedly (and rudely) told that they CANNOT do a mild pad Thai. The only mild dish on the menu is Chefs Signature Wok Fried Seafood Suki (which was indeed mild). Fried rice was on the bland, boring side. For all dishes, the proportion of protein to noodles or rice was inadequately small.

Was excited to try this place but when i arrived there was a server setting up outside complaining about having first customer in Thai language and we could hear and totally understand what she said , so we left. If someone isn't happy to have customers.

I eat Thai food a lot (I mean, a lot!). It is my go to for basically all life occasions. And this place has some of the most authentic, rich, and flavorful that I've had. Couldn't have enough so came back a week later and ordered everything again! Would highly recommend

I have been on a Thai kick recently and wanted to find one of the better places in the city to go to. Found this place on the Michelin guide so I said why not. The place itself is underwhelming just a regular restaurant you could go to any day of the week or for lunch. I got the beef spring rolls and shrimp pad thai. The beef spring rolls were amazing! The pad thai was also excellent but I definitely liked the spring rolls more. For the price the amount of food left me wanting more. Would definitely suggest going back again!

Nice and warmly lit restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating options!

My friend and I were seated immediately when we arrived at around dinnertime at 7pm on a Sunday. It quickly got pretty crowded afterwards.

We ordered the thai basil fried rice with beef and grilled marinated beef. I cannot recommend the beef dish enough -- it was crispy on the outside and marinated and juicy on the inside. And it even comes with sticky rice! I seriously considered taking these dishes home with me on my cross-country flight. 

Just a note that it's a bit hard to flag down a server around dinnertime since there are so many customers. It took us a little while to get water refills. However, I'm hesitant to deduct a star for this because I loved the food so much.
My favorite Thai restaurant in nyc, their northern Thai dishes are amazing, especially the spicy pork soup.

I have read multiple glowing reviews of this place - some fairly new and some dated - all singing a praise chorus for this place with its unique at the time it opened and spicing- ly excited menu. Even usually Scroogey NYT review gave  it a star - big deal for a no name at the time it opened.

No surprise that I was salivating the day of the delivery order - impatiently waiting for the resto to open for dinner so I can get my fill of it's deliciousness.

Two items arrived - one was green papaya salad with fermented fish and little crab (s). Another was spicy salad with fried fish bites. 

As I was on a low carb diet I didn't get any rice with it nor did I order any noodle dishes. my mistake. 

green papaya salad aka som tum was prominently featured in multiple food reviews as a unique take on papaya salads somehow - tasted like an ordinary green papaya salad. spice level was good and enjoyable. After finding tiny chopped pieces of what appeared to be half of a tiny slimy crab - I kept looking for his other crab buddies and was disappointed in my detective abilities. so I concluded this is basically a spicy ordinary green papaya salad with a slimy tiny pieces of a crab ie crab shell that was hard to chew and sort of nasty. Grade: C 

Spicy salad with fried leaf fish from the Asian Rivers (or was it the Amazon or both) sounded exotic and as with any fried fish skin didn't disappoint flavor wise. Ample Sugar in the sauce coupled with fish sauce (not from the exotic leaf fish i am sure) was a nice touch. 

Excited to try something flavorful, I ignored the fact that thinly chopped up lemongrass in this salad was also hard to chew. 

Also this dish was not spicy despite my request to have it be so. 

the portion size here however was so small that it took first three normal sized bites to put down almost half of this dish. Realizing that my dinner will be over soon if I don't slow down - I distracted myself by making shirataki noodles to supplement the meal. Grade: low B.

Overall two less than amazing app size dishes were 30 bucks and didn't hit the hunger spot.

would I try other dishes at this place - yea I would - but now with rice and maybe two orders of it - bc I imagine small portions is the word here. 

wondering how much of a close up their website photo of a fried chicken thigh really is bc it looks gigantic.

Kudos to this place for making something actually extra spicy when I asked for extra spicy. Every Thai restaurant in Florida I've been to doesn't even come close to what Somtum Der served me. It got me suffering but not suffering too badly, and I was barely able to finish the food but managed it because it was good. 

Their desserts were delicious too, and I needed a few of them along with a drink to calm my mouth.

Somtum Der was not our first choice for dinner tonight but we were drawn in by its Michelin star rating. We were also really taken aback and impressed by their elaborate Halloween decorations. They had hand carved pumpkins in all sorts of cool designs.

I loved how their menu is fully illustrated. For someone indecisive like me, this is key in aiding me in choosing. I came really close to choosing one of their many larb salads and ordering rice as a side, but I ended up with the beef pad see ew because my stomach was grumbling that night and I had come straight from an intense workout class. 

Though basic, my pad see ew was done well and exactly the carb-heavy dinner I needed. The flavors were good, the noodles thicky and chewy, and there was plenty of egg, meat, and veggies to fill me up. I did find their version of pad see ew to be sweeter than those at other Thai restaurants. It tasted like they used oyster sauce as the main seasoning. However, the dish was still well balanced and the flavors didn't stray too far from a traditional pad see ew.

We also ordered the spicy pork shrimp rolls to share. These are pretty much thinner versions of spring rolls but still crispy and light enough to eat before a main course.

I'd love to come back for their lunch special deal or to try their array of soups, salads, and other rice dishes!

Still one of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan. Prices are very reasonable for the portions. I am not a pad thai person at all because most places make it way too sweet, but their balance of sweet and sour is perfect. I eat the same dishes every time and it never disappoints. The single most underrated dish on their menu is the raw shrimp (if you can do raw); get it with a side of coconut rice.

TLDR: one of the best places I've been to for Thai in the city.

Came here with a small group of friends. Each of them were from Thailand and wanted me to try authentic Thai food in the city. My favorites of the night were the Moo Ping Kati Sod (coconut milk pork skewer), Khao Klook Ka Pi (shrimp paste fried rice), Nam Tok Moo (spicy grilled pork salad), and the Tum Thai Kai Kem (papaya salad with salted egg). Honestly everything was good and it was difficult for me to pick favorites. I will say that the papaya salad was a little sweeter than I'm used to but I actually preferred it! 

Service was quick, friendly, and attentive. I can't wait to come again and try the rest of the menu!

Super cute spot with a nice ambiance. Tables are really set close together. Came in around 7pm on a Wednesday and didn't have to wait at all (restaurant was half full). 
Ordered skewers, larb, and ki mao. 
Loved the texture of the ki mao noodles. Wasn't too oily and had great flavor
Larb was pretty decent too but just would be open to trying something different 
Skewers we're stand out very good would come back just for the skewers. 

Btw their "medium"' is definitely a bit more spicy than I'm used to for a medium. Could have gone with a non spicy dish to balance the meal
Unique and amazing northern Thai. Everything I has was fantastic and fresh! Great and not some predictable pad Thai place.

We found ourselves here on a Wednesday night, and were pretty eager to try Thai dishes from a reputed restaurant that once held a Michelin Star!

To our dismay, it took at least 15 min for us to be even greeted by the hostess, which almost drove us to the point of leaving for elsewhere. The service wasn't fast either -- a 30 min wait for dishes that weren't even out of the ordinary. The only reason I might cut them a slack was that it seemed busy. But otherwise, rather mediocre service. 

The four star is warranted, however, because the food is good. Rozena loved both dishes, as I did. The beef pad see ew is not a hard dish to create, and they sure didn't get it wrong. The pad thai with shrimps is a little spicy, which I thought was fantastic. 

Next time, I might show up around lunchtime, and here's a note to myself: Order the spicy mango salad with crispy salmon! 

In short, disappointing service, great food.

THAI FOOD IN NYC @somtumderny 

Had the pleasure of going back to Som Yum Der in New York. We are here for only a few days before going to Philly so we had to maximize this opportunity to eat cuisines that we cant have back in Chicago!

Went here because we were craving Thai food and wow : what a great lunch set deal . All sets came with a drink too 

 fried chicken set $14 (highlight): came with sticky rice and papaya salad . SUPER crunchy and juicy. With well balanced spices and light batter from the Isan area
pad Thai set $12 : with choice of beef, shrimp, chicken or veggie
Pad See Ew $12 : rice noodles with sweet soy sauce. Nice and chewy noodles, not too oily
Spicy Basil Fried rice $12: comes with a sunny side up egg. Nice and fluffy rice, super flavorful

Extra:
shrimp sashimi $16 (highlight): I was craving sashimi and fresh seafood, saw that folks on Google recommended this and wow I'm so glad we ordered this! delicately fresh, paired with chilli's,  fish sauce, vinegar/lime

Such a fantastic meal. Their menu is pretty big so you can always find something new to try: whether soups, noodles, curries, etc

Nice vibe. Nice waitress. The foods are super delicious. 
If I have a chance to come to NY again I will be back for sure.

i was recommended by a Thai friend and the food is super tasty and amazing. Honestly, one of the best Thai places in nyc - 100% recommend :) I didn't take a a picture but their papaya salad has always been my favorite

Omg literally authentic Thai food I love it. It tasted like what u would order in Thailand and the spice level matches with an actual Thai person. Their Tom zap is rlly spicy and so good. Their garlic pork and rice is pretty average nothing special and their chicken is also average. This is equivalent to a food court in Thailand  and would def come back. The price is pretty acceptable too, it is was $250 for 8 people and we each got a dish and some appetizers to share.

Easily the BEST Thai restaurant in all of NYC. I've been twice in one week and I was blown away by the quality and taste of the dishes here. The biggest differentiating factor was that the food is here is far less oily than most other Thai restaurants I've been to. The pad Thai and pad see ew were my favorites- perfectly seasoned and the spice was on point. 

Service was super fast and efficient and the ambience inside made it feel like a true authentic Thai experience.

Fantastic Thai food.  We have been here 2 times and both times everything that we ordered was amazing. Their appetizers are really good! Great cocktails.  Seating is limited, but the ambience is lively. Food can be ordered to be spicy.  I would recommend making reservations ahead of time. For the quality of food, the pricing is very reasonable. Would be a good date spot.

The food here was amazing. Must come back for more. The balance of flavors. The authentic taste. Mind blowing. 

Besides just tasting fantastic The most unique dish of the evening the really spoke volumes was the bamboo shoot side dish. My taste buds have never tasted something so exquisite and flavorful. Must try !

This place was worth the hype. We ordered the papaya salad, pork skewers, pad thai and one of the rice dishes. Everything was delicious-- we cleaned every single dish off. I also got a Lychee Martini which was amazing as well. By far the best Thai I've had outside of Thailand. Highly recommend!

Somtum Der is a popular Thai eatery in the east village. I was pleased to find a day accept reservations, and I definitely recommend making one if you can because it gets crowded! 

The menu is a bit confusing but it is helpful that there are photos of each dish listed. When you order they will also ask you what spice level you want. I went with medium because I found that medium is usually not that spicy, but it was pretty spicy here, so beware! 

To start our table ordered the fried chicken which was served with a spicy dipping sauce. It's good for a max of 3-4 people since the pieces are pretty small. 

My friend and I shared a larb dish and pad kee mao noodles. Both were tasty and on the smaller side. I think I could have eaten a little more! But prices are pretty reasonable, so I recommend ordering as your heart desires to be safe! 

I also tried the Thai iced tea. I thought the tea flavor was a bit under developed, it probably should've been brewed longer. But overall the food was good and I would be happy to come back to try more. 

Side note- if you're considering coming for a birthday, they have a fun tradition of blasting a birthday song so that the whole restaurant celebrates with you!

Som tum der never disappoints!! The papaya salad with salted egg was amazing and extremely flavorful. Since it's quite salty and rich, it would go well with some jasmine rice. Another appetizer I always get is the fried chicken thigh! Amazing seasoning and chicken is very juicy. The pad Thai and Pad See Ew was delicious too

Som Tum (Thai papaya salad) is one of my favorite dishes of all time, so a restaurant that specializes in it is a dream come true.

Their grilled sticky rice is my favorite thing off the menu, besides the som tum of course.

The portion is on the smaller end, but this price is definitely not bad for a Michelin recommended restaurant! I'm a big fan of basil and I really enjoyed this kraprao! A bit on the salty side but manageable - spices made me sweat I guess that's another sign of authenticity haha!

Coming here with high expectations because it had new and interesting Thai dishes, I just thought the food here was ok. The pork skewers weren't that flavorful, the dipping sauce gave it some flavorful but for the price, nothing to write home about. The rice dish with the assortment of different toppings I thought was just ok too, pretty basic. I went for the different Thai dishes and not ones that everyone gets (like pad thai), but came away underwhelmed.

5 stars, their papaya salad is insanely delicious. a burst of flavor and freshness in every bite. the pad thai is good too, heavier on the sauce which i like. their grilled entrees aren't amazing, just 4 stars for those.

Many people recommended this place to me when they've heard that I planned my vacation in NYC. I looked it up and promised myself that I had to visit SomTum der!

Worth walking from subway station  I wish I could order more because there were so many dishes I have been craving since I haven't been back to Thailand almost 3 years because of the pandemic.

Not a single complaint at all and from what I have tried today...... I could say that they tasted authentic to me as a Thai person who was born and raised there

Why are you Still reading? Get out and try it now :)

My wife is THAI we know thai food-
We came here tonight-
Waitress was very RUDE.
Food had no flavor.
Menu  limited for vegetarians.
Would not recommend your place!
We  we're shocked
Forced to give u one star

The waitress who took our order was rude and angry about helping us. The food was not good. The Panna cotta was the only thing that was nice. We tried many dishes but it felt like a waste. Not sure how this place has such great reviews, was not worth the trip.

Excellent food. If you come here I'd recommend trying dishes they are known for (gold star next to them on the menu) rather than pad thai which you can get elsewhere. I also really like their coconut skewers.

Ok this place was on my list to try since last year but I never made it out here for some reason.  Finally got a good friend to come with me so that I could try more of their dishes.  I'm not sure exactly what the difference is yet, but Somtum Der is supposed marked as "northern" Thai.  I've been told that northern Thai is more savory/less sweet than southern Thai cuisine but I'll have to verify that with an actual Thai person!

Things we tried: 

Papaya Salad with Chili Sauce (Tum Suo Der)
PROS:
- great quantity, not skimpy
- well balanced in terms of the ingredients going into the dish
- good flavor, not overly salty or sauced
CONS:
- WAY too hot, even though we asked for mild.  And my friend and I both can take heat.  Those thai chilis are no joke!

Meat skewers (Moo Ping Kati Sod)
PROS:
- really good quantity, comes with rice noodles so it is pretty filling
- the rice noodles balance out the saltiness of the meat.
CONS:
- it would be nice to have some balance of meat, carb with some vegetables. Even a cucumber would work.  This was very...heavy.

Fried chicken
PROS:
- fantastic quantity, we had a hard time finishing this one
- crispy outside, came out hot but not overly greasy
CONS:
- chicken could have been more moist. It wasn't dry but it wasn't juicy though.

Spicy Beef Salad (larb)
PROS:
- nice quantity, definitely shareable
- nice flavor, def not bland
CONS:
- way way way too hot. We literally couldn't finish it.  What did help was the order of coconut rice (on skewer sticks). This helped take off some of the heat but it was almost too hard to eat and neither one of us wanted to take it home.  There's just no way to take out the heat once you add in the Thai chilis.

Would I come back? Definitely! I'd want to try one of their noodle dishes.  But anything spicy I'd stay away from.  I'd like to see some more vegetarian based dishes though in the future too!
Very good Som Tom salad, tastes like straight from Thailand and Tiger Cry was delicious as well, definitely want to visit this place again

The food was awesome!! Both my friend and I had pad thai and thai tea and it was perfect. We've heard great things about this place and wanted to try it out. It does get packed, especially in the evenings so I'd call ahead and make a reservation if possible. The only negative thing was that the waiter added an additional $3 to my tip even though I clearly wrote out the number on my receipt. I called and inquired and the management said "are you sure you don't want to tip more" can you believe that?!?!
My friend and I both tipped pretty well and they have the nerve to do that. Very disappointed in the waiter but everything else was great! I recommend going!

My niece recommended this place and wow, it did not disappoint. The food and service was awesome. Tasty and savory. This is definitely a place to frequent when in town. The locals are lucky to have this spot.

4.5! 

This place was hands down some of the best Thai food I've had! Not as good as what you'll actually get in Thailand, but close to it! The chicken was juicy and tasted so good, and the flavor did not get boring at all. It was layered so you kept tasting ingredients as time went on. Highly recommend and would go to again. The only thing I wish is that the portion sizes were a bit bigger.

I've been wanting to try this place for so long and it didn't disappoint. I absolutely loved their papaya salad(so authentic) and the service was great too, except I felt a tiny bit rushed. The only thing I'd say about the food is that it's a little bit too much on the sweeter side - like their basil fried rice and drunken noodles. Also at one point I asked for hot sauce and they brought me Sriracha... for how authentic they are, you would think they have a spice rack for Thai? But I would definitely return for that salad.

This is hands down one of the best Thai restaurants I have tried in NYC, and in the US as a whole. I visited Somtum Der with a friend that is from Thailand, and this was also the most authentic Thai food that they had in the last five years living here. None of the dishes felt oily and they were all well balanced in their spiciness. 

There were plenty of vegetarian options, of which we ordered the pad kee mao, impossible larb croquettes, and the vegetarian som tam. All three were delicious, and I thought the som tam was easily my favorite! We were able to see the chef using a mortar and pestle to mix together all the ingredients of the som tam in the kitchen, which my friend also mentioned is a very traditional way of preparing it. The flavor of the croquettes were also fantastic, although they didn't have as satisfying of a crisp as I wanted. 

Overall, this is a spot worth visiting no matter where you are in are NYC!

Excellent Thai place which makes most of your food extremely spicy which is how I like it. 

I would highly recommend fried chicken appetizer, and the duck larb (make sure to add sticky rice). Coming back here to try other menu items.

Somtum Der is such a cute and delicious Thai spot in East Village. Tried a variety of items on the menu and each plate was filled with flavor and spice. With that said if you're not into spicy, definitely stick with the milder offerings.
Just awesome, period. Not a bad dish on tie menu. Flavors unique to this place. Better than Norman Thai.

We tried the papaya salad with crab, gaeng om kai soup, grilled beef with rice skewers, and a side of the plain noodles.  Amazing flavors.  We've had these dishes before, but the execution here was on another level.  

We order spicy food on a regular basis, but I'm so glad we ordered "mild" spice levels here.  

Will definitely be back.

Papaya salad with salted egg - amazing textures and really refreshing. Duck larb was similarly on point with the flavors and textures. The fried chicken was tasty as well, but I think the standouts here are really the more traditional, uniquely Thai dishes.

I like the variety here. Some of the dishes are hard to get somewhere else but quality and prices here are meh. I've tried a lot of over 10 dishes here but nothing seems to hit the mark yet. Service has always been 1/5 here. Tables and chairs aren't comfortable.

After I posted the review for this place I just noticed that this place cheated on me. The price for the meal on that day include tax and tip it should not over than $50 (for 22% of tip). But they charged me $89.83 on my gift card. First time I thought they just holding but it more that a month already after that day.

First time having Northern Thai food and despite admittedly lacking a lot of understanding of what's typical for the cuisine, I really enjoyed my meal and would definitely come back again! 

The papaya salad was very spicy (get something else I'd you can't handle spice), but very delicious.

The soup was kind of like a more flavorful version of hot and sour soup, packed with some spice, and the meat inside was super tasty.

The pork neck was the highlight of the meal for me - this would be my top recommendation if you're trying to decide what to get.

The fried rice was good but pretty average as far as fried rice goes.

The Thai tea with milk was solid but I need to give a special shout-out to the Longan Juice. I only had a few sips but it was perfectly sweet and very refreshing.

Somtum Der is my favorite Thai restaurant that I've been to in New York. I started with the larb appetizer with impossible meat (having a vegetarian larb option is really wonderful) and the flavor was great. The peppers in the larb are spicy so be careful but I thought it was wonderful. I had the drunken noodles for my entree and it's hands down the best I've had, I could honestly eat it everyday. Definitely give Somtum Der a visit if you get a chance, you won't be disappointed.

Hands down my favorite Thai restaurant in the city. If you like spicy, flavorful, acidic, this is it. They specialize in Isan cuisine here. My go-tos are any of the papaya salads (love the salted duck egg one), the spicy prawn sashimi is to dieeee for, all the larbs are solid, and spicy chili paste fried rice with crispy leaf fish is probably one of the best fried rices you could ask for - it's got the right amount of crispy from the fish, salt from the salted duck egg and spicy from the seasoning. 

For desserts I highly recommend the Thai tea panna cotta and grass jelly with fresh milk. Not too sweet but feels refreshing and light after a meal. I would stay away from the snow ice with salak as it's kind of ginormous in serving and the artificial flavoring didn't really hit for me. 

Vibes inside are chill, really warm lighting and unpretentious. The food also comes out surprisingly fast. Really amazing spot to go with a group or one on one to kickback with some drinks and a bunch of food.

The food was a bit shy of being an authentic Thai cuisine. The service was okay and the ambience was okay. One plate of food costs on average $15 which is definitely not enough for 1 person. We ordered 5 plates and still weren't full. Overall, the experience was very average. Just had more expectations..

My go to Thai, thankfully it's it the neighborhood - looove this place so much. Authentic (& properly spicy) northern Thai food, never disappoints. Excellent sim tum, fried chicken, crispy fish salad, Isaan sausage, sticky rice...just to name a few. 
Friendly and pleasant service too. I highly recommend it!

The best Thai food I have ever had. The Tum Thai, moo ping kati sod & the Pad Thai Mun Pun was to die for. This is my new go to for Thai food. 

Fair warning, all the food is on the spicier end, but so sooooo good.

If your looking for somewhere to have a solid Thai meal Somtom Der is a solid choice. A varied menu with reasonable portions that will leave you satisfied. It's a spot that won't give yo us life changing experience; but also won't ruin your day. Very hospital staff, and an interesting view of the street from inside. 

A place that you won't regret.

I've been to Somtum Der twice, but forgot to write a review the first time so I am combining my two visits into this one. The first visit was on July 9th, 2022, and the second on September 10th, last Saturday. Both times I went with another person, and we shared everything. 

The first time, we got Tum Thai Kai Kem, a papaya salad with salted egg, and Chef's signature wok-fried seafood suki, wok-fried rice vermicelli with seafood, vegetables, and their signature suki sauce. The papaya salad was interesting in a good way, but not my favorite not because they made it wrong but because I do not have sophisticated palate to appreciate it fully. If you also do not have too much exposure to Isan cuisine, I would recommend the Chef's signature work-fried seafood suki, as it is more similar to the mainstream Thai food.  

In the most recent visit, we got Goong Chae Nam Pla, Thai prawn sashimi with house special green chili sauce, Khao Pad Nam Prik Pai Pla Sa Lid, spicy fried rice with crispy leafy fish, and Yum Goong Yang, chunks of grilled prawns and other vegetables. Thai prawn sashimi is my favorite across my two visits. The shrimps were fresh and chewy, and the sauce had just the right amount of spice, adding more flavors. The spicy fried rice was also great; I especially loved the leafy fish, well-seasoned and crispy, making the whole dish more flavorful and vibrant. Yum Goong Yang Salad was my least favorite, even though it was pretty good, prawns chewy and vegetables fresh. I just felt like I've had something similar elsewhere; it was not very much distinguishable from other dishes of the kind. 

Overall, I liked all my dishes in both visits and would be down to come back for more variety. Perhaps I will develop the palate to appreciate Isan cuisine more as I try more dishes.

Authentic northeast Thai food!!! Never disappointed each time I am here . They open at 6pm though we got here at5:30pm walk around get some coffee and went back at 6 PM they have people half full indoor already .  Always recommended

Had a great Thai lunch here while in town to see a film screening. As a vegan, I appreciate how many vegan options they had.  I ordered the Pad See Eiw as the vegetarian option.  I should have specified I wanted it VEGAN, because there were eggs in it, but that was purely MY error, and not the error of the server or the restaurant.

The place was packed, which tells you how fresh and authentic this food was.  Service was attentive and wonderful, restaurant was clean.  My friend ordered the Pad Thai with shrimp and was very pleased with her meal also.

The only con I can think of was that the portions weren't that large.  I'm not a big eater by any means, and I was actually still a bit hungry after I finished my meal.  This NEVER happens with me, as I rarely am able to finish a meal.  I do hate how Americans give mammoth portions which leads to a lot of waste, but I thought this one could have been a bit bigger to be honest.

All-in-all, it was a yummy lunch with fresh ingredients, and I would absolutely go back.  If you like Thai food, you will enjoy Somtum Der!

The dishes that were good were great, and the Thai tea panna cotta  was Devine!! The sad news, I was mid eating the dessert and she brought the check and they took my panna cotta ( crying inside) 

Medium is spicy, I love spicy and it was Sssspicy!
Overall it was good, get the panna cotta and hold it tight, trust me you want every bite.

Warning that the pad Thai has only one level of spice which is medium (in Thai spice) which was actually a little too spicy for me. It's also less sweet than other Thai restaurants, but definitely still very flavorful. So if you can handle a high level of spice, would recommend trying. I would return to try a different dish
Small place. Average food and overpriced. Could have much better Thai food for much lower price.

In the heat of the summer, I visited Somtum Der and had Tum Pla Tu + Kao Mun (Thai Macharel in Papaya Salad served with coconut rice). It was the most refreshing papaya salad that I have had at a restaurant. Great balance of citrus, fish, spice, salt and sweetness! 

I also had a cocktail called Dirty Green (Casamigos Blanco Tequila, Fresh Cucumber, Mint, Lime Juice, Matcha). It tasted like a mojito but made with tequila and matcha. Amazing! 

This little restaurant really packs a punch! I love it!

Somtum Der is a jewel for authentic Thai food in NYC. It is not your typical pad-thai standard establishment , but it brings out a whole new side to Thailand that you are not used to: Street food!
The venue is spacious and decorated really nicely and offers a bunch of community tables and spaces to hang out and eat great food.  
The highlights of the day were the vegetarian / impossible meat larb (spicy meat eaten as a lettuce wrap), the chicken skewers and the Pad see Ew.
All the food is really Thailand level spicy, I ordered a medium and I still felt the heat at times.  I would suggest to start small and build up with the added sauces available.
My drink of choice was a Thai beer which came cold and fast.

We had a 6 person group with a reservation and experienced fast attentive service. would definitely come back!

One of my favorite spots in the city. The Pad See Eiw has the perfect texture and flavor. I can't speak to the dine in service, but I've only had speedy and pleasant experiences with my pickup orders.

DELICIOUS & Authentic!  My husband and I ordered and shared 4 dishes.  All came out quickly and delicious one bite after the other.  The cocktails were super tasty as well.  The staff was very professional & efficient.  Cute venue, warm & cozy.  Definitely will return!

Very solid Thai spot that brings some interesting street food inspiration to a dinner place.  We both got the pad see ew and I got mine medium - had great flavor and a really nice kick.  I think we also shared spring rolls which came with a house made aioli like sauce which were delicious and we got a few beers to drink.  Very chill vibe with the set up having open bench like tables to sit at.  The location is also great as there's lots of bars nearby to hop around.  Would def come back if I'm in the area!

kind of small portions, decent but expected
got the pad see ew tofu
expensive for amount 
thai iced tea was good

Welp I think when you see a restaurant packed it's either really good if it's a local spot or hype if it's been featured on a local news or New York magazine. 

This spot was the former. The food was actually really good, they quite the selection of choices and the service was really fast considering they were slammed. It was impressive actually. 

I won't even try to butcher the names of these dishes we ordered some apps for the table. I had the seafood with rice noodles I tasted some of the other dishes. Really the food was not commercial good it was home cooked good. We really enjoyed it and their are lite beers that compliment the food. It was a very nice meal.
I love that place.  The spicy pork spring rolls, papaya salad (it's not sweet but spicy-crunchy)  and the pork Pad Thai are wonderful. Not your typical Thai place - it's the real deal.

Came here for lunch on a Friday afternoon. Place was fairly crowded already. We ordered a bit of everything to try, their spice level was exactly what we liked. Price was a bit on higher end though and portion was on smaller end as well. Expected of place in city though

Got food poisoning from here. 

Also: Perfectly average Thai food, not sure what the hype is about in the midst of these rave reviews. Some places I would risk again and again for food poisoning because they are that amazing (lol) but this ain't it. Not going back. 

Thai tea was good though. Not too sweet n
The pad Thai was spicy but not too spicy. It seemed fairly authentic. The spring rolls were amazing!

First time trying Northeastern Thai cuisine, and this place was so delicious for a reasonable price!

We ordered a variety of dishes, all of which were flavorful and delicious. My favorite was definitely the pork neck, which is one of their specials--it was so tender and flavorful, and the sauce is a great addition too! The papaya salad doesn't miss either.

Also, if you want to try a drink, the longan juice is super fresh and sweet.

I think the food here is pretty unique! The dishes don't seem like your typical Thai or viet dishes. I'd highly recommend a papaya salad since they have many different kinds. I also loved the coconut sticky rice skewers - the texture is chewy and kinda smoky paired with a grilled meat was really good. Of course we got a typical carb as well which was the most typical dish of all but still solid! They also have really good cocktails, the lychee is my top choice!

I'll keep it simple....

THIS IS THE BEST THAI FOOD I HAVE EVER HAD IN NYC... EVER !!

The Food Menu is very unique owing to Isan / Northern Thai Cuisine and it is ABSOLUTELY spicy and delightfully tasty..

The drinks menu is also very unique...

No matter WHAT You order, You won't be disappointed..

We had Pad Kee Mao (Pork), Impossible Larb Wraps, Martinis, Sundried Pork with Sriracha sauce, Thai Ice tea and so much more..

The people who work here are SO nice, polite and kind...

Itching to go back to this place to try everything on the menu... WHAT AN ABSOLUTE TREAT - AFTER AGES !!
I've been around the block and this is hands down the best Thai food in Manhattan, nothing else to say.  Needs it's Michelin star back or a Bib Bourmand at the minimum.

Since our first time visiting Somtum Der, I have craving for more of their delicious finger licking and freshly prepared food. They have the Michelin star for a reason. I loved the papaya salad and crispy leaf fish fried rice. The drinks are well balanced and the ambience is quite laid back. It was a pleasant dinner and it wasn't as expensive as I expected it to be. We will definitely be coming back for more.
I'm in love with their sticky rice and beef. Such a treat every time I'm in the mood for authentic cuisine.

Somtum Der has delicious, flavorful Thai food with good vibes, I highly recommend coming in for lunch with friends! I got the Basil Fried Rice and it had the perfect amount of spice, as I love a dish with a good kick to it, with the classic basil flavor. My friends got the classic pad see-ew, which were a delight to eat as well. They did forget one of the dishes until we mentioned, but were very nice about getting it out to us right away. Overall a great Thai food experience!

BEST THAI PLACE! Super spicy though... so prepare yourself! It's hard for me to find Thai food that exceeds my expectations - I feel like a lot of restaurants are just okay. But Somtum Der is def somewhere I keep coming back to and probably will be one of my only go-to Thai places! The variety of each dish and offering on the menu is amazing! There's definitely something for everyone. Even the simple noodles like Pad Thai have so much flavor! Highly recommend but prepare your taste buds for the spice!

As a Thai food enthusiast, I was excited to try this former Michelin star nominated restaurant but Somtum Der was a miss for me. 

We ordered the Fried Chicken, Impossible Larb Wraps, Basil Fried Rice and Pad Kee Mao. Both the Fried Chicken and Basil Fried Rice tasted delicious but the other two dishes were pretty mediocre. I usually prefer spicy food but the Impossible Larb Wraps were too spicy for us to enjoy or even finish. Most of the entrees also did not have a chicken option for the meat and the sauces had a strong fish scent.

Drinks: 
Lon gon juice

Entrees: for my table's order we asked for no spice 
Drunken noodle w/ shrimp 
Impossible Larb  
Pad see ew w/ vegetables 
Papaya salad with salted egg 
Pork neck 
Moo ping Kati sod pork

Desserts:
Black jelly w/ fresh milk 
Taro in condensed coconut milk
Thai tea panna cotta 

Everything was delicious! All of this is enough for 3-4 people

One of my favorite Thai places in the city! We made a reservation for a party of four on a Tuesday night but it was relatively easy to make and didn't have to be made weeks in advance. The staff was friendly and the dishes were super authentic. Be warned though their spices go hard and they definitely bring the heat! If you don't have a good spice tolerance make sure to order the non spicy dishes. The fried rice dish we got, the Khao Pad Kraprao Moo was a hit with my friends and I. Even though it's labeled as spicy it wasn't spicy at all and my friends loved it. We also tried the Tom Saab Kradook On which is a spicy soup and this one was very spicy but delicious. The skewers we ordered were also very tasty and came with coconut rice balls which were a nice sweet touch. 

Come Again? Yes! It was so flavorful and everything was reasonably priced. I also like how it's not too overhyped / impossible to get a table.

Oh boy is the food here good. I'd say its as good as sripraphai except you don't have to go to Queens to get this kind of legit thai food!

We asked for it mild, but the papaya salad with field crabs lit my mouth up worse than the Last Dab from Hot Ones! So be prepared if you order a papaya salad that it can be hotter than you expect!

We also had the fried chicken thigh, Marinated Beef with Sticky Rice, Spicy Basil Fried Rice, and Wok Fried Seafood Suki. I think its probably hard to go wrong here so just order everything that looks good.

Extremely rude service, Avg Thai food, extremely limited vegetarian selections, small food portions, and inconsistent food quality of the same dish. Four of us went and ordered only two vegetarian choices - a fried rice and pad see ew. When food came, we noticed how tiny the food portions were. Also the pad see ew didn't have any spice. My teen son wanted to eat more and we ordered repeat of the same. But the pad see ew was super spicy and fried rice was extremely salty, second time around. Somehow we tolerated salty fried rice but we told the waiter politely that pad see ew was inedible as it was super spicy. We explained to her, we generally eat a lot of spicy food and Thai food was our favorite any where we go. But instead of listening to us, she went off on a rude rant accusing us of not knowing how to order and since we tasted it (All four of us took a bite to confirm it was incredibly spicy), she can't fix anything. Never seen a restaurant have such rude staff yelling at fully paying customer, unwilling to listen let alone, get things right for paying customer! Never stepping in this restaurant again!

This place is phenomenal. The food is so tasty and flavorful. The drinks are good too but I'd come again more so for the food. We ordered a few apps and rice/noodle dishes. Everything came out fast and although I thought the portions were a bit small for a family style concept, this place is def worth it. Highly recommend for anyone looking for an authentic Thai experience.
