Authentic Thai restaurant. The food has a kick to it. I have tried a few of their lunch specials that come with  a drink. The dishes are extremely flavorful. I am so glad to have found a gem of a restaurant in Manhattan. My favorite Thai spot by far!

- recommend: Moo or Nue Ping Kati Sod (beef skewer), Pad Ki Mao/drunken noodles (seafood), thai sabai 
- Nam Tok Moo (medium spicy) was intensely spicy, the flavors were great but were overshadowed by spiciness, I can't even begin to imagine how hot "spicy" would've been. I like spicy but not when it distracts from the other flavor components
- the thai sabai cocktail was refreshing, would recommend if you enjoy Caipirinhas or Mojitos
- will be back to try the rest of the menu
-portions are modest but quality is evident

Came to this restaurant when it was an hour before closing and I am so surprised how they still managed to get all the food so tasteful. Highly recommend the pad Thai, and the raw shrimp. Super spicy but flavorful. Also order the fry rice dish and other appetizers and I can tell you.. NOTHING WENT WRONG. Everything were amazing.
Updating my review to 5 stars based on a recent visit. They also have real menus now which are very nice and describe everything well.
We were pleasantly surprised by the quality of food! Great interior and food esthetics. Would definitely recommend :)
underrated! Adorable spot and was easy to get a reservation. Thai cuisine but more unique than the basic spots. Would recommend! Dishes are good for sharing

I've been here twice. The first time was a late night unplanned dinner and I remember being very impressed with the pad se ew as it was unique in that it tasted like it had a lot of white pepper. I love white pepper. The service was fast and friendly.

The second time I tried the yum trai kai sardine which was very different from any Thai food I've had before. It was salty. It was sour. It was definitely very good! The pad ki mao was ok.

Recently my friend went to a Somtum der in a different borough. I had no clue it had multiple locations. 

Overall, the food was good and worth trying once, but Soothr still remains my go to dine in and take out Thai place in the neighborhood.

We had a fantastic meal at Somtum Der with our friends the other day! We didn't get pictures of all of our dishes (we came hungry!), every bite was delicious. I would say my favorite was the pork skewers or the fried chicken thigh.

We tried getting the thai tea Panna cotta (apparently, they're really well known for it), but unfortunately, they were out of it by the time we ordered it.

The chicken appetizer here was amazing, so crispy and the sauce was perfect with it. The drinks were also delicious. The pad see eiw was one of my favorite I've tried. They have so many interesting dishes here if you're not vegetarian. Highly recommend!

Tried Tom Klong Pla Dook Yang (fried fish soup) this time, liked the flavor, but the fried fish became soggy in the soup...
Moo Yor Tod (looks like tofu, taste like sausage) and Goong Char Nam Pla (shrimp sashimi) are as good as before.

I have been to Somtum Der more than a handful of times and will continue making the trip out for more trips. Somtum Der, in my opinion, is the best Thai restaurant in Manhattan and top five in NYC. The service is quick and the food is so flavorful, you'll be asking for seconds while still at the table.

Every time I have gone, I have ordered both the Papaya Salad which they are famous for and the Pad Kee Mao. The Papaya Salad is so spicy and hits flavors I have never experienced, sweet, salty and sour mixed into an incredible bite. The Pad Kee Mao is the one dish I would go running back to Somtum Der for. The noodles are so perfectly cooked every time and the flavor and texture of each bite is incredibly unique. 

Somtum Der needs to be on your NYC hit list. I fell in love with this place the first time I visited and will always bring guests here from out of town, it is incredible.

Really knocked my socks off with the exotic-ness of the dishes. From raw shrimp to amazing specialties. The decor is nice and vibration with a mysterious vibe on the outside. The place was busy and poppin with no spare on service. The waiter was always alert and catered to all my request with a kind gesture. Need recommendations, they got you! Need to adjust your spicyness to some dishes, say less and tell em. The taste was definitely unique and I would come back to try more dishes. They're specials are really good and changes from time to time so you get something new each time. Would def go here if I feel for some Thai and spicy.

I love this place. So much! I order it all the time and like to bring friends from out of town here. I always order the Khao Pad Kraprao Moo (minced pork and basil fried rice with an egg) and it's very spicy and delicious! Usually fills up in weekends but we walked in as a group of 5 one Saturday and only waited 10 minutes.

So so yummy!! Friend recommended this spot for spice lovers and the spice definitely did not disappoint!! We were impressed by all the dishes, but the standout for all of us was the raw shrimp. I also loved the Papaya Salad and Khao Pad Kraprao. We walked in at 6:30pm on a Sat night for a table of 4 and were seated immediately, though the place was packed! Solid spot for Thai food, definitely will come back very soon.

Hands down one of the best Thai restaurants I've ever been. The Somtum Thai papaya salad was so good! Best I've had in restaurants. However, I didn't favor the Tum Muo. It was more on the fishy/ salty side. This dish was described as as Isan Style papaya salad. Because these kind of dishes usually has an acquired taste I'm not complaining. The spicy liver salad was also top notch! It was tossed in larb dish seasonings. The spice level was true to itself. Some places gives a thai hot level but not really spicy at all.  This wasn't the case for this place. 

We got the Pad Thai & Chicken wings to go but still taste great the next day. Must of been even better fresh.

A place I would definitely go back to. They take reservations and some walk-ins. I would recommend a reservation because they were pretty busy.

Came here with the family on a whim when we couldn't find anywhere else that had open seating on a Friday night. The first thing I noticed was the smell of the restaurant. It was staaaanky! I'm usually not very picky about the smells of restaurants, but it kind of smelled like feet, which wasn't that pleasant during the meal. We ordered about 5-6 plates to share. The papaya salad was probably the best one out of all of them. They're pretty small plates and I would say not much protein/meat on the ones that were supposed to be more of an entree dish. They were also kind of pricey for what it was. All of them were quite flavorful, but also SUPER spicy which kind of dampened the flavors a bit, which was a bit unfortunate. We are Malaysians and can generally eat pretty spicy food, but this was next level and we were rinsing out our mouths towards the end. All in all, there definitely better Thai restaurants in NYC and likely won't return.

I have gone here multiple times to get their Pad See Eiw.
So so so delicious. The perfect amount of flavor, not too salty. And they give you enough to feel perfectly full haha
The service is okay. I don't remember much of the service but nothing stood out to be bad haha My friend has ordered something that the employees said is only a little bit spicy. And it ended up being extremely spicy lol so beware or what the employees tell you about spice.
There is usually a line to get in during the weekends so it is probably safer if you get a reservation!

Loved this spot! Food was delicious, and overall portions are quite reasonable so you can share multiple items if you go as a group.

Nut allergies are well labeled. Most dishes you could adjust spice level but not all dishes. I had the Pad See Ew and it was really flavorful, great portion size, shrimp was cooked perfectly and broccoli still had a perfect crunch to it. I also tried the coconut rice skewers that were great! Very reasonably priced. 

Reservations for large groups are a must! The restaurant is quite busy and loud so although you can go in large groups it is not a space just for the group. The waiter was really good about splitting the check into smaller groups and did an excellent job. They were fast, friendly and helpful with recommendations.
Delicious food, incredibly authentic. I suggest getting their pork skewers and their fried rice.

First time New York visit and I wanted to checkout the Southeast Asian foodie scene. Sometimes Der had the perfect menu so we took to subway over. It's pretty close ~5-10min walk from the subway. The aesthetics were super cute, clean loved the so Tun station. Fast service, we were greeted and seated right away. We ordered a variation of beef and pork laab, papay salad, pad Thai and sticky rice. The pad Thai always very flavorful. Both laab were juicy and had the perfect amount of seasoning, went along wonderfully with the sticky rice. Was not too big of a fan of the tum with crab but I LOVED the extra spicy Tom with vermicelli! All I could think about after eating here was my next visit lol this is probably one of the first place where their spicy is actually spicy! I came back two days later and ordered more laab and papaya! Definitely going to recommend to all my friends who are planning to visit NY. Can't wait for future visits!

Food: 4.5/5 | Service: 4/5 | Experience: 4/5

I made a reservation for 3 for a weekday night. Tables were pretty close to each other, but it was not too much of a bother. We ordered the fried chicken, kor moo yang, nam tok beef, suki seafood, and white sticky rice.

The food came out in stages rather than all at once. The fried chicken was pretty crispy. The kor moo yang pieces were smaller than expected, but it was quite tasty. The nam tok beef was my favorite dish. It was acidic and herby and felt light even though it was meat. The suki seafood was a bit too much of an amalgamation of food, but it was well spiced.

Overall, the portion sizes were smaller than I expected given the pictures on the menu, but the dishes definitely packed flavor.

Was really excited to try this place, but the eating experience was terrible. The entire staff was unmasked and coughing. It made for a very uncomfortable eating experience. Stayed no longer then 15 minutes after the food came out. I mean I get it, it's a restaurant but if you're entire staff is sick maybe serving guests with food coughed on isn't the best idea.
No other way to describe this place other than best thai in the City. They don't shy away from spice and heat, so be prepared, but truly has some of the most consistently good meals you can find

Looking for authentic Thai spice? This place is for you. Good and true tasting papaya salad is hard to come by, and this place is definitely one of the few places that's able to balance the tastes of Thai street food. Be warned though, this place's spice level had me sipping on my drink every bite! 

My favorite dish was probably the larb. The flavor profile is so similar to Thailand. Do yourself a favor and also add an order of the sticky rice to eat with these dishes -- not only does it calm the fire, but using it to soak up some of juices is a way we Thai people like to enjoy the meal! 

If you're wondering what papaya salad you should order, I think I would actually recommend getting the most basic option. We got one of the Isan styles that add crab, and it's a bit too salty for me. Also keep in mind that the Isan style papaya salad tend to be more salty anyway so it's just not my favorite style personally. But I would recommend trying one and sharing for the table if you're curious! 

The Pad Thai I think you can skip -- there was nothing too special about it. Service was very no thrills, but I appreciated their honesty about how much food to order. It can get pretty loud in the restaurant, and it's definitely more of a casual dining experience over a fancy one! The only thing I think that brought this down to 4 stars was the service and the portion sizes for the cost, but other than that the place is worth the try for the flavor. 

I also ordered the longan drink expecting that I needed something to cool down the spice, and I would recommend getting a drink on the side because it really helped a lot!

If I could give 0 stars I would. The food is total garbage. Don't waste your time and money; there's so many other options to go to. We ordered 2 Pad Se Ew with vegetables and 2 Special thai dish. They definitely cooked the dishes together and just split the portions because the portions for $16 was so small. To make things worse, one of my friends got 0 noodles on her plate and my other friend got all noodles. The seafood on their plate was overcooked and the "vegetables" for the pad se ew was literally 2 pieces of frozen fried tofu, broccoli and cabbage. Service was whatever and ambiance is...well there's no strong ac on these hot summer days so....
Long story short: don't come. It's a wonder how they even had a Michelin star to begin with but no surprise they lost it.

I really wanted to try this place, because someone from Singapore said it was the best Thai food he'd had! And the feel was authentic - I got the Tum Muo papaya salad, expecting it to be any other Thai papaya salad I'd had before, just with the additions of the Thai sausage, but be warned! The fish sauce in this is VERY FISHY. Like literally how it smells to be by the live seafood in an Asian market. I really could not eat more than a few bites of this because of that. I really was not used to this flavor and did not enjoy it one bit. It coated all the rest of the ingredients, so I just had to sum that dish up as a loss. The Pad Thai I ordered alongside it as a safe dish was really good, in terms of the flavors, the texture of the rice noodle, so I was able to finish that whole dish up on my own. Overall, great food that is authentic, nice service, but I would avoid the fishy papaya salad.

I stopped by Somtum Der with a party of 4 on a Tuesday night right before they opened at 6pm and were seated immediately. We did not have a reservation, but the place filled up pretty quickly.

I got the Pad Kee Mao which was pretty good. It wasn't really spicy as other pad kee maos i've had, but the flavor was there. The service was great, staff were really friendly. 

I would definitely come again.

Stopped by with a group of 3 and we were seated right away. Inside, the restaurant was spacious and cute. The staff was nice and refilled our waters, but the service was average. However, the food was overpriced for what it was and in my opinion, not worth it. I ordered the Chef's special wok fried seafood suki. This was a noodle dish but it was served with only a few strands of noodles. The dish was also drowned in sauce, which made it unenjoyable. The ingredients were also not very fresh. I'm not sure how this place has such high ratings but I left very disappointed and hungry. My friends also did not enjoy their food. There are definitely better Thai spots in the area. Don't think I'll be back unfortunately.

This is my favorite for authentic northeastern Thai food in NYC. If you want to try authentic Thai food, this is the spot! The ambience makes you feel like you're in Thailand. 

We recommend the grilled coconut milk marinated pork, papaya salad, goong chae nam pla (shrimp), and grilled pork neck. The service was great!

This place is SO GOOD. Some of my Thai friends have been raving about this place so I finally decided to check it out and I loved it. I never had northern Thai food but this changed my outlook as I love sour and spicy dishes. My friends and I ordered so much to share and I have to say, the larb ped and tum mangsavirat were my favorite - they were spicy but so so good. The waiter does ask how spicy you want, so definitely feel free to adjust. We got all dishes medium spicy but had to get rice to go with it, so maybe err on the safe side and get the dishes mild spicy if it's your first time here! I will most definitely be back to try other dishes!!

Really enjoyed my time at Somtum Der! Heard rave things about this place and it definitely lived up to the hype! The menu focuses more on authentic northern Thai food, which I wasn't as familiar with initially. 
The Tum Thai Kai Kem was a refreshing green papaya salad with a fermented crab/shrimp sauce and lime juice. Loved the balance of savory and citrus flavors. They also add in salted duck egg and dried shrimp flakes, which give the dish multiple layers of umami! 
The Sa Poak Kai Tod Der features their signature fried chicken that is very well-seasoned and clearly marinated with lemongrass. I wasn't a huge fan of the dip but it was like a tamarind based sauce with additional seasoning. 
The Khao Klook Ka Pi had a wonderful combo of barbecued pork and fermented shrimp paste! It had a nice balance of shrimp vs pork flavors and I loved the garlic/onion crisps that it came with. 
The staff were super friendly and nice. Surprisingly we got a spot for lunch very quickly on a weekend. Lots of seating inside with a nice summer-y bar decor in the back. I can see why this place is so popular and I for sure want to come back!

Som Tum Der is an absolute star of a restaurant. The food is always fabulous- spicy and bursting with the intense flavour of fresh herbs. There is more than one kind of papaya salad on the menu,  and each is divine in its own right. The warm grilled beef salad is also fabulous. I usually get a salad and either one of the grilled meat dishes (i love the sundried beef and the beef skewers specifically) or one of the fried rice dishes. All are superb. They used to have an addictive dipping sauce specifically for the skewers but they switched it out for one which isn't as good but still nice. I take all my out of town/out of neighborhood visitors to Somtum Der and they always remember it as one of their stellar food experiences in the city. And that's saying a lot.

I got to-go, so I can't speak to service or ambiance or anything like that. 

They are not joking when they say the crab pad thai (pad thai mun poo) is spicy. The only options are "spicy" and "extra spicy", and oh my god it was so spicy. I really wish there was an option to make it slightly less spicy, because the heat overpowers the crab. 

The grilled sticky rice on a stick is awesome and my new favorite way of eating sticky rice. Will definitely be ordering it again. 

I also got the Larb Ped (Duck Larb) which... for being mild was also pretty spicy at times. It was good, except for some weirdly crunchy duck pieces with a texture I just personally didn't care too much for. 

Overall, will be ordering again. I think it would probably have been easier for me to order there instead of online, because the menu is a little intimidating (and i'm not a stranger to thai food!) but i'm decently impressed. 

i will say - food spot if you want legit thai food. probably not a spot i would order from drunk at midnight when i want a pad thai, but there are a hundred other places in the east village for drunk thai food.

This Thai restaurant is kind unique in that it features Thai food from northeastern region of Thailand. Flavors seem to be more on the sour, tangy side, which is very different from the southern region of Thailand. Beware some of the dishes are quite spicy, notably the sashimi shrimp and duck salad. I was dying after those two dishes, and kept having to chug water (my spice tolerance is normally pretty high).

1. Fave dish would be the sashimi shrimp before I got killed by the chili peppers  shrimp tasted fresh, and was refreshing 
2. Second fave dish would be the papaya salad- flavors were on point ‍
3. Third fave was the beef skewers- coconut milk was an interesting touch 
4. Fried chicken- was not expecting it to have bones? But generally pretty flavorful 
5. Pork neck- this was quite fatty, not sure if I'm a huge fan 
6. Duck salad- we got the medium spicy, but for some reason it was still very spicy?? Must be the chili peppers 

Overall verdict: very interesting flavors and unique dishes! Different from your typical basic Thai items. Would recommend!

Excellent friendly and proactive service.

Theres ample room in the casual space.

The food was all quite good. Flavors were strong and unique.

First came here a few years ago and everything my friend and I ordered was AMAZING. Family from out of town came to visit recently and wanted good Thai food so I suggested we come here. The restaurant was a lot less busy than what I remembered, service and food was also subpar than what I remembered. I feel like the flavor fell a bit and portions got smaller. Just good, but nothing better than any other place.

Ordered takeout via Caviar. Spicy pad Thai, the Kuay Tieo Pad See Eiw, and Tum Thai (papaya salad). Papaya salad was the only saving grace, the other two noodle dishes were horrible. Absolutely horrible. Quite flavorless and disappointing.

This is a fantastic choice for Thai food. I had the tum mangsavirat (papaya salad) and pad ki mao with vegetables. I loved the tangy flavor and fresh vegetables in the papaya salad. The noodles had a delicious, smoky flavor. I especially loved the tofu, which was cut into discs. All of the food was of very high quality.

I got the vegetable Pad Thai with tofu and it was good but I wish there were some more spices. The food came very quickly though! We were very impressed with the service and the staff was very friendly.

We came here for dinner and we were able to make a reservation. We did have to call in since our party was a bit bigger but they were able to accommodate us. The staff was very nice. 

We ordered a lot of things but my favorite was the shrimp and the coconut sticky rice. The shrimp was good and spicy but it was very fresh. The temperature of all the food came out really well. This was some of the best Thai food I've had in NYC. I will definitely come back for the shrimp itself.
This is one of the best Thai restaurants downtown. We highly recommend the chicken appetizer and skewers plus the crab fried rice. We are definitely coming back for the fish.
Got delivery, and the usuals i like were quite different this time. The crab fried rice and chicken soup lacked its usual nuanced flavors and was very salty.

It's a real taste of local Thai foods 
Spicy, tangy and tasty  
If you like an authentic spicy dishes, here's the place

Came on a Thursday night to enjoy a cute dinner with friends! We got this recommendation from Thai friends who said this spot comes close to authentic thai food so we knew we needed to check it out

the service was really good! we ordered a bunch of things and it came out pretty quick. plus they were very on it when it came to refilling our water - everyone was kind, helpful, and very happy! we made sure to leave a generous tip

the food: the skewers, fried chicken, spicy pork were so bomb. loved that things were actually spicy. my favorite is def the beef skewers it was so juicy and tender. lots of authentic thai flavor in these dishes. i was very disappointed in the pad thai - it seriously lacked flavor. it was so bland i used sauces from other dishes to make it taste better. the spicy papaya salad was supposed to have crab but it only had the shell - definitely not worth it and was annoying to pick out.

overall had a pleasant experience and would recommend!

My friend and I stopped by for a weeknight dinner. We had reservations for 7pm but when we got there there were plenty of seats available.

We started with the Larb Moo, which was rather disappointing. At first glance, you can see that the dish we got looked like a very sad version of the thing in the menu. It didn't have any of the colourful herbs and spices like pepper and basil. The meat was fine-ish? Not much flavour that you could really tell underneath the overpowering sourness of the lemongrass. (To be clear I am familiar with how Thai food is often supposed to be sour. This was just overwhelmingly so; I think the flavours here were just really imbalanced.) I also didn't think this dish was spicy at all, despite the server's warning. Wouldn't recommend this dish.

We also had the pad see ew and the tom saab kradook on. Pad see ew was... fine? at best? But very bland. The noodles didn't have much flavour at all. It didn't feel like any of the sauce/flavour in general had been absorbed; when you took a bite, it was clear that the noodle was still really pale and bland on the inside. Not sure if the dish was lacking in seasoning, soy sauce, or a good wok (!) Otherwise it was fine but really nothing special.

The tom saab kradook on was generally not bad. The soup was Very sour as advertised and a little too heavy for our taste (more so than most other Thai soups I've had at other places). The strong lemongrass flavour also dominated the overall profile as well, especially since we didn't really feel like it was spicy. The chicken was generally tasty and well-cooked, definitely the high point of the meal.

Sigh I'm not sure if we just ordered the wrong things or what, but I came away from this meal with a distinct sense of disappointment, especially with such high expectations from its Bib Gourmand rating. And - it wasn't cheap either (and I def don't think the price point was commensurate).

I think I could be convinced to come again if I got some better recommendations for what to order lol... but for the time being I do not think I will be back :(

Somtum Der was once awarded a Michelin star, now it is just Michelin recommend. I wonder why that happened...

The food was delicious. The noodle dishes we ordered had so much flavor. The ambiance is very casual and relaxed. The service was just okay, but overall we enjoyed our visit

Our highlights:
- Isan fried rice noodles 
- Pad Thai

psa: the side sauce that comes with the pork skewers was horrible . The skewers were amazing, but that sauce it's a no for me

love, @partyxtwo

I knew this place was going to be good when I saw the giant Krok (Thai mortar and pestle) and that the other diners were speaking Thai.  I came here for lunch with a few of my friends and we ordered various dishes. Flavor was spicy, tangy, and pack with umami just what you want in Thai-Isan food. Arguably, the best Thai-Isan food in NYC or even America. The service was good and the ambiance reminded me of Thailand.

Now, addressing some of the less favorable reviews that I've come across. While everyone is entitled to their opinion on food and service, I find it funny that a bunch of East Asian-Americans claiming to know what Thai flavors are or what is authentic just because they visited Bangkok once in their life.  One particular critique stating the food was excessively sour appears to reflect a palate  accustomed to overly sweet Pad Thai. 

If you want the typical Thai flavor stick to your local neighborhood Thai spot but if you want something unique and exceptional try this spot out.

IG: @mrtravelfoodie

Let's start with I don't know how this place isn't always packed! I came at 12pm on a Saturday and we were the first ones at opening with nobody behind us. The service was amazing, the decor is interesting, but the food? PHENOMENAL!

We ordered:

Appetizers:
- Tum Suo Der
Soho:
- Tom Yum Goong (Creamy)
Salad:
- Nam Tok Nue
Noodle:
- Pad Ki Mao w/ Pork
Sides:
- Steamed sticky rice

Every single dish was INCREDIBLE, but my highlights were

1. Nam Tok Nue
2. Tom Yum Goong
3. Pad Ki Mao
4. Tum Suo Der

Even though I rank in this order, every dish was insanely tasty! Be warned though, the food is SPICY and creeps up on you. I was struggling in the middle of my meal but couldn't stop eating cuz it's sooo good!

Tonight was my second time to Somtum Der, and it was top notch once again. Somtum Der and Soothr are neck and neck for my fav Thai food ever. I don't remember what I got the first time I went, but this time we had the papaya salad for the table, and my girlfriend and I split two entrees: the veggie pad Thai and the chefs seafood wok. Both were SO good. I'm a seafood person but not a huge shrimp person because the vast majority of the time shrimp is chewy. This is the first time I've everrr had perfectly cooked shrimp. Not the least bit chewy, so tender and so delish. High quality all around. The lemongrass juice was very yummy too. It's a cute spot with attentive staff as well.
So delicious! Eaten here multiple times and never disappointed.  Working my through trying all the papaya salads!

I came here at the suggestion of reviews since I was curious in trying a new Thai spot.  Many of the diners mentioned that the flavors here are unique and different from your typical Thai cuisine and that couldn't be more accurate!

*AMBIANCE*
While they do take reservations, we came without one and had to wait about 30 minutes.  The tables are quite snug to each other but the ambiance felt warm.

*FOOD*
They have a large ample selection on their menu from rice dishes, noodles, to salads.  I was able to try their:

-Tamarind chicken wings (monthly special) 
-Shrimp Pad Thai

The chicken wings were so yummy, crunchy on the outside and tender on the inside. Almost if you thought about marinating a Korean fried chicken wing with Thai seasoning.  I would absolutely order this again.

The pad thai was tasty too and had a sweet sauce to it.  Texture wise, they had these tiny red flakes in them which was different and sometimes made it hard to eat.  I think would've preferred for there to be less of them.

*SERVICE*
Service was very good and attentive.  Water glasses were constantly filled and we got our dishes in a reasonable amount of time.

Overall, recommend trying if you want something different from your usual Thai spot!

burnt pork pad see ew for $20? all i could taste was burnt pork w light sauce on the noodles

good service though and perhaps dining in is better

We came here on a Sunday afternoon for lunch. We had prawn sashimi, larb ped salad (minced duck), chicken wings and pad Thai. All the dishes were delicious. The prawn sashimi and larb ped salad were more spicy than expected, but the prawn sashimi was still my favorite. I don't think I've had any dish like that at any other Thai restaurant in NYC before. I'd like to come back again and try other dishes.

Top North Eastern (Isan) Thai place in the city. It's been around over a decade with once a Michelin star for a reason (they are way better than new places like Zaap Zaap, etc.). Caution!! They are one of a few places in Manhattan that will deliver real Thai spicy levels if you ask for it and it is seriously uncompromising. My favorite is som tum Thai and plara with 3 chilies (dont do 4 or you lips would burn), nam tok moo, and tom zaab. There Isan-inspired drinks are also pretty soothing when you have that much spice on your lips.

I love this place! This is a perfect place to go for a casual meal- no frills. I came here a few months ago for lunch with two of my friends and still haven't forgotten about the food. 

When we went in, there were a lot of tables, so definitely not the type of place that you need a reservation for. Everything on the menu is priced very well- you can easily have a lunch or dinner here for less than $15 and will likely be just as good (if not better!) than a lot of the Thai restaurants near by. 

I got the Khao Pad Kraprao Moo/Nue, which had a perfectly fried egg and basil. The pad see ew was also well seasoned and had a balance of noodles, shrimp, and vegetables. I had a really nice experience at Somtum Der and definitely will be back!

Yummmmmmm - having walked to the area looking for a fun lunch nearby (only to discover that place didn't open for lunch - oops, should have checked yelp for the hours), we passed Somtum Der and a lightbulb went off. Hmmm, didn't I read something about this place? Wasn't there some fabulous dish I had to try here?

Well, in we stepped and were sat promptly. The place hits you with a mix of funky, fresh, fermented, sour, spicy smells the moment you walk in...totally tantalizing. We had a spicy papaya (superb) salad, a grilled pork dish with a spicy, funky (there's that word again) dipping sauce and a pad kee mao. Everything was excellent and very fast. Medium spicy was intense but we like the hot stuff so that worked for us. 

Thai iced tea and quick service rounded out the meal nicely. Very happy to have stumbled upon somtum der and would make it a point to return on purpose!

I've read many reviews commenting on how the food here doesn't taste like the typical Thai restaurants that we are used to, and this is all very true. We were seated right away on a Sunday not long after opening time.  Seating is a bit tight. They have a wide selection on their menu and most of the foods are not things we typically see as well.  We enjoyed the moo ping Kati sod (grilled coconut milk marinated pork skewers), and the spicy pad thai, they were both delicious. We also ordered pad pak (grilled vegetables over rice) and fried chicken but these we weren't so on board with, we felt that it wasn't so flavorful, maybe this is what the dish is supposed to taste like, but we just didn't really like it.  One thing that we thought is heavenly is the Thai tea Panna cotta. We were told we got the last one for the week and I'm so glad that we got it.  It was so soft and creamy and the flavor is just so perfect! We both lit up after trying it.

The Larb Moo is a must-try, showcasing flavors that hit the mark (for my cilantro lovers). The Chef's Signature Wok Fried Seafood Suki, while satisfactory, didn't quite match the Larb Moo. It's worth noting that, post-indulgence, we didn't feel our best, so consider prepping your body accordingly for the salty, spicy, and sweet food. Portion sizes lean on the smaller side; I'd advise opting for three dishes for two people.

The place was cute. Service was good but overall did not like the food. I enjoyed the papaya salad but was on salty end and the noodles were okay and the rice dish was nothing special. The portion weren't bad but flavors were way too salty

Cool, trendy, authentic Thai cuisine. Service was quick and extremely accommodating. The place is a little small but makes for a lively and packed atmosphere especially on a Friday night. Food was delicious and extremely flavorful. The Thai iced tea with milk was refreshing and smooth and was a great break between the savory, spicy dishes offered. Overall, a delicious time and a great experience. Would definitely come back again.

Fantastic and legit thai food! We had the fried chicken, grilled pork neck, Nam tok moo, pad thai and the coconut sticky rice - all good! Service was great as well. Would definitely go back to try other stuff.

The food at Somtum Der was really good. My favorite dish was the Larb Moo salad, which was flavorful and paired nicely with a side of white rice. I also had the Sa Poak Kai Tod Der, which was also good. I thought the chicken could have had more flavor on its own but it was great paired with the sauce it came with. Their menu has a really good lunch special deal that I think would definitely be worth coming back to try. Our server was great and very attentive. We sat in the booths in the back which were a bit snug but the overall ambiance was nice.

I found this to be some of the best Thai I've had in a very long time. We ordered things medium spicy which was perfect for me.  Our server was extremely helpful in recommending dishes that we all enjoyed. Unfortunately I can't remember the names of all the dishes but we had a couple of larbs, papaya salad, fish salad, a spicy pork dish and ended with a panna cotta. Every dish was fantastic. The lemongrass martini wasn't  too shabby either.  Great vibes and delicious food.

Great for traditional/classic thai food & for people who have good spice tolerance! For low spice tolerance, the chicken wings and pad thai were good! Got mild appetizers such as a papaya salad, but it was too spicy for us! Get a side of rice to help calm the spiciness!

This place, unfortunately, was mid at best. I got on of the spicy salads; I don't remember which one, I think it was a grilled fish salad that had onions on it? It was fine, but nothing to write home about and definitely a small
portion for the price. I also got lemongrass juice and that was good. My friend got pad thai and thai iced tea and she also thought her food was fine, but nothing stood out. What really turned me off was the service of this place. We went on a weekday night and I think there were two people waiting for seats. I understand the need to turn tables but the wait staff kept trying to rush us through everything - through ordering, eating, paying the bill, and rushing us out; it was really offputting. We were only at the restaurant for maybe 40 mins tops. I'm sure others probably will have better experiences but for me, I probably won't return here.
Great food and drinks! Despite being at a difficult location. Everything we tried was amazing and authentic. Even the lemon drop martini was outstanding

The food was delicious and flavorful. I got mild for the somtum and it still had a kick to it. I love the variety of somtums and other dishes. There's not many entrees such as curries or rice dishes but I still like the variety of starters. The staff was amazing. I would come back

After a 14 course 2 Michelin star restaurant, we literally went back to our hotel and needed comfort food! We wanted spicy, we wanted soup, we wanted flavor! So glad I ubereat Somtum Der! My Lao husband was so happy and went to bed so satisfied! To the point where he is planning on going back there before we leave the city! 

We ordered:
Tum poo-plara = papaya salad with salted crabs 
I asked for extra spicy 20+ peppers, they came through! So good, so authentic, so spicy!

Gaeng Om Kai: spicy chicken dill soup 
My fav! Husband approved! 

Lahp moo: minced pork salad
I asked for extra Thai peppers 

All in all, this was authenticity at its finest.
Just hella bomb Thai street food. Pretty casual atmosphere and it's pretty affordable relatively. I liked the pork jowl the most.

Popped into this spot for a quick lunch on a Friday! The restaurant was clean, with a wonderful ambiance and I was seated quickly. I ordered the pad kee mao lunch special and was blown away. As someone originally from Thailand, I crave the authentic flavors of Thai food and this hit the spot. The portion was perfect and the flavors were layered, decadent but light. The lunch special came with a drink and I had iced tea (YUM!). This was one of my favorite solo lunch dates in NYC ever :)

I would recommend this spot to anyone looking for an affordable, delicious and satisfying meal. Great spot to venture to alone or with friends.

It's rare to find a place where every dish stands out, but Somtum Der nailed it! We got there for lunch without a reservation and it was great. I would have to say Thai food is my FAVORITE cuisine!! 

**What we had:**
- Gai Yang: The grilled chicken was succulent and well-seasoned, perfect with the tangy dipping sauce.
- Sticky Rice: A must-have side that was perfectly sticky and complemented every dish
- Pad Thai
- Pad See Ew 

Each dish was a hit, making it hard to choose a favorite. But, if I had to choose, it wouldn't definitely be the Pad Thai! The flavors were authentic, vibrant, and the spiciness was just right--present but not overwhelming.

The service matched the quality of the food--efficient, friendly, and helpful, making sure we had everything we needed without being intrusive.

In conclusion, Somtum Der is a gem for anyone looking to explore Thai cuisine!!

10/10. My favorite Thai restaurant. Their Somtum/salad is amazing. Get it spicy, its worth it. Their whole menu is amazing and authentic. My personal favorites are Larb Moo, Larb Ped, and obviously their Somtum.
Amazing Thai food. We had Papaya Salad, Larb Moo and Pad Krab Pao. Make sure you know your spice level.

Food was good. Servers were very overwhelmed but still friendly and managed to get it done. Papaya salad and wings were excellent. Pad Thai and bbq pork were just ok. Would try something else next time.

Tl;dr - good food, but charged me more than price? 

The food was great, but I was just filling out my work reimbursements and I discovered that there was a mysterious $1 difference, where my receipt after taxes said $35.96 and yet I was charged $36.96 on the actual card charge they entered. 

This very well could have been a one-time mistake, but on the off chance it's a pattern, I thought I'd just document it here - might be worth checking and comparing the actual charge to your original receipt.

I love this spot as a not your-usual-yellow/green/red-curry Thai food place. It has a regional kick that is refreshing and spicy - allowing the texture of food and flavor of spice to come through. We order three dishes on different spiciness spectrum. A good blend. I'm a big fan of the sashimi shrimp and personally love rice/noodle be a bit al dente - so these sides also hit the sweet spot. The causal layout reminds me of good time eating in Thailand.

Came here at 6pm on a Sunday evening and got seated right away. It had a nice friendly ambiance with long tables in the middle and small tables on the sides. The waiters were friendly, and the food arrived quickly ~5 mins after ordering.

They also came to refill our water a few times.

Ordered the Spicy Shrimp Salad and Tamarind Chicken Wings. They were $20 and $16 respectively, coming to $2/shrimp and nearly $3 per wing. Although the food tasted good, these portions were very small for the expensive price.

This is a cute Thai spot that's brightly lit inside with beautiful wall murals and many tables inside. However, the dishes may be overpriced for the portion sizes - I kind of assumed when it was suggested we ordered 8-9 dishes for 6 people to share. We ordered 8 and weren't full in the end - it was a bummer. Flavor wise, I'm glad the spicy dishes actually had a kick to them. The service was also friendly and quick.

I had heard stellar reviews about this place so I was reallly looking forward. The menu looked amazing and it was hard to pick what to order! We started with the Somtum, very spicy I told them. I loved it, my sister thought it was too spicy. We also got the sticky rice skewers and beef- beef was too chewy in my opinion. The Somtum I felt too salty. We then also had the Tom Yum soup, nice and warm with veggies, but too much shrimp. We then also got the duck larb, which by that time we both couldn't finish because it was a lot of food. The vibe was nice and it started getting super packed by the time we finished eating. Overall the food was OK, I wasn't super impressed, and am not sure if we just ordered wrong.

Returning for a quick trip to NYC after five years, there was only one restaurant I missed. I almost hesitated because its rating had dipped to 4.1, but I'm thrilled I didn't let that stop me! Ordered all of my favorites and the food remains as exceptional as I remembered, and even more unbelievably, the familiar, friendly waitresses were still there. Despite trying other highly-rated Thai spots in town, like Fish Cheeks, nothing comes close to the flavors at Somtum Der.

I packed as much as I could to take back to the San Francisco Bay Area. You should have seen the faces of those TSA and flight attendants!! 

Somtum Der, please consider opening a location in Northern California so more people can savor your incredible Isan cuisine! And please give your fantastic staff some extra vacation days--they seemed a bit burnt out. :)

Really MID ahh food the coconut grilled rice skewers were the most tasteless Ls i've ever seen in my life. Prices are ridiculously high with barely any food attached. Interior is cool tho a bit crowded.

Stellar food and warm, attentive service. Their pad ki mao with beef and papaya salad are as good as it gets -- I was worried about the spice since I don't have the best tolerance but they asked us our preferred heat level, explained what to expect from each one, and the dishes turned out exactly as we hoped. You will not be disappointed here.
Very good Thai food In New York and I went three times I really like it. We will go back again but only one thing they must be using MSG.

After a show, my friend and I stumbled upon Somtum Der while scavenging the area for the nearest food. I opted for their Pad Thai, which was solid and authentic. To my surprise, I later discovered this restaurant is featured in the Michelin Guide. Despite this accolade, the restaurant was relatively empty, allowing us to be seated immediately.

The ambiance is quite charming, making it an ideal spot for a romantic date. The food, while undoubtedly authentic, didn't stand out and felt a bit overpriced for what it was. It seemed that we were paying more for the upscale environment rather than a truly elevated dining experience.

Pad Thai in Thailand is like the peanut butter and jelly sandwich of street food. Locals can perfect it in their sleep, and it's typically dished out by street vendors, not fancy restaurants. So, paying a premium for this everyday dish felt a bit like buying a designer-label PB&J (as ridiculous as that sounds lol.)

Despite the Michelin nod and the pleasant surroundings, the experience left me wondering if the premium was justified solely for the ambiance. For those seeking genuine flavors, you might find better value and authenticity elsewhere (perhaps at a mom-and-pop shop that doesn't charge you an arm and a leg). But for those that are on a date and want authentic Thai food with an elevated ambiance - this spot is for you.

Solid but nothing spectacular. We tried their signature fried chicken which had a new taste and texture but nothing overly flavored. Their signature noodles were delicious- would recommend you getting! And then the fried pork was also unique and would recommend.

Made a reservation so there was no wait.

Was recommended this restaurant by a friend and it did not disappoint! I ordered the pork basil fried rice with the pork and rice separate with medium spice- and it was amazing! They also gave you a side of spicy sauce with thai chilies- but it was personally too spicy for me. My friend ordered the pad see ew, which had a super nice flavor, with soft flat noodles. The thai tea latte with pretty good but nothing out of the ordinary, but the lemon thai tea was super good- the sourness of the lemon balanced out the sweetness of the tea so it didn't make me feel too bloated or full afterward! We went around 8:30pm without a reservation and luckily there was no wait! The only complaint is that it was super dark inside the restaurant so I could barely see the food in front of me, but I would say it's perfect for a vibey date night!
Delicious thai food. I recommend the Duck laab and the mango sticky rice. We'll be back!

I came here on a Monday night, and ordered Pad Ki Mao and Crispy fish- the noodles were flavorful, but the crispy fish had a rubbery/chewy texture to it. For some reason, my order took over an hr to come out, and ppl who arrived later received their meals.

I love love love this place!! I strongly recommend everyone to try this place out. The flavors of all the food - especially the vegetarian papaya salad and the pad kee mao and fried rice. The service was extremely quick too. I love the dimmed lighting, it seems like a cool spot t catch up with friends . The Thai lemon tea was delicious as well
Really good Thai food, very fresh ingredients, just no chicken dishes. Will definitely return.
Food AHMAZING, service good, and the ambiance is energetic and loud and fun and friendly vibes - it's good for groups. Can't wait to be back and take more friends
The service was quite good, but it's worth noting that the serving size was somewhat small. It might not be enough to satisfy larger appetites, so keep that in mind if you're planning to dine here.

Excellent veg green papaya salad, pork larb, shrimp pad Thai and fried chicken thigh. Veg Pad see Ew could have used some more rice noodles and the egg though good was odd looking. Pretty chill vibe, though service was quick and good. Super casual space. When asked "what do you recommend?" The waitress insisted on "fried rice". She must really like it as she was very insistent so much so, that  I was put off and ordered something else. To be super petty (hi, it's me), I did not like the menu. Not what was on it, but the fact that it had pictures. While it was helpful in iding a tantalizing fried chicken thigh, it was unhelpful in most other cases. Simpler is better (imho).

The store is super simple and clean. Mirror in the back makes it look very spacious which is nice. The staff are quite responsive.  The food seems like it was spiced to the American palette unfortunately. The food is not particularly spicy or overly flavored which was quite disappointing

Delicious Thai food at LES
We went weeks night and it was packed 
Love all the dishes we got.
My fav was tom yum soup and papaya salad

This spot is a michelin-rated restaurant that offers variety of Thai dishes, with a focus on northeastern Thai cuisine (Isan), including spicy salads, grilled meats, sticky rice, and curries. The restaurant also has a laid-back, modern atmosphere that's great for casual dining. If you're in New York and craving some excellent Thai food, Somtum Der is definitely worth a visit! Make sure to make reservation because it can be really busy especially in the evening.

Great soup, very few places that serve Cambodian food and so I'm very glad to see this. It's a great ambience. I highly recommend the curry, incredibly favorable and you can share with lots of people.

LOVEEEEEE. Ugh that papaya salad is SOOO GOOD. I still think about it . We need one of these in Long Island: those congestion tolls are a killer . I enjoyed all my food tbh. 10/10! Can't wait to go back
The sticky rice was good, and the crabs in Somtom were good; everything else was very salty, but the service was good. All the food seems to be repeated.

Good but not great. Would recommend the pork neck papaya salad, which was the best thing I had. Dining partner also loved the chicken soup. Ordered two larb salads, the duck one had a weird flavor and the pork liver one was just ok.

Food was really yummy and well priced. I had the the pad si eiw and it was just amazing. I had the New Sour so good, and the spike Thai tea that is a very cool idea and tasted amazing. Really recommend this place
good food good spring roll the sauce was super yum and epic yes i like i like the pad see ew yum
